AddTrackModel.text:
# AddTrackModel (Widget model, data-management plugin)

Holds the Add track widget's form: the data file and its index, the adapter and track type guessed from them, the track name and assembly, and the URL list for adding several tracks at once.

## Actions
- `setMixinData(arg: Record<string, unknown>, missing?: string | undefined) => void`: What the adapter's picker adds to the track config, and why it cannot make a track yet, if it cannot.
- `setWorkflowForm(key: string, form: object) => void`: Store one workflow's form; `workflowForm` in core reads and patches it.
- `setWorkflowName(name: string) => void`
- `setAdapterHint(obj: string) => void`
- `setTextIndexingConf(conf: IndexingAttr) => void`
- `setTextIndexTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setTrackData(obj: FileLocation) => void`
- `setIndexTrackData(obj: FileLocation) => void`
- `setDetectedIndex(obj: FileLocation, name: string) => void`: Records an index found beside the main file. Ignored when an index is already set, since a probe resolving late must never overwrite one typed while it was in flight.
- `setAssembly(str: string) => void`
- `setTrackName(str: string) => void`
- `setTrackType(str: string) => void`
- `clearData() => void`

## Getters
- `trackContainer: TrackContainer | undefined`: The track list a submitted track opens in.
- `trackAdapter: AdapterConfig | undefined`
- `trackName: string`
- `submittableTrackName: string`: The trimmed name the track is added under. Check this one for an all-whitespace entry: `!!trackName` accepts `' '` and creates a track whose name is blank in the selector.
- `uris: (string | undefined)[]`
- `isFtp: boolean`
- `isRelativeUrl: boolean`
- `wrongProtocol: boolean`
- `adapterHintNotConfigurable: boolean`: Returns true if the user selected an adapter from the dropdown but the extension point couldn't build a config for it
- `assembly: string | undefined`
- `trackAdapterType: string | undefined`
- `trackType: string`
- `warningMessage: "" | "Warning: JBrowse cannot access files using the ftp protocol" | "Warning: You entered a http:// resources but we cannot access HTTP\n resources from JBrow…`

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.literal('AddTrackWidget')`
- `view = types.safeReference( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('view', 'stateModel'), )`
- `trackContainerId = types.maybe(types.string)`: Which of the view's track containers the new track opens in, by id. Absent, the usual case, means the view itself. The same property on HierarchicalTrackSelectorWidget sets this one.

## Methods
- `getTrackConfig(timestamp: number) => DraftTrackConfig | undefined`

AppCoreJBrowseModel.text:
# AppCoreJBrowseModel (Root model, core)

Holds the loaded config file, usually at `rootModel.jbrowse`, with actions that add and remove its assemblies and tracks. The model builds on the [JBrowseRootConfig](/docs/config/jbrowserootconfig) config model, which a state model can do because a config model is itself an MST tree.

## Actions
- `addAssemblyConf(conf: AnyConfiguration) => BaseAssemblyConfig`
- `removeAssemblyConf(assemblyName: string) => void`
- `addTrackConf(loose: { trackId: string; type?: string | undefined; }) => TrackConfigEntry | undefined`
- `addConnectionConf(connectionConf: AnyConfiguration) => PluggableConfigNode & BaseConnectionConfig`: Adds to the config's own `connections`, which every visitor to this instance loads. Takes a snapshot as readily as a built config model — the array coerces — since callers hand it plain JSON (a session spec's `sessionConnections`, the…
- `deleteConnectionConf(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => boolean`
- `deleteTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfigurationModel | { trackId: string; }) => void`
- `updateTrackConf(trackConf: { [key: string]: unknown; trackId: string; }) => void`: Updates an existing track configuration. Used to sync editable configs back to the frozen tracks array. A trackId the array repeats replaces its last entry, the one the session resolves it to.
- `addPlugin(pluginDefinition: PluginDefinition) => void`
- `removePlugin(pluginDefinition: PluginDefinition) => void`: Removes the entry the loaded copy came from — the version-pinned definition, or the bare store ref that resolved to it. Not every entry sharing a name or a ref, so the update flow's remove-then-add swaps one version for another;…
- `setDefaultSessionConf(sessionConf: IStateTreeNode | { name: string; [key: string]: unknown; }) => void`: takes the live session or a plain session snapshot
- `addInternetAccountConf(internetAccountConf: AnyConfigurationModel) => PluggableConfigNode`
- `deleteInternetAccountConf(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => boolean`

## Getters
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`

AppSessionMixin.text:
# AppSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Session getters shared by the "app" products (desktop + web) that simply delegate to the root model — `version`, `history`, `menus`, `assemblyManager` — plus `renameCurrentSession`. Centralized here so the products compose one mixin instead of re-declaring (and diverging on) the same root delegations. The root must satisfy AppRootModel.

## Actions
- `renameCurrentSession(sessionName: string) => void`

## Getters
- `root: AppRootModel`
- `version: string`
- `gitCommit: string | undefined`
- `history: { canUndo: boolean; canRedo: boolean; undo(): void; redo(): void; } | undefined`
- `assemblyManager: AssemblyManager`

## Methods
- `menus() => Menu[]`

AssembliesMixin.text:
# AssembliesMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds `sessionAssemblies` (admin-aware, persisted-with-session assemblies) and `temporaryAssemblies` (used for ad-hoc read-vs-ref style assemblies).

## Actions
- `addSessionAssembly(conf: AnyConfiguration) => BaseAssemblyConfig`
- `addAssembly(conf: AnyConfiguration) => void`
- `removeAssembly(name: string) => void`
- `removeSessionAssembly(assemblyName: string) => void`
- `addTemporaryAssembly(conf: AnyConfiguration) => BaseAssemblyConfig`: used for read vs ref type assemblies.
- `removeTemporaryAssembly(name: string) => void`

## Getters
- `assemblies: BaseAssemblyConfig[]`: sessionAssemblies plus jbrowse config assemblies. Does not include temporaryAssemblies; this is the list shown in the AssemblySelector dropdown.
- `assemblyNames: string[]`: names of the assemblies returned by the `assemblies` getter

## Properties
- `sessionAssemblies = types.stripDefault( types.array(assemblyConfigSchemasType), [], )`
- `temporaryAssemblies = types.stripDefault( types.array(assemblyConfigSchemasType), [], )`

## Methods
- `findAssemblyConf(name: string) => BaseAssemblyConfig | undefined`: The assembly config whose name or one of whose aliases is `name`, from any of the three arrays the assemblyManager draws on, or undefined.

Assembly.text:
# Assembly (Assembly Management model, core)

Loads an assembly's reference sequence names, refName aliases and cytobands, and maps each data file's refNames onto the assembly's canonical names.

## Actions
- `setStatus(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Records what the in-flight load is doing. It sits in a separate actions block (rather than next to setLoaded) so loadPre can hand `self.setStatus` to the adapters as a plain callback: it fires after awaits, outside the action that started…
- `setRefNameMismatch(adapterCacheKey: string, mismatch: RefNameMismatch) => void`: Record that an adapter's reference names and this assembly's have nothing in common. Diagnostic only: `loadRefNameMap` still returns its map and the track still loads, because a wrong guess here must not take a working track away from…
- `setLoaded({ regions, refNameAliases, lowerCaseRefNameAliases, canonicalToSeqAdapterRefNames, cytobands, geneticCodes, }: RefNameMaps & { regions: Region[]; cytobands: F…`: Applies all load-time state in a single transaction so dependent autoruns fire once, with the precomputed lowercase/name lookups already in place by the time refNameAliases becomes observable.
- `setError(e: unknown) => void`
- `setLoadingP(p?: Promise<void> | undefined) => void`
- `loadPre() => Promise<void>`
- `load() => Promise<void>`: Resolves once regions + refNameAliases are set, and rejects with the load failure. Idempotent: concurrent callers share one attempt, and a failed attempt is discarded so the next call retries.

## Getters
- `name: string`
- `aliases: string[]`
- `displayName: string`
- `refNameColors: string[]`
- `allAliases: string[]`
- `initialized: boolean`
- `allRefNames: string[] | undefined`: note: lowerCaseRefNameAliases not included here: this allows the list of refnames to be just the "normal casing", but things like getCanonicalRefName can resolve a lower-case name if needed
- `namesByCanonicalRefName: Map<string, string[]> | undefined`: canonical refName -> every name this assembly has for that sequence, canonical first. The inverse of `refNameAliases`, memoized here because the readers that want it want the whole table (the About dialog's alias listing) rather than one…
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`
- `refNames: string[] | undefined`
- `refNameToIndex: Map<string, number> | undefined`: memoized refName -> first region index, so getRefNameColor is O(1) instead of an O(n) indexOf per call (matters for assemblies with many contigs rendered in overview scalebars/rulers)

## Properties
- `configuration = types.safeReference(assemblyConfigType)`

## Methods
- `getConf(arg: string) => any`
- `hasName(name: string) => boolean`
- `getCanonicalRefName(refName: string) => string`: Returns the canonical refName for a given alias or refName. Note: The canonical name may differ from what's in the FASTA file when refNameAliases with override:true are configured. To get the name that matches the FASTA file, use…
- `getRefNameColor(refName: string) => string | undefined`
- `getRegionForRefName(refName: string) => BasicRegion | undefined`: The whole-contig region for a CANONICAL refName — its extents, and so the bounds anything placing a span on it has to clamp into. Undefined before `regions` loads, and for a refName this assembly doesn't have.
- `getGeneticCodeId(refName: string) => number`: NCBI genetic-code (translation table) id for a refName, from the assembly's `geneticCodes` config map (e.g. a mitochondrial contig = 2). Falls back to the standard code (1) for unlisted refNames.
- `getSeqAdapterRefName(canonicalRefName: string) => string`: Given a canonical refName, returns the refName used by the sequence adapter (what's in the FASTA file). Falls back to the input if no mapping exists.
- `getCanonicalRefName2(refName: string) => string`: The total canonical-refName resolver, for any name arriving from outside — off a feature, out of an RPC result, out of a session spec. A name the assembly does not know comes back unchanged, and so does one asked for before the aliases…
- `isValidRefName(refName: string) => boolean`
- `isCircularRefName(refName: string) => boolean`: Whether the assembly's `circularRefNames` lists this refName, matched through its aliases.
- `getRefNamePosition(refName: string) => number | undefined`: Where a refName — canonical or any alias — sits in this assembly's own order, which is what chromosome painting hands its palette out by. Canonicalized first because a name off a feature can be the FILE's spelling (`1` against a canonical…
- `getAliasesForRefName(refName: string) => string[]`: The other names this assembly has for the same sequence as `refName` — its aliases, whether the name handed in is an alias or the canonical name. `chr1`, `1` and `NC_000001.11` each answer with the other two.
- `getRefNameMapForAdapter(adapterConf: AdapterConf, options: BaseOptions) => Promise<RefNameAliases>`: get Map of `canonical-name -> adapter-specific-name`, memoized per adapter config so concurrent callers share one load
- `getRefNameMismatch(adapterCacheKey: string) => RefNameMismatch | undefined`: The empty-intersection verdict for an adapter under this assembly, if the map load reached one. Keyed by `adapterConfigCacheKey`, which is what a track already computes as its `rpcSessionId` — so a track looks up the diagnostic for its…

AssemblyManager.text:
# AssemblyManager (Assembly Management model, core)

Keeps an `Assembly` for each assembly in the config and the session, and looks one up by name or alias.

## Actions
- `removeAssembly(asm: Assembly) => void`: private: you would generally want to add to manipulate jbrowse.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, or session.temporaryAssemblies instead of using this directly
- `addAssembly(configuration: any) => void`: private: you would generally want to add to manipulate jbrowse.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, or session.temporaryAssemblies instead of using this directly

## Getters
- `assemblyNameMap: Record<string, Assembly>`
- `assemblyNamesList: string[]`: the canonical name of every configured assembly, read the way the afterAttach autorun names the models it builds
- `confByName: Map<string, AnyConfigurationModel>`: Every name the *configs* answer to — each assembly's `name` and its `aliases` — mapped to its config, which exists before the assembly's model does. What has knows before the models exist, and resolved by the same precedence as…
- `assemblyList: AnyConfigurationModel[]`: combined jbrowse.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, and session.temporaryAssemblies
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`

## Properties
- `assemblies = types.array(assemblyFactory(conf, pm))`: this is automatically managed by an autorun which looks in the parent session.assemblies, session.sessionAssemblies, and session.temporaryAssemblies

## Methods
- `getCanonicalAssemblyName(asmName: string) => string`
- `getDisplayName(asmName: string) => string`
- `get(asmName: string) => Assembly | undefined`: The assembly `asmName` names, or undefined. Reports a name it doesn't know to `Core-handleUnrecognizedAssembly` so a plugin can supply it. That side effect is unwanted for a caller only asking *whether* the session has the assembly, which…
- `has(asmName: string) => boolean`: Whether the session knows this assembly. Use this, not `get`, to ask only whether the assembly is present: `!has(name)` is exactly the condition under which `get` reports `name` to `Core-handleUnrecognizedAssembly`, so probing with `get`…
- `loadingAssembly(asmNames: string[]) => Assembly | undefined`: The first of `asmNames` that hasn't finished loading — the one a view blocked on them is waiting for, and whose `statusMessage` / `statusProgress` its spinner should show. Returns the assembly itself (a stable reference, so a consuming…
- `settleAssemblyResolution(assemblyName: string) => Promise<void>`: Wait out whatever might still be about to supply `assemblyName`, and resolve once nothing is.
- `waitForAssembly(assemblyName: string) => Promise<Assembly | undefined>`: use this method instead of assemblyManager.get(assemblyName) to get an assembly with regions loaded
- `requireAssembly(assemblyName: string) => Promise<Assembly>`: waitForAssembly, but a name that cannot be resolved is an error rather than an `undefined` for the caller to interpret.
- `getRefNameMapForAdapter(adapterConf: AdapterConf, assemblyName: string | undefined, opts: AssemblyBaseOpts) => Promise<RefNameAliases>`: The refName map for an adapter under `assemblyName`. Throws if the assembly cannot be resolved — see requireAssembly. No `assemblyName` at all is not a failure, just nothing to rename.
- `isValidRefName(refName: string, assemblyName: string) => boolean`

Base1DView.text:
# Base1DView (General model, core)

Holds a one-dimensional axis of displayed regions, with its zoom and scroll offset, for views other than the linear genome view, such as the two axes of the dotplot.

## Actions
- `setDisplayedRegions(regions: Region[]) => void`
- `setBpPerPx(val: number) => void`
- `setVolatileWidth(width: number) => void`
- `showAllRegions() => void`: this makes a zoomed out view that shows all displayedRegions that makes the overview bar square with the scale bar
- `zoomOut() => void`
- `zoomIn() => void`
- `zoomTo(bpPerPx: number, offset?: any) => number`
- `scrollTo(offsetPx: number) => number`
- `centerAt(coord: number, refName: string | undefined, displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`
- `scroll(distance: number) => number`: note: the scroll is clamped to keep the view on the main screen
- `moveTo(start?: BpOffset | undefined, end?: BpOffset | undefined, minBpPerPx?: number | undefined) => void`: offset is the base-pair-offset in the displayed region, index is the index of the displayed region in the linear genome view

## Getters
- `width: number`
- `minBpPerPx: number`: zoom-in floor; overridden by extensions (e.g. the dotplot axes)
- `maxBpPerPx: number`: zoom-out ceiling; overridden by extensions (e.g. the dotplot axes)
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `displayedRegionsTotalPx: number`
- `maxOffset: number`
- `minOffset: number`
- `totalBp: number`
- `dynamicBlocks: BlockSet`
- `staticBlocks: BlockSet`
- `currBp: number`

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `displayedRegions = types.optional(types.frozen<IRegion[]>(), [])`
- `bpPerPx = 0`
- `offsetPx = 0`
- `minimumBlockWidth = types.stripDefault(types.number, 0)`

## Methods
- `pxToBp(px: number) => PxToBpResult`
- `bpToPx(args: { refName: string; coord: number; displayedRegionIndex?: number | undefined; }) => number | undefined`

BaseChordDisplay.text:
# BaseChordDisplay (Display model, circular-view plugin)

What the circular view's chord and ribbon displays share: the features, the slice index a feature end is looked up in, and the lifecycle getters `ChordDisplayFrame` publishes. A track draws on the arcs of the assemblies it names, so a one-genome variant track on a two-genome circle fetches and places only that genome's chords.

Composes BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `openErrorDialog() => void`
- `setFeatures(features: Feature[] | undefined) => void`
- `reload() => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Overridable hook (default no-op): drop whatever `hoveredFeature` reports. The writing twin of that getter, and what `installClearHoverOnViewportChange` calls.
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…
- `applyPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => void`: Write a draft over `plot` as a settings bag writes: a setting left out stays, `null` resets one, a channel (`writes: 'whole'`, such as `color` or `facet`) is replaced whole, and any other object takes the members the draft names, so a…

## Getters
- `view: CircularView`
- `trackAssemblyNames: string[]`: the track's assemblies that are on the circle, canonical and in the order the circle lays them out
- `fetchInert: boolean`: nothing of this track's is on the circle, so the fetch never runs; the SVG export's wait and the retry contract check both read it
- `loaded: boolean`
- `ready: boolean`
- `displayError: unknown`: what the error ring shows
- `svgReady: boolean`: the off-screen export gate, on the shared `computeSvgReady` policy. A radial display has no box to draw an error in, so the export fails rather than exporting a message
- `displayPhase: DisplayStatusPhase`
- `radiusPx: number`
- `curveDepth: number`: `mark.depth`, how deeply a chord curves toward the center, 0 to 1
- `bezierRadius: number`: the radius of a chord's Bezier control point when its ends are opposite each other
- `selectedFeatureId: string | undefined`
- `hoveredFeatureId: string | undefined`: the feature under the pointer, which the view hit-tests for every chord display at once
- `figureStage: ChordStage`: the polar stage on the unrotated figure, which the view's SVG turns: what the export, the highlight paths and the hit tests are placed on
- `drawnLanes: { count: number; features: readonly Feature[]; }`: Overridable hook: the drawn records, one per lane, in paint order
- `laneIndexById: ReadonlyMap<string, number>`: each drawn record's lane, by id
- `drawnCount: number`: how many lanes the canvas draws, a chord under a pixel included
- `shapes: Shape[]`: every drawn shape, as the export draws it
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `hoveredFeature: unknown`: Overridable hook (default `undefined`): what the pointer is currently over, for readers **outside** the display. `LinearGenomeViewContainer` publishes it to `session.hovered`, the view-wide "what is the user pointing at" channel a plugin…
- `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the singular word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants".
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features.
- `liveNotices: string[]`: Notices from the loaded data beside the config, such as a field no fetched feature has. Empty unless a display overrides it.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.string`

## Methods
- `shapeAt(_i: number) => Shape | undefined`: Overridable hook: lane `i` as the SVG side draws it, on the unrotated figure; undefined where it draws nothing
- `laneAt(_x: number, _y: number) => number | undefined`: Overridable hook: the topmost lane under a point on the unrotated figure
- `shapeFor(featureId: string) => Shape | undefined`: the shape a drawn record's id names, undefined where none draws
- `shapePathFor(feature: Feature) => string | undefined`: a drawn feature's outline as an SVG path on the unrotated figure, for anything that has to find a shape on screen without a DOM node
- `hitAt(dx: number, dy: number) => Feature | undefined`: the record drawn under a point CSS px from the circle's centre in the screen frame
- `assemblyOf(assemblyName: string | undefined) => string | undefined`: the assembly on the circle a feature names, in whatever spelling the adapter wrote. A feature that names none, as a VCF record does not, is on the track's first assembly.
- `canonicalRefName(assemblyName: string, refName: string) => string`: a refName as the adapter wrote it, in the assembly's canonical spelling
- `axisSlice(assemblyName: string | undefined, refName: string) => AxisSlice | undefined`: the slice of the unrolled axis that one end of a feature falls in
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The problems in a config that cannot be drawn as written: by default the schema's rules over its color objects and value axes, the ones `jbrowse validate` runs. A display with additional rules overrides it. `plotProblems` asks it of a…
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

BaseConnectionModel.text:
# BaseConnectionModel (Connection model, core)

Holds the tracks a connection has loaded. Each connection type overrides `connect` to fetch them from its source.

## Actions
- `connect() => Promise<void>`: no-op hook; concrete connections (UCSC/JB2 track hubs, etc.) override this to fetch and populate their `tracks`. Returns a promise so `afterAttach` can clear the loading flag once the fetch settles.
- `setLoading(loading: boolean) => void`
- `addTrackConf(trackConf: TrackConf) => PluggableConfigNode`
- `addTrackConfs(trackConfs: TrackConf[]) => void`
- `setTrackConfs(trackConfs: TrackConf[]) => void`

## Getters
- `connectionId: string`: the connection's unique id, resolved from its configuration (the config is the source of truth; connection names are not guaranteed unique)
- `name: string`

## Properties
- `tracks = types.array(pluginManager.pluggableConfigSchemaType('track'))`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `silent = types.optional(types.boolean, false)`: set when the connection is being re-established on session load (its open tracks are already restored from `connectionTrackConfigs`), so `doConnect` suppresses first-connect side effects like launching a view or a success snackbar.…

# BaseInternetAccountModel (Internet Account model, core)

Adds a token header to each request for a file on one of the account's domains, keeping the token in `sessionStorage`. Every internet account type builds on this model.

## Actions
- `getTokenFromUser(_resolve: (token: string) => void, _reject: (error: Error) => void) => void`: Must be implemented by a model extending or composing this one. Pass the user's token to `resolve`.
- `storeToken(token: string) => void`
- `retrieveToken() => string | undefined`
- `validateToken(token: string, _loc: UriLocation) => Promise<string>`: This can be used by an internetAccount to validate a token works before it is used. This runs when preAuthorizationInformation is requested, so it can check that a token is valid before sending it to a worker thread. It expects the token…
- `removeToken() => void`: Clears the stored token. Also drops the in-memory cached promise so a subsequent `getToken` re-prompts / re-derives rather than handing back the token that was just invalidated.
- `getToken(location?: UriLocation | undefined) => Promise<string>`: Try to get the token from the location pre-auth, from local storage, or from a previously cached promise. If token is not available, uses `getTokenFromUser`.
- `addAuthHeaderToInit(init?: RequestInit | undefined, token?: string | undefined) => { headers: Headers; body?: BodyInit | null | undefined; cache?: RequestCache | undefined; crede…`
- `fetchWithToken(loc: UriLocation | undefined, run: (token: string) => Promise<Response>) => Promise<Response>`: Run a request with the current token and, only if it comes back 401, put the token through `validateToken` and run it exactly once more. This is how every account's fetcher reaches a resource.
- `getPreAuthorizationInformation(location: UriLocation) => Promise<{ internetAccountType: string; authInfo: { token: string; configuration: ModelSnapshotType<Record<string, any>>; }; }>`: Gets the token and returns it along with the information needed to create a new internetAccount.
- `getFetcher(loc?: UriLocation | undefined) => (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit | undefined) => Promise<Response>`: Get a fetch method that will add any needed authentication headers to the request before sending it. If location is provided, it will be checked to see if it includes a token in it pre-auth information.
- `openLocation(location: UriLocation) => RemoteFileWithRangeCache`: Gets a filehandle that uses a fetch that adds auth headers

## Getters
- `name: string`
- `description: string`
- `internetAccountId: string`
- `authHeader: string`
- `tokenType: string`
- `domains: string[]`
- `toggleContents: ReactNode`: Can use this to customize what is displayed in fileSelector's toggle box
- `selectorLabel: string | undefined`: Can use this to add a label to the UrlChooser
- `showInFileSelector: boolean`: Whether the fileSelector offers this account as a source to pick. Turn it off for an account that only ever matches by domain and has nothing for the user to enter — HTTP Basic, whose ephemeral per-origin accounts would otherwise pile up…
- `tokenKey: string`: The sessionStorage key that holds this internetAccount's token

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.string`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(BaseInternetAccountConfig)`

## Methods
- `handlesLocation(location: UriLocation) => boolean`: Determine whether this internetAccount provides credentials for a URL

BreakpointSplitView.text:
# BreakpointSplitView (View model, breakpoint-split-view plugin)

Stacks linear genome views of the regions on each side of a structural-variant breakpoint, and draws the reads and variant calls that join them across the panels.

Composes BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `views` is one entry per stacked panel, each
declaring the `assembly`, a `loc`, and the `tracks` to show. The two panels
flank a structural-variant breakpoint:
```js
{
  type: 'BreakpointSplitView',
  views: [
    { assembly: 'hg38', loc: 'chr1:1,000,000-1,100,000', tracks: ['alignments'] },
    { assembly: 'hg38', loc: 'chr5:2,000,000-2,100,000', tracks: ['alignments'] },
  ],
}
```
Each `tracks` entry can also be a `{ trackId, displaySnapshot }` object to
set per-panel display options (e.g. a shorter alignments height).

## Actions
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => void`
- `setHoveredOverlay(arg: OverlayHover | undefined) => void`: `undefined` when the pointer leaves a curve, and when the picture moves out from under it — see `overlayTransformKey`.
- `setInteractiveOverlay(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setLinkViews(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setScrollZoom(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowHeader(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setMatchedTrackFeatures(obj: Record<string, Feature[][]>) => void`
- `reload() => void`: Re-run the overlay-feature fetch with no input change — what the Retry on its failure notification calls.
- `reverseViewOrder() => void`
- `squareView() => void`
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<BreakpointSplitViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `setViews(viewInits: BreakpointSplitViewInitView[]) => void`
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `ownViews: LinearGenomeView[]`: The census entry for this view: its panels are separate views, and it holds no tracks outside them.
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: scroll-to-zoom is a global, personal preference resolved from the session; toggling it in any view applies everywhere
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<BreakpointSplitViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; malformed?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolea…`: the launch state that still has something to apply — the gate the loading and import-form paths below read.
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `initialized: boolean`: True on the import form too: with no panels and none pending there is nothing left to initialize, and `AppReadyMarker` reads a false here as the app still loading — which held `data-app-phase` at `loading` for as long as an empty split…
- `error: unknown`: Resolved, like LGV's and linear-comparative's: it folds in the sub-views, whose assemblies are what `initialized` waits on. Without them a failed assembly leaves `initialized` false forever with nothing to report, and an SVG export waiting…
- `showLoading: boolean`: Spinner instead of content, i.e. sub-views exist but haven't loaded their assemblies yet. Named to match LGV/dotplot/synteny/circular, since ViewContainer reads this name to publish `data-view-phase`.
- `loadingAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly whose load the spinner is waiting on. Delegated to the first sub-view that hasn't initialized, since each LGV already resolves this for itself; before the sub-views exist, `init` is what names them.
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: The loading screen's text while `showLoading`, taken from the assembly being waited on; undefined otherwise.
- `showImportForm: boolean`: A failed assembly counts: the views it left behind never initialize, so there is nothing to show and no second attempt coming in this session. The form — which reports `error` in its banner — is then the only way forward, matching…
- `assemblies: (Assembly | undefined)[]`: One assembly per row, index-aligned with `views`.
- `matchedTracks: OverlayTrack[]`: The tracks open in every row, in the first row's order
- `overlayTracks: OverlayTrack[]`: The matched tracks the overlay draws for — alignments and variants.
- `fetchedTracks: OverlayTrack[]`: The overlay tracks the overlay fetch asks for: the variant tracks. An alignments track's reads come from the track's display instead.
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Same name and same meaning as `FetchMixin.fetchInert`, on a view rather than a display: with no variant track matched across the rows there is nothing for the overlay fetch to ask for, so `prepare` declines instead of running an empty…
- `overlayTransformKey: string`: Every number that moves the overlay under a stationary cursor, in one value — what `installClearHoverOnSurfaceMove` watches.
- `variantJunctionsByTrack: Map<string, Feature[][]>`: Each fetched variant track's records paired into junctions, keyed by trackId. A function of the fetched features alone, kept apart from `overlayMatches` so a track resize re-runs only the layout half.
- `readChainsByTrack: Map<string, ReadChain[]>`: Each alignments track's split reads and discordant pairs, read off the displays in every row and resolved into connections, keyed by trackId. Reads no row, so a resize or a scroll leaves it alone.
- `overlayMatches: Map<string, OverlayMatch>`: Every overlay track's connections with their layout rects, keyed by trackId. Cached, so scrolling within loaded data does not look a row up again.
- `drawnConnectionsByTrack: Map<string, DrawnConnection[]>`: The alignment connectors the overlay draws, classified, keyed by trackId: what the overlay paints and the connection key lists.
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders this view's displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownTracks: AbstractTrackModel[]`: The tracks this view puts in the census, excluding a nested view's.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('BreakpointSplitView')`
- `linkViews = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: sync scroll and zoom across the panels, so panning one pans them all
- `interactiveOverlay = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: let the connection and junction curves drawn between the panels respond to hover and click; off, they are a static overlay
- `showHeader = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: show the view's own header bar, above the panels' own
- `views = types.array( pluginManager.getViewType('LinearGenomeView').stateModel, )`
- `launch = types.frozen< LaunchInput<BreakpointSplitViewCommands> | undefined >()`: transient launch state: the declarative panels written on the view object as `views`, which need a measured width before they can be built rows. `preProcessSnapshot` moves them here off the snapshot, the afterAttach autorun applies them…
- `id = ElementId`
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar and keep it in the session

## Methods
- `exportSvg(opts?: ExportSvgOptions) => Promise<string>`: renders the view to SVG markup, which it returns; saves it through FileSaver unless `save: false`
- `getMatchedTracks(trackConfigId: string) => OverlayTrack[]`: Get tracks with a given trackId across multiple views. Callers that index the result by view level (getTrackOverlayData, getMatchedFeaturesInLayout) rely on it staying aligned with `views` — which holds only because overlays are driven by…
- `connectorRows(trackId: string) => ConnectorRow[]`: Per row, whether the track is minimized and whether the track's pileup draws a junction's connector, so the overlay leaves it out. Reads no scroll or zoom.
- `readSources(trackId: string) => (ReadSource | undefined)[]`: The reads each row's alignments display lays out, one entry per row.
- `connectionStylerIn(trackId: string, theme: JBrowsePalette) => ({ connection: { e1, e2, isSplit } }: DrawnConnection) => { color: string; label: string; }`: Each drawn connection's color and key label in `theme`, as the alignments display in the row of its first end paints it, so a curve between panels agrees with the arcs and connectors inside them.
- `getTrackOverlayData(trackId: string, yOffsetsOverride?: (number | undefined)[] | undefined) => { tracks: OverlayTrack[]; levels: OverlayLevel[]; layouts: ViewLayout[]; getX: (lev…`: Per-render precompute for an overlay track. Resolves an OverlayLevel of geometry per view level, then returns getX/getY closures for converting feature layout records to SVG coordinates.
- `getMatchedFeaturesInLayout(trackConfigId: string, features: Feature[][]) => { feature: Feature; layout: LayoutRecord; level: number; }[][]`
- `menuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `rubberBandMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `rubberbandClickMenuItemsAtPx(px: number) => MenuItem[]`: What a bare click on the shared rubberband strip offers: one row per panel, each holding that panel's own click menu at the base it paints under `px`. A pixel rather than an offset, since each panel maps it through that panel's `pxToBp`.

# ChordSyntenyDisplay (Display model, circular-view plugin)

Draws a `SyntenyTrack` in a `CircularView`, with a ribbon joining the two spans of each alignment.

Config slots: docs topic "config:ChordSyntenyDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes BaseChordDisplay, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

The circular-view display for a `SyntenyTrack`: each alignment is drawn as a
ribbon between its span on one side and its mate's span on the other, so an
inversion reads as a twist. The track config below is what creates it; its
colors are the config slots on [](/docs/config/chordsyntenydisplay):
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'volvox_self',
  name: 'Volvox self-alignment',
  assemblyNames: ['volvox', 'volvox'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/volvox_self.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'volvox',
    targetAssembly: 'volvox',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'ChordSyntenyDisplay',
      displayId: 'volvox_self-ChordSyntenyDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

the view's `assembly: ['hg38', 'mm39']` — see the
[synteny track guide](/docs/config_guides/synteny_track).

Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…

CircularView.text:
# CircularView (View model, circular-view plugin)

Lays one or more assemblies' chromosomes around a circle, and draws structural variants as chords and synteny alignments as ribbons across it.

Composes SyntenyFadeMixin, SyntenyColorsMixin, TrackColorsMixin, ParkedColorMixin, SyntenyFilterMixin, ImportFormSyntenyMixin, DiagonalizeProgressMixin, BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `assembly` names the genome, a `tracks` entry may
include display config inline, and `displayedRegionNames` lists the regions
to draw, which keeps an assembly's alt/unplaced contigs off the circle:
```js
{
  type: 'CircularView',
  assembly: 'hg38',
  displayedRegionNames: ['chr1', 'chr2', 'chr3'],
  tracks: [{ trackId: 'my-sv-vcf', encoding: { color: { value: 'red' } } }],
}
```
`assembly` also takes a list, for a synteny ribbon plot: each
assembly lays its contigs out in turn, so the first genome takes one arc of
the circle and the second the next, and a `SyntenyTrack` covering both draws
a ribbon per alignment between them. `displayedRegionNames` keyed by assembly
restricts each genome separately, and `autoDiagonalize` reorders the second
to follow the first:
```js
{
  type: 'CircularView',
  assembly: ['hg38', 'mm39'],
  displayedRegionNames: { hg38: ['chr1', 'chr2'] },
  tracks: ['hg38_vs_mm39'],
  autoDiagonalize: true,
}
```

## Actions
- `fitToWindow() => void`: size the figure so it exactly fills the smaller of the view's two dimensions
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => number`
- `setHeight(newHeight: number) => number`
- `setShowLegend(flag: boolean) => void`
- `rotateClockwiseButton() => void`
- `rotateCounterClockwiseButton() => void`
- `rotate(delta: number) => void`
- `resetView() => void`: reset rotation, pan, and zoom back to the default fit-to-window view
- `zoomInButton() => void`
- `zoomOutButton() => void`
- `zoomAboutViewMiddle(newBpPerPx: number) => void`: zoom about the circle's middle while the figure sits where the fit put it, and about the view's middle once a zoom to the cursor has panned it, so what the user zoomed toward stays in view
- `setBpPerPx(newVal: number) => void`
- `zoomToPoint(newBpPerPx: number, cursorX: number, cursorY: number) => void`: zoom toward/away from a point on the figure, keeping whatever is under it visually fixed. The point is its offset in screen px from the middle of the circle — what `offsetFromCenter` in the component hands back
- `setDisplayedRegions(regions: Region[]) => void`
- `activateTrackSelector() => Widget | undefined`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `setError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setHover(target: PointerTarget | undefined, clientX?: any, clientY?: any) => void`: the pointer is on `target`, or on nothing, at client `x`,`y`. A move that stays on one target keeps it, so only the tooltip follows it
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<CircularViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `clearView() => void`: back to the import form: no regions, no tracks, no pending launch and no error from the one before
- `showTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: any, displayInitialSnapshot?: any, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => any`
- `addTrackConf(configuration: Record<string, unknown>, initialSnapshot?: any) => any`
- `hideTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `openExportDialog() => void`
- `openReorderChromosomesDialog() => void`
- `openInLinearSyntenyView() => void`: a linear synteny view of this circle's genomes, a row each over the chromosomes the circle shows with the tracks it shows for that genome, its ribbon tracks between them, reordered, in this view's color and length filter. A self-alignment…
- `autoDiagonalize() => Promise<void>`: The init-time reorder, behind the "Reordering chromosomes" screen `withDiagonalizeProgress` drives.
- `exportSvg(opts?: ViewExportSvgOptions) => Promise<string>`: renders the view to SVG markup, which it returns; saves it through FileSaver unless `save: false`
- `launchTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: any, displayInitialSnapshot?: any) => Promise<any>`: showTrack for a track whose display state model may be lazily loaded: loads it, then shows
- `launchToggleTrack(trackId: string) => Promise<boolean>`: toggleTrack with launchTrack's loading behavior
- `launchTrackConf(configuration: Record<string, unknown>, initialSnapshot?: any) => Promise<any>`: `addTrackConf` with `launchTrack`'s loading behavior, for a track handed over inline rather than from a session list
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`
- `resizeWidth(distance: number) => number`
- `setAntialias(antialias: boolean | undefined) => void`
- `setFadeThinLatch(arg: boolean) => void`: Move the latched 'auto' thin-fade decision — `installAutoFadeLatch` is the only caller.
- `setOpacity(value: number) => void`: The opacity slider: the constant, or under a field its range scaled so its most opaque end equals `value`.
- `setOpacityField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Fade by `field` from the current opacity down to 0.3 of it, or with undefined draw every alignment at the opacity the fade reached.
- `observeAttributeRanges(ranges: Record<string, AttributeRange>) => void`: Fold one fetch's observed attribute spans into the domain this view paints and labels its ramps with. Called by each display as its fetch lands, because the accumulation has to outlive the payload it came from: the previous window's span…
- `resetAttributeRanges() => void`: Forget the accumulated domain, leaving `attributeRanges` reporting what the loaded fetches cover and nothing else.
- `setHideUnlabelled(value: boolean) => void`
- `setColorField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Set the field the view paints by over `encoding.color`, undefined unsetting it for the view's default, and rescale the ramp, which is the only way back from a domain one outlying window widened.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every alignment `value`, undefined returning to the view's default.
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: The picker Color by's Solid color... opens.
- `setColorDomain(domain: string[]) => void`: Declare the order a text column's labels take. The labels listed lead, the rest follow sorted; an empty list gives back the order the fetches found them in.
- `setTrackColor(trackId: string, value: string | undefined) => void`: Pin one track's color under `encoding.color: 'track'`, or release it back to an automatic palette slot.
- `clearTrackColors() => void`
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setFilter(predicates: FieldPredicate[]) => void`
- `setLowerBound(field: string, value: number) => void`: The slider on one field: `field` at least `value`, or no lower bound at 0.
- `setImportFormSyntenyTrack(idx: number, val: ImportFormSyntenyTrack) => void`
- `clearImportFormSyntenyTracks() => void`: Drop the pending selections once a launch has applied them. Left in place they outlive the form: "Return to import form" would reopen on a finished upload from the previous launch, and a pair whose assemblies no longer match it reads as an…
- `setAwaitingAutoDiagonalize(arg: boolean) => void`
- `beginAutoDiagonalize(requested: boolean) => void`: Declare the gate at the top of one init apply pass: a reorder is pending iff THIS init asked for one. Assigning rather than raising is what hands the gate over cleanly — a superseded init that asked for a reorder and then skipped it would…
- `finishAutoDiagonalize() => void`: A reorder resolved, the init's or a manual one, so the view on screen is the diagonalized one — open the gate.
- `setDiagonalizeError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeCancel(arg?: (() => void) | undefined) => void`
- `cancelAutoDiagonalize() => void`: Abort an in-flight auto-diagonalize; `withDiagonalizeProgress`'s finally clears the wait flag, revealing the (undiagonalized) view.
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `showLegend: boolean`: `legend.show`: whether the key draws
- `ownTracks: TrackModelOf<DisplayModel>[]`: the tracks this view holds itself, for the census
- `width: number`
- `circleRegions: (Region | { circular: boolean; assemblyName: string; refName: string; start: number; end: number; reversed?: boolean | undefined; })[]`: `displayedRegions`, each marked `circular` where it is a whole sequence its assembly lists in `circularRefNames`
- `fitLayout: FitLayout`: the circle that fills the box: its scale, radius and padding
- `fitInput: FitInput`: what `fitLayout` measures the circle from
- `namesFeaturesOutside: boolean`: a circle of one contig is a map: its ring displays' features are named outside the circle with leaders, not along their rows
- `effectivePaddingPx: number`: `paddingPx`, capped in a small box and floored at what the labels drawn at the fit or at this zoom reach
- `ring: { spacingPx: number; radiusPx: number; }`: the ring at this zoom: its gaps' spacing and the radius that closes it — see `ringAt`
- `effectiveSpacingPx: number`: `spacingPx`, capped so the gaps take at most a quarter of the ring
- `totalGapUnits: number`: how many inter-slice gaps go round the circle, a genome boundary counting as several
- `radiusPx: number`
- `circumferencePx: number`
- `bpPerRadian: number`
- `centerXY: [number, number]`
- `totalBp: number`
- `maxBpPerPx: number`
- `minBpPerPx: number`
- `atMaxBpPerPx: boolean`
- `atMinBpPerPx: boolean`
- `figureSize: number`: figure is always square, so width === height
- `figureOriginXY: [number, number]`: the figure's top-left in the view's box, centered horizontally and placed by `figureMiddleY` vertically, plus the pan
- `circleCenterXY: [number, number]`: the circle's centre in the view's box
- `polarFrame: { canvasWidth: number; canvasHeight: number; centerX: number; centerY: number; offsetRadians: number; }`: what the ring and chord canvases both draw against: the view's box, the circle's centre in it and the figure's rotation
- `elisionMask: string`: which displayed regions are too narrow at this zoom to draw as themselves, one character each
- `elidedRegions: SliceRegion[]`: `displayedRegions` with each run of too-narrow regions in one assembly folded into one elided slice
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<CircularViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; malformed?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean | und…`: the launch state still to apply
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `chordSyntenyDisplays: ChordSyntenyDisplaySelf[]`: the ribbon displays of `syntenyTracks()`; a chromosome reorder reads its alignments from these
- `canDiagonalize: boolean`: whether a reorder applies: a ribbon track, and exactly two genomes (ADR-121)
- `paintedAssemblyName: string | undefined`: the genome whose ideogram a ribbon track paints by what aligns to it from the first, rather than in the colors of its chromosomes
- `ideogramPaint: ReadonlyMap<string, PaintRun[]>`: that genome's paint, by slice key
- `launchAssemblyNames: string[]`: the assemblies a pending launch names, which the gates wait on before `displayedRegions` exist
- `initialized: boolean`
- `assemblyErrors: string | undefined`
- `error: unknown`
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `showLoading: boolean`: whether the loading screen stands in for the form or the figure
- `loadingAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: the assembly whose load the spinner waits on
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: the loading screen's text while `showLoading`
- `showView: boolean`: whether the figure draws: regions, and every assembly loaded
- `showImportForm: boolean`: nothing to show or an error, unless `disableImportForm`, which an error does not override
- `status: ViewStatus`: the lifecycle as one value, as the linear view answers it
- `regionHost: RingHost`: the strip a linear display lays out along and draws its ring from (ADR-119)
- `chordRadiusPx: number`: Where the chord displays start: inside the innermost ring, or at the ruler when the view holds none.
- `chordDisplays: ChordLayerDisplay[]`: the displays drawing across the circle, in track order: every first display registered for this view rather than laid out as a ring
- `hoveredChord: ChordHit | undefined`: the chord or ribbon under the pointer
- `hoveredBand: AxisSlice`: the chromosome whose band is under the pointer, on the chord axis
- `chordFocusGaps: number`: that chromosome as the chord stage's focus: its slice's gap count, the name a foot gives it, or -1 for none
- `bandComposition: { name: string; shares: PartnerShare[]; } | undefined`: the hovered chromosome's name and the share of it each chromosome aligned to it covers, most first
- `hoversChord: boolean`: whether the pointer is on a chord or ribbon, which only changes as it crosses onto one or off it
- `chordAxis: ChordAxis`: the circle's slices on the unrolled genome axis, unchanged by a zoom or rotation
- `chordScale: PolarScale`: the scale from the unrolled axis to radians
- `autoFadeWidthPx: number`: the narrowest capped mean ribbon span on screen, which the auto fade judges
- `chordThinFadeFloor: 1 | 0.15`: the least alpha the thin fade leaves a ribbon, 1 while it is off
- `staticSlices: Slice[]`: the slices at this zoom, in radians
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: one row per track: its name beside the color or ramp it paints with
- `antialias: boolean | undefined`: `render.antialias`, undefined while it follows the data.
- `fadeThinAlignments: boolean`: The resolved fade-thin flag every display renders by. 'auto' fades once sub-pixel ribbons dominate any loaded display, latched with a deadband (`fadesThinAt`, ADR-083) so a view near the threshold does not flip while panning. View-wide, so…
- `defaultOpacity: number`: The constant opacity a reset returns to: low on the synteny view for dense whole-genome hairballs, opaque on the dotplot.
- `opacitySetting: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot`: `encoding.opacity` as its snapshot holds it.
- `opacityFade: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot | undefined`: What the color pass fades each alignment by: the field's mapping with its range as shares of `opacityLevel`, or undefined while `encoding.opacity` draws its constant, so the slider recolors nothing either way.
- `opacityLevel: number`: The opacity every alignment draws at before a field's fade: the shader's uniform (`opacityLevel`).
- `opacityField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.opacity` fades by, undefined while it draws its constant.
- `colorSetting: SyntenyColorSnapshot`: `encoding.color` as its snapshot holds it, with the view's default field where it names neither a field nor a constant.
- `impliedColorField: string | undefined`: The field the view paints while `encoding.color` names neither a field nor a constant, undefined for its default scheme.
- `colorPaint: SyntenyColorPaint`: What `encoding.color.scale` declares over a field's own scale: its `type`, `domain`, `range` or `scheme` for its colors, `reverse`, and a ramp's pinned ends and middle. Read from these slots alone, so a key-only edit repaints nothing.
- `colorValue: string | undefined`: `encoding.color.value`: the color every alignment paints under the default mode in place of the view's own scheme, or undefined for that scheme.
- `colorDomain: readonly string[]`: `encoding.color.scale.domain`, the order a text column's labels take. Read from that slot alone, so a key-only edit (`legend.title`, `scale.names`) recolors nothing.
- `colorRange: readonly string[]`: The colors a text column's labels take in domain order: `encoding.color.scale.range`, else its `scheme` sampled once per domain value
- `colorableAttributes: string[]`: Distinct numeric columns across the overlaid tracks, in first-seen order — two tracks declaring `dn` offer one `dn` mode, not two.
- `attributeRanges: Record<string, AttributeRange>`: The span each numeric channel covers: unioned over the loaded displays, and over every fetch this view has already taken (`seenAttributeRanges`). A column has no declared domain, so this is what its ramp scales to, what the legend labels…
- `colorableTracks: ColorableTrack[]`: `colorableTrackConfigs` paired with whatever color the user pinned. This is the single definition of "the tracks that get colors" — the palette, the legend and the palette menu all read it, so they cannot disagree about which tracks are in…
- `trackColorAssignments: Map<string, string>`: trackId -> the color it draws in under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Assigned across the whole view rather than per display, so an automatic slot can't duplicate a color pinned on a sibling.
- `colorField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.color` paints by, undefined for the default color.
- `hideUnlabelled: boolean`: Whether the filter drops the alignments with no value for the field the view paints by, the "Hide unlabelled rows" box.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the mode has a key worth a box: a track palette, a ramp, a reader-named column, or strand wherever the shape does not show it (`shapeShowsStrand`), which leaves the color the only strand cue.
- `colorLegendChips: ColorChip[]`: Legend rows naming the overlaid tracks — one per track with its palette color, however many levels it is on, and only under `encoding.color: 'track'`, since every other mode has a fixed legend.
- `colorScales: ColorScale[]`: The active mode's key, or none for a mode without one. View-wide rather than per display because the key is one box for the whole view, and the ramp domain it labels is the view's.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field
- `predicates: FieldPredicate[]`: The `filter` list as the predicate compiler reads it.
- `minLength: number`: The lower bound on `length`, 0 for none.
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders this view's displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownViews: AbstractViewModel[]`: The views nested directly inside this one, which the census counts as separate views — a synteny stack's genome rows, a breakpoint split view's panels.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('CircularView') as unknown as string`
- `offsetRadians = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultOffsetRadians)`: the figure's rotation in radians, the linear view's offsetPx
- `bpPerPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultBpPerPx)`: the zoom level, base-pairs per pixel. Capped by `minimumRadiusPx`, and refit over by the first resize unless `autoFit` is false.
- `autoFit = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: whether the view refits to its box on resize; a manual zoom or pan clears it
- `tracks = types.array( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('track', 'stateModel'), )`
- `hideVerticalResizeHandle = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: chrome switch, for an embed that drives the view itself
- `hideTrackSelectorButton = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: chrome switch, for an embed that drives the view itself
- `disableImportForm = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: never show the import form, even on an error, for an embed that picks the assembly itself (the SV inspector)
- `legend = types.stripDefault(hiddenLegendConfigSchema, {})`: the key naming each track's ring, chords or ribbons in the corner, a [](/docs/config/hiddenlegend) object: `{ show: true }` draws it
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultHeight)`: the view's height in px, which sizes the fitted circle. Left at its default in a multi-view session, the view opens square to its width
- `displayedRegions = types.stripDefault(types.frozen<Region[]>(), [])`: the regions the circle lays out, one arc each, in this order. `displayedRegionNames` names the same thing by refName and is the shorter form.
- `minimumRadiusPx = types.stripDefault( types.number, defaultMinimumRadiusPx, )`: how far out the circle may zoom, as the smallest radius it shrinks to; it is what caps bpPerPx
- `spacingPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultSpacingPx)`: the gap drawn between adjacent chromosome arcs
- `paddingPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultPaddingPx)`: blank margin between the circle and the edge of the figure
- `minVisibleWidth = types.stripDefault( types.number, defaultMinVisibleWidth, )`: arcs thinner than this many pixels are elided instead of drawn, so a few thousand unplaced contigs do not become a ring of hairlines
- `trackSelectorType = types.stripDefault(types.string, 'hierarchical')`: ignored: the hierarchical selector is the only one. Declared because saved sessions and share links carry it.
- `launch = types.frozen<LaunchInput<CircularViewCommands> | undefined>()`: the launch keys still to apply, moved here by `preProcessSnapshot` and cleared once applied; not written by hand
- `render = types.stripDefault(syntenyRenderConfigSchema, {})`: How the ribbons rasterize, a [](/docs/config/syntenyrender) object: `antialias` fades a sub-pixel ribbon by its on-screen width, so an unfiltered whole-genome view doesn't read as a full-opacity hairball. Unset, it fades once sub-pixel…
- `encoding = types.stripDefault(syntenyEncodingConfigSchema, {})`: The channels every track in the view paints with, a [](/docs/config/syntenyencoding) object. Its `color` is a [](/docs/config/syntenycolor) channel: `"strand"`, `"query"`, `"reference"`, `"track"`, a measurement (`identity`, `mapq`,…
- `trackColors = types.map(types.string)`: trackId -> explicit color under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Absent means the track takes an automatic slot from the palette.
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `filter = types.stripDefault(fieldPredicateArray(), [])`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries an alignment must all pass. A field is any field `color` takes, or `length`, the alignment's bp on its own axis: `[{ field: 'length', gte: 10000 }]` clears a…
- `id = ElementId`
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar and keep it in the session

## Methods
- `syntenyTracks() => ComparativeTrackModel[]`: the tracks drawing ribbons, which the view's color settings paint
- `loadedAttributeRanges() => Record<string, AttributeRange>[]`: each ribbon display's attribute spans, over the alignments it holds
- `legendCigarOps() => number`: a ribbon draws no indel blocks, so the key lists none
- `shapeShowsStrand() => boolean`: a ribbon twists against its two arcs' directions, and nothing on the circle shows which way an arc runs
- `chordAt(dx: number, dy: number) => ChordHit | undefined`: the chord or ribbon under a point `dx`,`dy` CSS px from the circle's centre in the screen frame
- `bandAt(dx: number, dy: number) => string | undefined`: the place of the chromosome whose ideogram band holds a point `dx`,`dy` CSS px from the circle's centre in the screen frame
- `bandCenter(key: string) => [number, number] | undefined`: the middle of the ideogram band `key` names, CSS px from the circle's centre in the screen frame: the point `bandAt` answers `key` for
- `linearTracksFor(assemblyName: string) => TrackInit[]`: the tracks a linear view of one genome on this circle opens with: each track on that genome but the synteny tracks, a ring as its display and a chord track as the linear view's own
- `tracksMenuItem() => MenuItem`: each track's own menu, which on a linear view hangs off its label and on the circle has nowhere else to go
- `legendSpecIn(palette?: JBrowsePalette | undefined) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in another theme, the SVG export's
- `menuItems() => MenuItem[]`: return the view menu items
- `colorableTrackConfigs() => { trackId: string; name: string; }[]`
- `colorableAttributeNames() => string[]`: The columns the tracks declare in their adapter's `attributeColumns` (the ortholog-table adapter's slot), one color mode each.
- `legendAlpha() => number`: The plot's opacity composites the key's chips, as it does the alignments.
- `colorSurface() => SyntenyColorSurface`: Overridable hook: what draws each alignment, a ribbon with match and indel blocks or one flat point (the dotplot). The key, the menu's help text and which fields key at all read it.
- `offersReferenceColor() => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the view has a shared reference for the `reference` field to anchor on. It needs a stack of two or more levels; below that it is query or target by another name.
- `trackColorFor(trackId: string) => string`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `lowerBound(field: string) => number`: The lower bound the filter puts on `field`, 0 for none.

CoarseTierMixin.text:
# CoarseTierMixin (Mixin model, core) The zoomed-out tier a display draws in place of its detail past a threshold the display sets: MAF's summary bars. This mixin adds the swap decision, the per-region payloads and the read that fills them, through the shared fetch skeleton on a separate rotation, so the detail fetch's cancel never reaches it. While the tier is up the byte gate measures the coarse read, so its refusal is the banner and the detail fetch stands down. ## Actions - `setCoarseTier(entries: CoarseTierEntry

[], read: CoarseTierRead) => void` - `clearCoarseTier() => void` - `setCoarseTierLoading(loading: boolean) => void` - `fetchCoarseTier(_read: CoarseTierRead, _ctx: FetchContext) => Promise>`: Overridable hook (no-op base): the coarse read over `read.regions`, returning one payload per region it covered, or a refusal. `ctx` is the skeleton's — its `callRpc` passes the signal and the status slot, and `isStale` guards any write… ## Getters - `coarseAdapterSlot: string | undefined`: Overridable hook (default none): the slot on the track's adapter the coarse source sits in — `summaryAdapter` on MAF. With no slot there is no source and the tier never stands in. - `coarseTierPastThreshold: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the display's own line past which the tier stands in — a bp/px slot, a span floor. - `coarseReadKey: unknown`: Overridable hook (default `''`): what the read depends on beyond its span and its adapter — a zoom bucket, the settings axis. A value compared structurally, so a held read whose key differs re-reads. - `coarseSourceConfig: unknown`: The coarse source's config, read off the live track config so a re-pointed adapter follows. - `hasCoarseSource: boolean` - `coarseTierActive: boolean`: Whether the coarse tier stands in for the detail right now. - `coarseTierStandsIn: boolean`: Whether the tier is standing in for the detail on screen right now: the tier's verdict over a measured view. - `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: `RegionTooLargeMixin`'s hook: measure the adapter of the fetch that is about to run, so the estimate and the budget describe one file. - `coarseTierIssueKey: { adapter: (Record & { type: string; }) | undefined; read: unknown; }`: The whole key a read is held under: the coarse adapter and the display's own term. - `fetchSuspended: boolean`: `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`'s hook: the coarse read is the measurement pass while the tier stands in, so the detail fetch has nothing to do. - `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The foundation's phase with the too-large banner swapped for the tier — see `coarseTierDisplayPhase`. - `svgReady: boolean`: The export gate under the same swap — see `coarseTierSvgReady`.

ColorWritesMixin.text:
# ColorWritesMixin (Mixin model, core)

The writes a display's `encoding.color` channel takes from a menu row or a picker: the field it paints by (`colorByField`) and the constant every feature paints (`setColorValue`). Each rewrites the object as written, so what a pick leaves alone stays as it was, and a pick of what already paints writes nothing, since every color tier keys on the object's arrays. A pick away from a field parks it (`ParkedColorMixin`), so picking it again keeps its domain, range and key names. A dialog's Apply button writes the whole object through `applyPlot`, which rebuilds the display's config for the draft,…

Composes ParkedColorMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `colorByField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Paint by `field`, keeping its domain, range and key names while it is the field already painting or the one parked; undefined paints `value` and parks the field.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every feature `value`, a CSS color or a `jexl:` callback, parking the field; undefined lets each feature's own color paint.
- `pickDefaultColor() => void`: Color by's Default: no field and no constant, so the track's own color paints, a `jexl:` expression included.
- `pickSolidColor() => void`: Color by's Solid color...: paints the constant kept beside a painting field, where there is one, and opens the display's picker.
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.

## Getters
- `writtenColor: ColorSlots`: The `encoding.color` channel as these writes and an Apply button read it, `writtenColorOf`.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field

## Properties
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members

## Methods
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`

ComparativeFetchMixin.text:
# ComparativeFetchMixin (Mixin model, core)

The fetch foundation of the two comparative displays (LinearSyntenyDisplay, DotplotDisplay): `KeyedFetchMixin` — `FetchMixin`'s rotation, loading flag, error, status, durable cancel and retry, plus the `currentFetchKey` / `loadedFetchKey` freshness pair the LGV global family runs on — and, on top, the two-way loading answer a shared canvas wants — `loading` off the `fetchLanded` hook, `refetching` off `isLoading` — and the one-shot reversed-assembly flag.

Composes KeyedFetchMixin, FetchMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setAssembliesSwapped(arg: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchResult(commit: () => void, key: FetchKey) => void`: The commit half of a keyed fetch: run the display's own store in the same transaction as the key stamp, so no observer can see fresh data under a stale key or the reverse. As the only writer of `loadedFetchKey`, this action makes…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter — the shared skeleton's reload epoch makes that bump override the freshness gate, even against a fetch that commits mid-reload, so nothing here has to remember to invalidate for the retry's sake)…
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.

## Getters
- `fetchLanded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): a fetch has completed and data is present, even if it mapped zero features. Not a feature-count test — an empty-but-finished fetch has landed, or an empty plot spins its overlay forever. Each display…
- `hasDrawable: boolean`: Overridable hook: the display holds something an SVG export can draw. Defaults to `fetchLanded`; the dotplot answers with its instance geometry rather than its `geometry` computed, because `svgReady` is polled outside any reactive context…

# ConfigurationEditorWidget (Widget model, config plugin)

Widget for a config's settings: a short form over the common ones and a JSON editor over all of them. Holds the target configuration and debounce-saves edits back to the session.

## Actions
- `setTrackId(trackId: string) => void`: edit the working copy of `trackId`, saving any edit still pending on the previous target first
- `setTarget(newTarget: AnyConfigurationModel | undefined) => void`: edit a config node directly, saving any edit still pending on the previous target first
- `setExpandedDisplayId(displayId: string | undefined) => void`

## Getters
- `target: AnyConfigurationModel | undefined`
- `base: AnyConfigurationModel | undefined`: the track's config as the session's base holds it (its config.json entry, or the one the session added it with), which a slot's reset returns to; undefined for an inline target

## Properties

- `type = types.literal('ConfigurationEditorWidget')`
- `trackId = types.maybe(types.string)`: the track whose working copy this edits, re-resolved on every read so an undo that replaces the copy moves the editor with it

# DiagonalizeProgressMixin (Mixin model, core)

The auto-diagonalize lifecycle state shared by the comparative views (LinearSyntenyView, DotplotView, CircularView): the in-flight wait, its live RPC status and signal, and the flag that gates `settled` so a screenshot or browser test can't capture a pre-reorder hairball.

## Actions
- `setAwaitingAutoDiagonalize(arg: boolean) => void`
- `beginAutoDiagonalize(requested: boolean) => void`: Declare the gate at the top of one init apply pass: a reorder is pending iff THIS init asked for one. Assigning rather than raising is what hands the gate over cleanly — a superseded init that asked for a reorder and then skipped it would…
- `finishAutoDiagonalize() => void`: A reorder resolved, the init's or a manual one, so the view on screen is the diagonalized one — open the gate.
- `setDiagonalizeError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeCancel(arg?: (() => void) | undefined) => void`
- `cancelAutoDiagonalize() => void`: Abort an in-flight auto-diagonalize; `withDiagonalizeProgress`'s finally clears the wait flag, revealing the (undiagonalized) view.

# DotplotDisplay (Display model, dotplot-view plugin)

Config slots: docs topic "config:DotplotDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).
