# DotplotView (View model, dotplot-view plugin)

Plots the alignments between two assemblies, one on each axis, as a dot plot.

Composes SyntenyViewMixin, SyntenyColorsMixin, TrackColorsMixin, ParkedColorMixin, SyntenyFilterMixin, ImportFormSyntenyMixin, DiagonalizeProgressMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `views` lists the two assemblies on the axes and
`tracks` the synteny track(s) to plot (self-vs-self is allowed):
```js
{
  type: 'DotplotView',
  views: [{ assembly: 'hg38' }, { assembly: 'mm10' }],
  tracks: ['hg38_vs_mm10.paf'],
  encoding: { color: 'query' },
}
```
`autoDiagonalize` and a per-axis `loc` on each `views` entry are the other
launch keys; everything else is a property below.

## Actions
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: DotplotRenderingBackend) => void`
- `setHoveredFeature(hit: DotplotPlotPickHit | undefined) => void`: Point the whole plot's hover state at one pick hit: the track whose geometry was hit takes the segment index, every other track clears, so `undefined` (a miss) clears the plot. An action rather than a loop in the pointer handler so the N…
- `setCursorMode(mode: CursorMode) => void`
- `setDrawCigar(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setAxisGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setAxisLabels(labels: boolean) => void`
- `setRatio(ratio: 1 | undefined) => void`
- `setLineWidth(value: number) => void`
- `clearView() => void`: returns to the import form
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => number`
- `setHeight(newHeight: number) => number`
- `setError(e: unknown) => void`
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<DotplotViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `zoomOut() => void`
- `zoomIn() => void`
- `scrollXY(dx: number, dy: number) => void`: Pan both axes one gesture step. Each delta is in the scroll direction of its axis, not screen px — the vertical axis lays out bottom-up, and both callers (wheel, drag) already hold the flipped value for other reasons.
- `zoomAt(factor: number, [x, y]: Coord) => void`: Zoom both axes by `factor`, holding the locus under a plot-area point still. The anchor is the same component-px `Coord` the drag handlers pass around, so each axis converts it with that axis's `fromScreenPx`, as `getCoords` does.
- `activateTrackSelector() => Widget`
- `showTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: object, displayInitialSnapshot?: DisplayInitialSnapshot, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => any`: `initialSnapshot` is annotated rather than inferred from its default. A bare `{}` accepts a number, so this signature satisfied `applySyntenyTrackSelections`' `(trackId, level) => void` callback — passing `model.showTrack` there…
- `hideTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `setAssemblyNames(x: string, y: string) => void`
- `zoomInToMouseCoords(mousedown: Coord, mouseup: Coord) => void`: zooms into clicked and dragged region. Under `coord.ratio` both axes take the larger of the two fits, so the whole box stays in view on the axis whose plot dimension is shorter.
- `addHighlightFromMouseCoords(mousedown: Coord, mouseup: Coord) => void`: highlights the clicked and dragged region: the x-span becomes a band on the horizontal axis and the y-span a band on the vertical axis, so the drag rect is their intersection
- `showAllRegions() => void`
- `initializeDisplayedRegions() => void`
- `openInCircularSyntenyView() => void`: a circular view of the two axes' genomes with this view's tracks as ribbons, the second genome reordered to follow the first, and this view's color and length filter
- `launchLinearSyntenyView(mousedown: Coord, mouseup: Coord) => void`: opens a linear synteny view on the clicked and dragged region: the horizontal axis' span on the top row, the vertical axis' below, each fitted to this view's width, with every track that has a linear synteny display, painted and filtered…
- `launchTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: object, displayInitialSnapshot?: DisplayInitialSnapshot, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => Promise<any>`: showTrack for a track whose display state model may be lazily loaded: loads it, then shows
- `launchToggleTrack(trackId: string) => Promise<boolean>`: toggleTrack with launchTrack's loading behavior
- `exportSvg(opts?: ViewExportSvgOptions) => Promise<string>`: renders the view to SVG markup, which it returns; saves it through FileSaver unless `save: false`
- `applySquare(ratio: number) => void`: Set both axes to the average bpPerPx (hview divided by `ratio`), re-anchoring each on the locus that was at its center. setBpPerPx alone would leave offsetPx untouched while bpPerPx changed under it, scrolling the plot; the centerAt calls…
- `squareView() => void`: Equalize both axes' bpPerPx. Also what the aspect-ratio lock applies to absorb divergence from box-zoom and other per-axis operations — deliberately not clamped to either axis's own maxBpPerPx, since a shared bpPerPx that fits the larger…
- `squareViewProportional() => void`
- `setResolution(resolution: LodMode) => void`
- `setShowLegend(show: boolean) => void`: The legend host's setter: closing the key hides it for this mode only, so picking another mode brings its key up.
- `setLegendShow(show: boolean) => void`: The "Show legend" checkbox: writes `legend.show`, and showing it brings back a key closed in this mode.
- `dismissLegendSection() => void`: One section is the whole key here.
- `setOpacity(value: number) => void`: The opacity slider: the constant, or under a field its range scaled so its most opaque end equals `value`.
- `setOpacityField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Fade by `field` from the current opacity down to 0.3 of it, or with undefined draw every alignment at the opacity the fade reached.
- `observeAttributeRanges(ranges: Record<string, AttributeRange>) => void`: Fold one fetch's observed attribute spans into the domain this view paints and labels its ramps with. Called by each display as its fetch lands, because the accumulation has to outlive the payload it came from: the previous window's span…
- `resetAttributeRanges() => void`: Forget the accumulated domain, leaving `attributeRanges` reporting what the loaded fetches cover and nothing else.
- `setHideUnlabelled(value: boolean) => void`
- `setColorField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Set the field the view paints by over `encoding.color`, undefined unsetting it for the view's default, and rescale the ramp, which is the only way back from a domain one outlying window widened.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every alignment `value`, undefined returning to the view's default.
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: The picker Color by's Solid color... opens.
- `setColorDomain(domain: string[]) => void`: Declare the order a text column's labels take. The labels listed lead, the rest follow sorted; an empty list gives back the order the fetches found them in.
- `setTrackColor(trackId: string, value: string | undefined) => void`: Pin one track's color under `encoding.color: 'track'`, or release it back to an automatic palette slot.
- `clearTrackColors() => void`
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setFilter(predicates: FieldPredicate[]) => void`
- `setLowerBound(field: string, value: number) => void`: The slider on one field: `field` at least `value`, or no lower bound at 0.
- `setImportFormSyntenyTrack(idx: number, val: ImportFormSyntenyTrack) => void`
- `clearImportFormSyntenyTracks() => void`: Drop the pending selections once a launch has applied them. Left in place they outlive the form: "Return to import form" would reopen on a finished upload from the previous launch, and a pair whose assemblies no longer match it reads as an…
- `setAwaitingAutoDiagonalize(arg: boolean) => void`
- `beginAutoDiagonalize(requested: boolean) => void`: Declare the gate at the top of one init apply pass: a reorder is pending iff THIS init asked for one. Assigning rather than raising is what hands the gate over cleanly — a superseded init that asked for a reorder and then skipped it would…
- `finishAutoDiagonalize() => void`: A reorder resolved, the init's or a manual one, so the view on screen is the diagonalized one — open the gate.
- `setDiagonalizeError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeCancel(arg?: (() => void) | undefined) => void`
- `cancelAutoDiagonalize() => void`: Abort an in-flight auto-diagonalize; `withDiagonalizeProgress`'s finally clears the wait flag, revealing the (undiagonalized) view.
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `ownTracks: TrackModelOf<DisplayModel>[]`: The census entry for this view: the tracks it holds itself. Declared rather than derived — see `BaseViewModel.ownTracks`.
- `width: number`
- `borderX: number`: Left margin: fits the vertical (vview) axis labels. Derived purely from that axis's regions + zoom — never from viewWidth — so it can't feed back through viewWidth = width - borderX into a render loop.
- `borderY: number`: Bottom margin: fits the horizontal (hview) axis labels. See borderX.
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<DotplotViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; malformed?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean | unde…`: the launch state that still has something to apply — the gate every loading and import-form path below reads.
- `assemblyErrors: string | undefined`
- `highlights: HighlightType[]`: the session's highlights on either axis' assembly
- `assembliesInitialized: boolean`
- `axisAssemblyError: Error | undefined`: A dotplot plots one assembly against another, so anything but two names here cannot lay out. `initializeDisplayedRegions` walks the two axes in step with this array, so one name leaves the other axis with no regions and `initialized` never…
- `error: unknown`: The view's terminal state: whatever the import form's submit threw, else a pair of axes that cannot lay out, else whatever the assemblies did. Declared here so every reader below uses the same expression; re-spelling it in `showImportForm`…
- `initialized: boolean`
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `initPending: boolean`: An `init` blob that has not been applied yet — `installInitAutorun` clears it as the last thing an apply pass does. The plot is assembling itself: the axes can already exist, and be initialized, while the tracks or the region restriction…
- `showImportForm: boolean`: Whether to show the import form
- `showLoading: boolean`: Whether to show a loading indicator instead of the import form or view
- `loadingAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly whose load the spinner is waiting on. `init` names them before assemblyNames is materialized, so it is the source until then.
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: The loading screen's text while `showLoading`, taken from the assembly being waited on; undefined otherwise.
- `status: ViewStatus`: The view's lifecycle as one value — ready, error, loading or noRegions — for a host that draws its own chrome and has to render all four. Same shape and same precedence as the linear view's, through `computeViewStatus`.
- `viewWidth: number`: Plot area width. Floored at 0: the axis borders have a MIN_BORDER floor, so a container narrower than that would otherwise yield a negative canvas dimension and a negative maxBpPerPx.
- `viewHeight: number`: Plot area height. Floored at 0, see viewWidth.
- `gridlinesEmpty: boolean`: The setting is on and neither axis has ruler ticks to extend across the plot. The ticked checkbox then changes nothing, so the menu says why instead of looking broken. The whole-genome view is this.
- `hasVisibleRegions: boolean`: Both axes have a region on screen, so the plot has a grid to draw and a first block to anchor its backdrop rect on. The grid reads the two block lists' heads, which only this makes safe.
- `views: (Dotplot1DView & { readonly width: number; readonly maxBpPerPx: number; readonly labelMarginPx: number; toScreenPx(alongPx: number): number; fromScreenPx(scree…`
- `drawCigar: boolean`: `indels.show`: whether each alignment's CIGAR shapes its line.
- `indelGaps: boolean`: Whether each indel is left a gap rather than drawn.
- `axisGrid: boolean`: `axis.grid`: whether each axis' ticks run across the plot.
- `axisLabels: boolean`: `axis.labels`: whether each axis numbers its major ticks.
- `ratio: 1 | undefined`: `coord.ratio`: 1 while both axes are held at one bp/px.
- `sharedFitBpPerPx: number`: The zoom-out limit both axes share under `coord.ratio`: one bpPerPx has to fit the LONGER genome, so it is the larger of the two axes' own fits. Read back by each axis as its `maxBpPerPx` (see `axisMaxBpPerPx`), so every route to a zoom —…
- `dotplotDisplays: DotplotDisplayModel[]`: Every DotplotDisplay under this view's tracks. Filtered by `type` rather than taken as `tracks[i].displays[0]`: `showTrack` only ever builds one view-compatible display, but a hand-written or legacy session snapshot is hydrated verbatim,…
- `trackWarnings: TrackWarning[]`: Every loaded track's render warnings, under the name to report them by. Shared with the synteny view's own report (see `collectTrackWarnings` for why the name has to come off the display's `parentTrack`), and a cached computed rather than…
- `surfaceReadiness: ComparativeSurface`: The plot rect as the displays drawing onto it see it: first paint, plus the two flags that mean what is on screen is not the answer yet. Published here so a display reads one field, and so `settled` below and every display's `displayPhase`…
- `displayPhase: DisplayStatusPhase`: What the shared canvas publishes as `data-display-phase`: the ranking over the plots drawing onto it. Its twin `settled` below is the stricter question — see `comparativeReadiness`.
- `settled: boolean`: Canvas has painted and no display is still fetching, so what's on screen is the final settled content. The `data-display-drawn` on `dotplot_webgl_canvas`, which screenshot capture and the browser-test suites wait on, reads this — so it…
- `hoveredDisplay: DotplotDisplayModel | undefined`: The one track that owns the plot's hover, or undefined. At most one can: `setHoveredFeature` points a single display at the hit and clears every other in the same batch.
- `hoveredTooltipLines: string[] | undefined`: The hovered alignment's tooltip lines, or undefined when nothing is hovered.
- `hoveredHighlight: DotplotHoverHighlight | undefined`: The hovered alignment's restroke geometry — see `DotplotDisplay.hoveredFeatureHighlight`.
- `geometryByDisplayKey: Map<number, DotplotGeometryData>`: Per-display GPU geometry keyed by `displayKey`. The upload autorun diffs this map: new entries upload, vanished entries evict. Drawn in insertion order, so tracks paint bottom-of-the-list last.
- `plotTransform: { viewBpH: number; viewBpV: number; bpPerPxHInv: number; bpPerPxVInv: number; viewHeight: number; }`: The cumBp -> plot px reconstruction, as the numbers everything that draws or hit-tests this plot runs on: the viewport-start cumBp per axis, the inverse bpPerPx per axis, and the plot height the v axis is flipped through (it lays out…
- `dotplotBlocks: RenderBlock[]`: One canvas-wide block per loaded display, in the map's insertion order, so tracks paint bottom-of-the-list last. An empty list is a real frame, not a skip: the backend clears before drawing, so painting zero displays is what wipes the plot…
- `dotplotRenderState: DotplotRenderState`: Aggregated per-frame render state — a resolved value, never undefined; "the view isn't measured yet" is the `canRender` precondition below.
- `canRender: boolean`: Render-lifecycle precondition (overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook): before the axes have regions and a measured width there is nothing to paint against. With the autorun pair gated here, `dotplotRenderState` can stay a…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook: a measured plot with no tracks on it paints nothing this tick and nothing is coming, so it has finished rather than being pending. The backend answers "did content reach the canvas" off the blocks…
- `hasLodCapableAdapter: boolean`: Whether any track's adapter has tiers to switch between, which gates the "Level of detail" setting.
- `resolution: LodMode`: `data.resolution`: the stored tier every track fetches.
- `showLegend: boolean`: The legend-host half of `LegendMixin` a view needs: whether the key draws, which is `legend.show`, the mode having a key, and the reader not having closed it in this mode. `ChromeLegend` and `SvgLegend` read it.
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: The key `ChromeLegend` draws on screen and `SvgLegend` in the export.
- `defaultOpacity: number`: The constant opacity a reset returns to: low on the synteny view for dense whole-genome hairballs, opaque on the dotplot.
- `opacitySetting: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot`: `encoding.opacity` as its snapshot holds it.
- `opacityFade: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot | undefined`: What the color pass fades each alignment by: the field's mapping with its range as shares of `opacityLevel`, or undefined while `encoding.opacity` draws its constant, so the slider recolors nothing either way.
- `opacityLevel: number`: The opacity every alignment draws at before a field's fade: the shader's uniform (`opacityLevel`).
- `opacityField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.opacity` fades by, undefined while it draws its constant.
- `colorSetting: SyntenyColorSnapshot`: `encoding.color` as its snapshot holds it, with the view's default field where it names neither a field nor a constant.
- `impliedColorField: string | undefined`: The field the view paints while `encoding.color` names neither a field nor a constant, undefined for its default scheme.
- `colorPaint: SyntenyColorPaint`: What `encoding.color.scale` declares over a field's own scale: its `type`, `domain`, `range` or `scheme` for its colors, `reverse`, and a ramp's pinned ends and middle. Read from these slots alone, so a key-only edit repaints nothing.
- `colorValue: string | undefined`: `encoding.color.value`: the color every alignment paints under the default mode in place of the view's own scheme, or undefined for that scheme.
- `colorDomain: readonly string[]`: `encoding.color.scale.domain`, the order a text column's labels take. Read from that slot alone, so a key-only edit (`legend.title`, `scale.names`) recolors nothing.
- `colorRange: readonly string[]`: The colors a text column's labels take in domain order: `encoding.color.scale.range`, else its `scheme` sampled once per domain value
- `colorableAttributes: string[]`: Distinct numeric columns across the overlaid tracks, in first-seen order — two tracks declaring `dn` offer one `dn` mode, not two.
- `attributeRanges: Record<string, AttributeRange>`: The span each numeric channel covers: unioned over the loaded displays, and over every fetch this view has already taken (`seenAttributeRanges`). A column has no declared domain, so this is what its ramp scales to, what the legend labels…
- `colorableTracks: ColorableTrack[]`: `colorableTrackConfigs` paired with whatever color the user pinned. This is the single definition of "the tracks that get colors" — the palette, the legend and the palette menu all read it, so they cannot disagree about which tracks are in…
- `trackColorAssignments: Map<string, string>`: trackId -> the color it draws in under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Assigned across the whole view rather than per display, so an automatic slot can't duplicate a color pinned on a sibling.
- `colorField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.color` paints by, undefined for the default color.
- `hideUnlabelled: boolean`: Whether the filter drops the alignments with no value for the field the view paints by, the "Hide unlabelled rows" box.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the mode has a key worth a box: a track palette, a ramp, a reader-named column, or strand wherever the shape does not show it (`shapeShowsStrand`), which leaves the color the only strand cue.
- `colorLegendChips: ColorChip[]`: Legend rows naming the overlaid tracks — one per track with its palette color, however many levels it is on, and only under `encoding.color: 'track'`, since every other mode has a fixed legend.
- `colorScales: ColorScale[]`: The active mode's key, or none for a mode without one. View-wide rather than per display because the key is one box for the whole view, and the ramp domain it labels is the view's.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field
- `predicates: FieldPredicate[]`: The `filter` list as the predicate compiler reads it.
- `minLength: number`: The lower bound on `length`, 0 for none.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this display paints a canvas in its **current** configuration, as opposed to a deliberate static placeholder (LD with the triangle off, sequence past base resolution — both render a message where…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): what is on the canvas was painted from data a later change has made wrong, so `painted` below should answer *pending* until the repaint lands even though `canvasDrawn` is still true. The per-region fetch…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders this view's displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownViews: AbstractViewModel[]`: The views nested directly inside this one, which the census counts as separate views — a synteny stack's genome rows, a breakpoint split view's panels.

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.literal('DotplotView')`
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultHeight)`: the height of the plot in pixels
- `trackSelectorType = types.stripDefault(types.string, 'hierarchical')`: ignored: the hierarchical selector is the only one. Declared because saved sessions and share links carry it.
- `assemblyNames = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: the two assemblies being compared, horizontal axis first. A spec normally names these per axis instead, as `views[0].assembly` and `views[1].assembly`.
- `indels = types.stripDefault(syntenyIndelsConfigSchema, {})`: The insertions and deletions inside each alignment, a [](/docs/config/syntenyindels) part: `{ show: false }` plots each alignment as one straight segment, and `{ encoding: { opacity: 0 } }` leaves each indel a gap in its line.
- `axis = types.stripDefault(dotplotAxisConfigSchema, {})`: Both genome axes' guide, a [](/docs/config/dotplotaxis) object: `grid` extends each axis' ruler ticks across the plot as faint lines, the way LinearGenomeView's `axis.grid` extends its ruler down over the tracks, and `labels` numbers the…
- `coord = types.stripDefault(syntenyCoordConfigSchema, {})`: The coordinate system, a [](/docs/config/syntenycoord) object: `{ ratio: 1 }` keeps hview and vview at one bpPerPx so the plot stays square. Wheel zoom already preserves the ratio; box-zoom and other independent ops trigger an autorun…
- `lineWidth = types.stripDefault(types.number, DEFAULT_LINE_WIDTH)`: Line width in CSS pixels of every alignment in the plot
- `hview = types.optional(DotplotHView, {})`: the horizontal axis, as a full 1D view state. A spec writes `views[0]` instead, which the launcher resolves into this.
- `vview = types.optional(DotplotVView, {})`: the vertical axis, the counterpart to `hview`. A spec writes `views[1]`.
- `tracks = types.array(pm.pluggableMstType('track', 'stateModel'))`
- `launch = types.frozen<LaunchInput<DotplotViewCommands> | undefined>()`: transient launch state: the settings written on the view object that need resolving before they can be view state — the two axis assemblies, track recipes, highlights. `preProcessSnapshot` moves them here off the snapshot, the afterAttach…
- `data = types.stripDefault(syntenyDataConfigSchema, {})`: What the fetch reads, a [](/docs/config/syntenydata) object: `resolution` picks a tiered file's stored tier. One value for the view, so every track draws at the same tier.
- `legend = types.stripDefault(legendConfigSchema, {})`: Whether the view draws its color key, a [](/docs/config/legend) object. The key's close button hides it for the current mode only and is never saved.
- `encoding = types.stripDefault(syntenyEncodingConfigSchema, {})`: The channels every track in the view paints with, a [](/docs/config/syntenyencoding) object. Its `color` is a [](/docs/config/syntenycolor) channel: `"strand"`, `"query"`, `"reference"`, `"track"`, a measurement (`identity`, `mapq`,…
- `trackColors = types.map(types.string)`: trackId -> explicit color under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Absent means the track takes an automatic slot from the palette.
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `filter = types.stripDefault(fieldPredicateArray(), [])`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries an alignment must all pass. A field is any field `color` takes, or `length`, the alignment's bp on its own axis: `[{ field: 'length', gte: 10000 }]` clears a…
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar and keep it in the session

## Methods
- `syntenyTracks() => ComparativeTrackModel[]`: Annotated for the reason `ComparativeTrackModel` documents: the array is `any`.
- `loadedAttributeRanges() => Record<string, AttributeRange>[]`: Each loaded display's observed attribute spans, which the mixin unions into the domain the legend labels its ramp with.
- `colorSurface() => "points"`: Flat points, never a CIGAR op.
- `getCoords(mousedown: Coord, mouseup: Coord) => { x1: PxToBpResult; x2: PxToBpResult; y1: PxToBpResult; y2: PxToBpResult; } | undefined`: Both corners of a drag rect, in bp on each axis. Undefined for a drag too small to be a selection — the same threshold the interaction hook uses to tell a drag from a click.
- `pickFeatureAt(x: number, y: number) => DotplotPlotPickHit | undefined`: The alignment under a pointer position (plot px, y downward), across every track on the shared canvas, or undefined.
- `getHHighlightCoords(region: { assemblyName?: string | undefined; refName: string; start: number; end: number; }) => { width: number; left: number; } | undefined`: Map a highlight region to {left, width} px on the horizontal axis. left is already screen-offset. Returns undefined when the region isn't on hview's assembly/displayed regions.
- `getVHighlightCoords(region: { assemblyName?: string | undefined; refName: string; start: number; end: number; }) => { top: number; height: number; } | undefined`: Map a highlight region to {top, height} px on the vertical axis. Returns undefined when the region isn't on vview's assembly/displayed regions.
- `highlightMenuItems(_highlight: HighlightType) => MenuItem[]`: a highlight chip's menu rows after Dismiss; extend this to add one
- `menuItems() => ({ label: string; icon: OverridableComponent<SvgIconTypeMap<{}, "svg">> & { muiName: string; }; onClick: () => void; type?: undefined; checked?: undefine…`
- `colorableTrackConfigs() => { trackId: string; name: string; }[]`
- `colorableAttributeNames() => string[]`: The columns the tracks declare in their adapter's `attributeColumns` (the ortholog-table adapter's slot), one color mode each.
- `legendAlpha() => number`: The plot's opacity composites the key's chips, as it does the alignments.
- `legendCigarOps() => number | undefined`: Overridable hook: the indel ops the key lists a chip for, so it names only what the eye can find. `undefined` is the static menu preview; the dotplot draws flat points and never a CIGAR op.
- `offersReferenceColor() => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the view has a shared reference for the `reference` field to anchor on. It needs a stack of two or more levels; below that it is query or target by another name.
- `shapeShowsStrand() => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether an alignment's shape shows its strand, which spares the strand colors a key. A linear ribbon twists against its rows' directions, which their rulers show; a whole-genome dotplot is mostly dots with no slope to…
- `trackColorFor(trackId: string) => string`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `lowerBound(field: string) => number`: The lower bound the filter puts on `field`, 0 for none.

DrawerWidgetSessionMixin.text:
# DrawerWidgetSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds the widget drawer to a session: the open widgets, which one is showing, and the drawer's side, width and minimized state.

## Actions
- `setDrawerPosition(arg: DrawerPosition) => void`
- `updateDrawerWidth(drawerWidth: number, availableWidth?: number) => number`
- `resizeDrawer(distance: number, availableWidth?: number) => number`
- `addWidget(typeName: string, id: string, initialState?: any, conf?: unknown) => Widget`
- `showWidget(widget: Widget) => void`
- `hideWidget(widget: Widget) => void`: closes the widget, and removes it from the session when its type sets `discardOnClose`. Minimizing the drawer is not closing.
- `minimizeWidgetDrawer() => void`
- `showWidgetDrawer() => void`
- `popoutWidget() => void`: show the visible widget in a modal dialog, freeing the drawer column
- `returnWidgetToDrawer() => void`
- `setModalWidgets(flag: boolean) => void`
- `hideAllWidgets() => void`
- `closeModalWidget() => void`: the modal's close button: a popped-out widget goes back to the drawer, and with no drawer to go back to the widget closes
- `openWidget(typeName: string, id: string, initialState?: any, conf?: unknown) => Widget`: adds the widget, replacing one with the same id, and shows it
- `editConfiguration(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel | { trackId: string; }, opts?: { expandedDisplayId?: string | undefined; } | undefined) => void`: opens a configuration editor to configure the given thing, and sets the current task to be configuring it

## Getters
- `visibleWidget: Widget | undefined`
- `drawerVisible: boolean`: whether the drawer column is on screen: there is something to show, it is not minimized to the FAB, and it is not currently a modal instead.
- `modalWidgetVisible: boolean`: whether the visible widget shows in a modal: popped out of the drawer, or on a host with no room for one

## Properties

# DropboxOAuthInternetAccount (Internet Account model, authentication plugin)

Fetches a file from a Dropbox share link through the Dropbox API, with an OAuth 2.0 token from the Dropbox login.

Config slots: docs topic "config:DropboxOAuthInternetAccount" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes OAuthInternetAccount — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `validateToken(token: string, location: UriLocation) => Promise<string>`
- `storeRefreshToken(refreshToken: string) => void`
- `removeRefreshToken() => void`
- `postTokenGrant(grant: Record<string, string>, describeError: (response: Response) => Promise<string>) => Promise<string>`: POST a grant to the token endpoint and read the access token out of the answer. Both grants this account makes — trading the authorization code on the way in, trading the refresh token when the access token expires — are the same…
- `exchangeAuthorizationForAccessToken(code: string, redirectUri: string, codeVerifier: string | undefined) => Promise<string>`
- `exchangeRefreshForAccessToken(refreshToken: string) => Promise<string>`
- `validateTokenWithProbe(token: string, probe: (token: string) => Promise<Response>, describeError: (response: Response, reason?: string) => Promise<string>) => Promise<string>`: Prove a token against the resource and, if the resource answers 401, refresh it once and prove the new one. Returns whichever token worked; throws if neither does, or if the resource fails for any other reason. Every OAuth account…
- `getTokenViaAuthFlow() => Promise<string>`: Opens the provider's auth page and returns a promise for the resulting token. For Electron, drives the flow directly via IPC; for web, opens a popup and waits for the redirect message.
- `getTokenFromUser(resolve: (token: string) => void, reject: (error: Error) => void) => Promise<void>`

- `toggleContents: Element`: The FileSelector icon for Dropbox

- `conf: OAuthInternetAccountConfig`: The config typed off the concrete schema. `ConfigurationReference` erases `self.configuration` to `any` (the reference's MST instance brand doesn't include the schema's slot definitions), so reads go through this getter to recover per-slot…

- `retrieveRefreshToken() => string | undefined`

Everything the two single-view embedded products' sessions (react-linear-genome-view, react-circular-genome-view) share: the mixin set they compose and the three getters that read the root model. The twin of createEmbeddedRootModel one level down.

- `setHighlightsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setHighlightLabelsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`

- `setErrorDialog(state: ErrorDialogState | undefined) => void`

- `teardownConnection(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => void`: Close every track a connection contributed — the live instance's tracks plus any persisted open-track configs (a dormant connection, never expanded this session, still renders its opened tracks from `connectionTrackConfigs`) — from all…
- `deleteConnection(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => boolean`: Fully remove a connection: tear down its tracks and live instance, then delete its config.
- `addConnectionConf(connectionConf: AnyConfiguration) => BaseConnectionConfig`: Adds to the **config**, not the session: `jbrowse.connections`, which every visitor to this instance loads. jbrowse-web overrides this so a non-admin's connection goes to `sessionConnections` instead — see WebSessionConnectionsMixin, whose…
- `clearConnections() => void`

- `updateConnectionTrackConfig(trackConf: Record<string, unknown> & { trackId: string; }) => void`: Persist an edit to an opened connection track. The full config is stored (not a delta): the connection's fetched "base" isn't present at load, so only a complete config resolves synchronously.

- `pruneConnectionTrackConfig(trackId: string) => void`: Drop a connection track's persisted config once no open view still references it, so the session doesn't accumulate closed tracks.
- `hydrateConnection(connectionId: string) => void`: Lazily establish a single connection by id if it isn't already live; the track selector calls it when the connection's category is expanded. Fetches without launching a view or showing a success snackbar; already-open tracks keep rendering…

- `updateDrawerWidth(drawerWidth: number, availableWidth?: number) => number`
- `resizeDrawer(distance: number, availableWidth?: number) => number`
- `addWidget(typeName: string, id: string, initialState?: any, conf?: unknown) => Widget`
- `showWidget(widget: Widget) => void`
- `hideWidget(widget: Widget) => void`: closes the widget, and removes it from the session when its type sets `discardOnClose`. Minimizing the drawer is not closing.

# ExternalTokenInternetAccount (Internet Account model, authentication plugin)

Internet account that authenticates requests with a user-supplied external token, prompting for the token via a dialog and optionally validating it with a HEAD request. See [TokenEntryInternetAccount](../tokenentryinternetaccount) for the shared behavior.

Config slots: docs topic "config:ExternalTokenInternetAccount" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes TokenEntryInternetAccount — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `getTokenFromUser(resolve: (token: string) => void, reject: (error: Error) => void) => void`: Prompt the user for a token via the account's dialog form, resolving with the entered token or rejecting if the user cancels.
- `validateToken(token: string, location: UriLocation) => Promise<string>`: Optionally validate the token with a HEAD request before use, per the `validateWithHEAD` config slot. Only a 401 drops the token: there is nothing to renew it with, so the next read re-opens the dialog.

## Getters
- `validateWithHEAD: boolean`: validate the token with a HEAD request before it is used

## Properties
- `type = types.literal(typeName)`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`

FacetWritesMixin.text:
# FacetWritesMixin (Mixin model, core)

The writes a display's `facet` object takes from a menu row, a dialog or a chip drag: the field the sections split by (`facetByField`) and their order (`setFacetSort`). Each rewrites the object as written, so what a pick leaves alone stays, and a pick of the field already grouping writes nothing. A display that resets its scroll when the sections change does it from `HiddenGroupsMixin`'s `dropGroupState`, which also runs for a facet an agent, a share link or "Edit plot" writes

## Actions
- `facetByField(field: string) => void`: Split the sections by `field`, `''` for none, keeping the order and hidden sections while it is the field already grouping.
- `setFacetSort(sort: readonly string[]) => void`: The order the sections take, the ones it names first; `[]` sorts them all.

## Getters
- `writtenFacet: WrittenFacet`: The `facet` object as written.

# FeatureGateMixin (Mixin model, features plugin)

The density axis of the region-too-large gate, composed after `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`. A display opts in by composing this and calling `commitGateMeasurements` from its fetch's `onComplete`.

## Actions
- `setDensityStats(displayedRegionIndex: number, stats: RegionDensityStats) => void`
- `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: `RegionTooLargeMixin`'s hook: the density axis drops its counts on the trigger that drops the byte estimate, so a gate's measurements always come from one file.
- `commitGateMeasurements(measurements: RegionGateMeasurement[], issued: GateFetchState) => void`: Judged by the tier captured at issue.

## Getters
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: `types.compose` resolves a collision to the later argument, so this mixin must follow the one declaring the byte-gate opt-in.
- `visibleFeatureDensityPerPx: number`: Density at the debounced `coarseBpPerPx`, so the verdict shares the layout cadence.
- `maxFeatureDensity: number | undefined`: Undefined when the axis may not act.
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`

## Methods
- `observedMaxDensity(bpPerPx: number) => number`

FetchMixin.text:
# FetchMixin (Mixin model, core)

Cancel-safe fetch lifecycle for any display that loads data over RPC. Owns the entire fetch state machine (abort rotation, staleness tracking, error capture, status reporting); consumers see only `runFetch`, `cancelFetch`, `isLoading`, `error`, `statusMessage`, and `fetchGeneration`.

## Actions
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.

**The** foundation for a display holding a single global (non-regional) dataset: HiC's contact matrix, the LD triangle, multi-way synteny's lanes.

## Actions
- `commitFetchResult(commit: () => void, key: FetchKey) => void`: The commit half of a keyed fetch: run the display's own store in the same transaction as the key stamp, so no observer can see fresh data under a stale key or the reverse. As the only writer of `loadedFetchKey`, this action makes…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter — the shared skeleton's reload epoch makes that bump override the freshness gate, even against a fetch that commits mid-reload, so nothing here has to remember to invalidate for the retry's sake)…

- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…

- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.

- `host: RegionHost`: The hosting view as the `RegionHost` contract — see `containingHost` for the cast it owns, why the name is `host` and not `view`, and why both foundations still declare the name over one body.
- `canvasWidthPx: number`: The CSS width of this display's on-screen canvas, in px; see `trackCanvasWidthPx`. A heatmap laid out over the whole content reads the content width instead (`TriangleMatrixMixin.canvasWidth`).
- `staticBlockSignature: string | undefined`: The static-block set as a signature, or `undefined` before the view is measured — the building block every `viewSignature` in this family starts from. Multi-way synteny is exactly this; HiC appends its resolution. Declared here so the…
- `dynamicBlockSignature: string | undefined`: The same over `dynamicBlocks`, for a display whose fetch window is the live viewport rather than the snapped block set (LD).
- `viewportEmpty: boolean`: No content block is on screen, so this display has nothing to fetch and nothing to paint — see `viewportEmpty.ts` for the one viewport that reaches it, how narrow that is, and why the state still has to be terminal rather than a permanent…
- `canRender: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook with the LGV precondition both foundations share — see `foundationCanRender`.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook off `fetchInert`: a display that will never fetch here shows a placeholder where its canvas would be, so `painted` and the pre-first-paint scrim term stop waiting on a paint that cannot come. This is…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it…
- `svgReady: boolean`: Policy single-sourced in `computeSvgReady`; this family supplies only the freshness half, which `foundationSvgReady` reads as `dataCurrent` or the vacuous currency of `viewportEmpty`. Note it requires the dataset to actually be current,…
- `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The display's mutually-exclusive visual state, mapped in `foundationDisplayPhase` — every foundation calls it and supplies only its staleness argument, so a term added to `computeActivityPhase` reaches all of them without being wired twice.
- `viewSignature: string | undefined`: Overridable hook, the one freshness input a display supplies: the signature of what the current *view* calls for — its block set (`blockKeySignature`) plus any view-derived fetch tier, like HiC's binsize; both comparative views' region…
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the held data matches the key, but the screen will settle on different data — a dependent fetch is still out, or a fetch input the display writes itself has moved. The same hook `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`…
- `currentFetchKey: FetchKey | undefined`: Key of the fetch the current view, settings and adapter call for. The fetch skeleton's freshness key: captured at issue, compared against the stamp above, and written to it at commit. Its identity survives a recomputation onto equal…
- `dataCurrent: boolean`: The shared freshness answer every foundation gives: data has been committed (`loadedFetchKey` is only ever written beside it), it was fetched for the current view and settings, and the display is not about to supersede it itself. A pan…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by `computeActivityPhase` and `foundationSvgReady`: a load this display depends on beyond its primary fetch has not landed for the first time, so the frame the primary fetch calls current is still…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): what is on the canvas was painted from data a later change has made wrong, so `painted` below should answer *pending* until the repaint lands even though `canvasDrawn` is still true. The per-region fetch…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: The opt-in. Overridden with a literal `true` by gated displays, and `check-gated-adapter-budgets` insists on a literal: this mixin returns early on it in an autorun and in `commitFetchBytes`.
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.
- `regionTooLarge: boolean`
- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.
- `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate.
- `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen.

## Methods
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.

HeightModeMixin.text:
# HeightModeMixin (Mixin model, core)

Track-height strategy over `TrackHeightMixin()`, which it composes and whose `height` and `resizeHeight` it overrides. `growTargetHeight` (default = the allotted height). Brings `heightMode`/`autoHeight`/`fitHeightToDisplay`, `grownHeight`, the reactive `height` override, `setHeightMode`, and the grow-aware `resizeHeight`, and the grow-exit bake reaction that writes the grown height into the slot when the mode leaves grow

Composes TrackHeightMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setHeightMode(mode: "fit" | "fixed" | "grow") => void`: Set the track-height strategy by writing the unified `heightMode` slot; the modes are mutually exclusive by construction. Leaving grow bakes the grown height into the `height` slot in the same action, so the switch is atomic:…
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`: Drag-resize. A manual drag means the user wants a fixed height, so leave grow first — otherwise the reactive `height` getter re-derives `grownHeight` on the next relayout and the drag appears to do nothing. The displayed (grown) height is…
- `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void`
- `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number`
- `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first.

## Getters
- `heightMode: "fit" | "fixed" | "grow"`: The track-height strategy (`fixed`/`grow`/`fit`).
- `fitTargetHeight: number`: The height the track is allotted (`TrackHeightMixin.allottedHeight`: the slot's, or a ring's band) — the fit target the fit/grow layout scales or packs content into. Read there instead of the reactive `height` getter to break the grow-mode…
- `growMaxHeight: number`: Ceiling `grow` mode sizes the track to, in px (content past it scrolls). Lives here rather than as a constant so a track whose whole point is a deep pileup can raise it; both displays that own a `grownHeight` read this, so the two can't…
- `autoHeight: boolean`: `grow` mode as a boolean, derived from the unified `heightMode` slot.
- `fitHeightToDisplay: boolean`: `fit` mode as a boolean, derived from the unified `heightMode` slot.
- `growTargetHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height this display's laid-out content wants, in px, before the `growMaxHeight` cap. Canvas answers with its settled feature stack, alignments with its stacked-sections height. The default is the raw slot, so a…
- `grownHeight: number`: Target track height for `grow`: what the content wants, capped so a deep stack doesn't grow the track to thousands of px (the remainder scrolls). What `installGrowExitBake` bakes into the slot on exit.
- `height: number`: In grow mode the track height follows the laid-out content reactively — no autorun writes the height config slot, so a settled relayout never churns the persisted session nor bakes a momentary height. Fixed/fit read the slot (fit shrinks…
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollContentHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the content that scrolls, in px.
- `scrollViewportHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the window it scrolls behind, in px.
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.

HiddenGroupsMixin.text:
# HiddenGroupsMixin (Mixin model, core)

The sections a reader hid from an in-track grouping's chips: the `facet.hidden` keys while the stack groups by the facet's field, `hideGroup` and `showAllGroups` writing them, `hiddenGroupKeys` reading them, `groupStateKey` (with the `ownGroupState` hook) for a live figure to key on, and the `dropGroupState` reset that fires when the host's `groupKeySpace` moves

## Actions
- `hideGroup(key: string) => void`: Drop a section from the stack. Reversed by `showAllGroups`, which the "Show" menu offers while anything is hidden, since a hidden section has no chip to restore it.
- `showAllGroups() => void`
- `dropGroupState() => void`: Overridable hook: forget the volatile per-group state a display keeps. A no-op by default, since the hidden sections are config.

## Getters
- `ownGroupState: unknown`: Overridable hook: the per-group state a display keeps beyond the hidden sections, as a plain value. `undefined` by default; alignments returns its collapses and height overrides, the state its `dropGroupState` clears.
- `hiddenGroups: ReadonlySet<string>`: The sections the user hid: `facet.hidden`, while the stack groups by the facet's field.
- `hiddenGroupKeys: ReadonlySet<string>`: Every key the stack drops. A fresh Set per change, so a layout memo comparing its inputs by identity sees a hide.
- `groupStateKey: unknown`: All the per-group state as a plain, comparable value: the hidden sections, sorted, beside `ownGroupState`. A live figure keys on it, since a display's own state is volatile and in no snapshot; a Set would serialize as `{}`.

# HierarchicalTrackSelectorWidget (Widget model, data-management plugin)

Lists a view's available tracks as a tree of categories, with a filter box, favorites and recently used tracks, and a group for each connection.

## Actions
- `setSortTrackNames(val: boolean) => void`
- `setSortCategories(val: boolean) => void`

- `addToSelection(trackIds: string[]) => void`

- `clearSelection() => void`

- `addToRecentlyUsed(id: string) => void`
- `clearRecentlyUsed() => void`
- `setView(view: IBaseViewModel | undefined) => void`
- `setTrackContainerId(id: string | undefined) => void`
- `setCategoryMode(id: string, mode: CategoryMode | undefined) => void`
- `clearCategoryModes() => void`
- `clearFilterText() => void`
- `setFilterText(newText: string) => void`
- `setCategoryCollapsed(id: string, collapsed: boolean) => void`: the single gate on accordion state: a folder is a mode the user picked, not an accordion that happens to be shut, so every collapse/expand — one row, a bulk menu item, or "expand all" — passes it by
- `setFolderCategory(id: string, isFolder: boolean) => void`: folder and collapsed are the same slot, so leaving folder mode always yields an expanded category
- `expandAllCategories() => void`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string) => Promise<void>`: shows or hides a track, recording one it showed as recently used
- `collapseSubCategories() => void`
- `collapseTopLevelCategories() => void`
- `toggleCategory(id: string) => void`: expanding a dormant connection's category loads the connection

## Getters
- `trackContainer: TrackContainer | undefined`: The track list this selector shows and writes into: the view itself, or one of its containers when `trackContainerId` names one.
- `shownTrackIds: Set<string>`
- `favoritesSet: Set<string>`
- `recentlyUsedSet: Set<string>`
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `activeSortTrackNames: any`
- `activeSortCategories: any`
- `configAndSessionTrackConfigurations: AnyTrackConfig[]`: the tracks this view can be offered — its assemblies' sequence tracks, then the session's list filtered to what it can draw
- `sessionTrackIds: Set<any>`: a non-admin's added/copied tracks, which the tree groups under a "Session tracks" category. Membership is the session's own list — the source of truth — not a suffix baked into the trackId
- `filterQuery: string`: the normalized filter box contents; empty when nothing is being searched for
- `filterActive: boolean`: a query is being searched for, which forces categories open (isFilterForcedOpen)
- `mainGroupTracks: TrackNodeSource[]`: the config's own and the session's tracks, resolved and sorted. Its own getter, so a connection loading re-reads none of them
- `allTracks: TrackGroup[]`: the main group, then one group per connection config whether or not it is loaded. A dormant connection has no tracks and defaults collapsed; expanding it loads it (see toggleCategory)

# JBrowseDesktopRootModel (Root model, core)

Holds JBrowse Desktop's top-level state: the loaded config, the session, internet accounts, undo history, the app menus and the text-indexing jobs.

Composes RootAppMenuMixin, HistoryManagementMixin, InternetAccountsMixin, BaseRootModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setOpenNewSessionCallback(cb: (arg: string) => Promise<void>) => void`
- `setOpenLinkCallback(cb: (arg: string) => Promise<void>) => void`: Wired by the Loader to open a JBrowse Web link as a new session (the Loader owns plugin-manager lifecycle, as with openNewSessionCallback).
- `setReturnToStartScreenCallback(cb: () => void) => void`: Wired by the Loader to tear down this plugin manager and show the start screen (the Loader owns plugin-manager lifecycle).
- `saveSession(val: SessionSnap) => Promise<void>`
- `updateTrackBase(trackConf: { [key: string]: unknown; trackId: string; }) => void`: Replace a track's base config: its sessionTracks entry when the session owns the track, otherwise its jbrowse.tracks entry.
- `setPluginsUpdated() => Promise<void>`: Persist the session, then rebuild the plugin manager from disk so the changed plugin set takes effect (Loader wires openNewSessionCallback to reload from the session path).
- `flushSession() => Promise<void>`: Save now rather than waiting out the autosave's 1s throttle. Every path that tears the session down has to call this first.
- `appendMenu(menuName: string) => void`: Add a top-level menu, if the app bar does not already have one with this name.
- `insertMenu(menuName: string, position: number) => void`: Insert a top-level menu, if the app bar does not already have one with this name.
- `appendToMenu(menuName: string, menuItem: MenuItem) => void`: Add a menu item to a top-level menu, creating the menu if it does not exist.
- `insertInMenu(menuName: string, menuItem: MenuItem, position: number) => void`: Insert a menu item into a top-level menu, creating the menu if it does not exist.
- `appendToSubMenu(menuPath: string[], menuItem: MenuItem) => void`: Add a menu item to a sub-menu, creating any part of the path that does not exist.
- `insertInSubMenu(menuPath: string[], menuItem: MenuItem, position: number) => void`: Insert a menu item into a sub-menu, creating any part of the path that does not exist.
- `initializeInternetAccount(internetAccountConfig: AnyConfigurationModel, initialSnapshot?: object) => any`
- `createEphemeralInternetAccount(internetAccountId: string, initialSnapshot: Record<string, unknown>, url: string) => any`
- `findAppropriateInternetAccount(location: UriLocation) => any`
- `setError(error: unknown) => void`
- `addDetachDisposer(disposer: () => void) => void`: Register something that must stop when the host detaches this root.
- `detach() => void`: Called when the host releases this root. Stops the worker pool and whatever was registered with `addDetachDisposer`, and leaves the tree itself alone.
- `setSession(sessionSnapshot?: any) => void`: Sets the active session. Remaps any legacy display type names (e.g. LinearPileupDisplay → LinearAlignmentsDisplay), drops nodes whose pluggable type this build has no plugin for (see `pruneUnbuildableNodes`), then walks the resulting MST…
- `setDefaultSession() => void`: Starts a new session from the config's defaultSession. An `id` in it (a pasted session export has one) is dropped, since sessions are autosaved by id and each new one would otherwise overwrite the last. The name has no date, because the…
- `setSessionPath(path: string) => void`
- `renameCurrentSession(newName: string) => void`

- `history = types.optional(TimeTraveller, { targetPath: '../session' })`: used for undo/redo

- `session = types.maybe(sessionModelType)`: `session` encompasses the currently active state of the app, including views open, tracks open in those views, etc.
