- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('LDTrackDisplay')`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `id = ElementId`

## Methods
- `rpcProps() => LDRpcProps`
- `columnX(column: number) => number`: Viewport x of a fractional column index: `i + 0.5` is column i's apex. Uses the payload's own column width, so it follows the live transform through a zoom's refetch.
- `locusViewportX(refName: string, coord: number) => number | undefined`: Viewport x of a locus, or undefined when it has none.
- `hitTest(mouseX: number, mouseY: number) => LDCellHit | undefined`: The computed cell under a display-px point: a pair outside the band, or one no estimator filled, is not drawn and not hit.
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `renderSvg(opts: ExportSvgDisplayOptions) => Promise<ReactNode>`
- `cellToScreen(x: number, y: number) => { x: number; y: number; }`: Pre-rotation cell coordinates to display px.
- `screenToCell(x: number, y: number) => { x: number; y: number; }`: The exact inverse of `cellToScreen`.
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `rampColorScales({ id, title, extent: { min, max }, }: { id: string; title: string; extent: { min?: number | undefined; max: number; }; }) => ColorScale[]`: The legend's ramp, once there is a domain to span: its bottom where the scale paints it, a log scale's floor included, titled by `encoding.color.legend.title` where written, else `title`. An end of the domain the loaded values run past…
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The problems in a config that cannot be drawn as written: by default the schema's rules over its color objects and value axes, the ones `jbrowse validate` runs. A display with additional rules overrides it. `plotProblems` asks it of a…
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

LegendMixin.text:
# LegendMixin (Mixin model, core)

The legend, whole. A display declares the color scales it paints with (`colorScales`, a getter hook, and `colorScalesIn` where they follow the theme) and the mixin derives the key from them (`legendSpec`, and `legendSpecIn` for the SVG export, through `legendSpecOf`), keeps the `legend.show` slot's getter and setter (`showLegend`, `setShowLegend`), dismisses sections one at a time (`dismissLegendSection`, undone by re-showing the legend), and answers whether there is a key to offer (`hasLegendKey`). `DisplayChrome` draws the on-screen key and the exporting view the exported one, in a gutter…

## Actions
- `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it.
- `dismissLegendSection(id: string) => void`: Close one section of the legend, leaving the others up.

## Getters
- `showLegend: boolean`: Whether the legend is drawn.
- `colorScales: ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default none): the color scales this display paints with, in the order the key lists them. Each becomes one section of the legend, so a display with two vocabularies (genotype colors and sample groups) declares two.
- `legendRight: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px the on-screen key is pushed left from the key's inset, for a display that draws a column of text down its right edge — the multi-way lanes' scales. Not read by the export.
- `legendTop: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px the on-screen key is pushed down from the key's inset, for a display whose top rows hold the data a reader reads the rest against — the multi-way anchor lane. Not read by the export.
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: The key, derived from `colorScales` less the sections the reader dismissed. `DisplayChrome` renders it on screen and `renderDisplaySvg` flattens it for the export, so the two describe one set of colors.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the display has a key at all. The "Legend" row is offered only when it does. Overridable for a display whose key is only waiting for data: a scale that stays empty until a region lands must not remove the toggle in the meantime.

## Methods
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.

LGVSyntenyDisplay.text:
# LGVSyntenyDisplay (Display model, linear-comparative-view plugin)

Draws where a `SyntenyTrack`'s alignments fall in a plain linear genome view, with menu items that open them in a synteny view.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LGVSyntenyDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes LodTierInfoMixin, LinearAlignmentsDisplay, HiddenGroupsMixin, ContextMenuMixin, FacetWritesMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, HeightModeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Shows a `SyntenyTrack`'s alignments in a plain linear view (rather than the
two-row synteny view). Same track config as a synteny track — just pick this
display type:
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'hg38_vs_mm10',
  name: 'hg38 vs mm10',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38', 'mm10'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/hg38_vs_mm10.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'hg38',
    targetAssembly: 'mm10',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LGVSyntenyDisplay',
      displayId: 'hg38_vs_mm10-LGVSyntenyDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

## Actions
- `fetchNeeded(needed: IndexedRegion[]) => void`: The inherited fetch, with each region's assembly respelled the way the track declares it. The view names its assembly canonically and the adapter answers a region by comparing that text against its configured `assemblyNames` in a worker…
- `setSelfLaneHidden(flag: boolean) => void`: Write the self lane into `facet.hidden`, or take it out.
- `setResolution(arg: LodMode) => void`
- `setAdapterHeader(read: AdapterRead<unknown>) => void`
- `setFilterFields(patch: Readonly<Record<string, readonly FieldPredicate[] | undefined>>) => void`: Replaces the entries on each field the patch names, `undefined` returning a field to its defaults; every other field keeps what was written.
- `setShowCoverage(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowInterbase(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowCoverageAlleles(show: boolean) => void`: Turns the coverage band's allele colors on or off, `coverage.alleles.show`
- `setCoverageMinAlleleFraction(fraction: number) => void`
- `setShowPileup(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowMismatches(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowSoftClips(value: boolean) => void`
- `setShowConnectors(flag: boolean) => void`: A main-thread tier-2/4 setting, not in `rpcProps`: toggling never refetches.
- `setMismatchOpacityField(field?: "baseQuality" | undefined) => void`: Writes `field` alone, so a written domain and range survive the fade being turned off and on.
- `setShowSashimi(show: boolean) => void`: Writes `sashimi.show` alone. Without the coverage band the arcs draw in a separate strip (`effectiveSashimiPlacement`).
- `setSashimiPlacement(placement: "auto" | "down" | "up") => void`
- `setShowSashimiLabels(show: boolean) => void`
- `setJunctionFilter(patch: JunctionFilterPatch) => void`
- `setDrawnReadConnections(mode: ReadConnectionsMode) => void`: What the "Read arcs" and "Read cloud" checkboxes write: 'off' hides the band and keeps its mark for the way back.
- `setReadConnectionsPlacement(placement: "down" | "up") => void`
- `setReadConnectionsStrokeWidth(width?: number | undefined) => void`: Stroke a one-read connection `width` px, keeping the written field, scale type and range ratio, or a constant width; undefined returns to the default 1 px.
- `setReadConnectionsColorField(field?: "insertSize" | "insertSizeAndOrientation" | "pairOrientation" | undefined) => void`: Paint the connections by `field`; unset follows the reads.
- `setShowOrdinaryPairs(show?: boolean | undefined) => void`
- `setConnectionFilter(patch: Partial<ConnectionFilter>) => void`
- `toggleGroupCollapsed(key: string) => void`: Collapse/expand a stacked group's pileup (coverage stays visible).
- `dropGroupState() => void`: The mixin's hook: the collapses and per-group height overrides, both of which use group keys.
- `clearMouseoverState() => void`
- `clearHoverUnlessPinned() => void`: What a cursor leaving a read or connector calls. `setHoverState` refuses writes while the right-click menu pins the hover, so the leave refuses them too. `clearMouseoverState` is the unconditional form, for `closeContextMenu`.
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setRpcData(displayedRegionIndex: number, data: GroupedAlignmentsResult, region: Region) => void`: Stage a region as fetched, with this display's payload shape — so a test stands up a loaded display in one call. Production goes through `ctx.commitRegion`.
- `clearSelection() => void`
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: The picker Color by's Solid color... opens, on the theme's plain read fill until a constant is written.
- `setBases({ show, field, unmodified, filter }: BasesPatch) => void`: Writes the `pileup.bases` members the patch names, as one action so a layer and its filter refetch once. The read fill is `colorByField`'s and stays as it is.
- `sortAtCenterLine(field: ColumnSortField) => void`
- `setSort(sort: SortSetting) => void`: The one writer of `sort`: a whole-window order, or a column sort.
- `setCollapseSections(flag: boolean) => void`: Draw each group as one row, overlap depth shown as tint. Clears the per-group height overrides: an override opts a lane out of the collapse, which means nothing once every lane is a stack again.
- `toggleGroupExpanded(key: string) => void`: Lift a group's cap to `pileup.maxLayoutHeight` without padding its band, or, if a drag or an earlier expand already sized it, return the group to the fit budget. Expanding overflows the viewport, which engages the pileup scroll.
- `resizeGroupHeight(key: string, dy: number) => void`: Drag a stacked group's pileup band taller/shorter by `dy` px. The override caps the group's rows and pads the band where the rows fall short, so the drag runs in both directions. The accumulation policy is in the pure…
- `setMarkHeight(height?: number | undefined) => void`: Set the per-read pixel size. Grow keeps growing at the new size. Fit derives the size, so a chosen size would be dormant: picking one drops back to fixed.
- `setPileupMaxLayoutHeight(height?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeightMode(mode: "fit" | "fixed" | "grow") => void`: The two pieces of transient state a uniform fit/grow contradicts that HeightModeMixin can't know about. The slot write and the scroll reset are its `setHeightMode`, captured as super above.
- `setFittedHeightPx(px: number) => void`: Caches the fitted read height; `featureHeight`/`featureSpacing` split it into a body and a derived gap. Written only by the driving autorun.
- `setCoverageHeight(height: number) => void`
- `setReadConnectionsHeight(height: number) => void`
- `setSashimiHeight(height: number) => void`
- `setUnit(unit: "chain" | "read") => void`: A new unit restacks the whole pileup, so the scroll resets: the `scrollableHeight` clamp catches only a shorter stack.
- `setHoverState(state: { overCigarItem: boolean; featureIdUnderMouse: string | undefined; mouseoverExtraInformation: TooltipPayload | undefined; hoverCoverageBand?: HoverCove…`: The whole hover state in one action, so no branch of the mousemove handler leaves a field stale. Refused while the right-click menu is open, since `openContextMenu` pins the hover to the read the menu acts on. `highlightedChainReadIds` is…
- `setContextMenuFeature(feature?: Feature | undefined) => void`
- `closeContextMenu() => void`: Close the right-click menu and release the hover it pinned. `setHoverState` refuses writes while the menu is up, so this is the only place the pin comes off.
- `selectFeature(feature: Feature) => void`
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: AlignmentsRenderingBackend) => void`
- `withFeatureById(featureId: string, onFeat: (feat: Feature) => void) => Promise<void>`: Fetch the feature behind `featureId` and hand it to `onFeat`. For a menu item that needs the whole feature but is offered before one is in hand.
- `selectFeatureById(featureId: string) => Promise<void>`
- `openContextMenu(info: AlignmentsContextMenuInfo) => void`: Open the right-click menu over a hit. The block, the clicked column and the mark hit arrive as one `ContextMenuHit`, so a consumer cannot read a block without its hit. Resets the read feature and, when the hit has one, fills it by async…
- `renderSvg(opts?: ExportSvgDisplayOptions | undefined) => Promise<ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | AwaitedReactNode>`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Fills `BaseDisplay`'s hover-clear hook, which the fetch foundation's reaction calls on every viewport change. A pan, zoom or internal scroll under a stationary cursor fires no mousemove or mouseleave, so the highlight and tooltip would…
- `hideGroup(key: string) => void`: Drop a section from the stack. Reversed by `showAllGroups`, which the "Show" menu offers while anything is hidden, since a hidden section has no chip to restore it.
- `showAllGroups() => void`
- `facetByField(field: string) => void`: Split the sections by `field`, `''` for none, keeping the order and hidden sections while it is the field already grouping.
- `setFacetSort(sort: readonly string[]) => void`: The order the sections take, the ones it names first; `[]` sorts them all.
- `colorByField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Paint by `field`, keeping its domain, range and key names while it is the field already painting or the one parked; undefined paints `value` and parks the field.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every feature `value`, a CSS color or a `jexl:` callback, parking the field; undefined lets each feature's own color paint.
- `pickDefaultColor() => void`: Color by's Default: no field and no constant, so the track's own color paints, a `jexl:` expression included.
- `pickSolidColor() => void`: Color by's Solid color...: paints the constant kept beside a painting field, where there is one, and opens the display's picker.
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it.
- `dismissLegendSection(id: string) => void`: Close one section of the legend, leaving the others up.
- `setScaleType(scaleType: string) => void`
- `setScaleZero(zero: boolean) => void`
- `setFenceQuantile(quantile: number) => void`
- `setDomainMin(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setDomainMax(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setMinScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMin`.
- `setMaxScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMax`.
- `setAutoscaleGroup(group?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setScoreRules(rules: (number | ValueScaleRule)[]) => void`: Replaces the y scale's rules whole, each entry in a form the config takes: a number, or `{ value, color, label }`.
- `resetYScale() => void`: Back to what the config.json says, or to what a session-owned track was added with, so an admin's declared axis survives a reset; slots the base leaves unset take their defaults.
- `setLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number, region: Region, payload: {} | undefined, fetchInputs?: FetchInputs) => void`: The raw write behind `ctx.commitRegion`, and **not what a fetch should call**. A display naming its span itself is the bug this family spent a release fixing, and the context gives a fetch no way to express it — see RegionFetchContext.…
- `evictRegionStore(keep: ReadonlySet<number>) => void`: The store's bound. Drops the entries a fetch can no longer be about: an index outside the view's buffered viewport, once the store is over `MAX_STORED_REGIONS`, oldest first.
- `dropLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`: Forget one region, as `evictRegionStore` does past its cap. Tests use it to stage an evicted region.
- `clearDisplaySpecificData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds beside the store — a second store, a verdict about the viewport that was just dropped. Called by `clearAllRpcData`, which runs on a displayed-regions change, on a viewport move…
- `clearSettingsBakedData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds that is wrong under a changed setting rather than merely stale — a payload whose shape the setting decides. Called by `invalidateSettings`, where `clearDisplaySpecificData` is…
- `clearAllRpcData() => void`: full reset: cancels fetch, clears error, loadedRegions, display-specific data, and the canvas-drawn flag. The too-large gate is derived (a pure function of the cached estimate × viewport), so it needs no explicit clear here — the fetch…
- `invalidateSettings() => void`: `SettingsInvalidate`'s reset: the half of `clearAllRpcData` a settings change still needs now that the settings and adapter axes are in `fetchInputs`. The in-flight fetch is superseded now rather than when its payload lands stamped stale,…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter) plus the full reset. Subclasses with extra teardown override and chain.
- `fetchRegions(needed: IndexedRegion[], work: (ctx: RegionFetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a per-region fetch. The work callback calls `ctx.commitRegion` as it stores each region's payload, which is what marks it loaded — see RegionFetchContext for why this function no longer does that itself. Only the three helpers in…
- `afterAttach() => void`: installs the fetch-lifecycle autoruns (DisplayedRegionsChange, FetchVisibleRegions, SettingsInvalidate, ClearBlockingStateOnViewportChange)
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.
- `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what the other axis measured, on the trigger that invalidates this one, so re-pointing an adapter never leaves `densityTooLarge` reporting on the previous file.
- `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing.
- `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch.
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`: Drag-resize. A manual drag means the user wants a fixed height, so leave grow first — otherwise the reactive `height` getter re-derives `grownHeight` on the next relayout and the drag appears to do nothing. The displayed (grown) height is…
- `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void`
- `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number`
- `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first.
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…
- `applyPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => void`: Write a draft over `plot` as a settings bag writes: a setting left out stays, `null` resets one, a channel (`writes: 'whole'`, such as `color` or `facet`) is replaced whole, and any other object takes the members the draft names, so a…

## Getters
- `resolution: LodMode`: the level-of-detail tier the reader pinned, or 'auto' for the adapter's own bpPerPx threshold. `lodTier` is what resolves it
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: synteny features open the SyntenyFeatureWidget; the inherited `selectFeature` action reads this getter, so no override is needed.
- `featureNoun: string`: A row here is a PAF block, not a read — the group-label chips say "Show all features". The ONE place that word is chosen: the two menu builders below that take a `noun` read it from here rather than spelling it again, so the chips and the…
- `selfLaneKeys: string[]`: The mate-assembly keys of the lane an all-vs-all track draws for the view's own assembly: the view's name, and every name the track declares for the same assembly, since the adapter keys a lane by the track's spelling.
- `selfLaneHidden: boolean`: Whether `facet.hidden` holds the self lane, the "Hide self-alignment lane" box.
- `hasLodCapableAdapter: boolean`: Whether this track's adapter has tiered storage to switch between — gates the "Level of detail" menu.
- `lodTier: LodTier`: The tier this display's fetch asks for: the alignments base's hook, resolved here on the main thread off the SETTLED zoom. It is the base's `zoomFetchArgs` term and rides the RPC at the call site, so a tier flip refetches the regions on…
- `liveLodTier: LodTier`: The same tier off the live zoom, for the base's `dataSuperseded`.
- `adapterHeader: unknown`: The header of the adapter config the display holds, undefined until its read lands.
- `lodTierInfo: LodTierInfo | undefined`: The file's tiers, undefined until the header lands, which the resolver treats as "trust the config slot".
- `unit: "chain" | "read"`
- `showCoverage: boolean`
- `coverageHeight: number`
- `showInterbase: boolean`
- `showCoverageAlleles: boolean`: Whether the coverage band colors its allele segments, `coverage.alleles.show`
- `coverageMinAlleleFraction: number`
- `interbaseIndicatorRule: InterbaseIndicatorRule`: `coverage.interbase.filter` as the worker's triangle rule.
- `showPileup: boolean`
- `markHeight: number`: `pileup.mark.height` as configured, independent of the fit squeeze. Consumers that EDIT the size (the "Custom..." height dialog) must start from it, not the fractional fit pitch `featureHeight` resolves to in fit mode, or opening the…
- `pileupMaxLayoutHeight: number`
- `showMismatches: boolean`
- `showSoftClips: boolean`
- `showConnectors: boolean`
- `mismatchOpacityField: "baseQuality" | undefined`: The field `pileup.mismatches.encoding.opacity` fades by, unset for none: the "Fade low-quality mismatches" checkbox.
- `mismatchQualityOpacity: QualityOpacity`: `pileup.mismatches.encoding.opacity` as mismatch.slang's `qualityFade` reads it.
- `fadeLowFrequency: boolean`
- `hasSashimi: boolean`: Whether the display declares the sashimi band, which a synteny block, having no introns, has no use for.
- `showSashimi: boolean`

- `perBaseBinBp: number`: Genomic bp one per-base cell stands for in the worker's extract: the foundation's `settledSubPixelBinBp`, and `1` in every color mode that does not paint a wall of them. Per-base quality and lettering emit an entry per aligned base of…
- `livePerBaseBinBp: number`: The same bin off the LIVE zoom, read by `dataSuperseded` alone. The debounced bin is the one the held data was fetched under, so it cannot show whether that data is sampled finely enough. Kept out of `zoomFetchArgs` because…
- `hoveredFeature: SimpleFeature | undefined`
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`'s supersession hook: the settled per-base bin or detail tier has not moved yet, but the live zoom has left it, so the clear is inevitable and not yet committed. Only the debounce half is here: once the settled bin…
- `ownGroupState: (string[] | { [k: string]: GroupSize; })[]`: The mixin's hook: the collapses and per-group height overrides `dropGroupState` clears below.
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: Opt into RegionTooLargeMixin's byte gate: `fetchNeeded` passes `resolvedByteLimit()` to `RenderAlignmentData`, whose first await is the index estimate, so an over-budget region is refused before a read downloads.
- `hiddenGroups: ReadonlySet<string>`: The sections the user hid: `facet.hidden`, while the stack groups by the facet's field.
- `hiddenGroupKeys: ReadonlySet<string>`: Every key the stack drops. A fresh Set per change, so a layout memo comparing its inputs by identity sees a hide.
- `groupStateKey: unknown`: All the per-group state as a plain, comparable value: the hidden sections, sorted, beside `ownGroupState`. A live figure keys on it, since a display's own state is volatile and in no snapshot; a Set would serialize as `{}`.
- `writtenFacet: WrittenFacet`: The `facet` object as written.
- `writtenColor: ColorSlots`: The `encoding.color` channel as these writes and an Apply button read it, `writtenColorOf`.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field
- `showLegend: boolean`: Whether the legend is drawn.
- `legendRight: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px the on-screen key is pushed left from the key's inset, for a display that draws a column of text down its right edge — the multi-way lanes' scales. Not read by the export.
- `legendTop: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px the on-screen key is pushed down from the key's inset, for a display whose top rows hold the data a reader reads the rest against — the multi-way anchor lane. Not read by the export.
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: The key, derived from `colorScales` less the sections the reader dismissed. `DisplayChrome` renders it on screen and `renderDisplaySvg` flattens it for the export, so the two describe one set of colors.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the display has a key at all. The "Legend" row is offered only when it does. Overridable for a display whose key is only waiting for data: a scale that stays empty until a region lands must not remove the toggle in the meantime.
- `scaleType: string`
- `scaleZero: boolean`: The y scale's `zero`: whether an autoscaled linear or symlog axis reaches 0.
- `fenceQuantile: number`: The y scale's fence quantile: what an unpinned end follows, 1 the extremes and below it that quantile of each sign.
- `clipFenceQuantile: number`: The quantile "Clip extreme outliers" fences at: the one an untick this session wrote over, else the scale's own default where that is below 1, else 0.99.
- `symlogConstant: number`: Raw slot; `0` means "derive from the domain". Resolve it with `resolveSymlogConstant` once the domain is known.
- `domainMin: number | undefined`: The lower bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `domainMax: number | undefined`: The upper bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `autoscaleGroup: string | undefined`: The y scale's autoscale group, `undefined` while it names none.
- `scaleTitle: string`: The y axis title, `''` while unset
- `grid: boolean`: The y axis grid
- `scoreRules: ValueScaleRule[]`: The y scale's rules, read off the live nodes.
- `axisReachesZero: boolean`: Overridable: whether the autoscaled domain reaches 0, `scaleZero` unless the display maps its score to something with no axis.
- `autoscaledDomain: [number, number] | undefined`: The domain an autoscaled axis draws: `autoscaleRange`, widened to every range its `autoscaleGroup` holds, nice-rounded inside this display's own bounds. Each member unions the others' own ranges and never their domains, so a pinned end…
- `resolvedDomainMin: number | undefined`: Resolved lower bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `resolvedDomainMax: number | undefined`: Resolved upper bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `pinsDomain: boolean`: Whether the user has pinned either end, which is a different question from whether either end resolved to a number: `defaultScoreDomain` fills the unset ends in, so a GC content track answers yes to the second with nothing configured. The…
- `axes: YAxis[]`: The axes, one per declared scale whose domain resolved: the position of each tick in the band's pixel space, through `computeYTicks` unless the scale supplies its own ladder, and the position of each of the scale's `rules` inside the…
- `host: RegionHost`: The containing LinearGenomeView, typed once for every display in this family — see `containingHost` for the cast it owns and why both foundations still declare the name.
- `canvasWidthPx: number`: The CSS width of this display's on-screen canvas, in px; see `trackCanvasWidthPx`.
- `settledSubPixelBinBp: number`: Genomic bp one cell of a per-base pass stands for at the settled zoom: `subPixelBinBp` off the host's debounced `coarseBpPerPx`, and 1 until the view initializes. A per-base encode or fetch reads this rather than the live zoom so a wheel…
- `canRender: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook with the LGV precondition both foundations share — see `foundationCanRender`.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook off `fetchInert`, as `GlobalFetchMixin` does: a display that will never fetch here shows a placeholder where its canvas would be.
- `trackVisibleRegions: VisibleRegion[]`: The visible blocks on the track's own assemblies, the ones this display fetches and is judged against. A view of several genomes leaves a single-genome track's other regions blank.
- `viewportWithinLoadedData: boolean`: true when every visible block lies within an already-fetched region — i.e. the viewport shows data we actually loaded, not the stale fringe left after a zoom-out/pan. Drives the loading overlay through the pre-refetch debounce.
- `viewportEmpty: boolean`: No content block is on screen, so this display has nothing to fetch and nothing to paint — see `viewportEmpty.ts` for the one viewport that reaches it, how narrow that is, and why the state still has to be terminal rather than a permanent…
- `fetchSuspended: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by the fetch plan: the display is drawing something in the features' place and wants no fetch while it does. `CoarseTierMixin` returns true while its tier stands in, so MAF never downloads the…
- `renderBlocks: RenderBlock[]`: Shared cached view for every LGV-based GPU display. A single displayedRegion may produce multiple render blocks (shared GPU buffer, different scissor clips on screen). Plugins that want to suppress rendering in certain states (e.g. no…
- `fetchInputs: FetchInputs`: What a fetch issued right now would stamp on a region: the settings tier (`FetchMixin.settingsFetchInputs`, the tier `staleSettingsDrawn` compares alone) and the zoom tier (the display's `zoomFetchArgs()` object). `fetchRegions` captures…
- `regionPayloads: ReadonlyMap<number, unknown>`: The store's payloads, keyed by `displayedRegionIndex`. A display narrows this once — `get rpcDataMap() { return self.regionPayloads as ReadonlyMap<number, MyResult> }` — and every reader it already had goes on reading a map.
- `hasRegionData: boolean`: A fetch has landed: at least one region's payload is in the store. The render callback's first-paint gate reads this, so an empty frame before any data cannot flip `canvasDrawn`; an empty but loaded region counts, and paints its empty…

- `dataCurrent: boolean`: This family's answer to the shared freshness question every display foundation must answer (`dataCurrent`): the held data corresponds to what is on screen right now. Four terms — spatial coverage of every visible block,…
- `loadedAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly the data in hand came from, once it can answer about refNames — `undefined` before that.
- `phaseViewportCurrent: boolean`: The loading scrim's staleness argument: what is drawn answers for what is on screen. Spatial coverage, `dataSuperseded` and `staleSettingsDrawn`; not `isCacheValid`, which belongs to `dataCurrent` and would scrim every zoom. `displayPhase`…
- `svgReady: boolean`: true once an off-screen (SVG) export can safely read this display's data. Policy single-sourced in `computeSvgReady`; this family supplies only the freshness half, which `foundationSvgReady` reads as `dataCurrent` or the vacuous currency…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook with `staleSettingsDrawn`, so `painted` — and `data-display-drawn` through it — reads pending over a canvas painted under the previous settings until the refetch lands, without blanking anything.
- `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The display's mutually-exclusive visual state, mapped in `foundationDisplayPhase` — every foundation calls it and supplies only its staleness argument, so a term added to `computeActivityPhase` reaches all three without being wired three…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by `computeActivityPhase` and `foundationSvgReady`: a load this display depends on beyond its primary fetch has not landed for the first time, so the frame the primary fetch calls current is still…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.

- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.

- `growMaxHeight: number`: Ceiling `grow` mode sizes the track to, in px (content past it scrolls). Lives here rather than as a constant so a track whose whole point is a deep pileup can raise it; both displays that own a `grownHeight` read this, so the two can't…

- `fitHeightToDisplay: boolean`: `fit` mode as a boolean, derived from the unified `heightMode` slot.
- `grownHeight: number`: Target track height for `grow`: what the content wants, capped so a deep stack doesn't grow the track to thousands of px (the remainder scrolls). What `installGrowExitBake` bakes into the slot on exit.
- `height: number`: In grow mode the track height follows the laid-out content reactively — no autorun writes the height config slot, so a settled relayout never churns the persisted session nor bakes a momentary height. Fixed/fit read the slot (fit shrinks…
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.

- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.

LinearAlignmentsDisplay.text:
# LinearAlignmentsDisplay (Display model, alignments plugin)

State model factory for LinearAlignmentsDisplay

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearAlignmentsDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes HiddenGroupsMixin, ContextMenuMixin, FacetWritesMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, HeightModeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

The display goes in a track's `displays` array; here are three complete
`AlignmentsTrack` configs to paste into `tracks`.

Basic BAM, opened taller:
```js
{
  type: 'AlignmentsTrack',
  trackId: 'ngs_reads',
  name: 'NGS reads',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'BamAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/sample.bam' },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
      displayId: 'ngs_reads-LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
      height: 250,
    },
  ],
}
```

CRAM colored by CpG methylation (modBAM MM/ML tags):
```js
{
  type: 'AlignmentsTrack',
  trackId: 'methylation',
  name: 'Methylation',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'CramAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/sample.cram' },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
      displayId: 'methylation-LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
      pileup: {
        bases: {
          show: true,
          encoding: { color: 'modifications' },
          unmodified: { show: true },
        },
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

Long reads with split/mate reads connected by arcs:
```js
{
  type: 'AlignmentsTrack',
  trackId: 'long_reads',
  name: 'Long reads',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'BamAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/longreads.bam' },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
      displayId: 'long_reads-LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
      height: 400,
      unit: 'chain',
      readConnections: { show: true },
    },
  ],
}
```

## Actions
- `setFilterFields(patch: Readonly<Record<string, readonly FieldPredicate[] | undefined>>) => void`: Replaces the entries on each field the patch names, `undefined` returning a field to its defaults; every other field keeps what was written.
- `setShowCoverage(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowInterbase(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowCoverageAlleles(show: boolean) => void`: Turns the coverage band's allele colors on or off, `coverage.alleles.show`
- `setCoverageMinAlleleFraction(fraction: number) => void`
- `setShowPileup(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowMismatches(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowSoftClips(value: boolean) => void`
- `setShowConnectors(flag: boolean) => void`: A main-thread tier-2/4 setting, not in `rpcProps`: toggling never refetches.
- `setMismatchOpacityField(field?: "baseQuality" | undefined) => void`: Writes `field` alone, so a written domain and range survive the fade being turned off and on.
- `setShowSashimi(show: boolean) => void`: Writes `sashimi.show` alone. Without the coverage band the arcs draw in a separate strip (`effectiveSashimiPlacement`).
- `setSashimiPlacement(placement: "auto" | "down" | "up") => void`
- `setShowSashimiLabels(show: boolean) => void`
- `setJunctionFilter(patch: JunctionFilterPatch) => void`

- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.

- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.

- `fitTargetHeight: number`: The height the track is allotted (`TrackHeightMixin.allottedHeight`: the slot's, or a ring's band) — the fit target the fit/grow layout scales or packs content into. Read there instead of the reactive `height` getter to break the grow-mode…
- `growMaxHeight: number`: Ceiling `grow` mode sizes the track to, in px (content past it scrolls). Lives here rather than as a constant so a track whose whole point is a deep pileup can raise it; both displays that own a `grownHeight` read this, so the two can't…
- `autoHeight: boolean`: `grow` mode as a boolean, derived from the unified `heightMode` slot.
- `fitHeightToDisplay: boolean`: `fit` mode as a boolean, derived from the unified `heightMode` slot.
- `grownHeight: number`: Target track height for `grow`: what the content wants, capped so a deep stack doesn't grow the track to thousands of px (the remainder scrolls). What `installGrowExitBake` bakes into the slot on exit.
- `height: number`: In grow mode the track height follows the laid-out content reactively — no autorun writes the height config slot, so a settled relayout never churns the persisted session nor bakes a momentary height. Fixed/fit read the slot (fit shrinks…
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

LinearBasicDisplay.text:
# LinearBasicDisplay (Display model, features plugin)

GPU-accelerated feature display with gene-specific UI on top of the shared canvas base display (`LinearFeatureBaseDisplay`).

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearBasicDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes LinearFeatureBaseDisplay, HiddenGroupsMixin, ContextMenuMixin, FeatureGateMixin, FacetWritesMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, HeightModeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

A `FeatureTrack` with compact features. `displayMode` is `normal`,
`compact`, `superCompact` or `collapsed` (one row):
```js
{
  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'genes',
  name: 'Genes',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'Gff3TabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/genes.gff3.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearBasicDisplay',
      displayId: 'genes-LinearBasicDisplay',
      height: 200,
      displayMode: 'compact',
    },
  ],
}
```

## Actions

- `setGeneGlyphMode(value: "all" | "auto" | "representative") => void`

- `setShowDescriptions(show: boolean) => void`

- `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it.

- `setLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number, region: Region, payload: {} | undefined, fetchInputs?: FetchInputs) => void`: The raw write behind `ctx.commitRegion`, and **not what a fetch should call**. A display naming its span itself is the bug this family spent a release fixing, and the context gives a fetch no way to express it — see RegionFetchContext.…
- `evictRegionStore(keep: ReadonlySet<number>) => void`: The store's bound. Drops the entries a fetch can no longer be about: an index outside the view's buffered viewport, once the store is over `MAX_STORED_REGIONS`, oldest first.
- `dropLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`: Forget one region, as `evictRegionStore` does past its cap. Tests use it to stage an evicted region.
- `clearDisplaySpecificData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds beside the store — a second store, a verdict about the viewport that was just dropped. Called by `clearAllRpcData`, which runs on a displayed-regions change, on a viewport move…
- `clearSettingsBakedData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds that is wrong under a changed setting rather than merely stale — a payload whose shape the setting decides. Called by `invalidateSettings`, where `clearDisplaySpecificData` is…
- `clearAllRpcData() => void`: full reset: cancels fetch, clears error, loadedRegions, display-specific data, and the canvas-drawn flag. The too-large gate is derived (a pure function of the cached estimate × viewport), so it needs no explicit clear here — the fetch…

- `fetchRegions(needed: IndexedRegion[], work: (ctx: RegionFetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a per-region fetch. The work callback calls `ctx.commitRegion` as it stores each region's payload, which is what marks it loaded — see RegionFetchContext for why this function no longer does that itself. Only the three helpers in…
- `afterAttach() => void`: installs the fetch-lifecycle autoruns (DisplayedRegionsChange, FetchVisibleRegions, SettingsInvalidate, ClearBlockingStateOnViewportChange)
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.
- `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing.
- `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch.
- `setHeightMode(mode: "fit" | "fixed" | "grow") => void`: Set the track-height strategy by writing the unified `heightMode` slot; the modes are mutually exclusive by construction. Leaving grow bakes the grown height into the `height` slot in the same action, so the switch is atomic:…
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`: Drag-resize. A manual drag means the user wants a fixed height, so leave grow first — otherwise the reactive `height` getter re-derives `grownHeight` on the next relayout and the drag appears to do nothing. The displayed (grown) height is…
- `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void`
- `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number`
- `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first.
