- `grownHeight: number`: Target track height for `grow`: what the content wants, capped so a deep stack doesn't grow the track to thousands of px (the remainder scrolls). What `installGrowExitBake` bakes into the slot on exit.
- `height: number`: In grow mode the track height follows the laid-out content reactively — no autorun writes the height config slot, so a settled relayout never churns the persisted session nor bakes a momentary height. Fixed/fit read the slot (fit shrinks…
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the singular word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants".
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

## Properties
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `pinnedFeatureIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: Feature ids the user pinned to the top of the layout via the feature right-click menu.
- `soloFeatureIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: "Show only these features": the collected set the user builds by ctrl+clicking features (or via the right-click menu).
- `soloApplied = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: Whether the collected soloFeatureIds set is actually isolating the view (worker drops non-members).
- `hiddenFeatureIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: "Hide this feature" exclusion set (inverse of solo): the worker drops these from layout/drawing.
- `expandedGeneIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: Genes the user opened from the isoform badge on the gene's label: these draw every isoform whatever `geneGlyphMode` or the fit ladder's isoform rung would otherwise collapse them to.
- `featureHighlights = types.stripDefault( types.array(FeatureHighlightModel), [], )`: Declarative feature highlights, typically seeded by a text search (highlight the gene you searched for).
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.string`

## Methods
- `filterSubMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `showSubmenuCheckboxItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `showSubmenuRadioGroups() => MenuItem[]`
- `trackMenuItems() => (MenuDivider | MenuSubHeader | NormalMenuItem | CheckboxMenuItem | RadioMenuItem | SubMenuItem | CustomMenuItem | { label: string; icon: OverridableCompo…`
- `contextMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `configuredFilters() => string[]`: The `jexl:` expressions the `filter` list holds.
- `baseFilters() => string[]`: The expressions the track's config declares, which "Clear all filters" returns to.
- `rampColorScales(id: string) => ColorScale[]`: The key a ramp paints, under the caller's scale `id`: the bar over its domain, and a row apiece for the values the ramp has no color for. Both displays composing this built it from the same three getters, so the derivation is here rather…
- `rpcProps() => { displayConfig: { facetField?: string | undefined; color: {…}; subfeatureLabels: "auto" | "below" | "none" | "overlay"; filter: FieldPredicate[]; labels…`
- `gpuProps() => { colorTable: Uint32Array<ArrayBuffer>; fieldPalette: { field: string; paint: (value: string) => string; tableOf(values: readonly string[], withTints: bo…`: What the main-thread encode needs beyond a region's own data: the packed color for every theme class the worker emitted, off `session.palette`, and the color field's scale, so a theme toggle or a recolor re-encodes what is loaded instead…
- `fitLayoutAt(memo: IncrementalLayout, reserved: LabelReservation) => Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: One fit-escalation candidate: the stack packed with the given label reservation, via that config's own memo instance so each keeps stable references across renders.
- `decimatedLayoutInputs(factors: LabelRoomFactors) => LayoutInputs`: Layout inputs for the `decimated` rung at one pair of whitespace factors.
- `solveLabelRoomFactors(trackHeight: number) => LabelRoomFactors | undefined`: The whitespace factors the `decimated` rung commits at: gene names first, then the rest, each the smallest whose packed stack fits `trackHeight` (smallest = most names kept), or undefined when even the most aggressive decimation overflows.
- `bodyScaleHeightProbe(cache: PackHeightCache, inputs: LabelRoomFactorFreeInputs, factors?: LabelRoomFactors | undefined) => (bodyScale: number) => number`: Measures a labelled stack's height at any body scale. Each scale needs a separate prep, since the pack reads body heights from it.
- `floatingLabels(palette: JBrowsePalette) => FloatingLabel[]`: The labels the floating label layer draws over the canvas, as records in the display's own px, for a host that shows the canvas but not this display's DOM: a ring of the circular view. The isoform badge is a control, not a label, and stays…
- `searchFeatureByID(id: string) => readonly [number, number, number, number] | undefined`
- `renderSvg(opts?: ExportSvgDisplayOptions | undefined) => Promise<ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | AwaitedReactNode>`
- `featureNarrowings() => Reversibles`: Everything this display is doing to narrow what the user sees, each declared once, so the "Filter by (n)" count, its undo rows and "Clear all filters" cannot disagree; a method, not a getter, because a getter cannot be super-captured.
- `featureMarks() => Reversibles`: Reversible state that MARKS features rather than hiding them — the highlight boxes and the pins holding features at the top of the layout.
- `zoomFetchArgs() => { geneGlyphMode: "all" | "auto" | "representative"; peptides: boolean; expandedGeneIds: IMSTArray<ISimpleType<string>> | undefined; }`: The worker's zoom-dependent decisions, resolved: the RPC spreads this object and the foundation stamps it beside each region, so a track with the overlay off and a fixed mode never refetches on zoom. `expandedGeneIds` only under…
- `groupByPlot(field: string | undefined, colorByGroup: boolean) => Plot`: The Group by dialog's choice of field as plot settings, which its Apply writes and its Edit plot button shows: the facet, keeping its domain while the field is the one already set; a color by the field when ticked, left alone while it…
- `scanGroupByCandidates(opts: GroupByScanOptions) => Promise<RegionTooLargeResult | GroupByCandidate[]>`: The attributes the features in view have and the sections each would make, for the Group by dialog: the render fetch's download over the visible blocks, under the same admission and byte budget.
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The schema's rules, then a `jexl:` color or filter that does not compile.
- `showSubmenuMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Flattened "Show" submenu: all checkbox toggles first, then the radio groups (each under a subHeader), then the legend.
- `colorBySubMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: The "Color by" radio choices (solid/strand/attribute).
- `colorMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Color-related track menu entries: a single "Color by" entry whose radios pick the track's own color or a field, and whose "Solid color..." item opens the solid+UTR color picker.
- `featureHeightMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: One "Feature height" menu with two independent radio groups: the size presets and, under a "Track sizing" subheader, how the track responds when there are more features than fit.
- `observedMaxDensity(bpPerPx: number) => number`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `regionHasData(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the display can draw what this region is marked loaded over, at the zoom the view has.
- `isCacheValid(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Whether the data held for a region still answers the current view. Not a hook a display fills: a display states its rule as `zoomFetchArgs` (what a fetch now would send the worker) and `regionHasData` (does what the last one stored still…
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

LinearFeatureBaseDisplay.text:
# LinearFeatureBaseDisplay (Display model, features plugin)

Shared GPU-accelerated feature display base for canvas-rendered tracks.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearFeatureBaseDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes HiddenGroupsMixin, ContextMenuMixin, FeatureGateMixin, FacetWritesMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, HeightModeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `beginYMorph(fromTops: Map<string, number>, fromMaxY: number) => void`
- `setMorphProgress(t: number) => void`
- `advanceAnimation(nowMs: number) => void`: the chrome's frame clock
- `endAnimation() => void`
- `setRpcData(displayedRegionIndex: number, data: FeatureDataResult, region: Region) => void`: Stage a region as fetched — the store's raw write with this display's payload shape, so a test stands up a loaded display in one call.
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: FeatureRenderingBackend) => void`
- `togglePinnedFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `clearPinnedFeatures() => void`
- `toggleExpandedGene(featureId: string) => void`: Open or re-collapse one gene's isoforms, from the badge on the gene's label.
- `clearExpandedGenes() => void`: Re-collapse every gene opened from a badge.
- `toggleSoloFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `applySolo() => void`
- `soloFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `clearSolo() => void`
- `hideFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `showAllHidden() => void`
- `setHover(featureId: string | undefined, subfeatureId: string | undefined, tooltip: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `clearHover() => void`
- `setFeatureHighlights(highlights: FeatureHighlight[]) => void`
- `setSearchHighlight(highlight: FeatureHighlight) => void`: A text search's highlight replaces the previous search's and leaves the right-click ones, which have a `featureId`, alone.
- `addFeatureHighlightForItem(target: HighlightTarget, refName: string) => void`
- `removeFeatureHighlightsForId(featureId: string) => void`
- `clearFeatureHighlights() => void`
- `openContextMenu(info: FeatureContextMenuInfo) => void`: Drops the hover first, so its tooltip does not sit under the menu; the highlight box stays on the target through `hoverBoxFeature`.
- `openFeatureDetails(fetch: () => Promise<Feature | undefined>, parentFeature?: ParentFeatureSummary | undefined) => void`: Open the feature-details widget on what `fetch` resolves to, with the adapter's header metadata beside it; a lookup that resolves to nothing is reported as a miss.
- `selectFeature(feature: Feature) => void`: Open the feature-details widget on a feature already in hand.
- `clearSelection() => void`
- `setShowNames(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowDescriptions(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowLabels(value: "auto" | "description" | "name" | "nameAndDescription" | "none") => void`: The five-value label mode, written as `setShowNames` and `setShowDescriptions`.
- `setFilter(filters?: string[] | undefined) => void`: Write the `filter` list's expressions, its other entries kept; undefined returns them to what the track's config declares.
- `setSequenceHoverPosition(pos: SequenceHoverPosition | undefined) => void`
- `openFilterDialog() => void`
- `setDisplayMode(value: "collapsed" | "compact" | "normal" | "superCompact") => void`
- `dropGroupState() => void`: The stack starts over from the top when its sections change.
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: the picker Color by's Solid color... opens
- `fetchFullFeature(featureId: string, displayedRegionIndex: number, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal; statusCallback?: StatusCallback; }) => Promise<SimpleFeature | undefined>`
- `selectFeatureById(featureId: string, subfeatureInfo: SubfeatureInfo | undefined, displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`
- `reload() => void`: Clears the loaded regions and fetches straight away, rather than waiting out `FetchVisibleRegions`' 600ms debounce as the rest of the family does — Retry and Force load are both clicks, and this is the display the user is most often…
- `fetchNeeded(needed: IndexedRegion[]) => void`
- `openPlotDialog(seed?: Plot | undefined) => void`: "Edit plot...", seeded with a draft a dialog has not applied.
- `applyGroupBy(field: string | undefined, colorByGroup: boolean) => void`: What the Group by dialog applies: `groupByPlot`, the draft its Edit plot button shows.
- `openColorByAttributeDialog() => void`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Fills `BaseDisplay`'s hover-clear hook, which the fetch foundation's reaction calls on every viewport change.
- `openGroupByDialog() => void`
- `hideGroup(key: string) => void`: Drop a section from the stack. Reversed by `showAllGroups`, which the "Show" menu offers while anything is hidden, since a hidden section has no chip to restore it.
- `showAllGroups() => void`
- `closeContextMenu() => void`
- `setDensityStats(displayedRegionIndex: number, stats: RegionDensityStats) => void`
- `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: `RegionTooLargeMixin`'s hook: the density axis drops its counts on the trigger that drops the byte estimate, so a gate's measurements always come from one file.
- `commitGateMeasurements(measurements: RegionGateMeasurement[], issued: GateFetchState) => void`: Judged by the tier captured at issue.
- `facetByField(field: string) => void`: Split the sections by `field`, `''` for none, keeping the order and hidden sections while it is the field already grouping.
- `setFacetSort(sort: readonly string[]) => void`: The order the sections take, the ones it names first; `[]` sorts them all.
- `colorByField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Paint by `field`, keeping its domain, range and key names while it is the field already painting or the one parked; undefined paints `value` and parks the field.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every feature `value`, a CSS color or a `jexl:` callback, parking the field; undefined lets each feature's own color paint.
- `pickDefaultColor() => void`: Color by's Default: no field and no constant, so the track's own color paints, a `jexl:` expression included.
- `pickSolidColor() => void`: Color by's Solid color...: paints the constant kept beside a painting field, where there is one, and opens the display's picker.
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it.
- `dismissLegendSection(id: string) => void`: Close one section of the legend, leaving the others up.
- `setLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number, region: Region, payload: {} | undefined, fetchInputs?: FetchInputs) => void`: The raw write behind `ctx.commitRegion`, and **not what a fetch should call**. A display naming its span itself is the bug this family spent a release fixing, and the context gives a fetch no way to express it — see RegionFetchContext.…
- `evictRegionStore(keep: ReadonlySet<number>) => void`: The store's bound. Drops the entries a fetch can no longer be about: an index outside the view's buffered viewport, once the store is over `MAX_STORED_REGIONS`, oldest first.
- `dropLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`: Forget one region, as `evictRegionStore` does past its cap. Tests use it to stage an evicted region.
- `clearDisplaySpecificData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds beside the store — a second store, a verdict about the viewport that was just dropped. Called by `clearAllRpcData`, which runs on a displayed-regions change, on a viewport move…
- `clearSettingsBakedData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds that is wrong under a changed setting rather than merely stale — a payload whose shape the setting decides. Called by `invalidateSettings`, where `clearDisplaySpecificData` is…
- `clearAllRpcData() => void`: full reset: cancels fetch, clears error, loadedRegions, display-specific data, and the canvas-drawn flag. The too-large gate is derived (a pure function of the cached estimate × viewport), so it needs no explicit clear here — the fetch…
- `invalidateSettings() => void`: `SettingsInvalidate`'s reset: the half of `clearAllRpcData` a settings change still needs now that the settings and adapter axes are in `fetchInputs`. The in-flight fetch is superseded now rather than when its payload lands stamped stale,…
- `fetchRegions(needed: IndexedRegion[], work: (ctx: RegionFetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a per-region fetch. The work callback calls `ctx.commitRegion` as it stores each region's payload, which is what marks it loaded — see RegionFetchContext for why this function no longer does that itself. Only the three helpers in…
- `afterAttach() => void`: installs the fetch-lifecycle autoruns (DisplayedRegionsChange, FetchVisibleRegions, SettingsInvalidate, ClearBlockingStateOnViewportChange)
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.
- `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing.
- `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch.
- `setHeightMode(mode: "fit" | "fixed" | "grow") => void`: Set the track-height strategy by writing the unified `heightMode` slot; the modes are mutually exclusive by construction. Leaving grow bakes the grown height into the `height` slot in the same action, so the switch is atomic:…
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`: Drag-resize. A manual drag means the user wants a fixed height, so leave grow first — otherwise the reactive `height` getter re-derives `grownHeight` on the next relayout and the drag appears to do nothing. The displayed (grown) height is…
- `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void`
- `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number`
- `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first.
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…
- `applyPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => void`: Write a draft over `plot` as a settings bag writes: a setting left out stays, `null` resets one, a channel (`writes: 'whole'`, such as `color` or `facet`) is replaced whole, and any other object takes the members the draft names, so a…

## Getters
- `rpcDataMap: ReadonlyMap<number, LoadedFeatureData>`: The fetched features, keyed by displayedRegionIndex — the foundation's per-region store, narrowed.
- `conf: LinearFeatureBaseDisplayConfig`: the config typed off the concrete schema; `ConfigurationReference` erases `self.configuration` to `any`, so direct reads route through this to stay typed (same move as `BaseAdapter<CONF>`).
- `colorSetting: ColorSetting`: The `color` object as written, its `value` and `field` raw: either may be a `jexl:` expression over a feature, which has none here.
- `workerColor: WorkerColor`: The two members the worker reads, the rest being the main thread's.
- `colorEncoding: string | FieldColorEncoding | undefined`: `colorSetting` as it paints, through the one resolver every display's color channel goes through: `encoding.color.value`, or a field through its scale, `score` a ramp and any other field ordinal while `scale.type` is unset.
- `colorField: string | undefined`: The field the color paints by, through any scale, or undefined while `encoding.color.value` paints.
- `solidColor: string | undefined`: The constant `encoding.color.value` holds, painting or kept beside a field; undefined where it holds none or a `jexl:` expression.
- `colorByMode: "attribute" | "default" | "solid" | "strand"`: The Color by radio that is ticked: a field, else a constant, else the track's own color.
- `categoricalColorField: CategoricalField | undefined`: The color channel's field while it paints through an ordinal scale, which a facet on the same field shares.
- `paintedColorField: CategoricalField | undefined`: The field the color channel paints through an ordinal or threshold scale, a threshold's values filed under their bins.
- `identityKeyEntries: { value: string; label: string; color: string; }[]`: The rows an identity scale's key names, empty under any other scale.
- `colorKeyTitle: string | undefined`: The key's heading: the channel's `legend.title`, or its field's preset's, else the field.
- `colorValueExtent: [number, number]`: The smallest and largest number the loaded regions' values of the painting field hold, which a ramp's open ends follow.
- `colorValueGaps: { missing: boolean; notNumber: boolean; }`: Whether a loaded feature has no value in the painting field, or has text that is not a number; a ramp's key lists these beside its bar.
- `colorRamp: { domain: [number, number]; lut: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; midNorm: number; colorOf: (value: number) => number; } | undefined`: The ramp a linear, log or symlog color paints through, over the loaded values where an end is left open.
- `paintColorValue: ((value: string) => string) | undefined`: The color a field value paints, while a field paints. A ramp paints a value-less feature the no-value grey, as the categorical and threshold scales do.
- `fieldPalette: FieldPalette | undefined`: `paintColorValue` with each value's packed colors held for every region and re-encode that asks, while the scale stands.
- `featureColor: string`
- `colorByAttribute: string`
- `liveNotices: string[]`: Each `filter` field no loaded feature carries.
- `geneGlyphNotice: GeneGlyphNotice | undefined`: Overridable hook (default absent): the isoform-collapse control the shared canvas body draws in its bottom-right chip stack, or nothing when the display has no gene glyphs.
- `facet: FacetSetting | undefined`: The `facet` object as written, or undefined while ungrouped.
- `hiddenGroupFeatureIds: ReadonlySet<string> | undefined`: The features of the sections the user hid, which sit unplaced by choice and so count as nothing the track failed to show.
- `layoutReady: boolean`: Whether features can be laid out: data is fetched, in-bounds, the view is measured.

- `showLabels: boolean`
- `geneNamesOnly: boolean`: Past the name threshold, with the gene features alone still under it: gene names stay and every other name goes.

- `isoformsHeightProbe: (maxIsoforms: number) => number`: Measures the `isoforms` rung's stack height at any isoform count, against the features the ladder measures its rungs with.

- `fitThinnedSolved: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: The `thinned` stack: every name at its font size over bodies shortened to `fitBodyScale`.

- `fitDecimatedFactors: LabelRoomFactors | undefined`: The whitespace factors the `decimated` rung commits at: the smallest whose packed stack fits `fitTargetHeight`, so the most names are kept.
- `fitDecimatedSolved: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: The `decimated` stack: names kept only on features with at least their tier's `fitDecimatedFactors ×` their label width in neighbour whitespace (plus pinned/highlighted, always).
- `fitDecimatedBodyScale: number | undefined`: The body scale the `decimated` rung commits at: with the names `fitDecimatedFactors` kept, the bodies grow back into whatever height the dropped names freed.
- `fitBodiesOnlyLayout: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`
- `fitBareLayout: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: The `bare` stack: `bodies` with the `below` subfeature-label rows spent at zero height, so the last reduction before a squeeze gives back rows whose text the squeeze was about to hide anyway.

- `fitMinScale: number`: Floor on the fit squeeze: the smallest vertical scale that still leaves every drawn box at least `MIN_FIT_BOX_PX` tall.
- `fitStage: FitStage`: The resolved fit outcome — which reservation `level` survived, its unscaled `layout`, and the vertical `scale` to fill the track — bundled so the three can never disagree.
- `fitScale: number`: Uniform vertical scale for fit mode; below 1 only while the stack is squeezed to fit.

- `groupSections: FeatureGroupSection[]`: The stacked sections in stacking order, each with the chip row the packer reserved above it, read off the same rows the glyphs paint; empty while ungrouped.

## Properties
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `pinnedFeatureIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: Feature ids the user pinned to the top of the layout via the feature right-click menu.
- `soloFeatureIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: "Show only these features": the collected set the user builds by ctrl+clicking features (or via the right-click menu).

- `hiddenFeatureIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: "Hide this feature" exclusion set (inverse of solo): the worker drops these from layout/drawing.
- `expandedGeneIds = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: Genes the user opened from the isoform badge on the gene's label: these draw every isoform whatever `geneGlyphMode` or the fit ladder's isoform rung would otherwise collapse them to.

- `type = types.string`

- `configuredFilters() => string[]`: The `jexl:` expressions the `filter` list holds.
- `baseFilters() => string[]`: The expressions the track's config declares, which "Clear all filters" returns to.
- `rampColorScales(id: string) => ColorScale[]`: The key a ramp paints, under the caller's scale `id`: the bar over its domain, and a row apiece for the values the ramp has no color for. Both displays composing this built it from the same three getters, so the derivation is here rather…
- `rpcProps() => { displayConfig: { facetField?: string | undefined; color: {…}; subfeatureLabels: "auto" | "below" | "none" | "overlay"; filter: FieldPredicate[]; labels…`
- `gpuProps() => { colorTable: Uint32Array<ArrayBuffer>; fieldPalette: { field: string; paint: (value: string) => string; tableOf(values: readonly string[], withTints: bo…`: What the main-thread encode needs beyond a region's own data: the packed color for every theme class the worker emitted, off `session.palette`, and the color field's scale, so a theme toggle or a recolor re-encodes what is loaded instead…
- `fitLayoutAt(memo: IncrementalLayout, reserved: LabelReservation) => Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: One fit-escalation candidate: the stack packed with the given label reservation, via that config's own memo instance so each keeps stable references across renders.
- `decimatedLayoutInputs(factors: LabelRoomFactors) => LayoutInputs`: Layout inputs for the `decimated` rung at one pair of whitespace factors.
- `solveLabelRoomFactors(trackHeight: number) => LabelRoomFactors | undefined`: The whitespace factors the `decimated` rung commits at: gene names first, then the rest, each the smallest whose packed stack fits `trackHeight` (smallest = most names kept), or undefined when even the most aggressive decimation overflows.
- `bodyScaleHeightProbe(cache: PackHeightCache, inputs: LabelRoomFactorFreeInputs, factors?: LabelRoomFactors | undefined) => (bodyScale: number) => number`: Measures a labelled stack's height at any body scale. Each scale needs a separate prep, since the pack reads body heights from it.
- `floatingLabels(palette: JBrowsePalette) => FloatingLabel[]`: The labels the floating label layer draws over the canvas, as records in the display's own px, for a host that shows the canvas but not this display's DOM: a ring of the circular view. The isoform badge is a control, not a label, and stays…
- `searchFeatureByID(id: string) => readonly [number, number, number, number] | undefined`
- `renderSvg(opts?: ExportSvgDisplayOptions | undefined) => Promise<ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | AwaitedReactNode>`
- `featureNarrowings() => Reversibles`: Everything this display is doing to narrow what the user sees, each declared once, so the "Filter by (n)" count, its undo rows and "Clear all filters" cannot disagree; a method, not a getter, because a getter cannot be super-captured.
- `featureMarks() => Reversibles`: Reversible state that MARKS features rather than hiding them — the highlight boxes and the pins holding features at the top of the layout.
- `zoomFetchArgs() => { geneGlyphMode: "all" | "auto" | "representative"; peptides: boolean; expandedGeneIds: IMSTArray<ISimpleType<string>> | undefined; }`: The worker's zoom-dependent decisions, resolved: the RPC spreads this object and the foundation stamps it beside each region, so a track with the overlay off and a fixed mode never refetches on zoom. `expandedGeneIds` only under…
- `groupByPlot(field: string | undefined, colorByGroup: boolean) => Plot`: The Group by dialog's choice of field as plot settings, which its Apply writes and its Edit plot button shows: the facet, keeping its domain while the field is the one already set; a color by the field when ticked, left alone while it…
- `scanGroupByCandidates(opts: GroupByScanOptions) => Promise<RegionTooLargeResult | GroupByCandidate[]>`: The attributes the features in view have and the sections each would make, for the Group by dialog: the render fetch's download over the visible blocks, under the same admission and byte budget.
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The schema's rules, then a `jexl:` color or filter that does not compile.
- `showSubmenuCheckboxItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `showSubmenuRadioGroups() => MenuItem[]`
- `filterSubMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Overridable hook (default none): the rows "Filter by" lists beside the dialog, one per `filter` member a display adds.
- `showSubmenuMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Flattened "Show" submenu: all checkbox toggles first, then the radio groups (each under a subHeader), then the legend.
- `contextMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: The feature right-click menu (open details, zoom to, get sequence, highlight scopes, pin/solo/hide, copy).
- `colorBySubMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: The "Color by" radio choices (solid/strand/attribute).
- `colorMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Color-related track menu entries: a single "Color by" entry whose radios pick the track's own color or a field, and whose "Solid color..." item opens the solid+UTR color picker.
- `featureHeightMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: One "Feature height" menu with two independent radio groups: the size presets and, under a "Track sizing" subheader, how the track responds when there are more features than fit.
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `observedMaxDensity(bpPerPx: number) => number`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `regionHasData(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the display can draw what this region is marked loaded over, at the zoom the view has.
- `isCacheValid(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Whether the data held for a region still answers the current view. Not a hook a display fills: a display states its rule as `zoomFetchArgs` (what a fetch now would send the worker) and `regionHasData` (does what the last one stored still…
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

# LinearGenomeView (View model, linear-genome-view plugin)

Stacks tracks under a horizontal axis of one or more genomic regions laid end to end, which the user scrolls, zooms and searches.

Composes BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

A `LinearGenomeView` is what you hand-author under `defaultSession.views`, and
every setting goes directly on the view object. `assembly`/`loc` fill in
`displayedRegions`/`bpPerPx`/`offsetPx` for you:
```js
defaultSession: {
  name: 'My session',
  views: [
    {
      type: 'LinearGenomeView',
      colorByFrame: true,
      assembly: 'hg38',
      loc: 'chr1:1,000,000-1,100,000',
      tracks: ['genes', 'alignments'],
    },
  ],
}
```
`assembly`, `loc`, `tracks`, `tracklist`, `nav` and `highlight` need
on-attach resolution and are captured into the `launch` property below;
`colorByFrame`, `showAminoAcids`, `showCenterLine` and `trackLabels` are plain
view props MST restores natively. Both are written the same way.
At runtime the same model is driven imperatively — every property and action
below is reachable on `viewState.session.views[0]`:
```js
const view = viewState.session.views[0]
await view.navToLocString('chr1:2,000,000-2,100,000')
view.showTrack('alignments')
view.zoomTo(view.bpPerPx * 2) // zoom out 2x
```

## Actions
- `closeSearchPicker() => void`: Dismiss the search picker without choosing a place.
- `setShowTrackOutlines(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setScrollZoom(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setColorByFrame(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setShowAminoAcids(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setShowCytobands(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setTrackLabelBand(trackId: string, band: number) => void`
- `setScrollPortExcess(px: number | undefined) => void`
- `resizeTracks(distance: number, from?: any) => number`: Grow or shrink every unminimized track by `distance` px in all, each by its share of the height it has above the display minimum. `from` is the heights to scale, by track instance id; a drag passes the heights it started with, so…
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => void`: A resize keeps the window in bp, so `bpPerPx` follows the new width and the view keeps framing the same sequence (ADR-070).
- `setError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setIsScalebarRefNameMenuOpen(isOpen: boolean) => void`
- `setHideHeader(b: boolean) => void`
- `setHideHeaderOverview(b: boolean) => void`
- `setScalebarOnly(b: boolean) => void`
- `setHideNoTracksActive(b: boolean) => void`
- `setAxisGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setVolatileGuides(guides: VolatileGuide[]) => void`: set temporary vertical guides (e.g., for LD display hover)
- `scrollTo(offsetPx: number) => number`
- `scrollToBp(startBp: number) => number`: `scrollTo`'s bp-space twin: place the window's left edge at a linearized bp coordinate, clamped to the same scroll limits.
- `zoomTo(bpPerPx: number, offset?: any) => number`
- `setOffsets(left?: BpOffset | undefined, right?: BpOffset | undefined) => void`: sets offsets of rubberband, used in the get sequence dialog can call view.getSelectedRegions(view.leftOffset,view.rightOffset) to compute the selected regions from the offsets
- `setSearchResults(searchResults: BaseResult[], searchQuery: string, assemblyName: string, onPick?: (result: BaseResult) => Promise<unknown>) => void`: Raise the picker over search results that name more than one place.
- `search(query: string, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal | undefined; } | undefined) => Promise<SearchHits>`: Search the view's assembly by name, for a host listing the hits itself. A row's `pick` lands as the search box does: it navigates there and shows the track the hit's index came from.
- `showTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: any, displayInitialSnapshot?: any, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => any`
- `hideTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `fitTracksToWindow() => void`: Resize every unminimized track so the view is exactly as tall as the scroll port it sits in. Does nothing until the view has measured one.
- `launchTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: any, displayInitialSnapshot?: any, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => Promise<any>`: showTrack for a track whose display state model may be lazily loaded: loads it, then shows
- `setHighlights(highlights: readonly (string | HighlightInput)[]) => void`: Replace the highlights `highlights` reads, each written as the launch spec's `highlight` writes one: a locstring, or an object whose `assemblyName` defaults to the view's. Throws on one that names no region, writing none.
- `showFiles(files: readonly File[]) => Promise<string[]>`: Show files from the user's disk as session tracks: one per data file, beside the index among them that names it, its type guessed from its name. Adds nothing when one file has no known type. Resolves the new tracks' ids.
- `moveTrack(moving: string, target: string) => void`: Move one shown track to another's position; each is a track model id or a trackId.
- `moveTrackDown(idOrTrackId: string) => void`
- `moveTrackUp(idOrTrackId: string) => void`
- `moveTrackToTop(idOrTrackId: string) => void`
- `moveTrackToBottom(idOrTrackId: string) => void`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `launchToggleTrack(trackId: string) => Promise<boolean>`: toggleTrack with launchTrack's loading behavior
- `setTrackLabels(setting: "hidden" | "offset" | "overlapping") => void`
- `setShowCenterLine(b: boolean) => void`
- `activateTrackSelector() => Widget`
- `toggleTrackSelector() => Widget`
- `horizontalScroll(distance: number) => number`
- `setDraggingTrackId(idx?: string | undefined) => void`
- `onTrackDragOver(targetId: string, currentY: number) => void`: called while dragging a track over the track at `targetId`; reorders once the cursor has moved far enough (see shouldSwapTracks) to avoid jitter when a short track is dragged over a tall one
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<InitState> | undefined) => void`
- `slide(viewWidths: number) => void`: perform animated slide
- `zoom(targetBpPerPx: number) => void`: perform animated zoom
- `cancelZoomAnimation() => void`: cancel an in-flight animated zoom. Any other zoom already stops the animation, so this is for stopping it *without* changing the zoom — the slider grabbing the thumb, before it has a value to commit.
- `setCoarseDynamicBlocks(blocks: BlockSet, bpPerPx: number) => void`
- `settleCoarseBlocks() => void`: Bring the coarse blocks to the viewport as it stands now, for a placement that JUMPED rather than travelled.
- `moveTo(start?: BpOffset | undefined, end?: BpOffset | undefined) => void`: offset is the base-pair-offset in the displayed region, index is the index of the displayed region in the linear genome view
- `setNewView(bpPerPx: number, offsetPx: number) => void`: Place the viewport by `bpPerPx` and `offsetPx`, the pixel pair the view stored before it stored the window. Prefer `setWindow`: pixels mean nothing without the width they were measured at, so a round trip through here is only exact while…
- `setWindow(windowWidthBp: number, windowStartBp: number) => void`: Place the viewport by the pair it is actually STORED as: the window's width and left edge, both in bp. The bp-space counterpart of `setNewView`, and the right one for anything that captures a viewport and puts it back later (an Undo, a…
- `setWindowFrame(windowWidthBp: number, windowStartBp: number) => void`: `setWindow` without the settle, for a writer that runs per animation frame. Flushing the coarse blocks sixty times a second is the one thing such a writer must not do: they are a 500ms throttle that a synteny follow pass and two autoscale…
- `setDisplayedRegions(regions: Region[]) => void`: Settles the coarse blocks, since this is the worst jump to leave unsettled: they are keyed by `displayedRegionIndex`, so a set that outlives the region list has a consumer reading one contig's data against another's blocks.
- `clampZoomToCeiling() => void`: Re-assert `maxBpPerPx` over the current zoom, for a container whose shared ceiling just fell — otherwise the view is stranded above it with zoom-out disabled and the slider's min past its value. Goes through `zoomTo` so the clamp keeps one…
- `showAllRegions() => void`
- `fitAllRegions() => void`: Fit the displayed regions to the width exactly, edge to edge.
- `horizontallyFlip() => void`
- `showAllRegionsInAssembly(assemblyName?: string | undefined) => void`
- `clearView() => void`: this "clears the view" and makes the view return to the import form
- `navTo(query: NavLocation, grow?: number | undefined) => void`: Navigate to a location based on its refName and optionally start, end, and assemblyName. Will not try to change displayed regions, use `navToLocations` instead. Only navigates to a location if it is entirely within a displayedRegion.…
- `navToMultiple(locations: NavLocation[], grow?: number | undefined) => void`: Navigate to a location based on its refName and optionally start, end, and assemblyName. Will not try to change displayed regions, use navToLocations instead. Only navigates to a location if it is entirely within a displayedRegion.…
- `showRegions(regions: Region[], location?: NavLocation | undefined) => void`: Replace the region list and place the viewport in one step. The pair is the unit a coarse-block consumer can act on: called separately they publish the viewport in between, and post-await in `navToLocations` they are two transactions, so a…
- `navToLocString(input: string, optAssemblyName?: string | undefined, grow?: number | undefined, opts?: { showHitTrack?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => Promise<boolean>`: Navigate to the given locstring, will change displayed regions if needed, and wait for assemblies to be initialized
- `navToLocations(regions: ParsedLocString[], assemblyName?: string | undefined, grow?: number | undefined) => Promise<void>`: Similar to `navToLocString`, but accepts a list of parsed location objects instead of a locstring. Will try to perform `setDisplayedRegions` if changing regions
- `navToLocation(parsedLocString: ParsedLocString, assemblyName?: string | undefined, grow?: number | undefined) => Promise<void>`: Similar to `navToLocString`, but accepts a parsed location object instead of a locstring. Will try to perform `setDisplayedRegions` if changing regions
- `highlightCurrentRegion() => void`: adds the region in view to the session's highlights
- `navToHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => Promise<boolean>`: navigates to a highlight, zoomed out a little for context. Goes through a locstring so it reaches a refName the view is not displaying
- `navigateNewestHighlight() => Promise<void>`: navigates to the most recently added highlight on this view's assemblies
- `editDisplayedRegions(edit: RegionEdit) => void`: a region edit from the ruler's menu as one action, which a synteny stack's follow reads as the reader's gesture on this row; see `setDisplayedRegionsKeepingCenter`
- `flyTo(centerBp: number, windowWidthBp: number) => void`: Animate to a window along the Van Wijk arc from the current window to the target, over a duration derived from the arc.
- `flyToCenter(coord: number, refName: string, displayedRegionIndex?: number | undefined) => void`: `centerAt`'s animated twin: the same destination, reached along the arc instead of jumped to, at the zoom the view is already on.
- `flyToFit(centerBp: number, fitWidthBp: number) => void`: A flight to a linear bp centre at the zoom the view is on, or is already flying to, widened where that is narrower than `fitWidthBp`. The current width mid-flight is a point on the arc, so a second flight read from it would land pulled…
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `axisGrid: boolean`: `axis.grid`: whether the ruler's ticks run down through the tracks.
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<InitState & { unknown?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; malformed?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean | undefined; }>…`: the launch state that still has something to apply — the gate every loading and error path below reads.
- `bpPerPx: number`: corresponds roughly to the zoom level, base-pairs per pixel.
- `offsetPx: number`: corresponds roughly to the horizontal scroll of the LGV
- `minimumBlockWidth: number`: a displayed region narrower than this many pixels draws as an elided block
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: scroll-to-zoom is a global, personal preference resolved from the session; toggling it in any view applies everywhere
- `pinnedTracks: TrackModelOf<LinearDisplayModel>[]`
- `unpinnedTracks: TrackModelOf<LinearDisplayModel>[]`
- `effectiveTrackLabels: "hidden" | "offset" | "overlapping"`: the effective track labels setting, resolving the stored `trackLabels` against the LinearGenomeViewPlugin config default
- `width: number`
- `trackWidthPx: number`: width minus track outline borders (1px each side when shown)
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `assemblyDisplayNames: string[]`
- `highlights: HighlightType[]`: the session's highlights on this view's assemblies
- `isTopLevelView: boolean`: checking if lgv is a 'top-level' view is used for toggling pin track capability, sticky positioning
- `stickyViewHeaders: boolean`: only uses sticky view headers when it is a 'top-level' view and session allows it
- `ownTracks: TrackModelOf<LinearDisplayModel>[]`: The census entry for this view: the tracks it holds itself. Declared rather than derived — see `BaseViewModel.ownTracks`.
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: See `BaseViewModel.rendersDisplays`.
- `scalebarDisplayPrefix: string | undefined`: Assembly name captioning the scalebar ahead of its refName labels, or undefined for none. A container view (e.g. LinearSyntenyView) opts its sub-views in by exposing showAssemblyNameInSubviewScalebar; duck-typed rather than matching a…
- `assembliesNotFound: string | undefined`
- `assemblyErrors: string | undefined`
- `assembliesInitialized: boolean`
- `initAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: the assembly named by a pending `init`, or undefined when no init is set. `init`'s assembly isn't in `assemblyNames` yet (that derives from displayedRegions, still empty pre-navigation), so init-phase readiness and error checks resolve it…
- `launchAssemblyName: string | undefined`: The assembly a pending launch is for: the one it names, else the one the view already shows. A re-launch of a materialized view (a `jb.setSession` document writing `loc` beside the built state) need not restate it; without the default the…
- `initialized: boolean`
- `hasDisplayedRegions: boolean`
- `loadingAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly whose load the spinner is waiting on: the one `init` names before navigation (it isn't in assemblyNames yet), else the first of the displayed assemblies that hasn't finished loading.
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: The loading screen's text while `showLoading`, taken from the assembly being waited on; undefined otherwise.
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `awaitingInitNavigation: boolean`: init is set but its async navigation (the afterAttach autorun) hasn't populated displayedRegions yet. `initialized` can already be true here (it only tracks assembly readiness), so without this the container would mount over empty regions…
- `showLoading: boolean`: Whether to show a loading indicator instead of the import form or view
- `showImportForm: boolean`: Whether to show the import form
- `ready: boolean`: Is there anything to draw yet? The gate anything reading block geometry — a ruler, a scalebar, a display — has to pass first, because `width`/`staticBlocks` throw by design before the view has been measured and navigated.
- `status: ViewStatus`: The same question as `ready` with the other three outcomes named, for a host that draws its own chrome and has to render all four. See `computeViewStatus`, whose precedence this defers to — and note its `ready` is narrower than the getter…
- `scalebarHeight: number`
- `trackLeadingChrome: number`: What TrackContainer puts *above* a track's rendering container: the gap over its Paper, and the Paper's own top border when outlines are on.
- `trackTrailingChrome: number`: ...and what it puts below: the resize divider, plus the matching bottom border.
- `trackChromeHeight: number`: A track's full cost beyond its display height.
- `headerHeight: number`
- `trackHeights: number`
- `trackHeightsWithChrome: number`
- `height: number`
- `resizableTrackHeights: Map<string, number>`: The display height of each track a whole-stack resize moves, by track instance id: every shown track that is not minimized.
- `totalBp: number`
- `fitBpPerPx: number`
- `maxBpPerPx: number`: The zoom-out limit. Equal to the fit for this view's regions, except while a container holds it on a coarser shared scale, such as a small genome next to a large one, drawn short so the two compare by length.
- `sharedFitBpPerPx: number`: The zoom-out ceiling a containing comparative view holds this row to, or 0 for a standalone view, a mode that is off, and a stack that cannot answer yet.
- `minBpPerPx: number`
- `error: unknown`
- `maxOffset: number`
- `minOffset: number`
- `displayedRegionsOrientation: RegionsOrientation`: Whether the displayed regions read left-to-right, right-to-left, or some of each. `horizontallyFlip` reverses the order and flips every region at once, so a flipped row is uniformly `reversed` and `mixed` takes going out of your way — the…
- `displayedRegionsTotalPx: number`
- `trackMap: Map<string, TrackModelOf<LinearDisplayModel>>`
- `showsWholeChromosome: boolean`
- `canShowCytobands: boolean`: an ideogram only reads correctly against an entire chromosome: on a sub-region it is a meaningless slice of bands, and the centromere shows up as a lone half-triangle. The chromosome also needs bands: a cytoband file often lists only the…
- `effectiveShowCytobands: boolean`: the `showCytobands` setting gated by whether cytobands can be shown at all (whole chromosome with bands in the cytoband file) and by the header overview they draw in being on, which the SVG export follows too
- `cytobandOffset: number`: the cytoband is displayed to the right of the chromosome name, and that offset is calculated manually with this method
- `isTrackSelectorOpen: boolean`
- `overviewLayout: ViewLayout`: geometry of the overview scalebar — derived from displayedRegions, width, and cytobandOffset so it stays cached by MobX
- `staticBlocks: BlockSet`: static blocks are an important concept jbrowse uses to avoid re-rendering when you scroll to the side. when you horizontally scroll to the right, old blocks to the left may be removed, and new blocks may be instantiated on the right.…
- `dynamicBlocks: BlockSet`: dynamic blocks represent the exact coordinates of the currently visible genome regions on the screen. Static blocks can go offscreen, while dynamic blocks represent exactly what is on screen
- `overviewBlocks: BaseBlock[]`: all overview scalebar blocks (content + elided), laid out on the overviewLayout. memoized so the scalebar doesn't recompute it per render
- `overviewRegionPxSpan: PxSpan | undefined`: leading/trailing pixel span of the visible regions projected onto the overviewLayout — the geometry of the overview's "you are here" rectangle, and of the top edge of the polygon drawn under it. Elided regions count: at whole-genome zoom…
- `staticBlocksTranslateX: number`: The x shift that maps the **staticBlocks frame** onto the viewport: `translateX(view.staticBlocksTranslateX)` on one container places every `gridlineTicks`, `scalebarLabels` and `paddingSpans` entry at once, and a pan then moves that…
- `gridlineTicks: { x: number; major: boolean; }[]`: Gridline tick positions (x relative to the staticBlocks frame), derived from staticBlocks + bpPerPx. Computed once and shared by every Gridlines instance (scalebar, main view, each pinned track) rather than recomputing the makeTicks loop…
- `scalebarLabels: { x: number; label: string; key: string; }[]`: Scalebar coordinate labels (x in the staticBlocks frame + display text). Sibling of gridlineTicks sharing the same makeBlockTicks formula, so labels line up exactly with their gridlines. staticBlocks chop a region into ~800px chunks;…
- `scalebarRefNameLabels: { labels: ScalebarRefNameLabel[]; caption: string | undefined; captionSpanPx: number; }`: The bold refName labels drawn along the scalebar, as plain data: `{key, refName, displayedRegionIndex, lastDisplayedRegionIndex, sticky, transform, maxWidth, paddingLeft, text}` each. One per run of same-refName regions, plus a "sticky"…
- `paddingSpans: readonly { key: string; x: number; width: number; kind: "boundary" | "elided" | "seam"; }[]`: Every span along the row that is not track data, as plain geometry in the staticBlocks frame — the same frame as gridlineTicks and scalebarLabels, so one `translateX(staticBlocksTranslateX)` places all three. A host that draws the row's…
- `totalWidthPx: number`: Integer-rounded sum of all visible block widths. Slightly less than view.width when the genome ends before the right edge; use view.width for SVG clip rects (display boundary) and this for paint canvas sizing (actual content width).
- `totalWidthPxWithoutBorders: number`: Like totalWidthPx but excluding inter-region boundary blocks. Used when column layout divides the canvas width by feature count.
- `visibleBp: number`
- `hasVisibleContent: boolean`: Whether any part of a displayed region actually falls inside the viewport. False both when the view holds no regions at all and when it holds some but is scrolled entirely off them; either way there is no visible span for the scalebar,…
- `visibleWholeBaseRegions: { assemblyName: string; refName: string; start: number; end: number; }[]`: What is on screen, as regions that address whole bases — what a reader means by "the visible region" when they ask to fetch it, bookmark it or read it back in a locString field. `visibleRegions` below is the other half: pixels, and…
- `visibleRegions: { refName: string; start: number; end: number; assemblyName: string; reversed: boolean | undefined; displayedRegionIndex: number; screenStartPx: number; screen…`: Returns the currently visible content blocks with screen pixel positions and displayedRegionIndex guaranteed. Used by WebGL displays for per-region data fetching and rendering.
- `contentRightEdgePx: number`: Right edge (px, viewport-relative) of the on-screen content, clamped to the track — where a right-pinned overlay such as a wiggle's color or score legend belongs, rather than out in the empty gutter the regions can leave at whole-genome…
- `bufferedVisibleRegions: { region: { refName: string; start: number; end: number; assemblyName: string; reversed: boolean | undefined; }; displayedRegionIndex: number; }[]`: visibleRegions expanded by a half-screen buffer on each side, clamped to displayedRegion bounds, with integer-rounded coordinates. Use this when fetching data that should extend slightly beyond the viewport for smooth scrolling.
- `visibleLocStrings: string`: a single "combo-locstring" representing all the regions visible on the screen
- `settledDynamicBlocks: ContentBlock[]`: **The blocks a debounced consumer clips to**: the coarse blocks once the view has settled at least once, the live ones before that.
- `coarseVisibleLocStrings: string`: same as visibleLocStrings, but only updated every 500ms
- `coarseTotalBpDisplayStr: string`
- `effectiveTotalBp: number`
- `effectiveTotalBpDisplayStr: string`
- `centerLineInfo: PxToBpResult | undefined`
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownViews: AbstractViewModel[]`: The views nested directly inside this one, which the census counts as separate views — a synteny stack's genome rows, a breakpoint split view's panels.

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.literal('LinearGenomeView') as unknown as string`: this is a string instead of the const literal 'LinearGenomeView' to reduce some typescripting strictness, but you should pass the string 'LinearGenomeView' to the model explicitly
- `windowStartBp = types.stripDefault(types.number, 0)`: Left edge of the viewport, in linearized bp — the concatenated `displayedRegions` space that `offsetPx` indexes, which has no inter-region padding, so the two differ only by `bpPerPx`. May be negative when the view is scrolled past the…
- `windowWidthBp = types.stripDefault(types.number, 0)`: Width of the viewport in bp. Zero means "not established yet": no width has been measured, so there is nothing to divide by. The first measure fills it in, and `bpPerPx` is `windowWidthBp / width` from then on.
- `legacyBpPerPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, 0)`: Used for migration only, and permanent: share links written before the window was stored contain `bpPerPx`/`offsetPx`, and there are many of them.
- `displayedRegions = types.stripDefault(types.frozen<Region[]>(), [])`: currently displayed regions, can be a single chromosome, arbitrary subsections, or the entire set of chromosomes in the genome. The entire set is not advised if your assembly is very fragmented
- `tracks = types.array( pluginManager.pluggableMstType<LinearDisplayModel>( 'track', 'stateModel', ), )`: array of currently displayed tracks state models instances
- `hideHeader = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: drop the header bar entirely — location box, navigation buttons and overview
- `hideHeaderOverview = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: keep the header, drop the whole-chromosome overview strip below it
- `hideNoTracksActive = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: suppress the "No tracks active" placeholder, for an embed that opens with no tracks on purpose
- `trackSelectorType = types.stripDefault(types.string, 'hierarchical')`: ignored: the hierarchical selector is the only one. Declared because saved sessions and share links carry it.
- `showCenterLine = types.optional(types.boolean, () => localStorageGetBoolean('lgv-showCenterLine', false), )`: show the "center line". A personal preference: never in a session snapshot. It, showCytobands, trackLabels, colorByFrame, showAminoAcids and showTrackOutlines start from this browser's last choice, which their setters record.
- `showCytobands = types.optional(types.boolean, () => localStorageGetBoolean('lgv-showCytobands', true), )`: whether to show the "cytobands" in the overview scale bar (the resolved, capability-gated value is the `effectiveShowCytobands` getter)
- `trackLabels = types.optional( types.string, () => localStorageGetItem('lgv-trackLabels') ?? '', )`: how to display the track labels, can be "overlapping", "offset", or "hidden", or empty string "" (which uses the LinearGenomeViewPlugin config default). The resolved value is the `effectiveTrackLabels` getter. See the…
- `axis = types.stripDefault(linearGenomeViewAxisConfigSchema, {})`: The ruler's guide, a [](/docs/config/lineargenomeviewaxis) object: `{ grid: false }` stops its ticks running down through the tracks.
- `colorByFrame = types.optional(types.boolean, () => localStorageGetBoolean('lgv-colorByFrame', false), )`: color CDS segments by reading frame
- `showAminoAcids = types.optional(types.boolean, () => localStorageGetBoolean('lgv-showAminoAcids', true), )`: draw translated codons on coding features once zoomed in far enough: an alternating per-codon shading, and the amino acid letters on top of it at base-level zoom. Independent of `colorByFrame`, which only recolors the segments by frame.
- `showTrackOutlines = types.optional(types.boolean, () => localStorageGetBoolean('lgv-showTrackOutlines', true), )`: show the track outlines
- `scalebarOnly = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: when true, only the header and coordinate scalebar are rendered
- `launch = types.frozen<LaunchInput<InitState> | undefined>()`: transient launch state: the settings written on the view object that need resolving before they can be view state — an assembly, a location, track recipes, highlights. `preProcessSnapshot` moves them here off the snapshot, the afterAttach…
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar and keep it in the session

Shared by trackHeights and getTrackYOffset so the two can't disagree. Reads `activeDisplay` — the display TrackContainer actually mounts — rather than re-picking…

Falls back to the raw refName if the region's assemblyName is missing or unknown so highlights authored without an assembly still render in single-assembly…
