LinearHicDisplay.text:
# LinearHicDisplay (Display model, hic plugin)

The Hi-C contact matrix as a triangle over the view.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearHicDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes PointerHoverMixin, TriangleMatrixMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, MatrixRampMixin, LegendMixin, GlobalFetchMixin, KeyedFetchMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

A `HicTrack` whose display pins the color scale's top, so two tracks set
alike share one scale, and runs one binsize coarser than the zoom picks:
```js
{
  type: 'HicTrack',
  trackId: 'hic',
  name: 'Hi-C',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'HicAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/contacts.hic' },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearHicDisplay',
      displayId: 'hic-LinearHicDisplay',
      encoding: {
        color: { scale: { type: 'symlog', domainMax: 500 } },
      },
      data: { resolution: -1 },
    },
  ],
}
```

## Actions
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: HicRenderingBackend) => void`
- `setLogScale(log: boolean) => void`: The Log scale toggle: `encoding.color.scale.type` symlog, which keeps every nonzero count visible, or unset for `observed`'s linear preset.
- `setColorDomainQuantile(quantile: number) => void`
- `setNormalization(normalization: string) => void`
- `setFileInfo(read: AdapterRead<HicHeader>) => void`
- `setResolution(steps: number) => void`: `data.resolution`, binsizes finer than the zoom's pick.
- `setBinSizeIdx(idx: number) => void`: Lock to `availableBinSizes[idx]`, clamped, stored as an offset from the auto pick so the choice keeps its meaning across zoom.
- `setBinSize(binSize: number) => void`: Lock to a binsize the file offers; any other is ignored.
- `stepResolution(delta: number) => void`: `delta` binsizes finer, clamped to the file's.
- `setPointer(state?: PointerPx | undefined) => void`: the chrome's `onPointerPosition`
- `setRpcData(data: D) => void`
- `setHeightMode(mode: "fit" | "fixed") => void`
- `colorByField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Paint by `field`, keeping its domain, range and key names while it is the field already painting or the one parked; undefined paints `value` and parks the field.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every feature `value`, a CSS color or a `jexl:` callback, parking the field; undefined lets each feature's own color paint.
- `pickDefaultColor() => void`: Color by's Default: no field and no constant, so the track's own color paints, a `jexl:` expression included.
- `pickSolidColor() => void`: Color by's Solid color...: paints the constant kept beside a painting field, where there is one, and opens the display's picker.
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setColorScheme(scheme: "blues" | "cividis" | "fall" | "inferno" | "juicebox" | "magma" | "purpleorange" | "redblue" | "redgreyblue" | "reds" | "redyellowblue" | "viridis") =…`: The scheme, with `reverse` back to unset so it follows the scheme. The painted field's own scheme writes `scheme` unset, so it keeps following the field.
- `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it.
- `dismissLegendSection(id: string) => void`: Close one section of the legend, leaving the others up.
- `commitFetchResult(commit: () => void, key: FetchKey) => void`: The commit half of a keyed fetch: run the display's own store in the same transaction as the key stamp, so no observer can see fresh data under a stale key or the reverse. As the only writer of `loadedFetchKey`, this action makes…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter — the shared skeleton's reload epoch makes that bump override the freshness gate, even against a fetch that commits mid-reload, so nothing here has to remember to invalidate for the retry's sake)…
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.
- `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what the other axis measured, on the trigger that invalidates this one, so re-pointing an adapter never leaves `densityTooLarge` reporting on the previous file.
- `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing.
- `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch.
- `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void`
- `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number`
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`
- `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first.
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`: Overridable hook (default no-op): drop whatever `hoveredFeature` reports. The writing twin of that getter, and what `installClearHoverOnViewportChange` calls.
- `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record<string, unknown>, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Each key runs through the display config schema's `preProcessSnapshot` (shorthand expansions and legacy-key migrations, as `showTrackGeneric` applies to a…
- `applyPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => void`: Write a draft over `plot` as a settings bag writes: a setting left out stays, `null` resets one, a channel (`writes: 'whole'`, such as `color` or `facet`) is replaced whole, and any other object takes the members the draft names, so a…

## Getters
- `availableNormalizations: string[] | undefined`
- `availableBinSizes: number[] | undefined`: Smallest first, so a positive `data.resolution` is always finer.
- `hasControl: boolean`: Whether the adapter names a control, which observed/control needs.
- `resolution: number`: `data.resolution`: binsizes finer than the zoom's pick.
- `colorDomainQuantile: number`: `encoding.color.scale.domainQuantile`: the quantile of the loaded values an unset `domainMax` follows, their maximum at 1.
- `clipColorDomainQuantile: number`: The quantile "Emphasize faint contacts" clips the domain at: `colorDomainQuantile` while it clips, else the one ticking it writes. Each fetch asks the worker for this one whichever is drawn, so the toggle reselects nothing.
- `normalization: string`: `data.normalization`, the one asked for.
- `colorField: "observed" | "observed/control" | "observed/expected"`: `encoding.color.field`, what the fetch asks the worker to put in each cell.
- `countFloors: HicCountFloors`: The `filter` list's floors on a cell's counts, which the worker applies before the ratio.
- `paintedColorField: "observed" | "observed/control" | "observed/expected"`: The field the loaded cells are: observed/expected falls back to the counts where the file has no expected values at the binsize.
- `hasBinSizes: boolean`: Whether the binsize list has arrived; every resolution control gates on it.
- `activeNormalization: string`: The normalization to request: the selection where the file has it, else the next best it does. A getter, so a file lacking the selection never marks the track edited.
- `loadedQuantileScore: number`: The loaded values' score at `clipColorDomainQuantile`: the worker's answer, or after an edit a selection over the loaded matrix, so a new percentile refetches nothing. The next fetch asks the worker for the new one.
- `colorExtent: readonly [number, number]`: What an open end of the color domain follows: the loaded values from 0, which is where a count's extent starts, to their `colorDomainQuantile` below 1, else their maximum.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Retry is two-stage: the contact fetch declines until the header it needs lands, and the header's arrival wakes it. `infoFetchFailure.test.ts` pins it.
- `appliedNormalizations: string[]`: The normalizations the loaded matrix has, the requested one first. Each region pair falls back on its own, per binsize (KR at 5 kb, nothing at 2.5 Mb is typical) and per chromosome (chrY often lacks SCALE), so a view across chromosomes can…
- `paintedFieldName: { name: string; isCount: boolean; }`: The painted field's name for the key and the tooltip.
- `autoBinSizeIdx: number`: The binsize index auto mode picks: the largest at most 2 bp/px, about half a bin per pixel, else the finest.
- `colorScales: ColorScale[]`: The value ramp. A top below the largest loaded value reads `≥`. The title names the loaded binsize, so a figure carries it, unless `encoding.color.legend.title` replaces it.
- `binSizeIdx: number`: The index in effect after `resolution`'s steps, clamped so steps set at another zoom cannot index out of range.
- `valueLabel: string`: What the tooltip calls a bin's value.
- `binSize: number | undefined`
- `canStepResolutionFiner: boolean`
- `canStepResolutionCoarser: boolean`
- `renderState: HicRenderState`
- `viewSignature: string | undefined`: The static blocks plus the binsize, so a pan inside them redraws and only a block entering or a binsize step refetches. Undefined until the header lands.
- `hoveredFeature: T | undefined`: what is under the pointer, re-resolved whenever the content under it moves
- `heightMode: "fit" | "fixed"`
- `matrixTop: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px reserved above the matrix.
- `canvasWidth: number`: The canvas spans the scrolled content, boundary padding included.
- `viewTransform: { viewScale: number; viewOffsetX: number; }`
- `matrixRegions: ReadonlyMap<number, D>`: The one payload under key 0, absent until the fetch lands. An empty matrix keeps the key: the cleared canvas is its picture.
- `matrixHeight: number`
- `matrixBlocks: RenderBlock[]`
- `yScalar: number`: The squash takes the content's base, without the boundary padding a scroll past either end adds.
- `triangleTransform: { yScalar: number; yOffsetPx: number; viewScale: number; viewOffsetX: number; }`
- `triangleFrame: TriangleFrame`
- `writtenColor: ColorSlots`: The `encoding.color` channel as these writes and an Apply button read it, `writtenColorOf`.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field
- `colorEncoding: MatrixColorEncoding<F>`: The color channel under the painted field's preset, with an unset `scale.reverse` turning round a scheme dark at its low end, since an unpainted cell is the page behind the matrix. The preset's scheme, and its direction with it, fill…
- `colorScaleType: "linear" | "log" | "symlog"`
- `colorScheme: "blues" | "cividis" | "fall" | "inferno" | "juicebox" | "magma" | "purpleorange" | "redblue" | "redgreyblue" | "reds" | "redyellowblue" | "viridis"`
- `colorReverse: boolean`: `scale.reverse`, or where unset whether the scheme runs dark at its low end.
- `colorRamp: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>`: The ramp's 256 entries: the GPU's texture, the Canvas2D fill and the legend read this one table. It reads `colorScheme` and `colorReverse` rather than the encoding, so a domain edit re-uploads no texture.
- `colorScale: { domain: [number, number]; lut: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; midNorm: number; colorOf: (value: number) => number; }`: `colorEncoding` over `colorExtent`: each pinned end holds and an open one follows the extent, as the mark display's ramps do.
- `colorDomain: [number, number]`
- `colorMidNorm: number`: Where `domainMid` sits on the normalized ramp, 0.5 unset, so a diverging scheme centres on it and equal distances from it take equal colors.
- `matrixColor: MatrixColorState`
- `colorFieldTitle: string`: The painted field's own key title, from its preset.
- `showLegend: boolean`: Whether the legend is drawn.
- `legendRight: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px the on-screen key is pushed left from the key's inset, for a display that draws a column of text down its right edge — the multi-way lanes' scales. Not read by the export.
- `legendTop: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px the on-screen key is pushed down from the key's inset, for a display whose top rows hold the data a reader reads the rest against — the multi-way anchor lane. Not read by the export.
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: The key, derived from `colorScales` less the sections the reader dismissed. `DisplayChrome` renders it on screen and `renderDisplaySvg` flattens it for the export, so the two describe one set of colors.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the display has a key at all. The "Legend" row is offered only when it does. Overridable for a display whose key is only waiting for data: a scale that stays empty until a region lands must not remove the toggle in the meantime.
- `host: RegionHost`: The hosting view as the `RegionHost` contract — see `containingHost` for the cast it owns, why the name is `host` and not `view`, and why both foundations still declare the name over one body.
- `canvasWidthPx: number`: The CSS width of this display's on-screen canvas, in px; see `trackCanvasWidthPx`. A heatmap laid out over the whole content reads the content width instead (`TriangleMatrixMixin.canvasWidth`).
- `staticBlockSignature: string | undefined`: The static-block set as a signature, or `undefined` before the view is measured — the building block every `viewSignature` in this family starts from. Multi-way synteny is exactly this; HiC appends its resolution. Declared here so the…
- `dynamicBlockSignature: string | undefined`: The same over `dynamicBlocks`, for a display whose fetch window is the live viewport rather than the snapped block set (LD).
- `viewportEmpty: boolean`: No content block is on screen, so this display has nothing to fetch and nothing to paint — see `viewportEmpty.ts` for the one viewport that reaches it, how narrow that is, and why the state still has to be terminal rather than a permanent…
- `canRender: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook with the LGV precondition both foundations share — see `foundationCanRender`.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook off `fetchInert`: a display that will never fetch here shows a placeholder where its canvas would be, so `painted` and the pre-first-paint scrim term stop waiting on a paint that cannot come. This is…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it…
- `svgReady: boolean`: Policy single-sourced in `computeSvgReady`; this family supplies only the freshness half, which `foundationSvgReady` reads as `dataCurrent` or the vacuous currency of `viewportEmpty`. Note it requires the dataset to actually be current,…
- `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The display's mutually-exclusive visual state, mapped in `foundationDisplayPhase` — every foundation calls it and supplies only its staleness argument, so a term added to `computeActivityPhase` reaches all of them without being wired twice.
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the held data matches the key, but the screen will settle on different data — a dependent fetch is still out, or a fetch input the display writes itself has moved. The same hook `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`…
- `currentFetchKey: FetchKey | undefined`: Key of the fetch the current view, settings and adapter call for. The fetch skeleton's freshness key: captured at issue, compared against the stamp above, and written to it at commit. Its identity survives a recomputation onto equal…
- `dataCurrent: boolean`: The shared freshness answer every foundation gives: data has been committed (`loadedFetchKey` is only ever written beside it), it was fetched for the current view and settings, and the display is not about to supersede it itself. A pan…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by `computeActivityPhase` and `foundationSvgReady`: a load this display depends on beyond its primary fetch has not landed for the first time, so the frame the primary fetch calls current is still…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): what is on the canvas was painted from data a later change has made wrong, so `painted` below should answer *pending* until the repaint lands even though `canvasDrawn` is still true. The per-region fetch…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: The opt-in. Overridden with a literal `true` by gated displays, and `check-gated-adapter-budgets` insists on a literal: this mixin returns early on it in an autorun and in `commitFetchBytes`.
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.
- `regionTooLarge: boolean`
- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.
- `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate.
- `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen.
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `height: number`
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollContentHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the content that scrolls, in px.
- `scrollViewportHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the window it scrolls behind, in px.
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the singular word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants".
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features.
- `liveNotices: string[]`: Notices from the loaded data beside the config, such as a field no fetched feature has. Empty unless a display overrides it.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('LinearHicDisplay')`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `id = ElementId`

## Methods
- `rpcProps() => { normalization: string; field: HicColorField; floors: HicCountFloors; }`: The settings that refetch. The binsize is zoom-derived and the quantile reselects on the main thread, so both ride as call arguments.
- `hitTest(mouseX: number, mouseY: number) => HicContactItem | undefined`: The contact under a display-px point, through the inverse of the transform the matrix was drawn with.
- `hoverHitAt(mouseX: number, mouseY: number) => HicContactItem | undefined`: No contact while the matrix loads: a global display replaces its whole frame, so the cells it holds are on their way out.
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The schema's rules, then the `filter` entries the worker cannot apply.
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `renderSvg(opts: ExportSvgDisplayOptions) => Promise<ReactNode>`
- `cellToScreen(x: number, y: number) => { x: number; y: number; }`: Pre-rotation cell coordinates to display px.
- `screenToCell(x: number, y: number) => { x: number; y: number; }`: The exact inverse of `cellToScreen`.
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `rampColorScales({ id, title, extent: { min, max }, }: { id: string; title: string; extent: { min?: number | undefined; max: number; }; }) => ColorScale[]`: The legend's ramp, once there is a domain to span: its bottom where the scale paints it, a log scale's floor included, titled by `encoding.color.legend.title` where written, else `title`. An end of the domain the loaded values run past…
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

# LinearMafDisplay (Display model, maf plugin) Draws the multiple alignment in a `MafTrack`, one row per aligned species, under a conservation band. Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearMafDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live). Composes ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin, ContextMenuMixin, TreeSidebarMixin, RowHeightMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, CoarseTierMixin, StoredHoverMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow. A complete `MafTrack` config to paste into `tracks`. `samples` lists the aligned species in track order; `rowHeight` sets the per-sample band height in px (or `0` to stretch rows to fill the track height): ```js { type: 'MafTrack', trackId: 'multiz', name: 'Multiz alignment', assemblyNames: ['hg38'], adapter: { type: 'BigMafAdapter', bigBedLocation: { uri: 'https://example.com/multiz.bb' }, samples: ['hg38', 'panTro4', 'mm10'], }, displays: [ { type: 'LinearMafDisplay', displayId: 'multiz-LinearMafDisplay', rowHeight: 16, coverage: { show: true }, }, ], } ``` ## Actions - `setRowProportion(n: number) => void` - `setColorScheme(scheme: "blues" | "cividis" | "fall" | "inferno" | "juicebox" | "magma" | "purpleorange" | "redblue" | "redgreyblue" | "reds" | "redyellowblue" | "viridis") =…`: Paint identity along a named ramp, clearing a written `scale.range`, which would win over it. - `setShowCoverage(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowCoverageAlleles(show: boolean) => void`: Turns the coverage band's allele colors on or off, `coverage.alleles.show` - `setCoverageMinAlleleFraction(fraction: number) => void` - `setShowInterbase(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowAlignments(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowConservation(arg: boolean) => void` - `setConservationUnit(arg: "base" | "codon") => void` - `setYField(field: "identity" | undefined) => void` - `setShowMismatches(arg: boolean) => void` - `setBasesField(field: "base" | "codon" | undefined) => void`: Turn the per-position layer on with `field`, or off with undefined, keeping the field it last painted. - `setShowFrames(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowInversions(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowReferenceRow(arg: boolean) => void` - `setSamples({ samples, treeNewick, samplesCanonical, }: { samples: MafSource[]; treeNewick: string | undefined; samplesCanonical: boolean; }) => void`: Receive the worker's `samples` and serialized Newick tree. - `setFitToHeight() => void`: Switch to fit-to-height mode: rows stretch to fill the track height. Seeds the `height` slot from the current content height so toggling on does not jump. - `resizeCoverageHeight(distance: number) => void`: Apply one drag delta to the coverage band. Reads the current height inside the action because `ResizeHandle` emits one delta per animation frame. Mirrors `resizeHeight`. - `resizeConservationHeight(distance: number) => void`: Per-frame drag delta for the conservation band — see `resizeCoverageHeight` for why this reads the height itself. - `sortRowsByBaseAt(refName: string, pos: number) => boolean`: Reorder the rows by the base each species has in the reference column at (refName, pos), writing the order to `rows.sort` as clustering and the arrangement dialog do, so "Reset row order" undoes all three. - `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: The picker Color by's Solid color... opens, on the theme's match tone until a constant is written. - `setRefSampleId(id: string | undefined) => void`: The reference row the last detail batch named — see `refSampleIdVolatile`. Written beside `setSamples` in the batch commit, so a stale batch names nothing. - `setFramesGateBlocked(blocked: boolean) => void`: Record whether the last frames read was declined as over budget. Set both ways by every fetch pass that reaches the frames adapter, so zooming back in clears it without anything else having to. - `clearDisplaySpecificData() => void`: Clears the verdict with the data: it describes a read of the viewport just thrown away, and chromosome nav would otherwise show "too much data" for an unmeasured region. - `startRenderingBackend(backend: MafRenderingBackend) => void` - `fetchNeeded(needed: IndexedRegion[]) => Promise`: The detail fetch. The summary tier's is `fetchCoarseTier` below, and `CoarseTierMixin` suspends this one while the tier is up. - `fetchCoarseTier(read: CoarseTierRead, ctx: FetchContext) => Promise>>` - `renderSvg(opts: ExportSvgDisplayOptions) => Promise> | Iterable | AwaitedReactNode>`: Dynamic import so the export path — and everything it pulls in — stays out of the bundle until someone actually exports. - `setScaleType(scaleType: string) => void` - `setScaleZero(zero: boolean) => void` - `setFenceQuantile(quantile: number) => void` - `setDomainMin(val?: number | undefined) => void` - `setDomainMax(val?: number | undefined) => void` - `setMinScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMin`. - `setMaxScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMax`. - `setAutoscaleGroup(group?: string | undefined) => void` - `setGrid(grid: boolean) => void` - `setScoreRules(rules: (number | ValueScaleRule)[]) => void`: Replaces the y scale's rules whole, each entry in a form the config takes: a number, or `{ value, color, label }`. - `resetYScale() => void`: Back to what the config.json says, or to what a session-owned track was added with, so an admin's declared axis survives a reset; slots the base leaves unset take their defaults. - `openContextMenu(info: Info) => void` - `closeContextMenu() => void` - `setShowTree(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowBranchLength(arg: boolean) => void` - `setShowRowLabels(arg: boolean) => void` - `setTreeAreaWidth(width: number) => void` - `setRunClustering(arg?: boolean | undefined) => void` - `setClusterRegion(arg?: string | undefined) => void` - `setSortRowsBy(arg?: RowSortSpec | undefined) => void`: Trigger (or clear) a one-shot declarative row sort; consumed and reset by `setupRowSortAutorun`. - `setHoveredTreeNode(node?: HoveredTreeNode | undefined) => void` - `setTreeCanvasRef(ref: HTMLCanvasElement | null) => void` - `setMouseoverCanvasRef(ref: HTMLCanvasElement | null) => void` - `setRowOrder(rows: readonly { name: string; }[], run?: ClusterRun | undefined) => void`: Arrange the rows in `rows`' order, ahead of any name the current order has that `rows` does not. A clustering run passes its result, and the tree and its provenance land with the order; any other reorder that moves a row drops the tree,… - `setRowLabels(labels: Readonly>) => void`: The labels drawn in place of row names, whole: a row the map does not name shows the name it arrived with. - `setRowFocus(names?: readonly string[] | undefined) => void`: Narrow the display to `names`, or show every row again. - `applyRowEdits(rows: readonly S[], rowColor?: RowColorSnapshot | undefined) => void`: The arrangement dialog's submit: the rows in their new order, each with the label the reader left on it, and the `rowColor` object the dialog shows, written where it differs from the config's. The labels go to `rows` by the rule… - `resetRowArrangement() => void`: Return every arrangement member — order, labels, tree, provenance and focus — to what the config declares, leaving `rows.field`, and the `rowColor` colors to `rowColorResetTarget`: the config's for the choice, which stays. - `setRowColorChoice(choice: string) => void`: Color the rows by `choice`, as a menu picks it: '' for None, `name` for Each row, or a field, starting from `rowColorFor`. A pick of the current choice writes nothing. - `focusLegendEntry(scaleId: string, value: string) => void`: `LegendHost`'s hook: a click on a row color key entry narrows the rows to those it lists. Every other scale's entries name colors, not rows, and stay inert. - `setRowHeight(n: number) => void`: Pin a px row height. `0` is the fit sentinel, but enter fit mode through `setFitToHeight` instead — displays whose `height` getter is content-derived have to re-seed the slot on the way in, and that is what the action is for. - `colorByField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Paint by `field`, keeping its domain, range and key names while it is the field already painting or the one parked; undefined paints `value` and parks the field. - `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every feature `value`, a CSS color or a `jexl:` callback, parking the field; undefined lets each feature's own color paint. - `pickDefaultColor() => void`: Color by's Default: no field and no constant, so the track's own color paints, a `jexl:` expression included. - `pickSolidColor() => void`: Color by's Solid color...: paints the constant kept beside a painting field, where there is one, and opens the display's picker. - `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant. - `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it. - `dismissLegendSection(id: string) => void`: Close one section of the legend, leaving the others up. - `setCoarseTier(entries: CoarseTierEntry

[], read: CoarseTierRead) => void` - `clearCoarseTier() => void` - `setCoarseTierLoading(loading: boolean) => void` - `setHoveredFeature(hit?: T | undefined) => void` - `clearHoveredFeature() => void` - `setLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number, region: Region, payload: {} | undefined, fetchInputs?: FetchInputs) => void`: The raw write behind `ctx.commitRegion`, and **not what a fetch should call**. A display naming its span itself is the bug this family spent a release fixing, and the context gives a fetch no way to express it — see RegionFetchContext.… - `evictRegionStore(keep: ReadonlySet) => void`: The store's bound. Drops the entries a fetch can no longer be about: an index outside the view's buffered viewport, once the store is over `MAX_STORED_REGIONS`, oldest first. - `dropLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`: Forget one region, as `evictRegionStore` does past its cap. Tests use it to stage an evicted region. - `clearSettingsBakedData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds that is wrong under a changed setting rather than merely stale — a payload whose shape the setting decides. Called by `invalidateSettings`, where `clearDisplaySpecificData` is… - `clearAllRpcData() => void`: full reset: cancels fetch, clears error, loadedRegions, display-specific data, and the canvas-drawn flag. The too-large gate is derived (a pure function of the cached estimate × viewport), so it needs no explicit clear here — the fetch… - `invalidateSettings() => void`: `SettingsInvalidate`'s reset: the half of `clearAllRpcData` a settings change still needs now that the settings and adapter axes are in `fetchInputs`. The in-flight fetch is superseded now rather than when its payload lands stamped stale,… - `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter) plus the full reset. Subclasses with extra teardown override and chain. - `fetchRegions(needed: IndexedRegion[], work: (ctx: RegionFetchContext) => Promise) => Promise`: Run a per-region fetch. The work callback calls `ctx.commitRegion` as it stores each region's payload, which is what marks it loaded — see RegionFetchContext for why this function no longer does that itself. Only the three helpers in… - `afterAttach() => void`: installs the fetch-lifecycle autoruns (DisplayedRegionsChange, FetchVisibleRegions, SettingsInvalidate, ClearBlockingStateOnViewportChange) - `setError(error?: unknown) => void` - `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not. - `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward. - `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)… - `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the… - `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The… - `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains… - `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings… - `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing… - `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise) => Promise`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on. - `markCanvasDrawn() => void` - `resetCanvasDrawn() => void` - `stopRenderingBackend() => void` - `renderNow() => void` - `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void` - `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry. - `attachRenderingBackend(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's. - `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval. - `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what the other axis measured, on the trigger that invalidates this one, so re-pointing an adapter never leaves `densityTooLarge` reporting on the previous file. - `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void` - `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing. - `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch. - `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void` - `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void` - `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number` - `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number` - `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first. - `applyDisplaySettings(settings: Record, options?: { allowSetters?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => { applied: string[]; unapplied: UnappliedSetting[]; faile…`: Apply a set of display settings to the live display, and report which were applied. Plugins that want to suppress rendering in certain states (e.g. no… - `fetchInputs: FetchInputs`: What a fetch issued right now would stamp on a region: the settings tier (`FetchMixin.settingsFetchInputs`, the tier `staleSettingsDrawn` compares alone) and the zoom tier (the display's `zoomFetchArgs()` object). `fetchRegions` captures… - `regionPayloads: ReadonlyMap`: The store's payloads, keyed by `displayedRegionIndex`. A display narrows this once — `get rpcDataMap() { return self.regionPayloads as ReadonlyMap }` — and every reader it already had goes on reading a map. - `hasRegionData: boolean`: A fetch has landed: at least one region's payload is in the store. The render callback's first-paint gate reads this, so an empty frame before any data cannot flip `canvasDrawn`; an empty but loaded region counts, and paints its empty… - `staleSettingsDrawn: boolean`: A visible block's held data was fetched under a settings or adapter key that has since moved: drawn, and wrong for the current settings, until the refetch `isCacheValid` already owes lands. The loading scrim's third staleness term, beside… - `dataCurrent: boolean`: This family's answer to the shared freshness question every display foundation must answer (`dataCurrent`): the held data corresponds to what is on screen right now. Four terms — spatial coverage of every visible block,… - `loadedAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly the data in hand came from, once it can answer about refNames — `undefined` before that. - `phaseViewportCurrent: boolean`: The loading scrim's staleness argument: what is drawn answers for what is on screen. Spatial coverage, `dataSuperseded` and `staleSettingsDrawn`; not `isCacheValid`, which belongs to `dataCurrent` and would scrim every zoom. `displayPhase`… - `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it… - `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook with `staleSettingsDrawn`, so `painted` — and `data-display-drawn` through it — reads pending over a canvas painted under the previous settings until the refetch lands, without blanking anything. - `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active - `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished… - `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off. - `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the… - `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,… - `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it… - `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track. - `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —… - `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false. - `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default. - `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot. - `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and… - `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only… - `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view. - `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button. - `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured. - `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops… - `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`. - `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it. - `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`. - `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act. - `regionTooLarge: boolean` - `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large. - `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate. - `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen. - `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets. - `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's. - `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame… - `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page. - `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel` - `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record; }>` - `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null` - `adapterConfig: Record` - `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible. - `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the singular word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants". - `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features. - `liveNotices: string[]`: Notices from the loaded data beside the config, such as a field no fetched feature has. Empty unless a display overrides it. - `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor. - `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`. - `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config. - `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`. - `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip. - `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons. - `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes. ## Properties - `type = types.literal('LinearMafDisplay')` - `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)` - `runClustering = types.maybe(types.boolean)`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `LinearGenomeView`'s `init`: a session or config sets this true and the real clustering RPC runs once automatically, with no dialog, as soon as the display reports itself ready.… - `clusterRegion = types.maybe(types.string)`: Where that run reads from, as a locstring (whitespace-separated for several). Clustering is region-scoped, so naming the locus lets a session cluster on the signal and then show it against its context. Cleared with `runClustering`, since… - `sortRowsBy = types.maybe(types.frozen())`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `runClustering`: set `{refName, pos}` to order the rows once by the value each row has at that genomic column — the session-expressible form of the right-click "Sort rows by ... here".… - `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members - `id = ElementId` ## Methods - `contextMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Items for the right-click menu, built from the column under the click. Captured when the menu opens, since `closeContextMenu` runs before an item's onClick. - `rowGeometry() => MafRowGeometryParams`: Where the rows sit on screen: the resolved row height plus the scroll offset and viewport. Every rows layer reads this one method, so no layer draws from the raw `rowHeight` sentinel or omits the scroll offset. - `rpcProps() => { rowFocus: string[] | undefined; interbaseIndicators: InterbaseIndicatorRule; }`: The fetch inputs both tiers send through `rpcArgs` and cache under. The focus is a row set since the worker ships only those genomes; the row order is not, since the client places the rows. No fetch-derived state belongs here… - `rowNavigationTargets(displayedRegionIndex: number, startBp: number, endBp: number, startRow: number, endRow: number) => RowNavigationTarget[]`: Where the rows `[startRow, endRow)` sit in their genomes across the reference bp range `[startBp, endBp)`, the loci an "open this species here" navigation targets. A row contributes nothing with no aligned base in the range, no fetched… - `frameHoverInfo(displayedRegionIndex: number, bp: number, rowIndex: number) => { name: string; } | undefined`: The CDS frame record covering absolute genomic `bp` (uint32) on display `rowIndex`, or undefined. Gated on `framesInUse`, so the gene name reads on hover in codon view with the strip off. - `coverageBandHit(displayedRegionIndex: number, x: number, y: number) => CoverageBandHit | undefined`: The interbase bar or indicator triangle under a canvas point in the coverage band, through the shared band's own hit test, or undefined for the depth area and everywhere else. - `coverageTooltipBin(displayedRegionIndex: number, basePos: number, bpPerPx: number, reversed?: boolean) => { identity: number; position: number; depth: number; fwdDepth?: number…`: The depth and SNP tooltip bin at the base under the cursor, with the percent identity at that position. Undefined when the region has no fetched data or depth is zero. - `interbaseTooltipBin(displayedRegionIndex: number, position: number) => { interbase: Record string[]`: The schema's rules, then what the rows cannot paint as written: a coverage layer filter test its layer does not make, a codon color with no reading frames, and a range on a field that paints the theme's colors. - `rowHoverInfo(displayedRegionIndex: number, bp: HoverBp, rowIndex: number, bpPerPx: number) => {…} | { sampleLabel: string; kind: "insertion"; length: number; sequence: str…`: The hover on `rowIndex` at the cursor's genomic position: an aligned base, an insertion, a deletion or a bridged region, tagged with the sample label. `bp` holds both readings of the cursor (`HoverBp`), which differ on a reversed region. - `identityHoverInfo(displayedRegionIndex: number, bp: number, rowIndex: number) => { identity: number; bases: number; } | undefined`: The mean identity of the window a heatmap cell or X-Y bar paints at base `bp` on `rowIndex`, and how many bases it averages, while identity draws. - `colorScalesIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: `colorScales` in another theme: the SVG export's, whose codon and CDS-frame swatches follow it. - `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]` - `rowsEncodePropsIn(colorPalette: MafColorPalette) => MafRowsEncodeProps`: What a region's rows encode reads beyond the region, in a given palette, since the SVG export's theme need not be the session's. A mode flip lives here so it re-encodes every region as a declared input. - `rowsEncodeProps() => MafRowsEncodeProps`: `rowsEncodePropsIn` in the session's palette, for the on-screen encode. - `codonHoverInfo(displayedRegionIndex: number, bp: number, rowIndex: number) => CodonHit | undefined`: The codon under the cursor on `rowIndex` at base `bp`, while the codon view draws, from the codons its cells were encoded from. - `conservationHoverInfo(displayedRegionIndex: number, bp: number) => { codons: boolean; start: number; end: number; identity: number; } | undefined`: The conservation bar painted over base `bp`, read from the bars the band draws, so a binned window or a codon answers as it paints. - `summaryHoverInfo(rowIndex: number, x: number) => MafSummaryRecord | undefined`: The summary record whose bar is drawn at canvas x `x` on display row `rowIndex`, or undefined: the hover on the summary tier. - `expandRows(rows: S[]) => S[]`: Overridable hook: the discovered rows as the rows drawn, the rows themselves by default; a variant display's phased mode expands each sample to its haplotypes. - `svgSidebarWidth(text?: ExportTextStyle | undefined) => number`: Px the SVG export reserves left of the track for `svgSidebar`, measured in the export's text. - `rowBand(row: S) => string`: Overridable hook: the band a row stacks in while `rowBanding` is set, by default its value of the banding field, '' for none. - `rowColorDeclaredValues(_field: string) => readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the values of the row field `field` the config declares, which the palette deals first, in this order, whether or not a loaded row carries them, so a row arriving later moves no color. None by default. - `dealtValueColorsFor(setting: RowColorSnapshot) => ReadonlyMap`: The color each value takes under `setting` (`dealValueColors`), which the arrangement dialog shows before it writes the setting. - `rowColorFor(choice: string) => RowColorSetting`: The `rowColor` object `choice` starts from (`startingRowColor`): the current object's where it shows that choice, else the config's. - `orderDropsRowTree(order: readonly string[]) => boolean`: Whether ordering the rows as `order` drops the tree: one a reorder rotates drops only for an order no rotation of it lists, and any other drops for any change. - `rowOrderWillDropTree(next: readonly { name: string; }[]) => boolean`: Whether the arrangement dialog's submit of `next` drops the tree: an order that moves no row is not written, so it drops nothing. - `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined` - `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme. - `regionHasData(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the display can draw what this region is marked loaded over, at the zoom the view has. - `isCacheValid(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Whether the data held for a region still answers the current view. Not a hook a display fills: a display states its rule as `zoomFetchArgs` (what a fetch now would send the worker) and `regionHasData` (does what the last one stored still… - `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act. - `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method. - `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks - `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged. - `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can. - `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

LinearManhattanDisplay.text:
# LinearManhattanDisplay (Display model, gwas plugin)

The mark display with the LD join: an index SNP each fetch joins r² to, picked once from the top hit, and the menus that color the points by it.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearManhattanDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes LinearMarkDisplay, FacetWritesMixin, HiddenGroupsMixin, StoredHoverMixin, ContextMenuMixin, LegendMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin, RowHeightMixin, TreeSidebarMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setIndexSnp(snp?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setLdColoring(on: boolean) => void`: Color each point by its r² to the index SNP, the index a pink diamond over them, or take that coloring off, leaving every other member and mark of the plot as it was (`withLd`, `withoutLd`). Turning it on picks the top hit on screen as the…
- `colorByLdToHit(hit: { refName: string; start: number; }) => void`: Right-click "Color by LD to this SNP": color by r² to the clicked point as the index, in one action so the fetch inputs settle once.
- `setIndexSnpToTopHit() => void`: Make the top hit on screen the index.
- `setSourceListing(read: AdapterRead<RowSourceListing | null>) => void`
- `setRowProportion(n: number) => void`: Write every sized span's `mark.height.band`; a band-0 span stays the line it draws.
- `setFitToHeight() => void`: Fit the rows to the plot. The `height` getter is the slot itself, so nothing needs seeding on the way in.
- `toggleCategory(field: string, values: readonly string[]) => void`: Hide a key row's categories, or show them all again where any is hidden: `field` the color's, `''` under an identity color.
- `showAllCategories() => void`
- `selectFeature(hit: MarkHitInfo) => void`: Open the feature widget on the read, the bin or the run a hit drew, inside its facet section, through `selectEncodedFeature`.
- `setRpcData(idx: number, data: EncodedLayersResult, region: Region) => void`: Stage a region as fetched, with this display's payload layout.
- `setShowRowSeparators(show: boolean) => void`
- `applyDefaultPlot(plot: DefaultPlot) => void`: Write a default plot: its marks, its axis, a row per value of its `rows` field where nothing splits the features yet, and its color where the display states none.
- `sortRowsByValueAt(refName: string, pos: number) => boolean`: Order the rows by what `rowCompare` reads over (refName, pos), off the loaded regions with no refetch: values and ramped numbers highest first, a span's categories in blocks of one category, the largest on screen first and then in the…
- `setFilter(filters?: string[] | undefined) => void`: Write the `filter` list's expressions; undefined returns them to what the track's config declares.
- `setPlotFields(fields?: PlotFields | undefined, error?: unknown) => void`
- `setPlotDefaultChecked() => void`
- `setPlotFieldsPromise(promise?: Promise<PlotFields> | undefined, scanned?: Region[]) => void`
- `ensurePlotFields() => Promise<PlotFields>`: Scan the features for the fields a plot can read. A scan that found a numeric field answers for the display's life; one that found none answers only for the window it read, and a failed one for nothing. A scan a newer one aborted answers…
- `openPlotDialog(seed?: Plot | undefined, seedOptions?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => void`: Open the plot as text, over the same settings the controls write. `seed` overlays a setting the caller has in hand but has not applied.
- `setPointSize(val?: number | undefined) => void`: Write every point mark's `encoding.size` number; undefined returns each to the default.
- `pinDistinctShapes() => void`: The ordinal analogue of the min/max dialog's "Use current range": every value a colliding shape key lists goes into the shape's `scale.domain`, in key order after what it already lists, so each takes a separate shape.
- `openMarkPlotDialog(seed?: Plot | undefined) => void`: Open the plot as controls: every mark, the channels its type reads, and what the rules say under each. The field scan runs behind it, as it does for the field dialog.
- `openPlotForm(draft: Plot) => void`: The text box's "Back to form", opened on its draft.
- `fetchNeeded(needed: IndexedRegion[]) => Promise<void>`: Fetch each needed region widened to the edges of the widest bin a shared step or a mark drawing at this zoom cuts, so no bin a drawn mark plots is cut at the fetch edge.
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: MarkRenderingBackend) => void`: identity encode — the stored payload is what the backend uploads
- `decideDefaultPlot() => Promise<void>`: Scan the current window, and write the default plot off it where the window holds features and nothing has been declared meanwhile. A failed scan is the error of a display with nothing to draw; a declared plot draws on, and the next window…
- `renderSvg(opts?: ExportSvgDisplayOptions | undefined) => Promise<ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | AwaitedReactNode>`
- `facetByField(field: string) => void`: Split the sections by `field`, `''` for none, keeping the order and hidden sections while it is the field already grouping.
- `setFacetSort(sort: readonly string[]) => void`: The order the sections take, the ones it names first; `[]` sorts them all.
- `hideGroup(key: string) => void`: Drop a section from the stack. Reversed by `showAllGroups`, which the "Show" menu offers while anything is hidden, since a hidden section has no chip to restore it.
- `showAllGroups() => void`
- `dropGroupState() => void`: Overridable hook: forget the volatile per-group state a display keeps. A no-op by default, since the hidden sections are config.
- `setHoveredFeature(hit?: T | undefined) => void`
- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`
- `openContextMenu(info: Info) => void`
- `closeContextMenu() => void`
- `setShowLegend(arg: boolean) => void`: Writes the slot, and showing the legend again restores the sections closed inside it.
- `dismissLegendSection(id: string) => void`: Close one section of the legend, leaving the others up.
- `setScaleType(scaleType: string) => void`
- `setScaleZero(zero: boolean) => void`
- `setFenceQuantile(quantile: number) => void`
- `setDomainMin(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setDomainMax(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setMinScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMin`.
- `setMaxScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMax`.
- `setAutoscaleGroup(group?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setScoreRules(rules: (number | ValueScaleRule)[]) => void`: Replaces the y scale's rules whole, each entry in a form the config takes: a number, or `{ value, color, label }`.
- `resetYScale() => void`: Back to what the config.json says, or to what a session-owned track was added with, so an admin's declared axis survives a reset; slots the base leaves unset take their defaults.
- `setRowHeight(n: number) => void`: Pin a px row height. `0` is the fit sentinel, but enter fit mode through `setFitToHeight` instead — displays whose `height` getter is content-derived have to re-seed the slot on the way in, and that is what the action is for.
- `setShowTree(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowBranchLength(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowRowLabels(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setTreeAreaWidth(width: number) => void`
- `setRunClustering(arg?: boolean | undefined) => void`
- `setClusterRegion(arg?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setSortRowsBy(arg?: RowSortSpec | undefined) => void`: Trigger (or clear) a one-shot declarative row sort; consumed and reset by `setupRowSortAutorun`.
- `setHoveredTreeNode(node?: HoveredTreeNode | undefined) => void`
- `setTreeCanvasRef(ref: HTMLCanvasElement | null) => void`
- `setMouseoverCanvasRef(ref: HTMLCanvasElement | null) => void`
- `setRowOrder(rows: readonly { name: string; }[], run?: ClusterRun | undefined) => void`: Arrange the rows in `rows`' order, ahead of any name the current order has that `rows` does not. A clustering run passes its result, and the tree and its provenance land with the order; any other reorder that moves a row drops the tree,…
- `setRowLabels(labels: Readonly<Record<string, string>>) => void`: The labels drawn in place of row names, whole: a row the map does not name shows the name it arrived with.
- `setRowFocus(names?: readonly string[] | undefined) => void`: Narrow the display to `names`, or show every row again.
- `applyRowEdits(rows: readonly S[], rowColor?: RowColorSnapshot | undefined) => void`: The arrangement dialog's submit: the rows in their new order, each with the label the reader left on it, and the `rowColor` object the dialog shows, written where it differs from the config's. The labels go to `rows` by the rule…
- `resetRowArrangement() => void`: Return every arrangement member — order, labels, tree, provenance and focus — to what the config declares, leaving `rows.field`, and the `rowColor` colors to `rowColorResetTarget`: the config's for the choice, which stays.
- `setRowColorChoice(choice: string) => void`: Color the rows by `choice`, as a menu picks it: '' for None, `name` for Each row, or a field, starting from `rowColorFor`. A pick of the current choice writes nothing.
- `focusLegendEntry(scaleId: string, value: string) => void`: `LegendHost`'s hook: a click on a row color key entry narrows the rows to those it lists. Every other scale's entries name colors, not rows, and stay inert.
- `setLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number, region: Region, payload: {} | undefined, fetchInputs?: FetchInputs) => void`: The raw write behind `ctx.commitRegion`, and **not what a fetch should call**. A display naming its span itself is the bug this family spent a release fixing, and the context gives a fetch no way to express it — see RegionFetchContext.…
- `evictRegionStore(keep: ReadonlySet<number>) => void`: The store's bound. Drops the entries a fetch can no longer be about: an index outside the view's buffered viewport, once the store is over `MAX_STORED_REGIONS`, oldest first.
- `dropLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`: Forget one region, as `evictRegionStore` does past its cap. Tests use it to stage an evicted region.
- `clearDisplaySpecificData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds beside the store — a second store, a verdict about the viewport that was just dropped. Called by `clearAllRpcData`, which runs on a displayed-regions change, on a viewport move…
- `clearSettingsBakedData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds that is wrong under a changed setting rather than merely stale — a payload whose shape the setting decides. Called by `invalidateSettings`, where `clearDisplaySpecificData` is…
- `clearAllRpcData() => void`: full reset: cancels fetch, clears error, loadedRegions, display-specific data, and the canvas-drawn flag. The too-large gate is derived (a pure function of the cached estimate × viewport), so it needs no explicit clear here — the fetch…
- `invalidateSettings() => void`: `SettingsInvalidate`'s reset: the half of `clearAllRpcData` a settings change still needs now that the settings and adapter axes are in `fetchInputs`. The in-flight fetch is superseded now rather than when its payload lands stamped stale,…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter) plus the full reset. Subclasses with extra teardown override and chain.
- `fetchRegions(needed: IndexedRegion[], work: (ctx: RegionFetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a per-region fetch. The work callback calls `ctx.commitRegion` as it stores each region's payload, which is what marks it loaded — see RegionFetchContext for why this function no longer does that itself. Only the three helpers in…
- `afterAttach() => void`: installs the fetch-lifecycle autoruns (DisplayedRegionsChange, FetchVisibleRegions, SettingsInvalidate, ClearBlockingStateOnViewportChange)
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
