## Getters
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: No byte gate: a Manhattan plot's case is a genome-wide view of summary statistics, which a region budget would refuse.
- `ldAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown> | undefined`: The `ldAdapter` on the track's `GWASAdapter`, or undefined for none. Read off the live track, since `self.adapterConfig` is a snapshot, which leaves out a slot at its default.
- `hasLdData: boolean`
- `joinsLd: boolean`: Whether a fetch joins r² to the index: the plot names `r2` or `ld_role` anywhere the worker reads, an expression or a filter included, and the adapter has an LD file to read them from. Without one, a plot reads `r2` off the features like…
- `ldColored: boolean`: Whether "Color by LD to index SNP" is on: a mark's encoding names an LD field, which is what the item writes and takes off.
- `joinedPlotFields: { numeric: string[]; categorical: string[]; }`: The two fields the LD join writes, for Edit plot to offer.
- `ldColorable: boolean`: Whether "Color by LD to index SNP" has a point mark to color.
- `topSnp: string | undefined`: The highest-scoring SNP on screen, as a 1-based `chr:bp`. `GWASAdapter` reports each region's top hits off the file, so no filter, zoom gate or mark of the plot moves it. A fetch reaches past the screen and a region scrolled off screen…
- `settledTopSnp: string | undefined`: `topSnp` once the load covering the screen is complete, or undefined: mid-batch, `topSnp` is the best of what has arrived.
- `adapterOptions: { ld: string; } | undefined`: The index the fetch joins r² to, a fetch input, so picking one refetches. No index exists until the first load provides a top hit.
- `indexPending: boolean`: The plot joins LD and no index is picked yet, though the loaded data names a top hit: the one-time pick is due, and its refetch with it.
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: `MultiRegionDisplayMixin`'s supersession hook, true while the mark display's row listing is unsettled or the index pick is due.
- `displayNotices: string[]`: The notices the display shows. Where the plot joins LD, it shows one when no point on screen lies in the LD window of the index, so none can be colored by it.
- `conf: LinearMarkDisplayConfig`: the config typed off the concrete schema
- `prefersOffset: boolean`: the track label sits above the plot so the y-axis stays on the edge
- `menusOfferPlotFields: boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the track menu offers the scanned fields, so a declared plot still scans, and rescans while it holds none.
- `markTypes: ("bar" | "line" | "link" | "point" | "rect" | "rule" | "text")[]`: The declared marks' types, in draw order.
- `declaredFacet: FacetSetting | undefined`: The `facet` object as written, or undefined while unfaceted.
- `rowGroups: RowGroup[]`: The `rowGroups` entries, each slot filled in.
- `rowAttributeFields: readonly string[]`: The fields a row carries beside its name, which a facet bands the rows by: `group` where `rowGroups` declares groups. Config alone, so whether a facet bands or splits is known before a feature loads.
- `bandsRows: boolean`: Whether the facet stacks the rows in bands: `rows` drawn and the facet on a row attribute.
- `facet: FacetSetting | undefined`: The facet the worker splits the features into sections by: `declaredFacet`, unless it bands the rows, which are split by `rows` alone and banded here.
- `groupKeySpace: string`: `HiddenGroupsMixin`'s hook: a section key means nothing outside the facet that issued it, so moving the field drops what was hidden.
- `markEntries: MarkEntry[]`: Each mark's type and zoom range, what the mark list is built from.
- `textMarkEntries: TextMarkEntry[]`: Each mark as the text layer places it: the entry with whether it names a `y` and whether its color is written, a constant or a scale. Its own getter so a slot only a label reads never remakes the mark list.
- `markView: MarkView`: The marks at the view's zoom: whether each draws, inside its `minBpPerPx`..`maxBpPerPx` range where 0 is no bound.
- `markSizes: number[]`: Each mark's px, a point's `encoding.size` or a stroked mark's `encoding.strokeWidth` number, its type's default where none is written, and 0 for a bar, span or text, which draw none.
- `markRowProportions: number[]`: Each mark's `mark.height.band`, which a span alone reads.
- `rowProportion: number | undefined`: The proportion the Row height dialog shows: the first sized span's, or undefined where no span has a height, so the dialog asks for none.
- `hasLinkMark: boolean`: Whether any mark is a link, whose feet place through the view's regions rather than the block's own range.
- `pointSize: number`: The size the Point size menu shows: the first point mark's, or the default where no mark is a point.
- `encodings: MarkEncoding[]`: The declared marks' encodings, as the worker takes them.
- `sharedSteps: MarkTransformConfig[]`: The steps every mark runs before its own `transform`: the display's, then the facet's.
- `markStepLists: MarkTransformConfig[][]`: The steps that run before each mark's encode, in order: the display's, the facet's, then the mark's own.
- `markChannels: StepChannels[]`: The channels each mark's steps fill where its encoding leaves them unwritten.
- `markColors: ColorSource[]`: Where each mark's color comes from (`markColor.ts`), read from the config alone, so editing a color recolors the loaded regions rather than fetching them again.
- `facetSteps: TransformStep[]`: The facet's own steps as the worker takes them, run over each section before any mark's; with no field to split on they run over the one section there is, after the display's own steps.
- `layerRequests: LayerRequest[]`: The worker request, one layer per mark: its encoding and the lanes its type reads. Every mark is sent, the one outside its zoom range included, so the worker encodes a layer the view will not draw: measured at 280 ns a feature, 28 ms per…
- `origin: number`
- `configuredFilters: () => string[]`: The `jexl:` expressions the `filter` list holds.
- `filterSteps: TransformStep[]`: The `filter` list as the worker's steps: each expression its own step, and the field tests one step of predicates.
- `baseFilters: () => string[]`: The expressions the track's config declares, which "Clear all filters" returns to.
- `rowsField: string`: `rows.field` as written: the field each value of which takes a row.
- `showRowSeparators: boolean`: Whether a line runs between rows, `axis.grid`.
- `drawsRows: boolean`: Whether the display draws one row per value: a `rows` field and no `facet` splitting the features, which draws in the rows' place.
- `splitField: string | undefined`: The field the worker splits the features on: the facet's, else the rows'. One split serves both, so `rows` sends it as `facet`.
- `rowGroupMatchers: CompiledRowGroup[]`: The `rowGroups` entries whose `match` compiles.
- `rowBanding: RowBanding | undefined`: `TreeSidebarMixin`'s hook: the facet's bands where it bands the rows, its `sort` first and then the `rowGroups` groups in the order they are declared.
- `featurePayloads: ReadonlyMap<number, MarkRegionData>`: The layers as they came back, keyed by displayedRegionIndex: the foundation's per-region store.
- `rowListing: RowSourceListing | undefined`: The adapter's row listing where it names the rows drawn: its field is `rows.field`, or the key a `flatten` in the shared steps wrote over its field. Undefined for an adapter that lists no rows, for one that lists another field, and until…

- `adapterSources: ListedRowSource[] | undefined`: The sources the adapter lists whatever a region holds, a multi-BigWig's files or a MAF's species, in the adapter's order.
- `guideTreeNewick: string | undefined`: `TreeSidebarMixin`'s hook: the guide tree the adapter lists over the rows, a MAF's species tree.
- `discoveredRows: RowSource[]`: `TreeSidebarMixin`'s hook: every row the adapter lists over the rows' field, in its order and with its label and color, so a source with nothing in the loaded regions keeps its row; then the other values the worker split the loaded regions…

- `rowKeys: RowKeys`: `rowKeySpace`'s keys.
- `facetLayout: FacetLayout`: The sections drawn over every loaded region, in the domain's order and less the hidden ones, and where each key's rows start; under `rows`, one row per value in the rows' order, which no chip names.
- `rpcDataMap: ReadonlyMap<number, MarkRegionData>`: The layers the display draws. Under a facet or `rows` every row is a key the row table places, so a chip and the band beside it agree whichever region a span came from, and a reorder, a focus, a hidden section or a deeper section moves no…

- `scaleDataMap: ReadonlyMap<number, MarkRegionData>`: `rpcDataMap` with each layer's key and extents over the instances the row table draws, its lanes shared: what the legend, the axis and the size scales read, so a row the focus or a hidden section hides leaves them as it leaves the plot.

- `highlightedHit: MarkHitInfo | undefined`: The mark the hover or the open context menu is on, or undefined.

- `showBranchLength: boolean`: Whether the tree draws nodes at their branch length (dendrogram) or evenly by topology (cladogram).
- `showRowLabels: boolean`: Whether each row's name is drawn over the left of the plot.

- `rowNoun: string`: Overridable hook: what one row is called, which titles the row color key where it lists the rows by name in a shared panel. "Row" by default, which only a display that shares a panel would show; a wiggle overlay's rows are subtracks.
- `internalRowFields: readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the row fields that are display plumbing, which the arrangement dialog never lists as a column.
- `rowColorFields: readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the row fields a reader can color the rows by, offered beside None and Each row. By default every field a row has but its name, label and colors.
- `rowBandingNotices: string[]`: A line for the corner notice when rows have arrived and none has the field `rowBanding` bands by, which then bands nothing. Each display spreads it into its `notices`.
- `rowPaletteDeals: boolean`: Whether the palette deals each row a color by name: only where the rows share one panel and their color paints the marks.
- `rowColorDealRows: readonly S[]`: The rows the palette deals over: `expandedRows`, in the order their source lists them, so no `rows.sort` (the config's or a reorder's), focus or relabel recolors a row, and a tables export deals the same.
- `rowColorIsCustom: boolean`: Whether `rowColor` gives its field's values colors the config does not, so "Reset row order" is offered for a recolor too: whether `rowColorResetTarget` has anything to write. A choice of row color source is no arrangement, so it is never…
- `rowColorChoice: string`: The choice of what colors the rows, as the arrangement dialog and a menu offer it: '' for none dealt, `name` for a palette color each, or a field.
- `rowColorField: string`: The field that colors the rows, or '' for `name`.
- `dealtValueColors: ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: The color each value of the config's `rowColor` field takes, listed pairs first and then in the order dealt.
- `rowColorFieldsOffered: readonly string[]`: The fields a reader can color the rows by: `rowColorFields`, and the current one where the rows lack it, so it still shows as chosen.
- `resolvedRowColors: ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: Each row's color, by name: its `rowColor` entry, else the row's `color`, else the palette's where `rowPaletteDeals`. The one answer every display paints a row's color from.
- `rowArrangementIsCustom: boolean`: Whether the arrangement differs from what the config declares — what "Reset row order" is offered on.
- `editableSources: S[]`: The rows in the reader's arrangement, each with its resolved `rowColor`, and with no focus or band: the list the arrangement dialog edits, so a submit writes back only what the reader chose. `expandedRows` itself while nothing is arranged…
- `rowColorKeyInputs: RowColorKeyInputs`: What the row color key and its focus read of the colors.
- `rowColorScales: CategoricalScale[]`: The row color key, which every display spreads into its `colorScales`: one scale titled by the `rowColor` field, or none where it has no entries. Its entries (`rowColorKeyEntries`) show where the labels cannot name the colors: by a field,…
- `clusterableSources: S[]`: Overridable hook: `editableSources` narrowed to the focus, the rows a clustering run clusters, and deliberately not the display's decorated `sources`, whose palette and band a run has no business writing back. MAF applies a focus as given…
- `parsedTree: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: `rowTree` parsed. A run rotated its tree in the same write as the order it produced; a tree that arrived as data rotates towards `rows.sort` here, and the guide tree is `guideTree`'s parse.
- `rotatableRowTree: string | undefined`: The tree a reorder rotates rather than drops, as newick: a supplied `rows.tree`, one with no provenance, else the guide tree while `guideTreeHonoursDomain`. A computed tree is never one, since its run rotated it already.
- `root: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: The parsed tree narrowed to the focus.
- `bandedRows: { rows: S[]; bands: RowBand[]; }`: `bandedSources` and `rowBands`, from one pass over the rows.
- `bandedSources: S[]`: `clusterableSources` stacked in bands by `rowBanding`, each band's rows in their arranged order: the rows each display paints its palette over. `clusterableSources` itself while nothing bands.
- `rowBands: readonly RowBand[]`: Each band's value, label and the rows it spans in `bandedSources`; none while nothing bands.
- `sources: S[]`: Overridable hook: the rows drawn, top to bottom, `bandedSources` by default. MAF drops its hidden reference row.
- `treeRoot: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: Overridable hook: the tree `hierarchy` positions, `root` by default. `computeClusterHierarchy` declines to position a tree whose leaves are no longer the rows drawn, so a display that hides a row prunes it from the tree here too, or the…
- `drawsTree: boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the dendrogram draws at all, true by default; off wherever the rows it would lay against are not drawn. This is the single gate: the on-screen sidebar, the SVG export, `spatialIndex` (subtree hover) and the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Fills `FetchMixin`'s hook: a declared `runClustering` run is due, so the loading scrim and the export wait for the rows it orders. The run clears the flag when it settles, failed or not.
- `rowsContentHeight: number`: The px the rows stack to, `sources` × `effectiveRowHeight`, which the dendrogram's leaves spread over: the content the rows scroll through, never the viewport they scroll inside.
- `hierarchy: ClusterHierarchyNode | undefined`: The dendrogram positioned against the rows drawn, or undefined while there is no tree or `drawsTree` is off. `computeClusterHierarchy` checks the tree's leaves against the drawn row names, the backstop against anything reordering `sources`…
- `spatialIndex: TreeSpatialIndex | undefined`: The hit index the sidebar's subtree hover reads, built from `hierarchy`.
- `clusterPartition: string[][] | undefined`: The names of the rows a clustering run clusters, by band, so each band clusters apart and the run writes one forest; undefined while fewer than two bands stack.
- `treelessBandCount: number`: How many bands the tree draws no dendrogram for, because it holds no clade whose leaves are that band's rows in order; 0 with no tree or no bands.
- `treeHasBranchLengths: boolean`: Whether the tree has merge heights, so a dendrogram layout differs from the cladogram; gates the "Tree branch lengths" toggle.
- `host: RegionHost`: The containing LinearGenomeView, typed once for every display in this family — see `containingHost` for the cast it owns and why both foundations still declare the name.
- `canvasWidthPx: number`: The CSS width of this display's on-screen canvas, in px; see `trackCanvasWidthPx`.
- `settledSubPixelBinBp: number`: Genomic bp one cell of a per-base pass stands for at the settled zoom: `subPixelBinBp` off the host's debounced `coarseBpPerPx`, and 1 until the view initializes. A per-base encode or fetch reads this rather than the live zoom so a wheel…
- `canRender: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook with the LGV precondition both foundations share — see `foundationCanRender`.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook off `fetchInert`, as `GlobalFetchMixin` does: a display that will never fetch here shows a placeholder where its canvas would be.
- `trackVisibleRegions: VisibleRegion[]`: The visible blocks on the track's own assemblies, the ones this display fetches and is judged against. A view of several genomes leaves a single-genome track's other regions blank.
- `viewportWithinLoadedData: boolean`: true when every visible block lies within an already-fetched region — i.e. the viewport shows data we actually loaded, not the stale fringe left after a zoom-out/pan. Drives the loading overlay through the pre-refetch debounce.
- `viewportEmpty: boolean`: No content block is on screen, so this display has nothing to fetch and nothing to paint — see `viewportEmpty.ts` for the one viewport that reaches it, how narrow that is, and why the state still has to be terminal rather than a permanent…
- `fetchSuspended: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by the fetch plan: the display is drawing something in the features' place and wants no fetch while it does. `CoarseTierMixin` returns true while its tier stands in, so MAF never downloads the…
- `layoutReady: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): whether a searchable feature layout currently exists. Any display defining a feature-lookup method (`searchFeatureByID`) must override it, so callers can tell "laid out, but off-display" from "no layout…
- `renderBlocks: RenderBlock[]`: Shared cached view for every LGV-based GPU display. A single displayedRegion may produce multiple render blocks (shared GPU buffer, different scissor clips on screen). Plugins that want to suppress rendering in certain states (e.g. no…
- `fetchInputs: FetchInputs`: What a fetch issued right now would stamp on a region: the settings tier (`FetchMixin.settingsFetchInputs`, the tier `staleSettingsDrawn` compares alone) and the zoom tier (the display's `zoomFetchArgs()` object). `fetchRegions` captures…
- `regionPayloads: ReadonlyMap<number, unknown>`: The store's payloads, keyed by `displayedRegionIndex`. A display narrows this once — `get rpcDataMap() { return self.regionPayloads as ReadonlyMap<number, MyResult> }` — and every reader it already had goes on reading a map.
- `hasRegionData: boolean`: A fetch has landed: at least one region's payload is in the store. The render callback's first-paint gate reads this, so an empty frame before any data cannot flip `canvasDrawn`; an empty but loaded region counts, and paints its empty…
- `staleSettingsDrawn: boolean`: A visible block's held data was fetched under a settings or adapter key that has since moved: drawn, and wrong for the current settings, until the refetch `isCacheValid` already owes lands. The loading scrim's third staleness term, beside…
- `dataCurrent: boolean`: This family's answer to the shared freshness question every display foundation must answer (`dataCurrent`): the held data corresponds to what is on screen right now. Four terms — spatial coverage of every visible block,…
- `loadedAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly the data in hand came from, once it can answer about refNames — `undefined` before that.
- `phaseViewportCurrent: boolean`: The loading scrim's staleness argument: what is drawn answers for what is on screen. Spatial coverage, `dataSuperseded` and `staleSettingsDrawn`; not `isCacheValid`, which belongs to `dataCurrent` and would scrim every zoom. `displayPhase`…
- `svgReady: boolean`: true once an off-screen (SVG) export can safely read this display's data. Policy single-sourced in `computeSvgReady`; this family supplies only the freshness half, which `foundationSvgReady` reads as `dataCurrent` or the vacuous currency…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook with `staleSettingsDrawn`, so `painted` — and `data-display-drawn` through it — reads pending over a canvas painted under the previous settings until the refetch lands, without blanking anything.
- `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The display's mutually-exclusive visual state, mapped in `foundationDisplayPhase` — every foundation calls it and supplies only its staleness argument, so a term added to `computeActivityPhase` reaches all three without being wired three…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.
- `regionTooLarge: boolean`
- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.
- `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate.
- `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen.
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `height: number`
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the singular word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants".
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('LinearManhattanDisplay')`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `indexSnp = types.maybe(types.string)`: The index SNP the LD join reads r² to, as a 1-based `chr:bp`. The display picks the top hit on screen once, when a plot first joins LD or LD coloring is turned on; after that only the user moves it.
- `hiddenCategories = types.frozen< readonly HiddenCategory[] | undefined >()`: The categories the key's rows hide, each a value of the field a categorical color reads or a color an identity key lists: session state the Categories menu toggles, applied where the colors resolve, so a toggle refetches nothing. Kept…
- `runClustering = types.maybe(types.boolean)`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `LinearGenomeView`'s `init`: a session or config sets this true and the real clustering RPC runs once automatically, with no dialog, as soon as the display reports itself ready.…
- `clusterRegion = types.maybe(types.string)`: Where that run reads from, as a locstring (whitespace-separated for several). Clustering is region-scoped, so naming the locus lets a session cluster on the signal and then show it against its context. Cleared with `runClustering`, since…
- `sortRowsBy = types.maybe(types.frozen<RowSortSpec>())`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `runClustering`: set `{refName, pos}` to order the rows once by the value each row has at that genomic column — the session-expressible form of the right-click "Sort rows by ... here".…
- `id = ElementId`

## Methods
- `resolveAdapterOptions({ ld }: { ld: string; }, region: Region, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<{ ld: LdJoin; } | undefined>`: The LD join as one region's fetch asks the adapter for it.
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `contextMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `defaultPlotOf(fields: PlotFields) => DefaultPlot | undefined`: Overridable hook: what the display draws with nothing declared, off the scanned fields, or undefined where they decide nothing and the plot dialog opens instead.
- `expandRows(rows: RowSource[]) => RowSource[]`: `TreeSidebarMixin`'s hook: each row tagged with the group of the first `rowGroups` entry its name matches.
- `plotRequest() => { layers: LayerRequest[]; transform: TransformStep[]; facet?: FacetSpec | undefined; }`: The plot as the worker reads it: each mark's encoding and lanes, and the filters as transform steps. Every field and expression the plot names is in it, and `adapterOptions` is not, so a display may derive its options from what the plot…
- `rpcProps() => { layers: LayerRequest[]; transform: TransformStep[]; facet?: FacetSpec; opts?: object; }`: the fetch inputs SettingsInvalidate watches: `plotRequest`, all of it evaluated in the worker, and the `adapterOptions` each region resolves
- `floatingLabels(palette: JBrowsePalette) => FloatingLabel[]`: The text marks' labels as records in the display's own px, for a host that shows the plot canvas but not the text layer over it: a ring of the circular view. Placed and culled as on screen.
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The rule list over a config, as lines. It replaces the schema's rules rather than adding to them, since it checks the colors and `encoding.y` itself.
- `liftMarkPlot(plot: Plot) => MarkPlotSettings`: A draft as the rule list reads it, merged over `plot` and lifted by the config schema, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It changes no state on this display.
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `svgSidebarWidth(text?: ExportTextStyle | undefined) => number`: Px the SVG export reserves left of the track for `svgSidebar`, measured in the export's text.
- `rowBand(row: S) => string`: Overridable hook: the band a row stacks in while `rowBanding` is set, by default its value of the banding field, '' for none.
- `rowColorDeclaredValues(_field: string) => readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the values of the row field `field` the config declares, which the palette deals first, in this order, whether or not a loaded row carries them, so a row arriving later moves no color. None by default.
- `dealtValueColorsFor(setting: RowColorSnapshot) => ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: The color each value takes under `setting` (`dealValueColors`), which the arrangement dialog shows before it writes the setting.
- `rowColorFor(choice: string) => RowColorSetting`: The `rowColor` object `choice` starts from (`startingRowColor`): the current object's where it shows that choice, else the config's.
- `orderDropsRowTree(order: readonly string[]) => boolean`: Whether ordering the rows as `order` drops the tree: one a reorder rotates drops only for an order no rotation of it lists, and any other drops for any change.
- `rowOrderWillDropTree(next: readonly { name: string; }[]) => boolean`: Whether the arrangement dialog's submit of `next` drops the tree: an order that moves no row is not written, so it drops nothing.
- `regionHasData(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the display can draw what this region is marked loaded over, at the zoom the view has.
- `isCacheValid(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Whether the data held for a region still answers the current view. Not a hook a display fills: a display states its rule as `zoomFetchArgs` (what a fetch now would send the worker) and `regionHasData` (does what the last one stored still…
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

LinearMarkDisplay.text:
# LinearMarkDisplay (Display model, marks plugin)

A display declared in config: a list of marks, each with an encoding from feature fields to channels, drawn in order over one score axis from one worker fetch per region.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearMarkDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes FacetWritesMixin, HiddenGroupsMixin, StoredHoverMixin, ContextMenuMixin, LegendMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin, RowHeightMixin, TreeSidebarMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setSourceListing(read: AdapterRead<RowSourceListing | null>) => void`
- `setRowProportion(n: number) => void`: Write every sized span's `mark.height.band`; a band-0 span stays the line it draws.
- `setFitToHeight() => void`: Fit the rows to the plot. The `height` getter is the slot itself, so nothing needs seeding on the way in.
- `toggleCategory(field: string, values: readonly string[]) => void`: Hide a key row's categories, or show them all again where any is hidden: `field` the color's, `''` under an identity color.
- `showAllCategories() => void`
- `selectFeature(hit: MarkHitInfo) => void`: Open the feature widget on the read, the bin or the run a hit drew, inside its facet section, through `selectEncodedFeature`.
- `setRpcData(idx: number, data: EncodedLayersResult, region: Region) => void`: Stage a region as fetched, with this display's payload layout.
- `setShowRowSeparators(show: boolean) => void`
- `applyDefaultPlot(plot: DefaultPlot) => void`: Write a default plot: its marks, its axis, a row per value of its `rows` field where nothing splits the features yet, and its color where the display states none.
- `sortRowsByValueAt(refName: string, pos: number) => boolean`: Order the rows by what `rowCompare` reads over (refName, pos), off the loaded regions with no refetch: values and ramped numbers highest first, a span's categories in blocks of one category, the largest on screen first and then in the…
- `setFilter(filters?: string[] | undefined) => void`: Write the `filter` list's expressions; undefined returns them to what the track's config declares.
- `setPlotFields(fields?: PlotFields | undefined, error?: unknown) => void`
- `setPlotDefaultChecked() => void`
- `setPlotFieldsPromise(promise?: Promise<PlotFields> | undefined, scanned?: Region[]) => void`
- `ensurePlotFields() => Promise<PlotFields>`: Scan the features for the fields a plot can read. A scan that found a numeric field answers for the display's life; one that found none answers only for the window it read, and a failed one for nothing. A scan a newer one aborted answers…
- `openPlotDialog(seed?: Plot | undefined, seedOptions?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => void`: Open the plot as text, over the same settings the controls write. `seed` overlays a setting the caller has in hand but has not applied.
- `setPointSize(val?: number | undefined) => void`: Write every point mark's `encoding.size` number; undefined returns each to the default.
- `pinDistinctShapes() => void`: The ordinal analogue of the min/max dialog's "Use current range": every value a colliding shape key lists goes into the shape's `scale.domain`, in key order after what it already lists, so each takes a separate shape.
- `openMarkPlotDialog(seed?: Plot | undefined) => void`: Open the plot as controls: every mark, the channels its type reads, and what the rules say under each. The field scan runs behind it, as it does for the field dialog.
- `openPlotForm(draft: Plot) => void`: The text box's "Back to form", opened on its draft.
- `fetchNeeded(needed: IndexedRegion[]) => Promise<void>`: Fetch each needed region widened to the edges of the widest bin a shared step or a mark drawing at this zoom cuts, so no bin a drawn mark plots is cut at the fetch edge.
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: MarkRenderingBackend) => void`: identity encode — the stored payload is what the backend uploads
- `decideDefaultPlot() => Promise<void>`: Scan the current window, and write the default plot off it where the window holds features and nothing has been declared meanwhile. A failed scan is the error of a display with nothing to draw; a declared plot draws on, and the next window…
- `renderSvg(opts?: ExportSvgDisplayOptions | undefined) => Promise<ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | AwaitedReactNode>`
- `facetByField(field: string) => void`: Split the sections by `field`, `''` for none, keeping the order and hidden sections while it is the field already grouping.
- `setFacetSort(sort: readonly string[]) => void`: The order the sections take, the ones it names first; `[]` sorts them all.
- `hideGroup(key: string) => void`: Drop a section from the stack. Reversed by `showAllGroups`, which the "Show" menu offers while anything is hidden, since a hidden section has no chip to restore it.
- `showAllGroups() => void`
- `dropGroupState() => void`: Overridable hook: forget the volatile per-group state a display keeps. A no-op by default, since the hidden sections are config.

- `clearHoveredFeature() => void`
