LinearSyntenyView.text:
# LinearSyntenyView (View model, linear-comparative-view plugin)

Stacks a linear genome view per genome, and draws the synteny tracks between adjacent rows as ribbons joining the aligned regions.

Composes SyntenyFadeMixin, SyntenyViewMixin, SyntenyColorsMixin, TrackColorsMixin, ParkedColorMixin, SyntenyFilterMixin, ImportFormSyntenyMixin, DiagonalizeProgressMixin, BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `views` declares the member assemblies (stacked
as linear views) and `tracks` the synteny feature track connecting them with
a ribbon:
```js
{
  type: 'LinearSyntenyView',
  views: [{ assembly: 'hg38' }, { assembly: 'mm10' }],
  tracks: ['hg38_vs_mm10.paf'],
  mark: { interpolate: 'bump' },
  encoding: { color: 'query' },
}
```
The launch keys are `views`, `tracks`, `levelHeights`, `autoDiagonalize`,
`coord` and `collapseEmptyRows`; everything else is a property below and
needs no list to join.

## Actions
- `setNavigation(members: { follow?: boolean | undefined; anchor?: number | undefined; }) => void`: Rewrite members of `navigation`, keeping the rest.
- `setFollowReport(report: Partial<FollowReport>) => void`: Merge into `followReport`. Declared ahead of afterAttach, which installs the follow that calls it.
- `setFollowSynteny(flag: boolean) => void`
- `setFollowAnchorIndex(idx: number) => void`
- `clearClickedFeatures() => void`: Release the clicked ribbon in every band before a band sets a new one: the drawer shows one feature, so one ribbon is outlined
- `holdFollowAnchor<T>(fn: () => T) => T`: Run a navigation of a row as a placement by the follow rather than as a gesture. While following, a gesture on any row makes that row the anchor, and the follow distinguishes a gesture from its placements by root action: whatever `fn`…
- `takeOutRows() => void`
- `reconcileLevels() => void`: Keep exactly one synteny level per gap between adjacent views, growing or shrinking from the end, and both anchors inside the stack.
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => void`
- `setError(e: unknown) => void`
- `setViews(views: SnapshotIn<LinearGenomeViewModel>[]) => void`
- `addView(view: SnapshotIn<LinearGenomeViewModel>) => void`: Push a new genome row. The new trailing level starts with no synteny tracks.
- `removeRow(idx: number) => void`: Drop one genome row and the bands beside it. An interior row leaves one new band between the rows it separated, drawn by a track that connects them where the session has one — a track the removed bands were already showing first, which is…
- `reverseRows() => void`: Flip the stack top to bottom. Every band keeps the pair of rows it draws between, so its tracks stay with it.
- `setScrollZoom(arg: boolean) => void`
- `activateTrackSelector(level: number) => Widget`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string, level?: any) => boolean`
- `showTrack(trackId: string, level?: any, initialSnapshot?: object, displayInitialSnapshot?: DisplayInitialSnapshot, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) =>…`: No-op for a level that doesn't exist, matching hideTrack/toggleTrack.
- `launchTrack(trackId: string, level?: any, initialSnapshot?: object, displayInitialSnapshot?: DisplayInitialSnapshot, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) =>…`: showTrack for a track whose display state model may be lazily loaded: loads it, then shows
- `hideTrack(trackId: string, level?: any) => void`
- `panStack(dx: number) => void`: A band's drag, over `bandGestureRows`. The rows' scrolls nest under this action, so none of them reads as a gesture that would take the anchor.
- `squareView() => void`: Every row onto the rows' average bp/px, each keeping its centre.
- `showAllRegionsAcrossRows(sameScale: boolean) => void`: Every row onto its whole assembly, either all on one bp/px — the coarsest row's fit, so the largest genome fills its pane and the others draw shorter in proportion — or each fit to its pane. `coord.ratio` latches, so the shared scale holds…
- `setRatio(ratio: 1 | undefined) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeAnchorRow(row: number) => void`
- `applySharedScale() => void`: Latch `coord.ratio` and zoom every row onto the shared scale, keeping each row's regions and centre.
- `clearView() => void`: Back to the import form. Drops `launch` too, which `hasSomethingToShow` keys off while there are no rows.
- `compactAllViews() => void`
- `expandAllViews() => void`
- `resizeAllLevelHeights(distance: number, levelIdx?: any, from?: number[]) => number`: Resize every synteny band at once by `scaleBandHeights`, choosing the total so the bar under band `levelIdx` moves by `distance`: the bands down to it take exactly that, and the rest keep their proportion to them. `from` is the heights to…
- `autoScaleLevelHeights() => void`
- `appendRow({ assembly, loc, syntenyTrackId }: { assembly: string; loc?: string; syntenyTrackId?: string; }) => Promise<any> | undefined`: Append an assembly to the bottom of the stack, optionally showing a synteny track on the new level. Returns `launchTrack`'s promise rather than awaiting it, so the action stays synchronous.
- `setInterpolate(interpolate: "bump" | "linear") => void`
- `setCigarMode(arg: "full" | "matches" | "off") => void`
- `setAxisGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setOffscreenDrawn(drawn: boolean) => void`
- `setOverdrawPx(arg: number) => void`
- `showAllRegions() => void`: Every row back to its whole assembly, fit to the row's width, which also clears `coord.ratio`.
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<LinearSyntenyViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `exportSvg(opts?: ExportSvgOptions) => Promise<string>`
- `openInCircularSyntenyView() => void`: a circular view of this view's two genomes with its synteny tracks as ribbons, the second genome reordered to follow the first, and this view's color and length filter
- `setAntialias(antialias: boolean | undefined) => void`
- `setFadeThinLatch(arg: boolean) => void`: Move the latched 'auto' thin-fade decision — `installAutoFadeLatch` is the only caller.
- `setResolution(resolution: LodMode) => void`
- `setShowLegend(show: boolean) => void`: The legend host's setter: closing the key hides it for this mode only, so picking another mode brings its key up.
- `setLegendShow(show: boolean) => void`: The "Show legend" checkbox: writes `legend.show`, and showing it brings back a key closed in this mode.
- `dismissLegendSection() => void`: One section is the whole key here.
- `setOpacity(value: number) => void`: The opacity slider: the constant, or under a field its range scaled so its most opaque end equals `value`.
- `setOpacityField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Fade by `field` from the current opacity down to 0.3 of it, or with undefined draw every alignment at the opacity the fade reached.
- `observeAttributeRanges(ranges: Record<string, AttributeRange>) => void`: Fold one fetch's observed attribute spans into the domain this view paints and labels its ramps with. Called by each display as its fetch lands, because the accumulation has to outlive the payload it came from: the previous window's span…
- `resetAttributeRanges() => void`: Forget the accumulated domain, leaving `attributeRanges` reporting what the loaded fetches cover and nothing else.
- `setHideUnlabelled(value: boolean) => void`
- `setColorField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Set the field the view paints by over `encoding.color`, undefined unsetting it for the view's default, and rescale the ramp, which is the only way back from a domain one outlying window widened.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every alignment `value`, undefined returning to the view's default.
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: The picker Color by's Solid color... opens.
- `setColorDomain(domain: string[]) => void`: Declare the order a text column's labels take. The labels listed lead, the rest follow sorted; an empty list gives back the order the fetches found them in.
- `setTrackColor(trackId: string, value: string | undefined) => void`: Pin one track's color under `encoding.color: 'track'`, or release it back to an automatic palette slot.
- `clearTrackColors() => void`
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setFilter(predicates: FieldPredicate[]) => void`
- `setLowerBound(field: string, value: number) => void`: The slider on one field: `field` at least `value`, or no lower bound at 0.
- `setImportFormSyntenyTrack(idx: number, val: ImportFormSyntenyTrack) => void`
- `clearImportFormSyntenyTracks() => void`: Drop the pending selections once a launch has applied them. Left in place they outlive the form: "Return to import form" would reopen on a finished upload from the previous launch, and a pair whose assemblies no longer match it reads as an…
- `setAwaitingAutoDiagonalize(arg: boolean) => void`
- `beginAutoDiagonalize(requested: boolean) => void`: Declare the gate at the top of one init apply pass: a reorder is pending iff THIS init asked for one. Assigning rather than raising is what hands the gate over cleanly — a superseded init that asked for a reorder and then skipped it would…
- `finishAutoDiagonalize() => void`: A reorder resolved, the init's or a manual one, so the view on screen is the diagonalized one — open the gate.
- `setDiagonalizeError(error: unknown) => void`
- `setDiagonalizeCancel(arg?: (() => void) | undefined) => void`
- `cancelAutoDiagonalize() => void`: Abort an in-flight auto-diagonalize; `withDiagonalizeProgress`'s finally clears the wait flag, revealing the (undiagonalized) view.
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `followSynteny: boolean`: `navigation.follow`
- `followAnchorIndex: number`: `navigation.anchor`
- `bandGestureRows: LinearGenomeView[]`: The rows a drag or a wheel on a band moves: every row the follow cannot place. Off, that is every row; on, it is the anchor and any row whose level toward the anchor has no synteny track.
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: scroll-to-zoom is a global, personal preference resolved from the session; toggling it in any view applies everywhere
- `initialized: boolean`
- `error: unknown`: The view's own failure or the first failed row's, so an export or launcher waiting on a stack with a failed row is told why.
- `stackError: unknown`: The failure that leaves the stack nothing to show: the view's own, or every row's. One failed row reports itself in its place in the stack.
- `assemblyNames: string[]`
- `axisGrid: boolean`: `axis.grid`: whether the ruler ticks run down through the bands.
- `offscreenDrawn: boolean`: Whether the `offscreen` part draws.
- `cigarMode: "full" | "matches" | "off"`: How the `indels` part draws: `off`, `matches` (gaps) or `full`.
- `sharedFit: SharedFit`: The zoom-out limit every row shares while `coord.ratio` is 1 (`sharedFit.ts`). Each row reads it through its `maxBpPerPx`, detecting this view by the presence of this getter.
- `ratio: 1 | undefined`: `coord.ratio`: 1 while every row is held at one bp/px.
- `interpolate: "bump" | "linear"`: The curve every ribbon side takes, `mark.interpolate`.
- `allSyntenyDisplays: LinearSyntenyDisplayModel[]`: Every synteny display across every level.
- `hiddenFeatureCount: number`
- `followPairs: { level: LinearSyntenyViewHelper; stayingView: LinearGenomeView; movingView: LinearGenomeView; toMate: boolean; mateAssembly: string; }[]`: Each connected synteny level resolved into the pair of rows a follow moves it between: which row stays, which moves, which axis the anchor window is read off, and the assembly naming the level's lane of an all-vs-all track.
- `trackWarnings: TrackWarning[]`: Every synteny display's data-quality warnings (e.g. a reversed assembly row order), grouped under the track that raised each: what the header's warning button counts and its dialog reports.
- `trackContainers: TrackContainer[]`: Every band's track list, for a reader walking the session for displays.
- `ownTracks: { configuration: { trackId: string; }; displays: { type: string; configuration: AnyConfigurationModel; }[]; }[]`: Every track in the view, across its bands.
- `ownViews: LinearGenomeView[]`
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<LinearSyntenyViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; malformed?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean…`: the launch state that still has something to apply — the gate the loading and import-form paths below read.
- `hasSomethingToShow: boolean`
- `initPending: boolean`: A launch that has not finished applying: the rows can exist, and be initialized, while the synteny tracks are still several awaits away. The levels' `settled` gate reads it.
- `showAssemblyNameInSubviewScalebar: boolean`: Opts each row's scalebar into captioning its refName labels with the assembly name ("hg38" ahead of "chr1"). Read duck-typed by the child LinearGenomeView.
- `hasCigarData: boolean`: Whether any synteny display could show CIGAR detail, which gates the CIGAR setting. True while no display has fetched yet, and false with no synteny tracks.
- `presentCigarKinds: number`: Union across loaded displays of the CIGAR indel ops drawn on screen, which the legend lists chips for.
- `autoFadeWidthPx: number`: The width 'auto' compares against its thresholds: the narrowest capped mean block width of any loaded display with at least `FADE_AUTO_MIN_FEATURES` blocks, or `Infinity` with none.
- `anchorAssemblyName: string | undefined`: The assembly the 'reference' color field keys on: the one bordering the most synteny levels, ties to the topmost. In a stacked ref-vs-A / ref-vs-B layout that is the shared reference, so a region keeps its color across levels.
- `showLoading: boolean`: Whether to show a loading indicator instead of the import form or view
- `loadingAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly whose load the spinner is waiting on. `init` names them before the rows are built, so it is the source until then.
- `loading: ViewLoading | undefined`: The loading screen's text while `showLoading`, taken from the assembly being waited on; undefined otherwise.
- `showImportForm: boolean`: Whether to show the import form: nothing to show, or a failure that leaves the stack nothing to show (`stackError`), which the form reports in a banner.
- `status: ViewStatus`: The view's lifecycle as one value — ready, error, loading or noRegions — for a host that draws its own chrome. Same shape and precedence as the linear view's.
- `antialias: boolean | undefined`: `render.antialias`, undefined while it follows the data.
- `fadeThinAlignments: boolean`: The resolved fade-thin flag every display renders by. 'auto' fades once sub-pixel ribbons dominate any loaded display, latched with a deadband (`fadesThinAt`, ADR-083) so a view near the threshold does not flip while panning. View-wide, so…
- `hasLodCapableAdapter: boolean`: Whether any track's adapter has tiers to switch between, which gates the "Level of detail" setting.
- `resolution: LodMode`: `data.resolution`: the stored tier every track fetches.
- `showLegend: boolean`: The legend-host half of `LegendMixin` a view needs: whether the key draws, which is `legend.show`, the mode having a key, and the reader not having closed it in this mode. `ChromeLegend` and `SvgLegend` read it.
- `legendSpec: LegendSpec`: The key `ChromeLegend` draws on screen and `SvgLegend` in the export.
- `defaultOpacity: number`: The constant opacity a reset returns to: low on the synteny view for dense whole-genome hairballs, opaque on the dotplot.
- `opacitySetting: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot`: `encoding.opacity` as its snapshot holds it.
- `opacityFade: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot | undefined`: What the color pass fades each alignment by: the field's mapping with its range as shares of `opacityLevel`, or undefined while `encoding.opacity` draws its constant, so the slider recolors nothing either way.
- `opacityLevel: number`: The opacity every alignment draws at before a field's fade: the shader's uniform (`opacityLevel`).
- `opacityField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.opacity` fades by, undefined while it draws its constant.
- `colorSetting: SyntenyColorSnapshot`: `encoding.color` as its snapshot holds it, with the view's default field where it names neither a field nor a constant.
- `impliedColorField: string | undefined`: The field the view paints while `encoding.color` names neither a field nor a constant, undefined for its default scheme.
- `colorPaint: SyntenyColorPaint`: What `encoding.color.scale` declares over a field's own scale: its `type`, `domain`, `range` or `scheme` for its colors, `reverse`, and a ramp's pinned ends and middle. Read from these slots alone, so a key-only edit repaints nothing.
- `colorValue: string | undefined`: `encoding.color.value`: the color every alignment paints under the default mode in place of the view's own scheme, or undefined for that scheme.
- `colorDomain: readonly string[]`: `encoding.color.scale.domain`, the order a text column's labels take. Read from that slot alone, so a key-only edit (`legend.title`, `scale.names`) recolors nothing.
- `colorRange: readonly string[]`: The colors a text column's labels take in domain order: `encoding.color.scale.range`, else its `scheme` sampled once per domain value
- `colorableAttributes: string[]`: Distinct numeric columns across the overlaid tracks, in first-seen order — two tracks declaring `dn` offer one `dn` mode, not two.
- `attributeRanges: Record<string, AttributeRange>`: The span each numeric channel covers: unioned over the loaded displays, and over every fetch this view has already taken (`seenAttributeRanges`). A column has no declared domain, so this is what its ramp scales to, what the legend labels…
- `colorableTracks: ColorableTrack[]`: `colorableTrackConfigs` paired with whatever color the user pinned. This is the single definition of "the tracks that get colors" — the palette, the legend and the palette menu all read it, so they cannot disagree about which tracks are in…
- `trackColorAssignments: Map<string, string>`: trackId -> the color it draws in under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Assigned across the whole view rather than per display, so an automatic slot can't duplicate a color pinned on a sibling.
- `colorField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.color` paints by, undefined for the default color.
- `hideUnlabelled: boolean`: Whether the filter drops the alignments with no value for the field the view paints by, the "Hide unlabelled rows" box.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the mode has a key worth a box: a track palette, a ramp, a reader-named column, or strand wherever the shape does not show it (`shapeShowsStrand`), which leaves the color the only strand cue.
- `colorLegendChips: ColorChip[]`: Legend rows naming the overlaid tracks — one per track with its palette color, however many levels it is on, and only under `encoding.color: 'track'`, since every other mode has a fixed legend.
- `colorScales: ColorScale[]`: The active mode's key, or none for a mode without one. View-wide rather than per display because the key is one box for the whole view, and the ramp domain it labels is the view's.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field
- `predicates: FieldPredicate[]`: The `filter` list as the predicate compiler reads it.
- `minLength: number`: The lower bound on `length`, 0 for none.
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders this view's displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = types.literal('LinearSyntenyView')`
- `indels = types.stripDefault(syntenyIndelsConfigSchema, {})`: The insertions and deletions inside each alignment, a [](/docs/config/syntenyindels) part: `{ show: false }` draws each alignment as one block, and `{ encoding: { opacity: 0 } }` leaves each indel a gap.
- `mark = types.stripDefault(syntenyMarkConfigSchema, {})`: How every band's ribbons draw, a [](/docs/config/syntenymark) object: `{ interpolate: 'bump' }` curves their sides.
- `axis = types.stripDefault(linearSyntenyAxisConfigSchema, {})`: Each row's ruler guide, a [](/docs/config/linearsyntenyaxis) object: `{ grid: true }` continues the query row's scalebar ticks down through every band, each joined to the coordinate the alignment pairs it with.
- `offscreen = types.stripDefault(syntenyOffscreenConfigSchema, {})`: The marks along both edges of each band for the alignments the view cannot draw a ribbon for, a [](/docs/config/syntenyoffscreen) part: `{ show: false }` removes them and the second query per pair of rows they cost.
- `overdrawPx = types.stripDefault(types.number, DEFAULT_OVERDRAW_PX)`: pixels beyond the visible viewport edge that synteny lines are still drawn. Effective up to the pan buffer (`syntenyPanBufferPx`: 2000px, or half the viewport when that is wider) — the worker emits CIGAR detail and location markers only…
- `launch = types.frozen< LaunchInput<LinearSyntenyViewCommands> | undefined >()`: Transient launch state: the settings written on the view object that need resolving before they can be view state — the genome rows to open, the synteny tracks for each band, the shared scale. The afterAttach autorun applies and clears it.…
- `trackSelectorType = types.stripDefault(types.string, 'hierarchical')`: ignored: the hierarchical selector is the only one. Declared because saved sessions and share links carry it.
- `navigation = types.stripDefault(syntenyNavigationConfigSchema, {})`: How a move on one row carries to the others, a [](/docs/config/syntenynavigation) object: `{ follow: true }` has the rows follow the `anchor` row through the alignment.
- `coord = types.stripDefault(syntenyCoordConfigSchema, {})`: The coordinate system, a [](/docs/config/syntenycoord) object: `{ ratio: 1 }` holds every genome row on one bp/px, the coarsest row's fit, so the rows compare by drawn length instead of each filling its pane. It moves the rows' zoom-out…
- `diagonalizeAnchorRow = types.stripDefault(types.number, 0)`: Which genome row "Re-order chromosomes" keeps as it is: the rows below it are ordered against the row above them, and the rows above it against the row below. It matters wherever the top row is not the one whose order means something:…
- `levels = types.array(LinearSyntenyLevel)`: One synteny band per adjacent pair of `views`, each holding one track list. The track-selector and add-track widgets address a band through `trackContainerFor`.
- `views = types.array( pluginManager.getViewType('LinearGenomeView').stateModel, )`: N genome rows, with N-1 synteny `levels` between adjacent pairs (see reconcileLevels).
- `render = types.stripDefault(syntenyRenderConfigSchema, {})`: How the ribbons rasterize, a [](/docs/config/syntenyrender) object: `antialias` fades a sub-pixel ribbon by its on-screen width, so an unfiltered whole-genome view doesn't read as a full-opacity hairball. Unset, it fades once sub-pixel…
- `data = types.stripDefault(syntenyDataConfigSchema, {})`: What the fetch reads, a [](/docs/config/syntenydata) object: `resolution` picks a tiered file's stored tier. One value for the view, so every track draws at the same tier.
- `legend = types.stripDefault(legendConfigSchema, {})`: Whether the view draws its color key, a [](/docs/config/legend) object. The key's close button hides it for the current mode only and is never saved.
- `encoding = types.stripDefault(syntenyEncodingConfigSchema, {})`: The channels every track in the view paints with, a [](/docs/config/syntenyencoding) object. Its `color` is a [](/docs/config/syntenycolor) channel: `"strand"`, `"query"`, `"reference"`, `"track"`, a measurement (`identity`, `mapq`,…
- `trackColors = types.map(types.string)`: trackId -> explicit color under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Absent means the track takes an automatic slot from the palette.
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `filter = types.stripDefault(fieldPredicateArray(), [])`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries an alignment must all pass. A field is any field `color` takes, or `length`, the alignment's bp on its own axis: `[{ field: 'length', gte: 10000 }]` clears a…
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar and keep it in the session

## Methods
- `trackContainerFor(id: string) => TrackContainer | undefined`: The level that owns a given track list, by id. The track-selector and add-track widgets target a level through here, since this view holds one track list per band rather than a single list for the view.
- `syntenyTracks() => ComparativeTrackModel[]`: Every synteny track across every level, in order.
- `loadedAttributeRanges() => Record<string, AttributeRange>[]`: Each loaded display's observed attribute spans, which the mixin unions into the domain the legend labels its ramp with.
- `legendCigarOps() => number`: Only the indel ops drawn on screen get a chip.
- `offersReferenceColor() => boolean`: A stack of two or more levels shares an anchor assembly.
- `headerMenuItems(extraSubMenus?: MenuItem[]) => MenuItem[]`: The header's view-options menu: the zoom actions, the row coupling, what varies with the stack under "Rows", each synteny track's menu under "Tracks", then Export SVG. Every render setting is in `SyntenySettingsMenu` instead.…
- `menuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `rubberBandMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `rubberbandClickMenuItemsAtPx(px: number) => MenuItem[]`: What a bare click on the shared rubberband strip offers: one row per genome row, each holding that row's click menu at the base it paints under `px`. A pixel rather than an offset, since each row maps it through that row's `pxToBp`.
- `colorableTrackConfigs() => { trackId: string; name: string; }[]`
- `colorableAttributeNames() => string[]`: The columns the tracks declare in their adapter's `attributeColumns` (the ortholog-table adapter's slot), one color mode each.
- `legendAlpha() => number`: The plot's opacity composites the key's chips, as it does the alignments.
- `colorSurface() => SyntenyColorSurface`: Overridable hook: what draws each alignment, a ribbon with match and indel blocks or one flat point (the dotplot). The key, the menu's help text and which fields key at all read it.
- `shapeShowsStrand() => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether an alignment's shape shows its strand, which spares the strand colors a key. A linear ribbon twists against its rows' directions, which their rulers show; a whole-genome dotplot is mostly dots with no slope to…
- `trackColorFor(trackId: string) => string`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `lowerBound(field: string) => number`: The lower bound the filter puts on `field`, 0 for none.

LinearSyntenyViewHelper.text:
# LinearSyntenyViewHelper (General model, linear-comparative-view plugin)

Holds one level of a linear synteny comparison: its track list and height, composed with the shared rendering-lifecycle state.

Composes RenderLifecycleMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setHeight(n: number) => void`
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => void`: Drag this band taller or shorter, clamped like every other band drag: the floor keeps the bar itself grabbable, and a band already thinner than the floor stays where it is rather than jumping up to it. The stack-wide drag…
- `showTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: object, displayInitialSnapshot?: DisplayInitialSnapshot, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => any`
- `hideTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `toggleTrack(trackId: string) => boolean`
- `launchTrack(trackId: string, initialSnapshot?: object, displayInitialSnapshot?: DisplayInitialSnapshot, inlineConf?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) => Promise<any>`: showTrack for a track whose display state model may be lazily loaded: loads it, then shows
- `launchToggleTrack(trackId: string) => Promise<boolean>`: toggleTrack with launchTrack's loading behavior
- `setHoveredFeature(hit: SyntenyPickResult | undefined) => LinearSyntenyDisplayModel | undefined`
- `setClickedFeature(hit: SyntenyPickResult | undefined) => LinearSyntenyDisplayModel | undefined`: Clicked-state twin of `setHoveredFeature`, across the whole view rather than this band alone
- `showOffscreenMateContig(hit: OffscreenMateHit) => void`: What clicking a mark does: show where its alignments fall on the facing row. The row scrolls to them, or gains the contig or a slice of it, and never loses a region it was showing. The click takes the follow anchor, and the Undo gives back…
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: SyntenyRenderingBackend) => void`
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.

## Getters
- `parentView: ParentViewDuck`
- `level: number`: this level's place in the stack, and so which rows it draws between
- `rowPair: RowPair | undefined`: The two rows this level draws between — the upper one is the query axis — or undefined for a level with no row below it. Ungated: whether those rows are ready to draw is `connectedRows`' question.
- `connectedRows: RowPair | undefined`: `rowPair` once both rows are initialized with regions, which is also when the view has a width to draw at. Gated on those two rows alone, so a row loading or failed elsewhere in the stack holds back only the bands beside it. The one gate…
- `assemblyNames: string[]`: the assemblies of `rowPair`, or [] without one
- `linearSyntenyDisplays: LinearSyntenyDisplayModel[]`: All synteny displays under this level's tracks.
- `bandTransformKey: string`: Every number that moves a ribbon under a stationary cursor — each connected row's `offsetPx` and `bpPerPx`, plus the band height — as one key, which `installClearHoverOnSurfaceMove` watches. Empty until both rows are there, which no…
- `displayError: string | undefined`: Every failed track's error in this level, joined into the one value the band has room to report. On-screen only — an SVG export has nowhere to float a banner, so it fails outright from `awaitSvgReady`.
- `surfaceReadiness: ComparativeSurface`: This level's band as the displays drawing onto it see it: first paint, plus the parent-view flags that mean what is on screen is not the answer yet. `displayPhase` and `settled` are both computed from it.
- `displayPhase: DisplayStatusPhase`: What the shared canvas publishes as `data-display-phase`: the ranking over the ribbons drawing onto it. `settled` below is the stricter question — see `comparativeReadiness`.
- `settled: boolean`: The canvas has painted and no display is still fetching, so what is on screen is final. Drives `synteny_canvas`'s `data-display-drawn`, which screenshot capture and the browser suites wait on — so it means "done", not "first paint".…
- `syntenyCells: Map<number, SyntenyCell>`: Every cell the band's backend holds bytes for, in draw order: each display's ribbons, then its outline while a ribbon of it is selected. The upload autorun diffs this map — new entries upload, vanished entries evict — and the wrappers are…
- `ribbonGeometryByDisplayKey: Map<number, SyntenyInstanceData>`: Each track's ribbon geometry, in draw order — what the pick walks. The outline cells are left out: an outline is the selection's own silhouette, drawn over the ribbon it traces.
- `syntenyBlocks: RenderBlock[]`: One canvas-wide block per cell, so a ribbon's outline draws over the ribbon's fill and a later track over an earlier one.
- `syntenyRenderState: SyntenyRenderState`: Aggregated per-frame render state, always resolved — "the view isn't measured yet" is `canRender`'s precondition. An empty `perTrack` is a real frame rather than a skip: the frame clears before drawing, so painting zero tracks is what…
- `groundColor: string`: The band's ground — see `bandGroundColor`, which is the decision. Read here so the level's clear, its ribbons, its off-screen-mate strip and its SVG export all take it from one place.
- `offscreenMateStrips: OffscreenMateStrip[]`: The off-screen mate strips this band draws, hit-tests and exports: one computed value for the overlay, the pointer handlers, the tooltip and the SVG export.
- `hoveringFeature: boolean`: The pointer is over a ribbon somewhere in this band. Drives the canvas cursor, which is the only signal that a ribbon can be clicked at all — the hover shading is subtle at the default 0.25 opacity.
- `canRender: boolean`: Render-lifecycle precondition, overriding `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook: the render callback sizes the canvas off `parentView.width`, and a paint before both rows are up would mark the band drawn over ribbons that have not…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook: a band with no synteny track on it paints its ground this tick and nothing is coming, so it has finished rather than being pending. `renderBlocks` answers "did content reach the canvas" off the…
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this display paints a canvas in its **current** configuration, as opposed to a deliberate static placeholder (LD with the triangle off, sequence past base resolution — both render a message where…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): what is on the canvas was painted from data a later change has made wrong, so `painted` below should answer *pending* until the repaint lands even though `canvasDrawn` is still true. The per-region fetch…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `type = 'LinearSyntenyViewHelper'`
- `tracks = types.array( pluginManager.pluggableMstType('track', 'stateModel'), )`
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, 100)`

## Methods
- `displayFor(key: number) => LinearSyntenyDisplayModel | undefined`: The display a pick hit belongs to.
- `offscreenMateDestination(hit: OffscreenMateHit) => MateNavDestination | undefined`: Where a click on a mark would send its row, which the hover prints as the click's promise; undefined for a row the stack no longer has.
- `pickFeatureAt(x: number, y: number) => SyntenyPickResult | undefined`: The ribbon under a canvas-relative point, topmost first — the band's hover, click and context menu all ask this. CPU picking rather than a GPU id buffer: ADR-019.

LinearVariantDisplay.text:
# LinearVariantDisplay (Display model, variants plugin)

GPU-accelerated variant display with custom feature widget on click.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearVariantDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes LinearFeatureBaseDisplay, HiddenGroupsMixin, ContextMenuMixin, FeatureGateMixin, FacetWritesMixin, ColorWritesMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, HeightModeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

A complete `VariantTrack` config to paste into `tracks`:
```js
{
  type: 'VariantTrack',
  trackId: 'variants',
  name: 'Variants',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'VcfTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/variants.vcf.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearVariantDisplay',
      displayId: 'variants-LinearVariantDisplay',
      height: 150,
    },
  ],
}
```

## Actions
- `openFilterDialog() => void`: The base display's filter dialog, seeded with the VCF vocabulary (`VARIANT_FILTER_EXAMPLES`).
- `beginYMorph(fromTops: Map<string, number>, fromMaxY: number) => void`
- `setMorphProgress(t: number) => void`
- `advanceAnimation(nowMs: number) => void`: the chrome's frame clock
- `endAnimation() => void`
- `setRpcData(displayedRegionIndex: number, data: FeatureDataResult, region: Region) => void`: Stage a region as fetched — the store's raw write with this display's payload shape, so a test stands up a loaded display in one call.
- `startRenderingBackend(backend: FeatureRenderingBackend) => void`
- `togglePinnedFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `clearPinnedFeatures() => void`
- `toggleExpandedGene(featureId: string) => void`: Open or re-collapse one gene's isoforms, from the badge on the gene's label.
- `clearExpandedGenes() => void`: Re-collapse every gene opened from a badge.
- `toggleSoloFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `applySolo() => void`
- `soloFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `clearSolo() => void`
- `hideFeature(featureId: string) => void`
- `showAllHidden() => void`
- `setHover(featureId: string | undefined, subfeatureId: string | undefined, tooltip: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `clearHover() => void`
- `setFeatureHighlights(highlights: FeatureHighlight[]) => void`
- `setSearchHighlight(highlight: FeatureHighlight) => void`: A text search's highlight replaces the previous search's and leaves the right-click ones, which have a `featureId`, alone.
- `addFeatureHighlightForItem(target: HighlightTarget, refName: string) => void`
- `removeFeatureHighlightsForId(featureId: string) => void`
- `clearFeatureHighlights() => void`
- `openContextMenu(info: FeatureContextMenuInfo) => void`: Drops the hover first, so its tooltip does not sit under the menu; the highlight box stays on the target through `hoverBoxFeature`.
- `openFeatureDetails(fetch: () => Promise<Feature | undefined>, parentFeature?: ParentFeatureSummary | undefined) => void`: Open the feature-details widget on what `fetch` resolves to, with the adapter's header metadata beside it; a lookup that resolves to nothing is reported as a miss.
- `selectFeature(feature: Feature) => void`: Open the feature-details widget on a feature already in hand.
- `clearSelection() => void`
- `setShowNames(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowDescriptions(show: boolean) => void`
- `setShowLabels(value: "auto" | "description" | "name" | "nameAndDescription" | "none") => void`: The five-value label mode, written as `setShowNames` and `setShowDescriptions`.
- `setFilter(filters?: string[] | undefined) => void`: Write the `filter` list's expressions, its other entries kept; undefined returns them to what the track's config declares.
- `setSequenceHoverPosition(pos: SequenceHoverPosition | undefined) => void`
- `setDisplayMode(value: "collapsed" | "compact" | "normal" | "superCompact") => void`
- `dropGroupState() => void`: The stack starts over from the top when its sections change.
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: the picker Color by's Solid color... opens
- `fetchFullFeature(featureId: string, displayedRegionIndex: number, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal; statusCallback?: StatusCallback; }) => Promise<SimpleFeature | undefined>`
- `selectFeatureById(featureId: string, subfeatureInfo: SubfeatureInfo | undefined, displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`
- `reload() => void`: Clears the loaded regions and fetches straight away, rather than waiting out `FetchVisibleRegions`' 600ms debounce as the rest of the family does — Retry and Force load are both clicks, and this is the display the user is most often…
- `fetchNeeded(needed: IndexedRegion[]) => void`
- `openPlotDialog(seed?: Plot | undefined) => void`: "Edit plot...", seeded with a draft a dialog has not applied.

- `colorsByConsequenceImpact: boolean`
- `colorsBySvType: boolean`
- `colorByAttribute: string`: The attribute the Attribute dialog opens on, '' under the impact or SV type preset, each of which has a separate row.
- `featureNoun: string`: The noun for what the track holds, used in every menu row, chip and indicator, so a variant track shows "Variant height" and "Showing 3 variants" rather than "feature". The context menu's per-hit noun still comes from the annotation's type…

- `colorSetting: ColorSetting`: The `color` object as written, its `value` and `field` raw: either may be a `jexl:` expression over a feature, which has none here.
- `workerColor: WorkerColor`: The two members the worker reads, the rest being the main thread's.
- `colorEncoding: string | FieldColorEncoding | undefined`: `colorSetting` as it paints, through the one resolver every display's color channel goes through: `encoding.color.value`, or a field through its scale, `score` a ramp and any other field ordinal while `scale.type` is unset.
- `colorField: string | undefined`: The field the color paints by, through any scale, or undefined while `encoding.color.value` paints.
- `solidColor: string | undefined`: The constant `encoding.color.value` holds, painting or kept beside a field; undefined where it holds none or a `jexl:` expression.
- `colorByMode: "attribute" | "default" | "solid" | "strand"`: The Color by radio that is ticked: a field, else a constant, else the track's own color.
- `categoricalColorField: CategoricalField | undefined`: The color channel's field while it paints through an ordinal scale, which a facet on the same field shares.
- `paintedColorField: CategoricalField | undefined`: The field the color channel paints through an ordinal or threshold scale, a threshold's values filed under their bins.
- `identityKeyEntries: { value: string; label: string; color: string; }[]`: The rows an identity scale's key names, empty under any other scale.
- `colorKeyTitle: string | undefined`: The key's heading: the channel's `legend.title`, or its field's preset's, else the field.
- `colorValueExtent: [number, number]`: The smallest and largest number the loaded regions' values of the painting field hold, which a ramp's open ends follow.
- `colorValueGaps: { missing: boolean; notNumber: boolean; }`: Whether a loaded feature has no value in the painting field, or has text that is not a number; a ramp's key lists these beside its bar.

- `hiddenGroupFeatureIds: ReadonlySet<string> | undefined`: The features of the sections the user hid, which sit unplaced by choice and so count as nothing the track failed to show.
- `layoutReady: boolean`: Whether features can be laid out: data is fetched, in-bounds, the view is measured.
- `onScreenFeatureIds: ReadonlySet<string> | undefined`: The features whose bp span touches the viewport, less any in a hidden section, as one Set for as long as the membership holds.

- `onScreenWidthPx: number`
- `geneLabelDensityPerPx: number | undefined`: On-screen gene features per pixel, which `auto` holds to the same threshold so gene names outlast a crowd of other features. Undefined with no gene on screen.

- `labelsReservation: LabelReservation`: The `labels` and `decimated` rungs' reservation: names kept, descriptions dropped.

- `baseLaidOutDataMap: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: Full reservation (names + descriptions): rendered at fit stage `full` and in non-fit modes, and the first stack `fitStage` probes.
- `fitLabelsOnlyLayout: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: Names reserved, descriptions dropped — the `labels` stage's stack.
- `fitDecimatedFactors: LabelRoomFactors | undefined`: The whitespace factors the `decimated` rung commits at: the smallest whose packed stack fits `fitTargetHeight`, so the most names are kept.
- `fitDecimatedSolved: Map<number, FeatureDataResult>`: The `decimated` stack: names kept only on features with at least their tier's `fitDecimatedFactors ×` their label width in neighbour whitespace (plus pinned/highlighted, always).
- `fitDecimatedBodyScale: number | undefined`: The body scale the `decimated` rung commits at: with the names `fitDecimatedFactors` kept, the bodies grow back into whatever height the dropped names freed.

- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…

- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.

- `fitHeightToDisplay: boolean`: `fit` mode as a boolean, derived from the unified `heightMode` slot.

- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.

- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.

- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.

LinearWiggleDisplay.text:
# LinearWiggleDisplay (Display model, wiggle plugin)

The quantitative display: one plot per rendering, drawn over one source or over many. `rows: 'source'` puts each source in a separate row, with the clustering sidebar, row labels and separators beside them, and holds the arrangement a reader sets; unset, every source shares one plot box.

Config slots: docs topic "config:LinearWiggleDisplay" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

Composes ContextMenuMixin, TreeSidebarMixin, ParkedColorMixin, LegendMixin, StoredHoverMixin, WiggleCommonMixin, YFieldConfigMixin, WiggleScoreConfigMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin, MultiRegionDisplayMixin, FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin, TrackHeightMixin, BaseDisplay — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

A complete `QuantitativeTrack` config to paste into `tracks`:
```js
{
  type: 'QuantitativeTrack',
  trackId: 'coverage',
  name: 'Coverage',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'BigWigAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/coverage.bw' },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearWiggleDisplay',
      displayId: 'coverage-LinearWiggleDisplay',
      height: 100,
    },
  ],
}
```

Reads the region data already in hand — no refetch, no RPC — and writes the order through `rows.sort`, the same channel clustering and the arrangement dialog write, so "Reset row…

A clustering run passes its result, and the tree and its provenance land with the order; any other reorder that moves a row drops the tree,…

The labels go to `rows` by the rule…

- `viewportWithinLoadedData: boolean`: true when every visible block lies within an already-fetched region — i.e. the viewport shows data we actually loaded, not the stale fringe left after a zoom-out/pan. Drives the loading overlay through the pre-refetch debounce.
- `viewportEmpty: boolean`: No content block is on screen, so this display has nothing to fetch and nothing to paint — see `viewportEmpty.ts` for the one viewport that reaches it, how narrow that is, and why the state still has to be terminal rather than a permanent…
- `fetchSuspended: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by the fetch plan: the display is drawing something in the features' place and wants no fetch while it does. `CoarseTierMixin` returns true while its tier stands in, so MAF never downloads the…
- `layoutReady: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): whether a searchable feature layout currently exists. Any display defining a feature-lookup method (`searchFeatureByID`) must override it, so callers can tell "laid out, but off-display" from "no layout…
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the held data is loaded and covers the viewport, but a fetch input has moved past it, so the data is about to be refetched. A display sets this hook rather than overriding `dataCurrent`, for the reason…
- `renderBlocks: RenderBlock[]`: Shared cached view for every LGV-based GPU display. A single displayedRegion may produce multiple render blocks (shared GPU buffer, different scissor clips on screen). Plugins that want to suppress rendering in certain states (e.g. no…
- `fetchInputs: FetchInputs`: What a fetch issued right now would stamp on a region: the settings tier (`FetchMixin.settingsFetchInputs`, the tier `staleSettingsDrawn` compares alone) and the zoom tier (the display's `zoomFetchArgs()` object). `fetchRegions` captures…
- `regionPayloads: ReadonlyMap<number, unknown>`: The store's payloads, keyed by `displayedRegionIndex`. A display narrows this once — `get rpcDataMap() { return self.regionPayloads as ReadonlyMap<number, MyResult> }` — and every reader it already had goes on reading a map.
- `hasRegionData: boolean`: A fetch has landed: at least one region's payload is in the store. The render callback's first-paint gate reads this, so an empty frame before any data cannot flip `canvasDrawn`; an empty but loaded region counts, and paints its empty…
- `staleSettingsDrawn: boolean`: A visible block's held data was fetched under a settings or adapter key that has since moved: drawn, and wrong for the current settings, until the refetch `isCacheValid` already owes lands. The loading scrim's third staleness term, beside…
- `dataCurrent: boolean`: This family's answer to the shared freshness question every display foundation must answer (`dataCurrent`): the held data corresponds to what is on screen right now. Four terms — spatial coverage of every visible block,…
- `loadedAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly the data in hand came from, once it can answer about refNames — `undefined` before that.
- `phaseViewportCurrent: boolean`: The loading scrim's staleness argument: what is drawn answers for what is on screen. Spatial coverage, `dataSuperseded` and `staleSettingsDrawn`; not `isCacheValid`, which belongs to `dataCurrent` and would scrim every zoom. `displayPhase`…
- `svgReady: boolean`: true once an off-screen (SVG) export can safely read this display's data. Policy single-sourced in `computeSvgReady`; this family supplies only the freshness half, which `foundationSvgReady` reads as `dataCurrent` or the vacuous currency…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook with `staleSettingsDrawn`, so `painted` — and `data-display-drawn` through it — reads pending over a canvas painted under the previous settings until the refetch lands, without blanking anything.
- `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The display's mutually-exclusive visual state, mapped in `foundationDisplayPhase` — every foundation calls it and supplies only its staleness argument, so a term added to `computeActivityPhase` reaches all three without being wired three…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: The opt-in. Overridden with a literal `true` by gated displays, and `check-gated-adapter-budgets` insists on a literal: this mixin returns early on it in an autorun and in `commitFetchBytes`.
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.
- `regionTooLarge: boolean`
- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.
- `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate.
- `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen.
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `height: number`
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollContentHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the content that scrolls, in px.
- `scrollViewportHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the window it scrolls behind, in px.
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.
- `parentTrack: AbstractTrackModel`
- `RenderingComponent: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; onHorizontalScroll?: (distance: number) => void; blockState?: Record<string, unknown>; }>`
- `DisplayBlurb: React.FC<{ model: typeof self; }> | null`
- `adapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`
- `isMinimized: boolean`: Returns true if the parent track is minimized. Used to skip expensive operations like autoruns when track is not visible.
- `featureNoun: string`: Overridable hook (default `'feature'`): the singular word for one of the things this display draws, as a menu row or a chip says it — "Hide this read", "Showing 3 variants".
- `featureWidgetType: { type: string; id: string; }`: The widget `openFeatureWidget` opens for one of this display's features. Displays may override it. The default is the generic feature widget, for displays drawing plain features.
- `plotKeys: string[]`: The grammar settings this display's config declares with `plot` (`plotKeysOf`): what "Edit plot..." edits. Empty on a display with none, which then offers no editor.
- `plot: Plot`: Those settings as declared, defaults left off and a shorthand written as a config file writes it. An agent edits a `structuredClone` of it, checks it with `plotProblems` and hands it to `applyPlot`.
- `configNotices: string[]`: `configProblemsOf` the live config.
- `notices: string[]`: Every line the display has to say about what it cannot draw as written, as an agent's settle report reads them: `configNotices`, then `liveNotices`.
- `cornerNotices: string[]`: The lines the display chrome's corner chip lists: `notices`, less any a display shows in a separate chip.
- `plotExamples: readonly PlotExample[]`: The worked examples this display type declares, which "Edit plot..." offers as buttons.
- `configDocsUrl: string`: This display type's page in the config reference, which lists every setting it takes.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('LinearWiggleDisplay')`
- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`
- `runClustering = types.maybe(types.boolean)`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `LinearGenomeView`'s `init`: a session or config sets this true and the real clustering RPC runs once automatically, with no dialog, as soon as the display reports itself ready.…
- `clusterRegion = types.maybe(types.string)`: Where that run reads from, as a locstring (whitespace-separated for several). Clustering is region-scoped, so naming the locus lets a session cluster on the signal and then show it against its context. Cleared with `runClustering`, since…
- `sortRowsBy = types.maybe(types.frozen<RowSortSpec>())`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `runClustering`: set `{refName, pos}` to order the rows once by the value each row has at that genomic column — the session-expressible form of the right-click "Sort rows by ... here".…
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `id = ElementId`

## Methods
- `sharedRpcProps() => { resolution: number; yField: string; }`: The fetch cache keys, spread into the display's own `rpcProps()`. The color settings are not among them: every mode partitions by sign on the main thread, so moving the pivot re-encodes and refetches nothing.
- `sharedGpuProps() => { wiggleColor: ResolvedWiggleColor; origin: number; summaryField: string; effectiveExtent: string; renderingType: string; }`: The encoder inputs — everything but the row list and the row layout. Spread into the display's `gpuProps()`; see `sharedRpcProps` for why it isn't an override.
- `rpcProps() => { resolution: number; yField: string; }`: `y` is a fetch key as written, so picking another stored summary refetches arrays the worker already shipped; `extent` is not (WIGGLE_DISPLAY.md, "`y`, `mark.extent`").
- `gpuProps() => { sources: { name: string; color?: string | undefined; }[]; rowLayout: boolean; wiggleColor: ResolvedWiggleColor; origin: number; summaryField: string; e…`: The row list is this display's own: the encoder places each payload source by its position here, so a filter or a reorder re-uploads bytes already in hand.
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The schema's rules, then what the plot cannot paint as written: threshold cuts past eight, and a gradient on a line.
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `contextMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`: Right-click menu, built from the column under the click. The position is captured here rather than read inside the onClick, because `closeContextMenu` runs first when an item is clicked.
- `expandRows(rows: S[]) => S[]`: Overridable hook: the discovered rows as the rows drawn, the rows themselves by default; a variant display's phased mode expands each sample to its haplotypes.
- `svgSidebarWidth(text?: ExportTextStyle | undefined) => number`: Px the SVG export reserves left of the track for `svgSidebar`, measured in the export's text.
- `rowBand(row: S) => string`: Overridable hook: the band a row stacks in while `rowBanding` is set, by default its value of the banding field, '' for none.
- `rowColorDeclaredValues(_field: string) => readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the values of the row field `field` the config declares, which the palette deals first, in this order, whether or not a loaded row carries them, so a row arriving later moves no color. None by default.
- `dealtValueColorsFor(setting: RowColorSnapshot) => ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: The color each value takes under `setting` (`dealValueColors`), which the arrangement dialog shows before it writes the setting.
- `rowColorFor(choice: string) => RowColorSetting`: The `rowColor` object `choice` starts from (`startingRowColor`): the current object's where it shows that choice, else the config's.
- `orderDropsRowTree(order: readonly string[]) => boolean`: Whether ordering the rows as `order` drops the tree: one a reorder rotates drops only for an order no rotation of it lists, and any other drops for any change.
- `rowOrderWillDropTree(next: readonly { name: string; }[]) => boolean`: Whether the arrangement dialog's submit of `next` drops the tree: an order that moves no row is not written, so it drops nothing.
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `regionHasData(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the display can draw what this region is marked loaded over, at the zoom the view has.
- `isCacheValid(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Whether the data held for a region still answers the current view. Not a hook a display fills: a display states its rule as `zoomFetchArgs` (what a fetch now would send the worker) and `regionHasData` (does what the last one stored still…
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

# LodTierInfoMixin (Mixin model, core)

What the tiered adapter said about its file, held by every display that resolves a level-of-detail tier (LinearSyntenyDisplay, DotplotDisplay, LGVSyntenyDisplay, MultiWaySyntenyDisplay) and read by their `lodTier` getters through `resolveLodTier`. Filled by `installLodTierInfoFetch`.

## Actions
- `setAdapterHeader(read: AdapterRead<unknown>) => void`

## Getters
- `adapterHeader: unknown`: The header of the adapter config the display holds, undefined until its read lands.
- `lodTierInfo: LodTierInfo | undefined`: The file's tiers, undefined until the header lands, which the resolver treats as "trust the config slot".

MatrixRampMixin.text:
# MatrixRampMixin (Mixin model, core)

A matrix display's `encoding.color` as it paints: the painted field through its preset's ramp (`colorEncoding`), that ramp's scheme, direction and 256-entry table (`colorScheme`, `colorReverse`, `colorRamp`), the domain and middle stop it spans over the display's `colorExtent` (`colorDomain`, `colorMidNorm`), all four as the painters read them (`matrixColor`), the legend's ramp (`rampColorScales`), and the scheme pick (`setColorScheme`). A display that may paint a field other than the written one, because the file could not serve it, answers `paintedColorField`; one whose values follow the…

## Actions
- `setColorScheme(scheme: "blues" | "cividis" | "fall" | "inferno" | "juicebox" | "magma" | "purpleorange" | "redblue" | "redgreyblue" | "reds" | "redyellowblue" | "viridis") =…`: The scheme, with `reverse` back to unset so it follows the scheme. The painted field's own scheme writes `scheme` unset, so it keeps following the field.

## Getters
- `paintedColorField: F`: Overridable hook: the field the loaded cells are, the written one unless the display overrides it with what the file served.
- `colorExtent: readonly [number, number]`: Overridable hook: what an unset end of the domain follows, the unit interval unless the display overrides it with its loaded values.
- `colorEncoding: MatrixColorEncoding<F>`: The color channel under the painted field's preset, with an unset `scale.reverse` turning round a scheme dark at its low end, since an unpainted cell is the page behind the matrix. The preset's scheme, and its direction with it, fill…
- `colorScaleType: "linear" | "log" | "symlog"`
- `colorScheme: "blues" | "cividis" | "fall" | "inferno" | "juicebox" | "magma" | "purpleorange" | "redblue" | "redgreyblue" | "reds" | "redyellowblue" | "viridis"`
- `colorReverse: boolean`: `scale.reverse`, or where unset whether the scheme runs dark at its low end.
- `colorRamp: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>`: The ramp's 256 entries: the GPU's texture, the Canvas2D fill and the legend read this one table. It reads `colorScheme` and `colorReverse` rather than the encoding, so a domain edit re-uploads no texture.
- `colorScale: { domain: [number, number]; lut: Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; midNorm: number; colorOf: (value: number) => number; }`: `colorEncoding` over `colorExtent`: each pinned end holds and an open one follows the extent, as the mark display's ramps do.
- `colorDomain: [number, number]`
- `colorMidNorm: number`: Where `domainMid` sits on the normalized ramp, 0.5 unset, so a diverging scheme centres on it and equal distances from it take equal colors.
- `matrixColor: MatrixColorState`
- `colorFieldTitle: string`: The painted field's own key title, from its preset.

## Methods
- `rampColorScales({ id, title, extent: { min, max }, }: { id: string; title: string; extent: { min?: number | undefined; max: number; }; }) => ColorScale[]`: The legend's ramp, once there is a domain to span: its bottom where the scale paints it, a log scale's floor included, titled by `encoding.color.legend.title` where written, else `title`. An end of the domain the loaded values run past…

MultipleViewsSessionMixin.text:
# MultipleViewsSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds a list of views to a session, with actions to add, remove, replace and reorder them.

Composes DrawerWidgetSessionMixin, BaseSessionModel, SnackbarModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `moveViewDown(id: string, scopeIds?: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `moveViewUp(id: string, scopeIds?: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `moveViewToTop(id: string, scopeIds?: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `moveViewToBottom(id: string, scopeIds?: string[] | undefined) => void`
- `orderViews(ids: string[]) => void`: Put the named views into the given relative order, leaving unnamed views in their slots.
- `addView<N extends string>(typeName: N, initialState?: NoInfer<ViewSnapshotInput<N>> | undefined) => ViewModelOf<N>`: Requires the view type's state model to be loaded; for a lazily registered type use `launchView`.
- `replaceView<N extends string>(view: IBaseViewModel, typeName: N, initialState?: NoInfer<ViewSnapshotInput<N>> | undefined) => BaseViewModel & Pick<AbstractViewModel, "ass…`: swap `view` for a new view of `typeName`, in the slot it occupied.
- `removeView(view: IBaseViewModel) => void`
- `takeOutViewsMissingFrom(snapshot: unknown) => void`: Take out every view the given session snapshot will not keep, before a whole-tree `applySnapshot` destroys it where it stands.
- `setStickyViewHeaders(sticky: boolean) => void`
- `setUseWorkspaces(_useWorkspaces?: boolean | undefined) => void`: Does nothing: the workspace is always on. Kept because published protein3d and msaview bundles call it after placing a view.
- `launchView<N extends string>(typeName: N, initialState?: NoInfer<ViewSnapshotInput<N>> | undefined) => Promise<ViewModelOf<N>>`: `addView` for view types whose state model may be lazily loaded. The view is not in `session.views` until the promise resolves. `getViewType` first so an unknown type name fails by that name; the snapshot walk skips unregistered names and…
- `setDrawerPosition(arg: DrawerPosition) => void`
- `updateDrawerWidth(drawerWidth: number, availableWidth?: number) => number`
- `resizeDrawer(distance: number, availableWidth?: number) => number`
- `addWidget(typeName: string, id: string, initialState?: any, conf?: unknown) => Widget`
- `showWidget(widget: Widget) => void`
- `hideWidget(widget: Widget) => void`: closes the widget, and removes it from the session when its type sets `discardOnClose`. Minimizing the drawer is not closing.
- `minimizeWidgetDrawer() => void`
- `showWidgetDrawer() => void`
- `popoutWidget() => void`: show the visible widget in a modal dialog, freeing the drawer column
- `returnWidgetToDrawer() => void`
- `setModalWidgets(flag: boolean) => void`
- `hideAllWidgets() => void`
- `closeModalWidget() => void`: the modal's close button: a popped-out widget goes back to the drawer, and with no drawer to go back to the widget closes
- `openWidget(typeName: string, id: string, initialState?: any, conf?: unknown) => Widget`: adds the widget, replacing one with the same id, and shows it
- `editConfiguration(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel | { trackId: string; }, opts?: { expandedDisplayId?: string | undefined; } | undefined) => void`: opens a configuration editor to configure the given thing, and sets the current task to be configuring it
- `setSelection(thing: unknown) => void`: set the global selection, i.e. the globally-selected object. can be a feature, a view, or any other object
- `clearSelection() => void`: clears the global selection
- `setHovered(thing: unknown) => void`
- `setHighlightsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setHighlightLabelsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `addHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`: an identical entry is not added twice, so a spec launched again does not stack its bands. Adding shows the bands again, since a highlight made while they are off would otherwise read as nothing happening
- `removeHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`
- `updateHighlight(old: HighlightType, updates: Partial<HighlightType>) => void`
- `setHighlights(highlights: HighlightType[]) => void`
- `setPreferenceOverride(key: string, value: unknown) => void`: set a runtime user-preference override (see `getPreference`). Mutates volatile state; products persist these to localStorage. An `undefined` value deletes the key, so the store holds no dead keys that `getPreference` would read as absent.
- `clearPreferenceOverrides() => void`: clear every runtime preference override at once, so each falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" button.
- `clearPreferenceOverride(key: string) => void`: clear a single runtime preference override (see `getPreference`) so it falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the per-entry reset in the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" confirmation.
- `setScrollZoom(flag: boolean) => void`: set the global scroll-to-zoom preference (see the `scrollZoom` getter)
- `setName(str: string) => void`
- `setFocusedViewId(viewId: string | undefined) => void`: `undefined` is "no view is focused", which the property can hold (`types.maybe`). `takeOut` sets it when the focused view leaves the session. Otherwise the dead id would match no view, since every consumer compares `focusedViewId ===…
- `removeActiveDialog() => void`: Dismiss the dialog on screen as the dialog's close button would, so a dialog that settles a promise on close (an internet account's token prompt) settles it, and drop it from the queue if it did not.
- `queueDialog<T extends DialogComponentType>(callback: (doneCallback: () => void) => [T, ComponentProps<T>]) => void`
- `removeDialog(entry: [DialogComponentType, Record<string, unknown>]) => void`
- `notify(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, action?: SnackAction | SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `notifyError(errorMessage: string, error?: unknown, extra?: unknown, action?: SnackAction | undefined) => void`
- `setErrorDialog(state: ErrorDialogState | undefined) => void`
- `pushSnackbarMessage(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, actions?: SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `popSnackbarMessage() => SnackbarMessage | undefined`
- `removeSnackbarMessage(message: string) => void`

## Getters
- `visibleWidget: Widget | undefined`
- `drawerVisible: boolean`: whether the drawer column is on screen: there is something to show, it is not minimized to the FAB, and it is not currently a modal instead.
- `modalWidgetVisible: boolean`: whether the visible widget shows in a modal: popped out of the drawer, or on a host with no room for one
- `root: TypeOrStateTreeNodeToStateTreeNode<ROOT_MODEL_TYPE>`
- `jbrowse: JBrowseConfigModel`
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`
- `configuration: AnyConfigurationModel`
- `adminMode: boolean`
- `textSearchManager: TextSearchManager`
- `assemblies: BaseAssemblyConfig[]`
- `DialogComponent: DialogComponentType`
