MultiRegionDisplayMixin.text:
# MultiRegionDisplayMixin (Mixin model, core)

Per-region fetch lifecycle for LGV-based GPU displays. Installs the fetch autoruns in `afterAttach` and exposes overridable hooks (`fetchNeeded`, `rpcProps`, `zoomFetchArgs`, `regionHasData`, `gateEnabled`) plus the `fetchRegions` / `loadedRegions` machinery.

Composes FetchMixin, RenderLifecycleMixin, RegionTooLargeMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number, region: Region, payload: {} | undefined, fetchInputs?: FetchInputs) => void`: The raw write behind `ctx.commitRegion`, and **not what a fetch should call**. A display naming its span itself is the bug this family spent a release fixing, and the context gives a fetch no way to express it — see RegionFetchContext.…
- `evictRegionStore(keep: ReadonlySet<number>) => void`: The store's bound. Drops the entries a fetch can no longer be about: an index outside the view's buffered viewport, once the store is over `MAX_STORED_REGIONS`, oldest first.
- `dropLoadedRegion(displayedRegionIndex: number) => void`: Forget one region, as `evictRegionStore` does past its cap. Tests use it to stage an evicted region.
- `clearDisplaySpecificData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds beside the store — a second store, a verdict about the viewport that was just dropped. Called by `clearAllRpcData`, which runs on a displayed-regions change, on a viewport move…
- `clearSettingsBakedData() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what this display holds that is wrong under a changed setting rather than merely stale — a payload whose shape the setting decides. Called by `invalidateSettings`, where `clearDisplaySpecificData` is…
- `clearAllRpcData() => void`: full reset: cancels fetch, clears error, loadedRegions, display-specific data, and the canvas-drawn flag. The too-large gate is derived (a pure function of the cached estimate × viewport), so it needs no explicit clear here — the fetch…
- `invalidateSettings() => void`: `SettingsInvalidate`'s reset: the half of `clearAllRpcData` a settings change still needs now that the settings and adapter axes are in `fetchInputs`. The in-flight fetch is superseded now rather than when its payload lands stamped stale,…
- `reload() => void`: `FetchMixin.reload` (error, cancel, counter) plus the full reset. Subclasses with extra teardown override and chain.
- `fetchNeeded(_needed: IndexedRegion[]) => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): override to call one of the three helpers in `fetchEachRegion.ts` — `fetchEachRegion` (one RPC per region), `fetchAllRegions` (one RPC per genome, one result per region) or `fetchRegionsBatched` (one RPC, one…
- `fetchRegions(needed: IndexedRegion[], work: (ctx: RegionFetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a per-region fetch. The work callback calls `ctx.commitRegion` as it stores each region's payload, which is what marks it loaded — see RegionFetchContext for why this function no longer does that itself. Only the three helpers in…
- `afterAttach() => void`: installs the fetch-lifecycle autoruns (DisplayedRegionsChange, FetchVisibleRegions, SettingsInvalidate, ClearBlockingStateOnViewportChange)
- `setError(error?: unknown) => void`
- `setStatusMessage(status?: RpcStatus | undefined) => void`: Unthrottled: a display writing a phase label by hand must see every write land. The high-frequency RPC stream is thinned one level up, by the streams `self.statusWindow` hands out — and aggregated across them, which a write by hand is not.
- `stopActiveFetch() => void`: Abort the in-flight fetch (if any) and retire its slot. The shared preamble of both cancel paths; the difference between them is only what they do to `fetchCanceled` / `fetchGeneration` afterward.
- `openStatusStream(isCurrent: () => boolean) => StatusStream`: Open one operation's slot on the display's status field: an RPC `statusCallback` throttled through the display-wide window and guarded so a callback that fires after the node is torn down (RPCs resolve their status stream asynchronously)…
- `cancelFetch() => void`: cancel any in-flight fetch and bump fetchGeneration (always bumps, so callers can retrigger fetch autoruns even when nothing was in flight). This is the *internal* reset `clearAllRpcData` runs — it clears any user-cancel flag so the…
- `cancelFetchByUser() => void`: User-initiated cancel from the loading overlay. Stops the in-flight fetch and sets the durable `fetchCanceled` state. Unlike `cancelFetch`, it does not bump fetchGeneration, so the fetch autoruns do not immediately restart the load. The…
- `beforeDestroy() => void`: Abort an in-flight fetch on teardown. Without this, a display destroyed mid-fetch (track/view closed while loading) never signals the worker to abort the now-useless work, and its in-flight HTTP reads keep downloading. MST auto-chains…
- `beginFetch(signal: AbortSignal) => void`: The `onBegin` half of a fetch's bookkeeping: publish the in-flight signal (`isLoading`) and clear the durable user-cancel — a load starting is the single clear point that covers every retrigger path (reload, viewport change, settings…
- `endFetch(current: boolean) => void`: The `finally` half of `runFetch`'s bookkeeping, a separate action because `runFetchOnce`'s `finally` resumes on a microtask the flow does not own — a direct volatile write there is outside the action context, which is the one thing…
- `runFetch(work: (ctx: FetchContext) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`: Run a cancel-safe fetch (cancels any prior). The work callback gets a FetchContext with a signal to forward to the RPC and an isStale() check to short-circuit commits once the user has moved on.
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.
- `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what the other axis measured, on the trigger that invalidates this one, so re-pointing an adapter never leaves `densityTooLarge` reporting on the previous file.
- `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing.
- `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch.

## Getters
- `host: RegionHost`: The containing LinearGenomeView, typed once for every display in this family — see `containingHost` for the cast it owns and why both foundations still declare the name.
- `canvasWidthPx: number`: The CSS width of this display's on-screen canvas, in px; see `trackCanvasWidthPx`.
- `settledSubPixelBinBp: number`: Genomic bp one cell of a per-base pass stands for at the settled zoom: `subPixelBinBp` off the host's debounced `coarseBpPerPx`, and 1 until the view initializes. A per-base encode or fetch reads this rather than the live zoom so a wheel…
- `canRender: boolean`: Overrides `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s default-true hook with the LGV precondition both foundations share — see `foundationCanRender`.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook off `fetchInert`, as `GlobalFetchMixin` does: a display that will never fetch here shows a placeholder where its canvas would be.
- `trackVisibleRegions: VisibleRegion[]`: The visible blocks on the track's own assemblies, the ones this display fetches and is judged against. A view of several genomes leaves a single-genome track's other regions blank.
- `viewportWithinLoadedData: boolean`: true when every visible block lies within an already-fetched region — i.e. the viewport shows data we actually loaded, not the stale fringe left after a zoom-out/pan. Drives the loading overlay through the pre-refetch debounce.
- `viewportEmpty: boolean`: No content block is on screen, so this display has nothing to fetch and nothing to paint — see `viewportEmpty.ts` for the one viewport that reaches it, how narrow that is, and why the state still has to be terminal rather than a permanent…
- `fetchSuspended: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by the fetch plan: the display is drawing something in the features' place and wants no fetch while it does. `CoarseTierMixin` returns true while its tier stands in, so MAF never downloads the…
- `layoutReady: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): whether a searchable feature layout currently exists. Any display defining a feature-lookup method (`searchFeatureByID`) must override it, so callers can tell "laid out, but off-display" from "no layout…
- `dataSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the held data is loaded and covers the viewport, but a fetch input has moved past it, so the data is about to be refetched. A display sets this hook rather than overriding `dataCurrent`, for the reason…
- `renderBlocks: RenderBlock[]`: Shared cached view for every LGV-based GPU display. A single displayedRegion may produce multiple render blocks (shared GPU buffer, different scissor clips on screen). Plugins that want to suppress rendering in certain states (e.g. no…
- `fetchInputs: FetchInputs`: What a fetch issued right now would stamp on a region: the settings tier (`FetchMixin.settingsFetchInputs`, the tier `staleSettingsDrawn` compares alone) and the zoom tier (the display's `zoomFetchArgs()` object). `fetchRegions` captures…
- `regionPayloads: ReadonlyMap<number, unknown>`: The store's payloads, keyed by `displayedRegionIndex`. A display narrows this once — `get rpcDataMap() { return self.regionPayloads as ReadonlyMap<number, MyResult> }` — and every reader it already had goes on reading a map.
- `hasRegionData: boolean`: A fetch has landed: at least one region's payload is in the store. The render callback's first-paint gate reads this, so an empty frame before any data cannot flip `canvasDrawn`; an empty but loaded region counts, and paints its empty…
- `staleSettingsDrawn: boolean`: A visible block's held data was fetched under a settings or adapter key that has since moved: drawn, and wrong for the current settings, until the refetch `isCacheValid` already owes lands. The loading scrim's third staleness term, beside…
- `dataCurrent: boolean`: This family's answer to the shared freshness question every display foundation must answer (`dataCurrent`): the held data corresponds to what is on screen right now. Four terms — spatial coverage of every visible block,…
- `loadedAssembly: Assembly | undefined`: The assembly the data in hand came from, once it can answer about refNames — `undefined` before that.
- `phaseViewportCurrent: boolean`: The loading scrim's staleness argument: what is drawn answers for what is on screen. Spatial coverage, `dataSuperseded` and `staleSettingsDrawn`; not `isCacheValid`, which belongs to `dataCurrent` and would scrim every zoom. `displayPhase`…
- `svgReady: boolean`: true once an off-screen (SVG) export can safely read this display's data. Policy single-sourced in `computeSvgReady`; this family supplies only the freshness half, which `foundationSvgReady` reads as `dataCurrent` or the vacuous currency…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s `paintInert` hook — see there for why a failed fetch has to read as finished to the consumers outside the display, and `foundationPaintInert` for the second such state and why both fetch families answer it…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Fills `RenderLifecycleMixin`'s hook with `staleSettingsDrawn`, so `painted` — and `data-display-drawn` through it — reads pending over a canvas painted under the previous settings until the refetch lands, without blanking anything.
- `displayPhase: DisplayPhase`: The display's mutually-exclusive visual state, mapped in `foundationDisplayPhase` — every foundation calls it and supplies only its staleness argument, so a term added to `computeActivityPhase` reaches all three without being wired three…
- `isLoading: boolean`: true while a fetch is active
- `isLoadingOrCanceled: boolean`: `isLoading` widened to cover a user-canceled load: what a hover gate wants, since neither state has a frame on screen that a hit describes. Not a phase input — `computeActivityPhase` reads the two apart, because a cancel is finished…
- `fetchInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the states where this display deliberately skips fetching, so its data stays empty. Sequence sets it past base resolution ("Zoom in to see sequence"); LD sets it with the triangle toggled off.
- `awaitingPrerequisite: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read only by the retry contract check (`makeRetryContractCheck`): "this run declined because a prerequisite fetch in another autorun has not landed, and its arrival wakes this one again". It **defers** the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false), read by `computeActivityPhase` and `foundationSvgReady`: a load this display depends on beyond its primary fetch has not landed for the first time, so the frame the primary fetch calls current is still…
- `settingsFetchInputs: unknown`: The settings axis every fetch family invalidates on: this display's `rpcProps()` payload and its adapter config, as one value compared structurally. The per-region family watches it from `SettingsInvalidate` and stamps it on each region,…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: The opt-in. Overridden with a literal `true` by gated displays, and `check-gated-adapter-budgets` insists on a literal: this mixin returns early on it in an autorun and in `commitFetchBytes`.
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.
- `regionTooLarge: boolean`
- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.
- `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate.
- `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen.

## Methods
- `regionHasData(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the display can draw what this region is marked loaded over, at the zoom the view has.
- `isCacheValid(displayedRegionIndex: number) => boolean`: Whether the data held for a region still answers the current view. Not a hook a display fills: a display states its rule as `zoomFetchArgs` (what a fetch now would send the worker) and `regionHasData` (does what the last one stored still…
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.

Draws a multi-genome ortholog track as one lane per assembly inside a linear genome view, with ribbons joining each gene's placements between adjacent lanes.

- `laneGeneLabels(fontFamily: string | undefined, pinnedGroups?: ReadonlySet<string>, width?: number) => PlacedLaneLabel[]`: placed in the stack's px
- `coloredLayersOf(held: HeldLaneLayer) => EncodedChannels[]`: a held payload's layers, each colored as its mark declares
- `pickRibbonAt(x: number, y: number) => SyntenyPickResult | undefined`: `x` and `y` are container-relative; the topmost ribbon wins
- `slidableLaneAt(y: number) => string | undefined`: `y` is container-relative; undefined unless the lanes are frozen
- `hitTest(x: number, y: number) => HoverTarget | undefined`: `x` and `y` are container-relative
- `trackMenuItems() => MenuItem[]`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `colorScalesIn(_palette: JBrowsePalette) => ColorScale[]`: Overridable hook (default `colorScales`): the scales in another theme, the SVG export's, which need not be the session's. Only a display whose key takes colors from the theme answers it.
- `legendSpecIn(palette: JBrowsePalette) => LegendSpec`: `legendSpec` in the SVG export's theme.
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.
- `renderingProps() => { displayModel: ModelInstanceTypeProps<…> & {…} & {…} & { readonly RenderingComponent: FC<…>; readonly DisplayBlurb: FC<{ model: ModelInstanceTypeProps<{…`: props passed to the renderer's React "Rendering" component. these are client-side only and never sent to the worker. includes displayModel and callbacks
- `configProblemsOf(conf: AnyConfigurationModel) => string[]`: The problems in a config that cannot be drawn as written: by default the schema's rules over its color objects and value axes, the ones `jbrowse validate` runs. A display with additional rules overrides it. `plotProblems` asks it of a…
- `liftPlot(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => AnyConfigurationModel`: A draft as the config would hold it, merged over `plot`, throwing what a config file would be refused for. It leaves the display unchanged.
- `plotProblems(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => string[]`: What a draft would report once applied, throwing a refusal as `liftPlot` does: `configProblemsOf` the lifted draft. The draft still applies, and draws what it can.
- `plotWrites(draft: Plot, options?: PlotWriteOptions | undefined) => Record<string, unknown>`: What applying a draft would write, by setting: the lifted value where it differs from `plot`, `null` where it resets one. Throws a refusal.

OAuthInternetAccount.text:
# OAuthInternetAccount (Internet Account model, authentication plugin)

Gets an OAuth 2.0 access token from the provider's login window, and renews it with a refresh token kept in `localStorage`.

Config slots: docs topic "config:OAuthInternetAccount" (or jb.describeSlots(node.configuration) live).

## Actions
- `storeRefreshToken(refreshToken: string) => void`
- `removeRefreshToken() => void`
- `postTokenGrant(grant: Record<string, string>, describeError: (response: Response) => Promise<string>) => Promise<string>`: POST a grant to the token endpoint and read the access token out of the answer. Both grants this account makes — trading the authorization code on the way in, trading the refresh token when the access token expires — are the same…
- `exchangeAuthorizationForAccessToken(code: string, redirectUri: string, codeVerifier: string | undefined) => Promise<string>`
- `exchangeRefreshForAccessToken(refreshToken: string) => Promise<string>`
- `validateTokenWithProbe(token: string, probe: (token: string) => Promise<Response>, describeError: (response: Response, reason?: string) => Promise<string>) => Promise<string>`: Prove a token against the resource and, if the resource answers 401, refresh it once and prove the new one. Returns whichever token worked; throws if neither does, or if the resource fails for any other reason. Every OAuth account…
- `getTokenViaAuthFlow() => Promise<string>`: Opens the provider's auth page and returns a promise for the resulting token. For Electron, drives the flow directly via IPC; for web, opens a popup and waits for the redirect message.
- `getTokenFromUser(resolve: (token: string) => void, reject: (error: Error) => void) => Promise<void>`
- `validateToken(token: string, location: UriLocation) => Promise<string>`

## Getters
- `conf: OAuthInternetAccountConfig`: The config typed off the concrete schema. `ConfigurationReference` erases `self.configuration` to `any` (the reference's MST instance brand doesn't include the schema's slot definitions), so reads go through this getter to recover per-slot…
- `authEndpoint: string`
- `tokenEndpoint: string`
- `needsPKCE: boolean`
- `clientId: string`
- `scopes: string`
- `responseType: string`
- `refreshTokenKey: string`
- `authFlowParams: Record<string, string>`: Extra parameters to add to the authorization request. Empty here; a provider that needs extra parameters overrides this.

## Properties

- `configuration = ConfigurationReference(configSchema)`

## Methods
- `retrieveRefreshToken() => string | undefined`

ParkedColorMixin.text:
# ParkedColorMixin (Mixin model, core)

The field the last write took off a color object, with its domain, range and key names, so picking that field again gives them back (`colorForField`). A written field always paints, so the field a write leaves, for Default, Solid color or another field, is display state rather than config. Each writer parks before it writes, so no reader sees the field gone unparked

## Actions
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.

## Getters
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field

## Properties
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members

## Methods
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`

PreferencesSessionMixin.text:
# PreferencesSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Loads and saves a user's preference overrides (the BaseSession `preferencesOverrides` volatile) in localStorage. Products that let users edit preferences (web, desktop) compose it; embedded sessions omit it and resolve preferences from the `configuration.preferences` admin defaults only.

Composes BaseSessionModel, SnackbarModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setSelection(thing: unknown) => void`: set the global selection, i.e. the globally-selected object. can be a feature, a view, or any other object
- `clearSelection() => void`: clears the global selection
- `setHovered(thing: unknown) => void`
- `setHighlightsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setHighlightLabelsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `addHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`: an identical entry is not added twice, so a spec launched again does not stack its bands. Adding shows the bands again, since a highlight made while they are off would otherwise read as nothing happening
- `removeHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`
- `updateHighlight(old: HighlightType, updates: Partial<HighlightType>) => void`
- `setHighlights(highlights: HighlightType[]) => void`
- `setPreferenceOverride(key: string, value: unknown) => void`: set a runtime user-preference override (see `getPreference`). Mutates volatile state; products persist these to localStorage. An `undefined` value deletes the key, so the store holds no dead keys that `getPreference` would read as absent.
- `clearPreferenceOverrides() => void`: clear every runtime preference override at once, so each falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" button.
- `clearPreferenceOverride(key: string) => void`: clear a single runtime preference override (see `getPreference`) so it falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the per-entry reset in the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" confirmation.
- `setScrollZoom(flag: boolean) => void`: set the global scroll-to-zoom preference (see the `scrollZoom` getter)
- `setName(str: string) => void`
- `setFocusedViewId(viewId: string | undefined) => void`: `undefined` is "no view is focused", which the property can hold (`types.maybe`). `takeOut` sets it when the focused view leaves the session. Otherwise the dead id would match no view, since every consumer compares `focusedViewId ===…
- `removeActiveDialog() => void`: Dismiss the dialog on screen as the dialog's close button would, so a dialog that settles a promise on close (an internet account's token prompt) settles it, and drop it from the queue if it did not.
- `queueDialog<T extends DialogComponentType>(callback: (doneCallback: () => void) => [T, ComponentProps<T>]) => void`
- `removeDialog(entry: [DialogComponentType, Record<string, unknown>]) => void`
- `notify(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, action?: SnackAction | SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `notifyError(errorMessage: string, error?: unknown, extra?: unknown, action?: SnackAction | undefined) => void`
- `setErrorDialog(state: ErrorDialogState | undefined) => void`
- `pushSnackbarMessage(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, actions?: SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `popSnackbarMessage() => SnackbarMessage | undefined`
- `removeSnackbarMessage(message: string) => void`

## Getters
- `root: TypeOrStateTreeNodeToStateTreeNode<ROOT_MODEL_TYPE>`
- `jbrowse: JBrowseConfigModel`
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`
- `configuration: AnyConfigurationModel`
- `adminMode: boolean`
- `textSearchManager: TextSearchManager`
- `assemblies: BaseAssemblyConfig[]`
- `DialogComponent: DialogComponentType`
- `DialogProps: Record<string, unknown>`
- `animationMode: AnimationMode`: resolved feature-layout animation mode (never undefined)
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: resolved scroll-to-zoom preference. Global and personal (never shared in a session snapshot); every wheel-zoom view reads this single value.
- `numberGrouping: boolean`: resolved thousand-separator preference. Read for display in the Preferences dialog; the formatter itself reads a plain module variable set at startup in each realm (see `setNumberGrouping`), because worker- built strings can't see a…
- `snackbarMessageSet: Map<string, SnackbarMessage>`

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `name = types.string`
- `focusedViewId = types.maybe(types.string)`: id of the view in focus
- `highlights = types.stripDefault( types.array(types.frozen<HighlightType>()), [], )`: translucent bands over genomic regions; every view draws the ones on the assemblies it shows
- `highlightsVisible = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`
- `highlightLabelsVisible = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: whether a band's label is written on it
- `heldForMissingPlugins = types.stripDefault( types.frozen<HeldNode[] | undefined>(), undefined, )`: views, tracks, displays and widgets `pruneUnbuildableNodes` took out of the tree because this build has no plugin for their type, each with the anchor that puts it back. No session code reads its contents, and `pruneUnbuildableNodes`…

## Methods
- `getPreferenceDefault(key: string) => unknown`: the admin/embedder `configuration.preferences` value for a key, ignoring any runtime override — i.e. what a reset falls back to
- `getPreference(key: string) => unknown`: resolved value of a user preference: a runtime override if the user set one, otherwise the admin/embedder `configuration.preferences` default. The override map is empty unless the product loads it (web/desktop).
- `getPreferenceChanges() => TrackConfigChange[]`: every scalar preference override that currently differs from its config/admin default, as `{ path, from, to }` rows whose path is the override's own key. A scalar pref (animationMode, scrollZoom) whose override equals the default is…

RegionTooLargeMixin.text:
# RegionTooLargeMixin (Mixin model, core)

The region-too-large gate: a display opts in by overriding `gateEnabled` and passing `byteLimit: self.resolvedByteLimit()` to its fetch RPC. The RPC measures the index before it downloads and answers a refusal when a region is over budget; the fetch runners commit what it measured, and `regionTooLarge` is derived from that last measurement. While the banner is up the fetch runs once per settled viewport and settings, which is the re-measure. Composed by `MultiRegionDisplayMixin` and `GlobalFetchMixin`. The rules and the numbers behind them: agent-docs/reference/REGION_TOO_LARGE.md.

## Actions
- `clearByteEstimate() => void`: Drops the estimate and the viewport stamp. `forceLoadTrack` survives: it is a track-wide approval.
- `clearGateMeasurements() => void`: Overridable hook (no-op base): drop what the other axis measured, on the trigger that invalidates this one, so re-pointing an adapter never leaves `densityTooLarge` reporting on the previous file.
- `setForceLoadTrack(flag: boolean) => void`
- `commitFetchBytes(perRegionBytes: (number | undefined)[], issued: GateFetchState, partial?: boolean) => void`: The byte axis of a finished fetch: the per-region max against the `gateFetchState()` captured at issue. An empty batch, or an ungated display, commits nothing.
- `forceLoad() => void`: The banner's button: exempt the track on both axes and refetch.

## Getters
- `gateEnabled: boolean`: The opt-in. Overridden with a literal `true` by gated displays, and `check-gated-adapter-budgets` insists on a literal: this mixin returns early on it in an autorun and in `commitFetchBytes`.
- `byteGateAdapterConfig: Record<string, unknown>`: The adapter config the gate measures — the one at `byteGateAdapterPath`. Overridable for a display whose adapter config is synthesized rather than read off the track.
- `configuredFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The display's `fetchSizeLimit` slot, from `regionTooLargeConfigSchemaFields`. `number | undefined`, because `getConf` returns `undefined` for a slot a composing display's schema never declared, which typing it `number` would hide —…
- `densityTooLarge: boolean`: The density axis's verdict, and the whole of that axis's opt-in: `FeatureGateMixin` overrides it beside the measurement that fills it, and a byte-only display leaves it false.
- `byteGateAdapterPath: ByteGateAdapterPath`: Where on the track config the measured adapter sits. A tiered display overrides this one hook (MAF: `['adapter', 'summaryAdapter']` while `showSummary`), and both the measurement and the budget follow it.
- `adapterFetchSizeLimit: number | undefined`: The measured adapter's own `fetchSizeLimit` slot, read off the live track config rather than the `adapterConfig` snapshot, which omits slots at their default.
- `configForceLoad: boolean`: The declarative `forceLoad` slot.
- `gateViewportSpanBp: number | undefined`: The span on screen, or undefined until the view is measured: the half of gateViewport the budget questions need. Split off because the identity half joins a string over `view.visibleRegions`, which rebuilds every gesture frame, and…
- `gateViewport: GateViewport | undefined`: What a measurement taken now would be about: the span on screen, and a key for the stretch of genome it covers **and the settings it would be taken under**. Undefined until the view is measured, and with gateViewportSpanBp the mixin's only…
- `aboveForceLoadFloor: boolean`: Whether the span on screen is at or above `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`, the one comparison against that constant. False on an unmeasured view.
- `gateExempt: boolean`: Nothing may gate on either axis: the `forceLoad` slot or the button.
- `estimatedFetchBytes: number | undefined`: The stored estimate's bytes; undefined when nothing has been measured.
- `gateMeasurementStale: boolean`: Whether the last measurement still describes what a fetch issued now would ask: the viewport on screen, under the settings on screen. True before any measurement. The triple's third term, the adapter tier, is not here — a tier swap drops…
- `gateByteLimit: number`: The byte budget: the adapter's limit, else the display's, doubled below `AUTO_FORCE_LOAD_BP`. Read only through `resolvedByteLimit()`.
- `gateActive: boolean`: Whether the gate may act right now, on any axis: opted in, not exempt, view measured. The view is read last, so an ungated display never touches it.
- `densityGateActive: boolean`: Whether the density axis may act: `gateActive`, and the span is above the floor — the one axis the floor applies to. Whether it has anything to say is `densityTooLarge`.
- `tooLargeStatus: RegionTooLargeStatus`: The verdict and its banner text, from the stored estimate against `resolvedByteLimit()` and the density axis when it may act.
- `regionTooLarge: boolean`
- `regionTooLargeReason: string`: Banner text for the axis that tripped; empty when not too large.
- `zoomCanReleaseGate: boolean`: Whether "zoom in to see features" is honest advice. Density always releases on zoom; bytes only if the last zoom-in moved the estimate.
- `gateSkipsMeasuredViewport: boolean`: The skip both fetch skeletons apply: the banner is up and its measurement already describes the viewport on screen.

## Methods
- `resolvedByteLimit() => number | undefined`: The budget the worker enforces and the banner compares against — the one spelling of that pair. Undefined when the gate may not act.
- `gateFetchState() => GateFetchState`: The gate as it stands for a fetch about to be issued. Calling it is the capture, which is why it is a method.

RenderLifecycleMixin.text:
# RenderLifecycleMixin (Mixin model, core)

Owns the GPU draw lifecycle for any display that paints to a canvas.

## Actions
- `markCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `resetCanvasDrawn() => void`
- `stopRenderingBackend() => void`
- `renderNow() => void`
- `setOffScreen(offScreen: boolean) => void`
- `setRenderError(error: unknown) => void`: set/clear the render-backend error. Called by `useRenderingBackend`: with the error when the canvas factory rejects (or context-loss re-init fails), and with `undefined` on successful (re)init and on retry.
- `attachRenderingBackend<B>(backend: B, setup: () => RenderingBackendCallbacks<B>) => void`: attach a GPU/Canvas2D backend and install the upload + render autorun pair. Idempotent: re-calling swaps the backend and does not run `setup` again, so the callbacks and everything they close over are the first call's.

## Getters
- `canRender: boolean`: Overridable precondition (default true): both lifecycle autoruns skip their callback entirely while this is false, so a display's `upload`/`render` need no readiness check.
- `rendersCanvas: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this display paints a canvas in its **current** configuration, as opposed to a deliberate static placeholder (LD with the triangle off, sequence past base resolution — both render a message where…
- `paintInert: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): the display has reached a state it will not paint its way out of, so `painted` below should answer *finished* rather than *pending*. Both LGV fetch families fill it through `foundationPaintInert`: a failed…
- `paintSuperseded: boolean`: Overridable hook (default false): what is on the canvas was painted from data a later change has made wrong, so `painted` below should answer *pending* until the repaint lands even though `canvasDrawn` is still true. The per-region fetch…
- `painted: boolean`: **The first-paint answer every consumer outside the display should read**, `canvasDrawn` being only the raw flag: a display that is deliberately not painting a canvas has finished, and reporting it unfinished leaves every waiter on it…

RootAppMenuMixin.text:
# RootAppMenuMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds actions to the root model that let plugins add menus and menu items to the app bar.

RowHeightMixin.text:
# RowHeightMixin (Mixin model, core)

The two-valued row height every multi-row display has. A `rowHeightConfigSchemaFields` slot whose `0` means fit-to-display-height, and an `autoRowHeight` getter saying what that fit divides. Brings the raw `rowHeight` getter, `setRowHeight`, and the resolved `effectiveRowHeight` every consumer reads

## Actions
- `setRowHeight(n: number) => void`: Pin a px row height. `0` is the fit sentinel, but enter fit mode through `setFitToHeight` instead — displays whose `height` getter is content-derived have to re-seed the slot on the way in, and that is what the action is for.

## Getters
- `rowHeight: number`: Raw per-row height setting: `0` is fit-to-display-height, any positive value is a fixed px height. The resolved value is `effectiveRowHeight` — consumers read that, never this. On the config rather than the display snapshot for the same…
- `autoRowHeight: number`: The height fit mode divides between the rows, declared here and **overridden by every display** — the quantity differs in each, so this stub is a slot for the answer rather than an answer. Declaring it lets `effectiveRowHeight` below read…
- `effectiveRowHeight: number`: Resolved per-row height. `rowHeight === 0` divides the display's own `autoRowHeight` across the rows; any positive value is the fixed px height, used as-is however many rows there are.

ScoreAxisMixin.text:
# ScoreAxisMixin (Mixin model, core)

ScoreScaleMixin is the one composer of this mixin, and a display takes the axis by taking that. The mixins stay separate because they answer different questions: this one derives the axis, and the other holds where the declaration is written.

## Getters
- `scaleType: string`: Overridable: where this display's scale type is written down.
- `scaleZero: boolean`: Overridable: where the y scale's `zero` is written down, whether an autoscaled linear or symlog axis reaches 0.
- `domainMin: number | undefined`: Overridable: the lower bound the config really pins, `undefined` where nothing does.
- `domainMax: number | undefined`: Overridable: the upper bound the config really pins.
- `defaultScoreDomain: [number | undefined, number | undefined]`: Overridable hook: what each end of the domain falls back to where the config leaves its bound unset. `[undefined, undefined]` — the default — means autoscale both ends, which is right for a track whose scores have no absolute meaning (a…
- `valueScales: ValueScale[]`: Overridable hook (default none): the scales this display draws its y through. A display that answers it gets an axis per band of each, with its cross-hatches, placed by `DisplayChrome` and `renderDisplaySvg`, and the ticks derived below.
- `autoscaleGroup: string | undefined`: Overridable: the group this display's unpinned ends autoscale in, beside every display in its view naming the same one.
- `autoscaleRange: [number, number] | undefined`: Overridable: what this display's own data spans, before any bound, nice-rounding or group widens it; what a group unions.
- `axisReachesZero: boolean`: Overridable: whether the autoscaled domain reaches 0, `scaleZero` unless the display maps its score to something with no axis.
- `autoscaledDomain: [number, number] | undefined`: The domain an autoscaled axis draws: `autoscaleRange`, widened to every range its `autoscaleGroup` holds, nice-rounded inside this display's own bounds. Each member unions the others' own ranges and never their domains, so a pinned end…
- `resolvedDomainMin: number | undefined`: Resolved lower bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `resolvedDomainMax: number | undefined`: Resolved upper bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `pinsDomain: boolean`: Whether the user has pinned either end, which is a different question from whether either end resolved to a number: `defaultScoreDomain` fills the unset ends in, so a GC content track answers yes to the second with nothing configured. The…
- `axes: YAxis[]`: The axes, one per declared scale whose domain resolved: the position of each tick in the band's pixel space, through `computeYTicks` unless the scale supplies its own ladder, and the position of each of the scale's `rules` inside the…

ScoreAxisWidget.text:

Drawer widget editing one display's value scale, its `encoding.y`. The display is a safe reference, so hiding its track or closing its view empties it rather than leaving the widget writing to a dead node.

- `type = types.literal('ScoreAxisWidget')`

ScoreScaleMixin.text:
# ScoreScaleMixin (Mixin model, core)

Value scale, read and written at a `YScalePaths` map's paths (`encoding.y`, the coverage band's `coverage.encoding.y`). `yChannelSchema` / `yFieldChannelSchema`. Brings `ScoreAxisMixin` plus `scaleType` / `scaleZero` / `fenceQuantile` / `clipFenceQuantile` / `symlogConstant` / `manual*` and their setters, i.e. the whole `ScoreScaleModel` interface the Y axis row and its drawer widget consume

Composes ScoreAxisMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setScaleType(scaleType: string) => void`
- `setScaleZero(zero: boolean) => void`
- `setFenceQuantile(quantile: number) => void`
- `setDomainMin(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setDomainMax(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setMinScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMin`.
- `setMaxScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMax`.
- `setAutoscaleGroup(group?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setScoreRules(rules: (number | ValueScaleRule)[]) => void`: Replaces the y scale's rules whole, each entry in a form the config takes: a number, or `{ value, color, label }`.
- `resetYScale() => void`: Back to what the config.json says, or to what a session-owned track was added with, so an admin's declared axis survives a reset; slots the base leaves unset take their defaults.

## Getters
- `scaleType: string`
- `scaleZero: boolean`: The y scale's `zero`: whether an autoscaled linear or symlog axis reaches 0.
- `fenceQuantile: number`: The y scale's fence quantile: what an unpinned end follows, 1 the extremes and below it that quantile of each sign.
- `clipFenceQuantile: number`: The quantile "Clip extreme outliers" fences at: the one an untick this session wrote over, else the scale's own default where that is below 1, else 0.99.
- `symlogConstant: number`: Raw slot; `0` means "derive from the domain". Resolve it with `resolveSymlogConstant` once the domain is known.
- `domainMin: number | undefined`: The lower bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `domainMax: number | undefined`: The upper bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `autoscaleGroup: string | undefined`: The y scale's autoscale group, `undefined` while it names none.
- `scaleTitle: string`: The y axis title, `''` while unset
- `grid: boolean`: The y axis grid
- `scoreRulesDrawn: boolean`: Whether this display draws the y scale's rules, which is whether the Y axis panel offers Include 0 and the reference lines: a scale it places y through rules a band for them to cross, which a density plot's color-mapped rows and a color…
- `scoreRules: ValueScaleRule[]`: The y scale's rules, read off the live nodes.
- `defaultScoreDomain: [number | undefined, number | undefined]`: Overridable hook: what each end of the domain falls back to where the config leaves its bound unset. `[undefined, undefined]` — the default — means autoscale both ends, which is right for a track whose scores have no absolute meaning (a…
- `valueScales: ValueScale[]`: Overridable hook (default none): the scales this display draws its y through. A display that answers it gets an axis per band of each, with its cross-hatches, placed by `DisplayChrome` and `renderDisplaySvg`, and the ticks derived below.
- `autoscaleRange: [number, number] | undefined`: Overridable: what this display's own data spans, before any bound, nice-rounding or group widens it; what a group unions.
- `axisReachesZero: boolean`: Overridable: whether the autoscaled domain reaches 0, `scaleZero` unless the display maps its score to something with no axis.
- `autoscaledDomain: [number, number] | undefined`: The domain an autoscaled axis draws: `autoscaleRange`, widened to every range its `autoscaleGroup` holds, nice-rounded inside this display's own bounds. Each member unions the others' own ranges and never their domains, so a pinned end…

- `pinsDomain: boolean`: Whether the user has pinned either end, which is a different question from whether either end resolved to a number: `defaultScoreDomain` fills the unset ends in, so a GC content track answers yes to the second with nothing configured. The…
- `axes: YAxis[]`: The axes, one per declared scale whose domain resolved: the position of each tick in the band's pixel space, through `computeYTicks` unless the scale supplies its own ladder, and the position of each of the scale's `rules` inside the…

# SessionTracksManagerSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds session tracks to a session, and stores the user's edits to any track as a delta against its base config.

Composes TracksManagerSessionMixin, ReferenceManagementSessionMixin, BaseSessionModel, SnackbarModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `addSessionTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfiguration) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Add a track config to *this session*: it is added to `sessionTracks`, travels with the session when it is saved or shared, and never reaches the config.json the server hands every visitor.
- `publishTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfiguration) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Publish a track config to the shared catalog if this user can, and fall back to their session if they cannot: an admin's goes to `jbrowse.tracks`, which the admin server writes back into the config.json every visitor is served; everyone…
- `addTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfiguration) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Deprecated alias of `addSessionTrackConf`. Call that, or `publishTrackConf`.
- `updateTrackConfiguration(trackConf: PlainTrackConfig) => void`: Persist an edited track config as a delta (trackConfigDeltas) against its base, the sessionTracks or config.json entry — only the changed slots — so the edits persist, are shared, undo and reset, while changes to untouched fields of the…
- `promoteTrackConfigDeltas(trackId?: string | undefined) => void`: Write this session's track edits into the base configs — the config.json an admin server hands every visitor — and drop the deltas they were held in. One track's, or every track's when `trackId` is omitted, of `promotableTrackIds`: a…
- `resetTrackConfiguration(trackId: string) => void`: Drop a track's delta (trackConfigDeltas) so it reverts to its base, the sessionTracks or jbrowse.tracks entry. Unlike deleteTrackConf this does not dereference the track from open views — the base config re-resolves in place, so an open…
- `deleteTrackConf(trackConf: AnyTrackConfig) => PluggableConfigNode[] | undefined`
- `dereferenceTrack(trackId: string, referring: ReferringNode[]) => void`: Remove `trackId` from every view referring to it and close any config editor widget open on it. Runs immediately: the walk that produced `referring` has finished, so mutating those views here is safe.
- `setSelection(thing: unknown) => void`: set the global selection, i.e. the globally-selected object. can be a feature, a view, or any other object
- `clearSelection() => void`: clears the global selection
- `setHovered(thing: unknown) => void`
- `setHighlightsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setHighlightLabelsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `addHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`: an identical entry is not added twice, so a spec launched again does not stack its bands. Adding shows the bands again, since a highlight made while they are off would otherwise read as nothing happening
- `removeHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`
- `updateHighlight(old: HighlightType, updates: Partial<HighlightType>) => void`
- `setHighlights(highlights: HighlightType[]) => void`
- `setPreferenceOverride(key: string, value: unknown) => void`: set a runtime user-preference override (see `getPreference`). Mutates volatile state; products persist these to localStorage. An `undefined` value deletes the key, so the store holds no dead keys that `getPreference` would read as absent.
- `clearPreferenceOverrides() => void`: clear every runtime preference override at once, so each falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" button.
- `clearPreferenceOverride(key: string) => void`: clear a single runtime preference override (see `getPreference`) so it falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the per-entry reset in the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" confirmation.
- `setScrollZoom(flag: boolean) => void`: set the global scroll-to-zoom preference (see the `scrollZoom` getter)
- `setName(str: string) => void`
- `setFocusedViewId(viewId: string | undefined) => void`: `undefined` is "no view is focused", which the property can hold (`types.maybe`). `takeOut` sets it when the focused view leaves the session. Otherwise the dead id would match no view, since every consumer compares `focusedViewId ===…
- `removeActiveDialog() => void`: Dismiss the dialog on screen as the dialog's close button would, so a dialog that settles a promise on close (an internet account's token prompt) settles it, and drop it from the queue if it did not.
- `queueDialog<T extends DialogComponentType>(callback: (doneCallback: () => void) => [T, ComponentProps<T>]) => void`
- `removeDialog(entry: [DialogComponentType, Record<string, unknown>]) => void`
- `notify(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, action?: SnackAction | SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `notifyError(errorMessage: string, error?: unknown, extra?: unknown, action?: SnackAction | undefined) => void`
- `setErrorDialog(state: ErrorDialogState | undefined) => void`
- `pushSnackbarMessage(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, actions?: SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `popSnackbarMessage() => SnackbarMessage | undefined`
- `removeSnackbarMessage(message: string) => void`

## Getters
- `trackBasesById: Map<string, TrackConfigEntry>`: Each track's base by trackId: its sessionTracks entry, else its config.json entry. Rebuilt when either list changes, never on an edit.
- `tracks: TrackConfigEntry[]`: Session tracks first, then the config tracks, each with its edits. An edit copies the list of bases and lays each delta at its track's position, so past that copy it costs the count of edited tracks.
- `promotableTrackIds: string[]`: The edited tracks `promoteTrackConfigDeltas` can write: those whose base is a config.json entry. A session track's delta has no file to go to.
- `root: TypeOrStateTreeNodeToStateTreeNode<ROOT_MODEL_TYPE>`
- `jbrowse: JBrowseConfigModel`
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`
- `configuration: AnyConfigurationModel`
- `adminMode: boolean`
- `textSearchManager: TextSearchManager`
- `assemblies: BaseAssemblyConfig[]`
- `DialogComponent: DialogComponentType`
- `DialogProps: Record<string, unknown>`
- `animationMode: AnimationMode`: resolved feature-layout animation mode (never undefined)
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: resolved scroll-to-zoom preference. Global and personal (never shared in a session snapshot); every wheel-zoom view reads this single value.
- `numberGrouping: boolean`: resolved thousand-separator preference. Read for display in the Preferences dialog; the formatter itself reads a plain module variable set at startup in each realm (see `setNumberGrouping`), because worker- built strings can't see a…
- `snackbarMessageSet: Map<string, SnackbarMessage>`

## Properties
- `sessionTracks = types.stripDefault( types.array(pluginManager.pluggableConfigSchemaType('track')), [], )`: Tracks the session added, each entry the base its edits (trackConfigDeltas) diff against, as a config.json entry is for a config track.
- `trackConfigDeltas = types.stripDefault( types.frozen<Record<string, PlainTrackConfig>>(), {}, )`: Per-track config overrides, keyed by trackId, stored as a *delta* against the base config (the sessionTracks or jbrowse.tracks entry) rather than a full copy — so a later change to an untouched field of the base still flows through (see…
- `id = ElementId`
- `name = types.string`
- `focusedViewId = types.maybe(types.string)`: id of the view in focus
- `highlights = types.stripDefault( types.array(types.frozen<HighlightType>()), [], )`: translucent bands over genomic regions; every view draws the ones on the assemblies it shows
- `highlightsVisible = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`
- `highlightLabelsVisible = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: whether a band's label is written on it
- `heldForMissingPlugins = types.stripDefault( types.frozen<HeldNode[] | undefined>(), undefined, )`: views, tracks, displays and widgets `pruneUnbuildableNodes` took out of the tree because this build has no plugin for their type, each with the anchor that puts it back. No session code reads its contents, and `pruneUnbuildableNodes`…

## Methods
- `withTrackEdits(base: TrackConfigEntry) => TrackConfigEntry`: `base` with its delta (trackConfigDeltas) merged over it, or `base` itself by identity when it has none, which keeps the hydration cache warm.
- `baseTrackConfig(trackId: string) => TrackConfigEntry | undefined`: The entry `trackId` edits over, hydrated: the one the session added it with, or its config.json entry. What a display's "is this arranged" and "reset" compare its live config against. Per-id reactive, like `getTrackById`.
- `getEditableTrackConfig(trackId: string, schemaType: IAnyType) => AnyConfigurationModel | undefined`: The config node `trackId` resolves to: a live node as it stands, otherwise a private working copy of its current frozen (base+delta) config, so a shown track's in-place quick-edits (setSlot) mutate this copy and never the shared frozen…
- `getTrackConfigChanges(trackId: string) => TrackConfigChange[]`: The overridden slots for `trackId` (empty when it has no delta): each changed setting's path, its base/default value and the edited value. Drives the "view changes" dialog opened from the edited badge.
- `isTrackOverride(trackId: string) => boolean`: Whether `trackId` has an edit over its base config, which drives the "Reset track settings" item and the edited badge. Changed slots, not mere presence in trackConfigDeltas: a delta can hold only content-free display stubs, which must not…
- `getTrackById(id: string) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Config for one trackId — a track, assembly sequence, or connection track — or undefined. Per-id reactive: every display resolves its config through this (via TrackConfigurationReference) and subscribes only to that track's id, so one…
- `getTracksById() => Record<string, AnyTrackConfig>`: Every track config the session can resolve, keyed by trackId. Prefer the per-id reactive `getTrackById(id)`: this map is rebuilt over every track on the first read after any edit, and reading it subscribes the caller to all of them. Kept…
- `getReferringMultiple(trackIds: string[]) => Map<string, ReferringNode[]>`: Walk the tree once and map each requested trackId to the nodes holding a `types.reference` that resolves to it (a view's track entry, a config editor widget). The method matches track configs by trackId, not identity, so a frozen base and…
- `getReferring(trackId: string) => ReferringNode[]`: The nodes currently referring to `trackId` (see getReferringMultiple).
- `getPreferenceDefault(key: string) => unknown`: the admin/embedder `configuration.preferences` value for a key, ignoring any runtime override — i.e. what a reset falls back to
- `getPreference(key: string) => unknown`: resolved value of a user preference: a runtime override if the user set one, otherwise the admin/embedder `configuration.preferences` default. The override map is empty unless the product loads it (web/desktop).
- `getPreferenceChanges() => TrackConfigChange[]`: every scalar preference override that currently differs from its config/admin default, as `{ path, from, to }` rows whose path is the override's own key. A scalar pref (animationMode, scrollZoom) whose override equals the default is…

SpreadsheetView.text:
# SpreadsheetView (View model, spreadsheet-view plugin)

Shows a VCF, BED, BEDPE or STAR-Fusion file as a filterable table whose rows open their genomic location in a new view.

Composes BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

Hand-authored under `defaultSession.views`, with every setting written
directly on the view object. `uri` loads a VCF, BED, BEDPE or STAR-Fusion file
straight into the grid, skipping the import form; `assembly` names the
assembly that resolves genomic coordinates in the rows:
```js
{
  type: 'SpreadsheetView',
  assembly: 'hg38',
  uri: 'https://example.com/variants.vcf.gz',
  fileType: 'VCF',
}
```

## Actions
- `setHeight(newHeight: number) => number`
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`: returns the distance applied, which minHeight can cut short
- `displaySpreadsheet(spreadsheet?: SpreadsheetSnapshot) => void`: show a parsed sheet. One with the same columns as the sheet it replaces, as a reloaded session's re-fetch is, keeps that sheet's column visibility, filters and search
- `setLaunch(launch?: LaunchInput<SpreadsheetViewCommands> | undefined) => void`
- `setError(error: unknown) => void`: a failed launch's error, shown in the import form's banner
- `setDrilldownTracks(trackIds: string[]) => void`
- `registerImportedTrack(assemblyName: string) => void`: Put the loaded file in the session as a track, so the views a row opens show the records it came from. Idempotent: a session that already has a track for the file reuses it.
- `loadSpreadsheet(assemblyName: string, superseded?: (() => boolean) | undefined) => Promise<void>`: fetch, parse and show the wizard's file: the one path a launch, a session reload and the Open button all take
- `returnToImportForm() => void`: drop the sheet and its cached location, so a session reload does not fetch the dismissed file again
- `applyInit(init: LaunchInput<SpreadsheetViewCommands>, superseded?: (() => boolean) | undefined) => Promise<void>`: point the import wizard at a launch's file and load it; without a uri or an assembly, only seed the import form with what it names
- `setDisplayName(name: string) => void`
- `setWidth(newWidth: number) => void`: Sets the view's width, which tells the app when it can start drawing. Certain views like lgv wait for it, because drawing before the width is known may fetch data for regions the view does not need.
- `setBodyMounted(flag: boolean) => void`: See `bodyMounted`. Written by the view's container, which is the only thing that knows whether it rendered the body.
- `setMinimized(flag: boolean) => void`

## Getters
- `pendingLaunch: LaunchInput<SpreadsheetViewCommands & { unknown?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; malformed?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined; legacyInit?: boolean |…`: the launch keys still waiting to be applied
- `showLoading: boolean`: true while the file loads, which `ViewContainer` publishes as `data-view-phase`; the import form stays on screen under a spinner
- `drilldownTrackIds: string[]`: every track a row's drill-down opens with, the loaded file's own first
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders this view's displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…
- `effectiveBodyMounted: boolean`: Whether this view's displays have a canvas to paint into: its body is in the DOM, counting the views it is nested inside, and the body renders them (`rendersDisplays`). This is the question a display's phase asks.
- `ownTracks: AbstractTrackModel[]`: The tracks this view puts in the census, excluding a nested view's.
- `ownViews: AbstractViewModel[]`: The views nested directly inside this one, which the census counts as separate views — a synteny stack's genome rows, a breakpoint split view's panels.

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('SpreadsheetView')`
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultHeight)`: the height of the sheet in pixels
- `hideVerticalResizeHandle = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: chrome switch, for an embed that sizes the view itself
- `drilldownTracks = types.stripDefault(types.array(types.string), [])`: trackIds the views a row opens start with, beside the loaded file's own track: the tumor and normal alignments, a coverage track, an assembly's synteny track
- `importWizard = types.optional(ImportWizardModel, () => ImportWizardModel.create(), )`
- `spreadsheet = types.maybe(Spreadsheet())`
- `launch = types.frozen< LaunchInput<SpreadsheetViewCommands> | undefined >()`: transient launch keys lifted off the view object, applied on attach and then cleared; author them directly on the view
- `id = ElementId`
- `displayName = types.maybe(types.string)`: displayName is displayed in the header of the view, or assembly names being used if none is specified
- `minimized = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, false)`: collapse the view to its header bar and keep it in the session

## Methods
- `menuItems() => { label: string; icon: OverridableComponent<SvgIconTypeMap<{}, "svg">> & { muiName: string; }; onClick: () => void; }[]`

# SvInspectorView (View model, sv-inspector plugin)

Shows a file of structural variants as a table beside a circular view that draws them as chords. The model holds a [SpreadsheetView](../spreadsheetview) and a [CircularView](../circularview) side by side, without extending either.

Composes BaseViewModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

```js

  type: 'SvInspectorView',
```

- `allFeatures: SimpleFeatureSerialized[]`: every record of the sheet, which the chord track holds; filters narrow it through visibleChordIds rather than rebuilding the track

- `variantTrackId: string`
- `featuresCircularTrackConfiguration: { type: string; trackId: string; name: string; adapter: { type: string; features: SimpleFeatureSerialized[]; } & { adapterId: string; }; assemblyNames: string[…`
- `rendersDisplays: boolean`: Overridable hook (default true): whether this view's mounted body renders this view's displays. A linear genome view collapsed to its ruler mounts the scalebar and none of its tracks, so a display in it can no more paint than one in a view…

## Properties
- `type = types.literal('SvInspectorView')`
- `height = types.stripDefault(types.number, defaultHeight)`: height of the whole view in pixels

- `spreadsheetView = types.optional(SpreadsheetModel, () => SpreadsheetModel.create({ type: 'SpreadsheetView', hideVerticalResizeHandle: true, }), )`
- `circularView = types.optional(CircularModel, () => CircularModel.create({ type: 'CircularView', hideVerticalResizeHandle: true, disableImportForm: true, }), )`

SyntenyColorsMixin.text:
# SyntenyColorsMixin (Mixin model, core)

The color settings every view drawing synteny tracks shares — the linear synteny view, the dotplot and the circular view: `TrackColorsMixin`'s `encoding` and palette, the `encoding.opacity` it fades by and the `filter`, over the tracks the view draws. A view supplies `syntenyTracks()`, its opacity default and, optionally, the field it paints by until told otherwise.

Composes TrackColorsMixin, ParkedColorMixin, SyntenyFilterMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setOpacity(value: number) => void`: The opacity slider: the constant, or under a field its range scaled so its most opaque end equals `value`.
- `setOpacityField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Fade by `field` from the current opacity down to 0.3 of it, or with undefined draw every alignment at the opacity the fade reached.
- `observeAttributeRanges(ranges: Record<string, AttributeRange>) => void`: Fold one fetch's observed attribute spans into the domain this view paints and labels its ramps with. Called by each display as its fetch lands, because the accumulation has to outlive the payload it came from: the previous window's span…
- `resetAttributeRanges() => void`: Forget the accumulated domain, leaving `attributeRanges` reporting what the loaded fetches cover and nothing else.
- `setHideUnlabelled(value: boolean) => void`
- `setColorField(field: string | undefined) => void`: Set the field the view paints by over `encoding.color`, undefined unsetting it for the view's default, and rescale the ramp, which is the only way back from a domain one outlying window widened.
- `setColorValue(value: string | undefined) => void`: Paint every alignment `value`, undefined returning to the view's default.
- `openSolidColorDialog() => void`: The picker Color by's Solid color... opens.
- `setColorDomain(domain: string[]) => void`: Declare the order a text column's labels take. The labels listed lead, the rest follow sorted; an empty list gives back the order the fetches found them in.
- `setTrackColor(trackId: string, value: string | undefined) => void`: Pin one track's color under `encoding.color: 'track'`, or release it back to an automatic palette slot.
- `clearTrackColors() => void`
- `parkColor(name: string, written: ColorSlots, next: unknown) => void`: Hold `written`'s field and its members under `name` where `next`, the write about to replace it, names another field; a string `next` is a constant.
- `setFilter(predicates: FieldPredicate[]) => void`
- `setLowerBound(field: string, value: number) => void`: The slider on one field: `field` at least `value`, or no lower bound at 0.

## Getters
- `defaultOpacity: number`: The constant opacity a reset returns to: low on the synteny view for dense whole-genome hairballs, opaque on the dotplot.
- `opacitySetting: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot`: `encoding.opacity` as its snapshot holds it.
- `opacityFade: SyntenyOpacitySnapshot | undefined`: What the color pass fades each alignment by: the field's mapping with its range as shares of `opacityLevel`, or undefined while `encoding.opacity` draws its constant, so the slider recolors nothing either way.
- `opacityLevel: number`: The opacity every alignment draws at before a field's fade: the shader's uniform (`opacityLevel`).
- `opacityField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.opacity` fades by, undefined while it draws its constant.

# ThemeManagerSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds the UI theme to a session: the selected theme, light or dark mode or following the OS, and the themes an admin adds through `extraThemes`.

## Actions
- `setThemeName(name: string) => void`: Pick a palette. A name from before light and dark were an axis sets the mode it spelled as well, so an old share link, a saved figure spec and `jbrowse-img --theme darkStock` all still mean what they said. A palette pinned to one mode also…
- `noteDarkReader() => void`
- `setSystemPrefersDark(dark: boolean) => void`
- `setSystemThemeOverride(mode?: PaletteMode | undefined) => void`: Hold a session on the mode its setting is not asking for, or `undefined` to return to the setting. The toolbar's sun/moon writes this, so it stays in the toolbar after a click. The OS flipping clears it, since by then the OS has come round…
- `setThemeMode(mode: ThemeModeSelection) => void`: Draw the session light or dark, leaving the palette alone. `system` follows the OS preference. Satisfies `ThemeModeSession`, so `useSessionPalette` works against an app session and an embedded one alike, and a host that tracks dark mode…

## Getters
- `themeName: string`: Which palette is in effect. A stored name whose theme an admin has since dropped reads as `default` without the stored value being touched, so it comes back if the plugin supplying it loads again.
- `themeMode: ThemeModeSelection`: Light, dark, or following the OS — the axis the palette is drawn along, and what the mode picker shows. `effectiveThemeMode` is the one to read for a color decision.
- `selectedThemeMode: PaletteMode`: Light or dark as the reader chose it, `system` resolved against the OS or the toolbar's hold. What a file leaves the session in, since Dark Reader never touches the file.
- `effectiveThemeMode: PaletteMode`: `selectedThemeMode`, but dark while Dark Reader darkens the page.
- `themeIsDark: boolean`: Whether what is drawn right now is dark. Read off the resolved palette rather than the mode, so a palette pinned to one mode — an `extraThemes` entry declaring `mode: 'dark'` — answers for itself.
- `themeOptions: SerializableThemeArgs`
- `palette: JBrowsePalette`: Every color JBrowse renders, resolved to plain strings. This is what rendering reads: it needs no React context, it crosses the RPC worker boundary as itself, and it costs no UI toolkit. Prefer it over `theme` anywhere the answer wanted is…
- `styleTheme: JBrowseStyleTheme`: The palette plus the sizing tokens `makeStyles` reads — spacing, corner radius, type scale. This is what a product mounts on `StyleThemeProvider`; it costs no UI toolkit, and it is derived from the same `themeOptions` as `theme`, so a…
- `theme: Theme`: The Material UI theme, for the components that are Material UI. Its palette is spliced from the same `resolvePalette` call as `palette` above, so the two cannot disagree.

## Methods
- `allThemes() => ThemeMap`
- `getActiveThemeOptions(name?: string | undefined) => ThemeOptions`: Raw `ThemeOptions` for the active theme, or a named override (used by the SVG-export theme picker). Unlike `theme` (a built, non-serializable MUI theme), this is the plain options object every view's SVG export threads into each display's…
