- `colorDomain: readonly string[]`: `encoding.color.scale.domain`, the order a text column's labels take. Read from that slot alone, so a key-only edit (`legend.title`, `scale.names`) recolors nothing.
- `colorRange: readonly string[]`: The colors a text column's labels take in domain order: `encoding.color.scale.range`, else its `scheme` sampled once per domain value
- `colorableAttributes: string[]`: Distinct numeric columns across the overlaid tracks, in first-seen order — two tracks declaring `dn` offer one `dn` mode, not two.
- `attributeRanges: Record<string, AttributeRange>`: The span each numeric channel covers: unioned over the loaded displays, and over every fetch this view has already taken (`seenAttributeRanges`). A column has no declared domain, so this is what its ramp scales to, what the legend labels…
- `colorableTracks: ColorableTrack[]`: `colorableTrackConfigs` paired with whatever color the user pinned. This is the single definition of "the tracks that get colors" — the palette, the legend and the palette menu all read it, so they cannot disagree about which tracks are in…
- `trackColorAssignments: Map<string, string>`: trackId -> the color it draws in under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Assigned across the whole view rather than per display, so an automatic slot can't duplicate a color pinned on a sibling.
- `colorField: string | undefined`: The field `encoding.color` paints by, undefined for the default color.
- `hideUnlabelled: boolean`: Whether the filter drops the alignments with no value for the field the view paints by, the "Hide unlabelled rows" box.
- `hasLegendKey: boolean`: Whether the mode has a key worth a box: a track palette, a ramp, a reader-named column, or strand wherever the shape does not show it (`shapeShowsStrand`), which leaves the color the only strand cue.
- `colorLegendChips: ColorChip[]`: Legend rows naming the overlaid tracks — one per track with its palette color, however many levels it is on, and only under `encoding.color: 'track'`, since every other mode has a fixed legend.
- `colorScales: ColorScale[]`: The active mode's key, or none for a mode without one. View-wide rather than per display because the key is one box for the whole view, and the ramp domain it labels is the view's.
- `parkedColor: ColorSlots | undefined`: The `color` object's parked field
- `predicates: FieldPredicate[]`: The `filter` list as the predicate compiler reads it.
- `minLength: number`: The lower bound on `length`, 0 for none.

## Properties
- `encoding = types.stripDefault(syntenyEncodingConfigSchema, {})`: The channels every track in the view paints with, a [](/docs/config/syntenyencoding) object. Its `color` is a [](/docs/config/syntenycolor) channel: `"strand"`, `"query"`, `"reference"`, `"track"`, a measurement (`identity`, `mapq`,…
- `trackColors = types.map(types.string)`: trackId -> explicit color under `encoding.color: 'track'`. Absent means the track takes an automatic slot from the palette.
- `parkedColors = types.maybe(types.frozen<Record<string, ColorSlots>>())`: By color object, the field the last write away from one left, with its members
- `filter = types.stripDefault(fieldPredicateArray(), [])`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries an alignment must all pass. A field is any field `color` takes, or `length`, the alignment's bp on its own axis: `[{ field: 'length', gte: 10000 }]` clears a…

## Methods
- `colorableTrackConfigs() => { trackId: string; name: string; }[]`: The tracks that can take a palette slot, in paint order. Overridden by the composing view; a method rather than a getter because that is the form MST overrides cleanly.
- `colorableAttributeNames() => string[]`: Columns the overlaid tracks declare (an ortholog table's `attributeColumns`), each of which the palette menu offers as a separate mode, less the reserved `color` column. Overridden by the composing view, which is the only thing that can…
- `loadedAttributeRanges() => Record<string, AttributeRange>[]`: One entry per loaded display: the span each numeric channel actually covered in the data that display fetched. Overridden by the composing view, which is the only thing that can reach the displays.
- `legendAlpha() => number`: Overridable hook: the alpha the key's chips are composited with. The ribbon views draw at a global alpha over the band's ground; a view that draws opaque leaves it.
- `legendCigarOps() => number | undefined`: Overridable hook: the indel ops the key lists a chip for, so it names only what the eye can find. `undefined` is the static menu preview; the dotplot draws flat points and never a CIGAR op.
- `colorSurface() => SyntenyColorSurface`: Overridable hook: what draws each alignment, a ribbon with match and indel blocks or one flat point (the dotplot). The key, the menu's help text and which fields key at all read it.
- `offersReferenceColor() => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the view has a shared reference for the `reference` field to anchor on. It needs a stack of two or more levels; below that it is query or target by another name.
- `shapeShowsStrand() => boolean`: Overridable hook: whether an alignment's shape shows its strand, which spares the strand colors a key. A linear ribbon twists against its rows' directions, which their rulers show; a whole-genome dotplot is mostly dots with no slope to…
- `trackColorFor(trackId: string) => string`
- `parkedColorOf(name: string) => ColorSlots | undefined`
- `lowerBound(field: string) => number`: The lower bound the filter puts on `field`, 0 for none.

TrackHeightMixin.text:
# TrackHeightMixin (Mixin model, core)

Internal vertical scroll. `scrollContentHeight` and `scrollViewportHeight` (both default 0 = doesn't scroll). Brings the derived `scrollableHeight`, the clamped `setScrollTop` and the autorun that re-clamps when content shrinks

## Actions
- `setScrollTop(scrollTop: number) => void`
- `setHostHeight(height: number | undefined) => void`
- `setHeight(displayHeight: number) => number`
- `resizeHeight(distance: number) => number`
- `expandToContentHeight() => number`: Grow the track by the content it is hiding, for the resize handle's double click. Goes through `resizeHeight` so grow mode's override leaves grow first.

## Getters
- `configuredHeight: number`: The height the `height` slot asks for, which a drag or a session sets.
- `allottedHeight: number`: The height the display lays itself out in: its host's where one sets it, else the slot's.
- `height: number`
- `resizing: boolean`: True for the duration of a height drag on this track, whichever handle is running it. A display whose row geometry is a function of the track height restretches every row per animation frame, and can use this to sit an expensive per-frame…
- `scrollContentHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the content that scrolls, in px.
- `scrollViewportHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the height of the window it scrolls behind, in px.
- `scrollableHeight: number`: How far the content scrolls. A sub-pixel overflow is 0: a fit mode that divides the viewport across n rows multiplies back to a few ULPs over it, and an extent of 1e-14px still draws a scrollbar and holds the wheel away from the page.

TrackMenuItemsSessionMixin.text:
# TrackMenuItemsSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds two track-menu wrappers (`getTrackListMenuItems` for the hierarchical selector, `getTrackActionMenuItems` for the in-view label menu) shared by the full web and desktop sessions. Both are pure functions of `getTrackActions`, which each session supplies (web gates on edit rights; desktop adds indexing).

## Methods
- `getTrackListMenuItems(config: AnyTrackConfig, view?: TrackActionView | undefined) => MenuItem[]`: flattened menu items for use in hierarchical track selector
- `getTrackActionMenuItems({ config, view, }: { config: BaseTrackConfig; view?: TrackActionView | undefined; }) => MenuItem[]`: track menu with About + "Track actions" submenu for the in-view label

TrackMenuSessionMixin.text:
# TrackMenuSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

The minimal track menus used by the embedded react views, which have no track-editing actions to offer: just "About track" plus any plugin-contributed items (`Core-extraTrackMenuItems`). Has the same shape as the full `TrackMenuItemsSessionMixin`, minus the Settings/Copy/Delete actions, so both menu surfaces stay consistent across products.

## Methods
- `getTrackListMenuItems(config: AnyTrackConfig, view?: TrackActionView | undefined) => MenuItem[]`: flattened menu items for use in hierarchical track selector
- `getTrackActionMenuItems({ config, view }: { config: AnyConfigurationModel; view?: TrackActionView; }) => MenuItem[]`

TracksManagerSessionMixin.text:
# TracksManagerSessionMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds track configs to a session: looking one up by trackId among the config's tracks, assembly sequences and connection tracks, and adding or editing one.

Composes ReferenceManagementSessionMixin, BaseSessionModel, SnackbarModel — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `addSessionTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfiguration) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Add a track config to *this session*.
- `publishTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfiguration) => TrackConfigEntry | undefined`: Add a track config wherever *this user's* catalog edits belong — the "Add track" workflows, where an admin adding a track means to add it for the whole site. `SessionTracksManagerSessionMixin` overrides it to send a non-admin's to the…
- `addTrackConf(trackConf: AnyConfiguration) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Deprecated alias of `addSessionTrackConf`. Call that, or `publishTrackConf`, which say which destination they mean.
- `updateTrackConfiguration(trackConf: { [key: string]: unknown; trackId: string; }) => void`: Persist edited track config back to the in-memory jbrowse config. The session-tracks mixin overrides this so a non-admin's edits become a shareable session-track override instead.
- `deleteTrackConf(trackConf: AnyTrackConfig) => void`
- `dereferenceTrack(trackId: string, referring: ReferringNode[]) => void`: Remove `trackId` from every view referring to it and close any config editor widget open on it. Runs immediately: the walk that produced `referring` has finished, so mutating those views here is safe.
- `setSelection(thing: unknown) => void`: set the global selection, i.e. the globally-selected object. can be a feature, a view, or any other object
- `clearSelection() => void`: clears the global selection
- `setHovered(thing: unknown) => void`
- `setHighlightsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setHighlightLabelsVisible(arg: boolean) => void`
- `addHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`: an identical entry is not added twice, so a spec launched again does not stack its bands. Adding shows the bands again, since a highlight made while they are off would otherwise read as nothing happening
- `removeHighlight(highlight: HighlightType) => void`
- `updateHighlight(old: HighlightType, updates: Partial<HighlightType>) => void`
- `setHighlights(highlights: HighlightType[]) => void`
- `setPreferenceOverride(key: string, value: unknown) => void`: set a runtime user-preference override (see `getPreference`). Mutates volatile state; products persist these to localStorage. An `undefined` value deletes the key, so the store holds no dead keys that `getPreference` would read as absent.
- `clearPreferenceOverrides() => void`: clear every runtime preference override at once, so each falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" button.
- `clearPreferenceOverride(key: string) => void`: clear a single runtime preference override (see `getPreference`) so it falls back to its config/admin default. Backs the per-entry reset in the Preferences dialog "Reset to defaults" confirmation.
- `setScrollZoom(flag: boolean) => void`: set the global scroll-to-zoom preference (see the `scrollZoom` getter)
- `setName(str: string) => void`
- `setFocusedViewId(viewId: string | undefined) => void`: `undefined` is "no view is focused", which the property can hold (`types.maybe`). `takeOut` sets it when the focused view leaves the session. Otherwise the dead id would match no view, since every consumer compares `focusedViewId ===…
- `removeActiveDialog() => void`: Dismiss the dialog on screen as the dialog's close button would, so a dialog that settles a promise on close (an internet account's token prompt) settles it, and drop it from the queue if it did not.
- `queueDialog<T extends DialogComponentType>(callback: (doneCallback: () => void) => [T, ComponentProps<T>]) => void`
- `removeDialog(entry: [DialogComponentType, Record<string, unknown>]) => void`
- `notify(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, action?: SnackAction | SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `notifyError(errorMessage: string, error?: unknown, extra?: unknown, action?: SnackAction | undefined) => void`
- `setErrorDialog(state: ErrorDialogState | undefined) => void`
- `pushSnackbarMessage(message: string, level?: NotificationLevel | undefined, actions?: SnackAction[] | undefined) => void`
- `popSnackbarMessage() => SnackbarMessage | undefined`
- `removeSnackbarMessage(message: string) => void`

## Getters
- `trackBasesById: Map<string, TrackConfigEntry>`: Each track's base by trackId: the entry its edits diff against. Here the config.json entry, which an edit writes directly.
- `tracks: TrackConfigEntry[]`
- `root: TypeOrStateTreeNodeToStateTreeNode<ROOT_MODEL_TYPE>`
- `jbrowse: JBrowseConfigModel`
- `rpcManager: RpcManager`
- `configuration: AnyConfigurationModel`
- `adminMode: boolean`
- `textSearchManager: TextSearchManager`
- `assemblies: BaseAssemblyConfig[]`
- `DialogComponent: DialogComponentType`
- `DialogProps: Record<string, unknown>`
- `animationMode: AnimationMode`: resolved feature-layout animation mode (never undefined)
- `scrollZoom: boolean`: resolved scroll-to-zoom preference. Global and personal (never shared in a session snapshot); every wheel-zoom view reads this single value.
- `numberGrouping: boolean`: resolved thousand-separator preference. Read for display in the Preferences dialog; the formatter itself reads a plain module variable set at startup in each realm (see `setNumberGrouping`), because worker- built strings can't see a…
- `snackbarMessageSet: Map<string, SnackbarMessage>`

## Properties
- `id = ElementId`
- `name = types.string`
- `focusedViewId = types.maybe(types.string)`: id of the view in focus
- `highlights = types.stripDefault( types.array(types.frozen<HighlightType>()), [], )`: translucent bands over genomic regions; every view draws the ones on the assemblies it shows
- `highlightsVisible = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`
- `highlightLabelsVisible = types.stripDefault(types.boolean, true)`: whether a band's label is written on it
- `heldForMissingPlugins = types.stripDefault( types.frozen<HeldNode[] | undefined>(), undefined, )`: views, tracks, displays and widgets `pruneUnbuildableNodes` took out of the tree because this build has no plugin for their type, each with the anchor that puts it back. No session code reads its contents, and `pruneUnbuildableNodes`…

## Methods
- `withTrackEdits(base: TrackConfigEntry) => TrackConfigEntry`: A track's base as the session resolves it, its edits applied. Here the base itself.
- `getTrackById(id: string) => AnyTrackConfig | undefined`: Config for one trackId — a track, assembly sequence, or connection track — or undefined. Per-id reactive: every display resolves its config through this (via TrackConfigurationReference) and subscribes only to that track's id, so one…
- `getTracksById() => Record<string, AnyTrackConfig>`: Every track config the session can resolve, keyed by trackId. Prefer the per-id reactive `getTrackById(id)`: this map is rebuilt over every track on the first read after any edit, and reading it subscribes the caller to all of them. Kept…
- `getReferringMultiple(trackIds: string[]) => Map<string, ReferringNode[]>`: Walk the tree once and map each requested trackId to the nodes holding a `types.reference` that resolves to it (a view's track entry, a config editor widget). The method matches track configs by trackId, not identity, so a frozen base and…
- `getReferring(trackId: string) => ReferringNode[]`: The nodes currently referring to `trackId` (see getReferringMultiple).
- `getPreferenceDefault(key: string) => unknown`: the admin/embedder `configuration.preferences` value for a key, ignoring any runtime override — i.e. what a reset falls back to
- `getPreference(key: string) => unknown`: resolved value of a user preference: a runtime override if the user set one, otherwise the admin/embedder `configuration.preferences` default. The override map is empty unless the product loads it (web/desktop).
- `getPreferenceChanges() => TrackConfigChange[]`: every scalar preference override that currently differs from its config/admin default, as `{ path, from, to }` rows whose path is the override's own key. A scalar pref (animationMode, scrollZoom) whose override equals the default is…

TreeSidebarMixin.text:
# TreeSidebarMixin (Mixin model, core)

Row set with a dendrogram sidebar, its arrangement the display's `rows` config object and its row colors the `rowColor` object, each written as a session edit to the track's config so undo, reset and a share link reach it and it survives unticking the track. Brings the sidebar toggles, the `runClustering` / `clusterRegion` and `sortRowsBy` declarative launch specs `setupTreeSidebarAutoruns` consumes, the row arrangement every shared consumer goes through, the rows derived from it (`editableSources`, `clusterableSources`) with the arrangement dialog's `applyRowEdits`, the `root` getter, and…

## Actions
- `setShowTree(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowBranchLength(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setShowRowLabels(arg: boolean) => void`
- `setTreeAreaWidth(width: number) => void`
- `setRunClustering(arg?: boolean | undefined) => void`
- `setClusterRegion(arg?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setSortRowsBy(arg?: RowSortSpec | undefined) => void`: Trigger (or clear) a one-shot declarative row sort; consumed and reset by `setupRowSortAutorun`.
- `setHoveredTreeNode(node?: HoveredTreeNode | undefined) => void`
- `setTreeCanvasRef(ref: HTMLCanvasElement | null) => void`
- `setMouseoverCanvasRef(ref: HTMLCanvasElement | null) => void`
- `setRowOrder(rows: readonly { name: string; }[], run?: ClusterRun | undefined) => void`: Arrange the rows in `rows`' order, ahead of any name the current order has that `rows` does not. A clustering run passes its result, and the tree and its provenance land with the order; any other reorder that moves a row drops the tree,…
- `setRowLabels(labels: Readonly<Record<string, string>>) => void`: The labels drawn in place of row names, whole: a row the map does not name shows the name it arrived with.
- `setRowFocus(names?: readonly string[] | undefined) => void`: Narrow the display to `names`, or show every row again.
- `applyRowEdits(rows: readonly S[], rowColor?: RowColorSnapshot | undefined) => void`: The arrangement dialog's submit: the rows in their new order, each with the label the reader left on it, and the `rowColor` object the dialog shows, written where it differs from the config's. The labels go to `rows` by the rule…
- `resetRowArrangement() => void`: Return every arrangement member — order, labels, tree, provenance and focus — to what the config declares, leaving `rows.field`, and the `rowColor` colors to `rowColorResetTarget`: the config's for the choice, which stays.
- `setRowColorChoice(choice: string) => void`: Color the rows by `choice`, as a menu picks it: '' for None, `name` for Each row, or a field, starting from `rowColorFor`. A pick of the current choice writes nothing.
- `focusLegendEntry(scaleId: string, value: string) => void`: `LegendHost`'s hook: a click on a row color key entry narrows the rows to those it lists. Every other scale's entries name colors, not rows, and stay inert.

## Getters
- `showTree: boolean`: Whether the dendrogram sidebar is drawn.
- `showBranchLength: boolean`: Whether the tree draws nodes at their branch length (dendrogram) or evenly by topology (cladogram).
- `showRowLabels: boolean`: Whether each row's name is drawn over the left of the plot.
- `treeAreaWidth: number`: Width in px of the sidebar the dendrogram draws in. On the config rather than the display snapshot for the same reason `height` is: the config node outlives the display instance, so a dragged width survives unticking and reticking the…
- `rowSort: string[]`: The row order, `rows.sort`: the rows it names lead, in its order, and the rest follow as `unlistedRowsSort` says.
- `rowLabels: Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The labels drawn in place of row names, `rows.labels`, by name.
- `rowTreeProvenance: ClusterProvenance | undefined`: What `rowTree` was computed from, the locus and the settings; undefined for a tree that arrived as data.
- `rowFocus: readonly string[] | undefined`: The row names a focus narrows the display to, `rows.kept` — a clade picked off the tree or a key row's rows — or undefined while every row shows.
- `rowColorSetting: RowColorSetting`: The `rowColor` object: the row field whose values take colors, `name` where it names none, and the values with an assigned color.
- `baseRowColorSetting: RowColorSetting`: The `rowColor` object this display's base declares, which a reset returns to and "is this the reader's" compares against.
- `baseRowSort: readonly string[]`: The `rows.sort` this display's base declares: the order a display whose rows are values found on features lists them in.
- `discoveredRows: S[]`: Overridable hook, which every display overrides: the rows as the data reports them, before any arrangement. A getter, and a stable-identity one wherever the rows come off region payloads, so a refetch of the same rows re-derives nothing.
- `guideTreeNewick: string | undefined`: Overridable hook: the guide tree the display's adapter supplies, as newick, which `rowTree` draws while some rotation of it lists `rows.sort`. It never enters `rows.tree`, since the adapter re-supplies it on every load. `undefined` by…
- `rowAlias: RowAlias | undefined`: Overridable hook: the name a row also answers to, for a display whose rows stand for something named by another name (a variant display's haplotype rows, each answering to its sample). An order, a label, a color and a focus written against…
- `unlistedRowsSort: UnlistedRowsSort`: Overridable hook: where the rows `rowOrder` does not list go, in the order they arrived by default.
- `rowBanding: RowBanding | undefined`: Overridable hook: the field the rows stack in bands by and the bands listed first, or undefined, the default, for no bands.
- `svgSidebar: SvgSidebarProps | undefined`: Overridable hook: what the SVG export draws in the sidebar left of the track, or undefined, the default, for none. `SvgTreeSidebar` draws it and `svgSidebarWidth` sizes the gutter from it.
- `rowsHeaderHeight: number`: Overridable hook: the px of bands, an axis inset or anything else the display stacks above its rows, 0 by default.
- `rowFocusLineHeight: number`: The line the "Showing N rows" chip takes above the first row while `rows.kept` narrows the rows, 0 while every row shows.
- `rowsTopOffset: number`: Where the rows start in the display's box: under the display's own `rowsHeaderHeight` and the focus chip's line. Every row painter, hit test, label, tree and export places the rows from here.
- `guideTree: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: `guideTreeNewick` parsed and rotated towards `rows.sort`; undefined while the display supplies none.
- `guideTreeHonoursDomain: boolean`: Whether the rotated guide tree lists `rows.sort`'s names in `rows.sort`'s order, which holds exactly when some rotation of it does.
- `rowTree: string | undefined`: The tree that arranges the rows, as newick: `rows.tree`, else the guide tree while `guideTreeHonoursDomain`. A reorder no rotation produces hides the guide tree, and a reset brings it back.
- `rowOrder: readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the row names in display order, `rows.sort` by default; MAF puts a drawn tree's leaves first.
- `expandedRows: S[]`: `discoveredRows` through `expandRows`: the rows at the granularity drawn, before any arrangement.
- `sharesPanel: boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the rows share one panel, so nothing but color tells them apart. False by default.
- `rowColorPaintsMarks: boolean`: Overridable hook: whether a row's color paints its data marks, which holds while nothing else colors them. True by default.
- `rowNoun: string`: Overridable hook: what one row is called, which titles the row color key where it lists the rows by name in a shared panel. "Row" by default, which only a display that shares a panel would show; a wiggle overlay's rows are subtracks.
- `internalRowFields: readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the row fields that are display plumbing, which the arrangement dialog never lists as a column.
- `rowColorFields: readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the row fields a reader can color the rows by, offered beside None and Each row. By default every field a row has but its name, label and colors.
- `rowBandingNotices: string[]`: A line for the corner notice when rows have arrived and none has the field `rowBanding` bands by, which then bands nothing. Each display spreads it into its `notices`.
- `rowPaletteDeals: boolean`: Whether the palette deals each row a color by name: only where the rows share one panel and their color paints the marks.
- `rowColorDealRows: readonly S[]`: The rows the palette deals over: `expandedRows`, in the order their source lists them, so no `rows.sort` (the config's or a reorder's), focus or relabel recolors a row, and a tables export deals the same.
- `rowColorIsCustom: boolean`: Whether `rowColor` gives its field's values colors the config does not, so "Reset row order" is offered for a recolor too: whether `rowColorResetTarget` has anything to write. A choice of row color source is no arrangement, so it is never…
- `rowColorChoice: string`: The choice of what colors the rows, as the arrangement dialog and a menu offer it: '' for none dealt, `name` for a palette color each, or a field.
- `rowColorField: string`: The field that colors the rows, or '' for `name`.
- `dealtValueColors: ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: The color each value of the config's `rowColor` field takes, listed pairs first and then in the order dealt.
- `rowColorFieldsOffered: readonly string[]`: The fields a reader can color the rows by: `rowColorFields`, and the current one where the rows lack it, so it still shows as chosen.
- `resolvedRowColors: ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: Each row's color, by name: its `rowColor` entry, else the row's `color`, else the palette's where `rowPaletteDeals`. The one answer every display paints a row's color from.
- `rowArrangementIsCustom: boolean`: Whether the arrangement differs from what the config declares — what "Reset row order" is offered on.
- `editableSources: S[]`: The rows in the reader's arrangement, each with its resolved `rowColor`, and with no focus or band: the list the arrangement dialog edits, so a submit writes back only what the reader chose. `expandedRows` itself while nothing is arranged…
- `rowColorKeyInputs: RowColorKeyInputs`: What the row color key and its focus read of the colors.
- `rowColorScales: CategoricalScale[]`: The row color key, which every display spreads into its `colorScales`: one scale titled by the `rowColor` field, or none where it has no entries. Its entries (`rowColorKeyEntries`) show where the labels cannot name the colors: by a field,…
- `clusterableSources: S[]`: Overridable hook: `editableSources` narrowed to the focus, the rows a clustering run clusters, and deliberately not the display's decorated `sources`, whose palette and band a run has no business writing back. MAF applies a focus as given…
- `parsedTree: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: `rowTree` parsed. A run rotated its tree in the same write as the order it produced; a tree that arrived as data rotates towards `rows.sort` here, and the guide tree is `guideTree`'s parse.
- `rotatableRowTree: string | undefined`: The tree a reorder rotates rather than drops, as newick: a supplied `rows.tree`, one with no provenance, else the guide tree while `guideTreeHonoursDomain`. A computed tree is never one, since its run rotated it already.
- `root: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: The parsed tree narrowed to the focus.
- `bandedRows: { rows: S[]; bands: RowBand[]; }`: `bandedSources` and `rowBands`, from one pass over the rows.
- `bandedSources: S[]`: `clusterableSources` stacked in bands by `rowBanding`, each band's rows in their arranged order: the rows each display paints its palette over. `clusterableSources` itself while nothing bands.
- `rowBands: readonly RowBand[]`: Each band's value, label and the rows it spans in `bandedSources`; none while nothing bands.
- `sources: S[]`: Overridable hook: the rows drawn, top to bottom, `bandedSources` by default. MAF drops its hidden reference row.
- `autoClusterReady: boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the declarative `runClustering` run may start, two or more `clusterableSources` by default.
- `treeRoot: HierarchyNode<NewickNode> | undefined`: Overridable hook: the tree `hierarchy` positions, `root` by default. `computeClusterHierarchy` declines to position a tree whose leaves are no longer the rows drawn, so a display that hides a row prunes it from the tree here too, or the…
- `drawsTree: boolean`: Overridable hook: whether the dendrogram draws at all, true by default; off wherever the rows it would lay against are not drawn. This is the single gate: the on-screen sidebar, the SVG export, `spatialIndex` (subtree hover) and the…
- `awaitingDependentData: boolean`: Fills `FetchMixin`'s hook: a declared `runClustering` run is due, so the loading scrim and the export wait for the rows it orders. The run clears the flag when it settles, failed or not.
- `rowsContentHeight: number`: The px the rows stack to, `sources` × `effectiveRowHeight`, which the dendrogram's leaves spread over: the content the rows scroll through, never the viewport they scroll inside.
- `hierarchy: ClusterHierarchyNode | undefined`: The dendrogram positioned against the rows drawn, or undefined while there is no tree or `drawsTree` is off. `computeClusterHierarchy` checks the tree's leaves against the drawn row names, the backstop against anything reordering `sources`…
- `spatialIndex: TreeSpatialIndex | undefined`: The hit index the sidebar's subtree hover reads, built from `hierarchy`.
- `clusterPartition: string[][] | undefined`: The names of the rows a clustering run clusters, by band, so each band clusters apart and the run writes one forest; undefined while fewer than two bands stack.
- `treelessBandCount: number`: How many bands the tree draws no dendrogram for, because it holds no clade whose leaves are that band's rows in order; 0 with no tree or no bands.
- `treeHasBranchLengths: boolean`: Whether the tree has merge heights, so a dendrogram layout differs from the cladogram; gates the "Tree branch lengths" toggle.

## Properties
- `runClustering = types.maybe(types.boolean)`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `LinearGenomeView`'s `init`: a session or config sets this true and the real clustering RPC runs once automatically, with no dialog, as soon as the display reports itself ready.…
- `clusterRegion = types.maybe(types.string)`: Where that run reads from, as a locstring (whitespace-separated for several). Clustering is region-scoped, so naming the locus lets a session cluster on the signal and then show it against its context. Cleared with `runClustering`, since…
- `sortRowsBy = types.maybe(types.frozen<RowSortSpec>())`: Transient declarative launch spec, the same idea as `runClustering`: set `{refName, pos}` to order the rows once by the value each row has at that genomic column — the session-expressible form of the right-click "Sort rows by ... here".…

## Methods
- `expandRows(rows: S[]) => S[]`: Overridable hook: the discovered rows as the rows drawn, the rows themselves by default; a variant display's phased mode expands each sample to its haplotypes.
- `svgSidebarWidth(text?: ExportTextStyle | undefined) => number`: Px the SVG export reserves left of the track for `svgSidebar`, measured in the export's text.
- `rowBand(row: S) => string`: Overridable hook: the band a row stacks in while `rowBanding` is set, by default its value of the banding field, '' for none.
- `rowColorDeclaredValues(_field: string) => readonly string[]`: Overridable hook: the values of the row field `field` the config declares, which the palette deals first, in this order, whether or not a loaded row carries them, so a row arriving later moves no color. None by default.
- `dealtValueColorsFor(setting: RowColorSnapshot) => ReadonlyMap<string, string>`: The color each value takes under `setting` (`dealValueColors`), which the arrangement dialog shows before it writes the setting.
- `rowColorFor(choice: string) => RowColorSetting`: The `rowColor` object `choice` starts from (`startingRowColor`): the current object's where it shows that choice, else the config's.
- `orderDropsRowTree(order: readonly string[]) => boolean`: Whether ordering the rows as `order` drops the tree: one a reorder rotates drops only for an order no rotation of it lists, and any other drops for any change.
- `rowOrderWillDropTree(next: readonly { name: string; }[]) => boolean`: Whether the arrangement dialog's submit of `next` drops the tree: an order that moves no row is not written, so it drops nothing.

TriangleMatrixMixin.text:
# TriangleMatrixMixin (Mixin model, core)

A matrix drawn as a triangle over the view's axis (Hi-C, LD): the fetched payload (`rpcData`), the canvas box (`canvasWidth`, `matrixHeight` under the `matrixTop` hook), the rotate-and-squash transform and its inverse (`cellToScreen`, `screenToCell`), the frame the marks read (`triangleFrame`), the one-cell region map and canvas-wide block the mark backend draws (`matrixRegions`, `matrixBlocks`), and the `heightMode` slot. Composes after `TrackHeightMixin`, `GlobalFetchMixin` and `LegendMixin`

## Actions
- `setRpcData(data: D) => void`
- `setHeightMode(mode: "fit" | "fixed") => void`

## Getters
- `heightMode: "fit" | "fixed"`
- `matrixTop: number`: Overridable hook (default 0): px reserved above the matrix.
- `canvasWidth: number`: The canvas spans the scrolled content, boundary padding included.
- `viewTransform: { viewScale: number; viewOffsetX: number; }`
- `matrixRegions: ReadonlyMap<number, D>`: The one payload under key 0, absent until the fetch lands. An empty matrix keeps the key: the cleared canvas is its picture.
- `matrixHeight: number`
- `matrixBlocks: RenderBlock[]`
- `yScalar: number`: The squash takes the content's base, without the boundary padding a scroll past either end adds.
- `triangleTransform: { yScalar: number; yOffsetPx: number; viewScale: number; viewOffsetX: number; }`
- `triangleFrame: TriangleFrame`

## Methods
- `cellToScreen(x: number, y: number) => { x: number; y: number; }`: Pre-rotation cell coordinates to display px.
- `screenToCell(x: number, y: number) => { x: number; y: number; }`: The exact inverse of `cellToScreen`.

# WebSessionConnectionsMixin (Mixin model, core)

Adds connections that a user creates to a web session, kept in the session beside the connections the config declares.

Composes ConnectionManagementSessionMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `addSessionConnectionConf(connectionConf: AnyConfiguration) => PluggableConfigNode & BaseConnectionConfig`: Add a connection config to *this session*: it is added to `sessionConnections`, travels with the session when it is saved or shared, and never reaches the config.json the server hands every visitor. Idempotent on `connectionId`.
- `addConnectionConf(connectionConf: AnyConfiguration) => BaseConnectionConfig`: Add a connection config wherever *this user's* edits belong: an admin's into the shared config (`jbrowse.connections`, which the admin server writes back into config.json for every visitor), everyone else's into the session. Two…
- `deleteConnection(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => boolean | (PluggableConfigNode & BaseConnectionConfig)[] | undefined`
- `makeConnection(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel, initialSnapshot?: object) => BaseConnectionModel`
- `breakConnection(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => void`: Remove a live connection instance. Tolerant of an already-dormant connection (its instance is stripped from the session on reload). Leaves persisted open-track configs alone — the connect() error path calls this and the user's already-open…
- `teardownConnection(configuration: AnyConfigurationModel) => void`: Close every track a connection contributed — the live instance's tracks plus any persisted open-track configs (a dormant connection, never expanded this session, still renders its opened tracks from `connectionTrackConfigs`) — from all…
- `clearConnections() => void`
- `captureConnectionTrack(trackId: string) => void`: Snapshot a just-opened connection track's config into `connectionTrackConfigs` so it survives session reload. No-op if the track isn't connection-provided or is already captured (edits go through `updateConnectionTrackConfig`).
- `updateConnectionTrackConfig(trackConf: Record<string, unknown> & { trackId: string; }) => void`: Persist an edit to an opened connection track. The full config is stored (not a delta): the connection's fetched "base" isn't present at load, so only a complete config resolves synchronously.
- `setConnectionTrackConfig(trackId: string, connectionId: string, config: Record<string, unknown>) => void`: Upsert one opened connection track's persisted config.
- `pruneConnectionTrackConfig(trackId: string) => void`: Drop a connection track's persisted config once no open view still references it, so the session doesn't accumulate closed tracks.
- `hydrateConnection(connectionId: string) => void`: Lazily establish a single connection by id if it isn't already live; the track selector calls it when the connection's category is expanded. Fetches without launching a view or showing a success snackbar; already-open tracks keep rendering…

## Getters
- `connections: BaseConnectionConfig[]`: list of config connections and session connections

## Properties
- `sessionConnections = types.stripDefault( types.array(pluginManager.pluggableConfigSchemaType('connection')), [], )`
- `connectionInstances = types.stripDefault( types.array(pluginManager.pluggableMstType('connection', 'stateModel')), [], )`
- `connectionTrackConfigs = types.stripDefault( types.frozen<Record<string, ConnectionTrackConfigEntry>>(), {}, )`: Persisted configs of connection tracks the user has opened, keyed by trackId. Unlike `connectionInstances` (stripped from snapshots, holds the whole fetched hub), this holds only the tracks in use, so an open connection track resolves…

WiggleCommonMixin.text:
# WiggleCommonMixin (Mixin model, wiggle plugin)

Extends `YFieldConfigMixin` with the narrowed rpcDataMap, the autoscale domain and the wiggle-specific config: the origin, rendering type, resolution and the line/gap settings. Extended on this chain with `.props()`/`.views()` rather than a mixin composed in, so no `types.compose` layer is added (ADR-041).

Composes YFieldConfigMixin, WiggleScoreConfigMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setRpcData(displayedRegionIndex: number, data: WiggleDataResult, region: Region) => void`: Stage a region as fetched, with this mixin's payload shape — so a test stands up a loaded display in one call. Production goes through `ctx.commitRegion`.
- `selectFeature(feat: WiggleHoveredFeature) => void`
- `setResolution(res: number) => void`
- `setOrigin(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setMark(mark: "bar" | "line" | "point" | "rect", interpolate?: "linear" | "step" | undefined) => void`: The plot's `mark.type`, and a line's `mark.interpolate`; any other type resets `interpolate`, which only a line reads.
- `setY(field: string) => void`: The field plotted on the value axis: a stored summary (`score`, `minScore`, `maxScore`) or any feature field.
- `setExtent(val: "min-max" | "none") => void`
- `setPointSize(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setStrokeWidth(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setScaleType(scaleType: string) => void`
- `setScaleZero(zero: boolean) => void`
- `setFenceQuantile(quantile: number) => void`
- `setDomainMin(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setDomainMax(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setMinScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMin`.
- `setMaxScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMax`.
- `setAutoscaleGroup(group?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setScoreRules(rules: (number | ValueScaleRule)[]) => void`: Replaces the y scale's rules whole, each entry in a form the config takes: a number, or `{ value, color, label }`.
- `resetYScale() => void`: Back to what the config.json says, or to what a session-owned track was added with, so an admin's declared axis survives a reset; slots the base leaves unset take their defaults.

## Getters
- `resolution: number`: Points per pixel the fetch asks for, clamped to what the Resolution menu offers: the slot is reachable from a track config, which runs no setter, and `0` there divides by zero inside the adapter.
- `rpcDataMap: ReadonlyMap<number, WiggleDataResult>`: The fetched scores, keyed by displayedRegionIndex — the foundation's per-region store, narrowed.
- `origin: number`: The value bars grow from, which a color scale also reads where its domain is unset.
- `lineWidth: number`: A line's width, `encoding.strokeWidth` or 1 px while unset.
- `size: number`: A point's diameter, `encoding.size` or 2 px while unset.
- `extent: "min-max" | "none"`
- `renderingType: "density" | "line" | "linecenter" | "scatter" | "xyplot"`
- `hasResolution: boolean`: Asked of the display's OWN adapter, which for the GC display is the synthesized GCContentAdapter rather than the track's raw sequence adapter — the two diverged when the adapter config moved onto the shared model. It answers the same…
- `effectiveExtent: "min-max" | "none"`: The extent actually drawn. A heatmap maps score to color and has no min-max presentation, so the autoscale domain reads this rather than the raw slot; otherwise the color ramp spans the min and max while the plot paints one summary, and…
- `tooltipShowsMinMax: boolean`: Whether a summary bin's tooltip lists its min and max: where they are drawn, or where the bar is one of them rather than the mean.
- `autoscaleSourceNames: Set<string> | undefined`: Source names to include when computing the autoscale domain; `undefined` means every fetched source. The wiggle display always fetches all sources and filters client-side, so it overrides this to the visible subset — otherwise a subtree…
- `scoreRuleValues: number[]`: Scores the axis must reach whatever the data does, so a rule drawn at one stays on it. `[]` here and overridden by the display that draws `encoding.y.rules`.
- `autoscaleRange: [number, number] | undefined`: What the sources visible in the settled blocks span, under the autoscale mode. `undefined` until the view and the data are ready, which is not the `[0, 1]` a caller falls back to — see `visibleStatsRange`.
- `domain: [number, number] | undefined`
- `defaultScoreDomain: [number | undefined, number | undefined]`: The bounds the adapter declares its values lie in, where it declares any (`getValueDomain`): a GC content track's [0, 1], so its axis reads alike at every locus. Config bounds still win.
- `yField: string`: The feature field the worker plots on the value axis, `encoding.y.field`, `score` by default. A fetch input: every composing display includes it in its `rpcProps()`, since the field is read where the features are.
- `summaryField: "maxScore" | "minScore" | "score"`: The stored summary the plot reads: the field where it names one, else `score`, which a field outside the three holds after the worker reads it.
- `isDensityMode: boolean`: Whether score maps to color instead of height; a display overrides it.
- `axisReachesZero: boolean`: A density row maps score to color and has no axis to start at 0, so its domain spans the values whatever the y scale's `zero` says.
- `scaleType: string`
- `scaleZero: boolean`: The y scale's `zero`: whether an autoscaled linear or symlog axis reaches 0.
- `fenceQuantile: number`: The y scale's fence quantile: what an unpinned end follows, 1 the extremes and below it that quantile of each sign.
- `clipFenceQuantile: number`: The quantile "Clip extreme outliers" fences at: the one an untick this session wrote over, else the scale's own default where that is below 1, else 0.99.
- `symlogConstant: number`: Raw slot; `0` means "derive from the domain". Resolve it with `resolveSymlogConstant` once the domain is known.
- `domainMin: number | undefined`: The lower bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `domainMax: number | undefined`: The upper bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `autoscaleGroup: string | undefined`: The y scale's autoscale group, `undefined` while it names none.
- `scaleTitle: string`: The y axis title, `''` while unset
- `grid: boolean`: The y axis grid
- `scoreRulesDrawn: boolean`: Whether this display draws the y scale's rules, which is whether the Y axis panel offers Include 0 and the reference lines: a scale it places y through rules a band for them to cross, which a density plot's color-mapped rows and a color…
- `scoreRules: ValueScaleRule[]`: The y scale's rules, read off the live nodes.
- `valueScales: ValueScale[]`: Overridable hook (default none): the scales this display draws its y through. A display that answers it gets an axis per band of each, with its cross-hatches, placed by `DisplayChrome` and `renderDisplaySvg`, and the ticks derived below.
- `autoscaledDomain: [number, number] | undefined`: The domain an autoscaled axis draws: `autoscaleRange`, widened to every range its `autoscaleGroup` holds, nice-rounded inside this display's own bounds. Each member unions the others' own ranges and never their domains, so a pinned end…
- `resolvedDomainMin: number | undefined`: Resolved lower bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `resolvedDomainMax: number | undefined`: Resolved upper bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `pinsDomain: boolean`: Whether the user has pinned either end, which is a different question from whether either end resolved to a number: `defaultScoreDomain` fills the unset ends in, so a GC content track answers yes to the second with nothing configured. The…
- `axes: YAxis[]`: The axes, one per declared scale whose domain resolved: the position of each tick in the band's pixel space, through `computeYTicks` unless the scale supplies its own ladder, and the position of each of the scale's `rules` inside the…

WorkspaceLayoutMixin.text:
# WorkspaceLayoutMixin (Mixin model, core)

The whole workspace as one MST tree:

## Actions
- `setActivePanelId(panelId: string | undefined) => void`
- `toggleMaximizedPanel(panelId: string) => void`: Show one cell at the size of the workspace, or go back; naming a different cell moves the mode. Unmounts every other cell's views rather than hiding them, to stay under the WebGL2 context ceiling (`agent-docs/reference/GPU_PORTABILITY.md`).
- `restorePanels() => void`
- `setActiveTab(panelId: string, tabId: string) => void`
- `renameTab(tabId: string, title: string | undefined) => void`
- `splitPanel(panelId: string, direction: "column" | "row", before?: any) => PanelNode | undefined`: Split a grid cell; the new cell gets one empty tab.
- `closePanel(panelId: string) => void`
- `addTab(panelId: string, viewIds?: string[]) => TabNode | undefined`: "New empty tab": a tab in an existing cell, showing the launcher.
- `closeTab(tabId: string) => void`: Close a tab, and its cell too if that was the last tab and not the workspace's last cell: a tabless cell renders nothing at all.
- `addViewToTab(tabId: string, viewId: string) => void`
- `dropTabInPanel(tabId: string, targetPanelId: string, index?: number | undefined) => void`: Drop a dragged tab into an existing panel, as a tab.
- `dropTabInNewSplit(tabId: string, targetPanelId: string, direction: "column" | "row", before: boolean) => string | undefined`: Drop a dragged tab on a panel edge: split, and put the tab in the new half.
- `setSizes(branchId: string, sizes: number[]) => void`
- `applyLayoutSpec(spec: LayoutSpecNode<LayoutViewRef>) => string[]`: Arrange the workspace as a spec states, in the shape a session spec's `layout` takes: a leaf's `views` names views by index into `session.views` or by id. A malformed leaf, an index past the end or an unknown id throws.
- `moveViewToNewTab(viewId: string) => string | undefined`: ViewMenu's "move to new tab": the view leaves its tab for a new one.
- `moveViewToSplit(viewId: string, direction: "column" | "row") => string | undefined`: ViewMenu's "move to split": the view moves to a new cell to the right (`row`) or below (`column`) of its current cell.
- `moveViewToTab(viewId: string, tabId: string) => void`: ViewMenu's "move to tab": the view joins an existing tab, which becomes the one shown.
- `homeUnassignedViews(viewIds: string[]) => void`
- `setPendingMove(move: PendingMove | undefined, _allViewIds?: string[] | undefined) => void`: Move one view to a new tab or a split beside its cell, keeping the rest of the arrangement. PUBLIC API: protein3d and msaview call it with the move alone. The second argument is an old plugin signature; the session's own views are read…
- `tileViews(mode: TileMode) => void`: Re-arrange the whole workspace, one view per cell, in one of four shapes, in `session.views` order.
- `layoutViews(spec: LayoutSpecNode<LayoutViewRef>) => string[]`: Arrange the session's views into panels: `applyLayoutSpec`, then `session.views` ordered to the spec's top-to-bottom order, which tabs read their order from. Leaves take view ids or indexes into `session.views`; a layout that seats no view…

## Getters
- `tree: LayoutTree`: Referentially stable, since `getSnapshot` is cached. Uncast on purpose: this assignment is what checks the models above agree with the interfaces in `tree.ts`.
- `panels: PanelNode[]`
- `tabs: TabNode[]`
- `visibleTree: LayoutTree`: The maximized cell alone, or the whole tree. The cell is resized to 1 because CSS hands out free space by grow factor only up to a total of 1, so a third-of-a-row cell would draw a third of the window.

## Properties
- `id = types.identifier`
- `viewIds = types.array(types.string)`
- `title = types.maybe(types.string)`: set only by an explicit rename; otherwise the name is derived from views
- `id = types.identifier`
- `size = types.optional(types.number, 1)`
- `tabs = types.array(LayoutTab)`
- `activeTabId = types.maybe(types.string)`
- `id = types.identifier`
- `size = types.optional(types.number, 1)`
- `direction = types.enumeration('LayoutDirection', ['row', 'column'])`
- `children = types.array( types.late((): typeof LayoutPanel => LayoutNode as never), )`
- `layout = types.optional(LayoutNode, emptyPanel)`
- `activePanelId = types.maybe(types.string)`
- `maximizedPanelId = types.maybe(types.string)`: Show only this cell, at the size of the whole workspace. Kept here rather than as a flag on `PanelNode` so no `tree.ts` operation has to say what it does to it.

## Methods
- `hasPanel(panelId: string) => boolean`
- `findTab(tabId: string) => TabHome | undefined`
- `tabContainingView(viewId: string) => TabHome | undefined`
- `panelContainingView(viewId: string) => PanelNode | undefined`

YFieldConfigMixin.text:
# YFieldConfigMixin (Mixin model, core)

`WiggleScoreConfigMixin` plus `encoding.y.field`, for a display that plots one configured feature field through a `yFieldChannelSchema`: the wiggle display. `LinearMarkDisplay` names a field per mark and composes the base instead.

Composes WiggleScoreConfigMixin, ScoreScaleMixin, ScoreAxisMixin — their members are listed below, nothing to follow.

## Actions
- `setScaleType(scaleType: string) => void`
- `setScaleZero(zero: boolean) => void`
- `setFenceQuantile(quantile: number) => void`
- `setDomainMin(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setDomainMax(val?: number | undefined) => void`
- `setMinScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMin`.
- `setMaxScore(val?: number | undefined) => void`: v4's name for `setDomainMax`.
- `setAutoscaleGroup(group?: string | undefined) => void`
- `setGrid(grid: boolean) => void`
- `setScoreRules(rules: (number | ValueScaleRule)[]) => void`: Replaces the y scale's rules whole, each entry in a form the config takes: a number, or `{ value, color, label }`.
- `resetYScale() => void`: Back to what the config.json says, or to what a session-owned track was added with, so an admin's declared axis survives a reset; slots the base leaves unset take their defaults.

## Getters
- `yField: string`: The feature field the worker plots on the value axis, `encoding.y.field`, `score` by default. A fetch input: every composing display includes it in its `rpcProps()`, since the field is read where the features are.
- `summaryField: "maxScore" | "minScore" | "score"`: The stored summary the plot reads: the field where it names one, else `score`, which a field outside the three holds after the worker reads it.
- `isDensityMode: boolean`: Whether score maps to color instead of height; a display overrides it.
- `axisReachesZero: boolean`: A density row maps score to color and has no axis to start at 0, so its domain spans the values whatever the y scale's `zero` says.
- `scaleType: string`
- `scaleZero: boolean`: The y scale's `zero`: whether an autoscaled linear or symlog axis reaches 0.
- `fenceQuantile: number`: The y scale's fence quantile: what an unpinned end follows, 1 the extremes and below it that quantile of each sign.
- `clipFenceQuantile: number`: The quantile "Clip extreme outliers" fences at: the one an untick this session wrote over, else the scale's own default where that is below 1, else 0.99.
- `symlogConstant: number`: Raw slot; `0` means "derive from the domain". Resolve it with `resolveSymlogConstant` once the domain is known.
- `domainMin: number | undefined`: The lower bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `domainMax: number | undefined`: The upper bound the config pins, `undefined` where it pins none.
- `autoscaleGroup: string | undefined`: The y scale's autoscale group, `undefined` while it names none.
- `scaleTitle: string`: The y axis title, `''` while unset
- `grid: boolean`: The y axis grid
- `scoreRulesDrawn: boolean`: Whether this display draws the y scale's rules, which is whether the Y axis panel offers Include 0 and the reference lines: a scale it places y through rules a band for them to cross, which a density plot's color-mapped rows and a color…
- `scoreRules: ValueScaleRule[]`: The y scale's rules, read off the live nodes.
- `defaultScoreDomain: [number | undefined, number | undefined]`: Overridable hook: what each end of the domain falls back to where the config leaves its bound unset. `[undefined, undefined]` — the default — means autoscale both ends, which is right for a track whose scores have no absolute meaning (a…
- `valueScales: ValueScale[]`: Overridable hook (default none): the scales this display draws its y through. A display that answers it gets an axis per band of each, with its cross-hatches, placed by `DisplayChrome` and `renderDisplaySvg`, and the ticks derived below.
- `autoscaleRange: [number, number] | undefined`: Overridable: what this display's own data spans, before any bound, nice-rounding or group widens it; what a group unions.
- `autoscaledDomain: [number, number] | undefined`: The domain an autoscaled axis draws: `autoscaleRange`, widened to every range its `autoscaleGroup` holds, nice-rounded inside this display's own bounds. Each member unions the others' own ranges and never their domains, so a pinned end…
- `resolvedDomainMin: number | undefined`: Resolved lower bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `resolvedDomainMax: number | undefined`: Resolved upper bound; `undefined` means autoscale this end.
- `pinsDomain: boolean`: Whether the user has pinned either end, which is a different question from whether either end resolved to a number: `defaultScoreDomain` fills the unset ends in, so a GC content track answers yes to the second with nothing configured. The…
- `axes: YAxis[]`: The axes, one per declared scale whose domain resolved: the position of each tick in the band's pixel space, through `computeYTicks` unless the scale supplies its own ladder, and the position of each of the scale's `rules` inside the…

AlignmentsArcColor.text:
# AlignmentsArcColor (Display setting config, alignments plugin)

The alignments displays' `readConnections.encoding.color` colors the read-connection arcs and the read cloud. Empty, the default, the arcs take the reads' `encoding.color` field where it is one an arc paints (`insertSize`, `pairOrientation`, `insertSizeAndOrientation`), and paint `insertSizeAndOrientation` under any other. A field set here colors the arcs whatever the reads show. A string is the field.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  readConnections: { show: true, encoding: { color: 'pairOrientation' } },
}
```
```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  readConnections: { show: true, mark: 'rule' },
  encoding: { color: 'insertSize' },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: maybeStringEnum (insertSizeAndOrientation, insertSize, pairOrientation)`: the pair field the arcs paint: insertSizeAndOrientation, insertSize or pairOrientation; unset takes the reads' color field where an arc paints it

AlignmentsBaseColor.text:
# AlignmentsBaseColor (Display setting config, alignments plugin)

The `pileup.bases.encoding.color` channel: the per-base variable painted as a cell per base over the reads, whatever `encoding.color` fills them with. `modifications` paints the MM/ML calls and `bisulfite` the conversion state against the reference, both through `pileup.bases.filter` and `unmodified`; `baseQuality` and `base` paint every aligned base. A string is the field. While a modification field paints, mismatches draw grey, and a read that no `encoding.color` paints takes a pale strand tint.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  pileup: { bases: { show: true, encoding: { color: 'modifications' } } },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: maybeStringEnum (baseQuality, base, modifications, bisulfite)`: the per-base variable painted over the reads: modifications, bisulfite, baseQuality or base; unset paints none

AlignmentsEncoding.text:
# AlignmentsEncoding (Display setting config, alignments plugin)

The alignments displays' `encoding`, the channels the reads paint through.

```js
{ type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay', encoding: { color: 'tags.HP' } }
```

## Slots
- `color: AlignmentsColor`: The read fill: `{ value: "steelblue" }` paints every read, `"strand"` a read dimension's own vocabulary and `"tags.HP"` a SAM tag.

AlignmentsSort.text:
# AlignmentsSort (Display setting config, alignments plugin)

The alignments displays' `sort` setting: the pileup's row order, by the `field` it ranks the reads on. A whole-window order is a string — `"position"` (by start, the default), `"length"` (widest first), `"spliced"` (reads whose CIGAR has a skip first), `"split"` (reads aligned in pieces first) or `"svSignal"` (the structural-variant evidence first, in tiers: split reads, then reads with an insertion or deletion of 50 bp or more, then paired reads the aligner did not call concordant, each with both ends placed above MAPQ 0, as the `svSignal` filter counts it). A column sort ranks the reads…

```js
{ type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay', sort: 'spliced' }
```
```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  sort: { field: 'tags.HP', pos: 1999, refName: 'ctgA' },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: string = 'position'`: position, length, spliced, split or svSignal order the whole window; strand, base, mapq, pairOrientation, a tags.XX tag, insertion, softclip or hardclip rank the reads over the column at pos
- `pos: maybeNumber`: a column sort's 0-based position
- `refName: maybeString`: a column sort's reference sequence
- `within: maybeNumber`: how many bases either side of pos an insertion, softclip or hardclip sort still ranks a mark

AlignmentsTrack.text:
# AlignmentsTrack (Track config, alignments plugin)

Holds read alignments, such as a BAM or CRAM file, which `LinearAlignmentsDisplay` draws. The track has few settings, and the display holds most of the config and state.

Slots are top-level fields of the track config, beside trackId and name.

Adapters: BamAdapter, CramAdapter, HtsgetBamAdapter, SamAdapter.

Displays: LinearAlignmentsDisplay, LinearMarkDisplay.

A BAM track — swap the adapter to `CramAdapter` with a `uri` to a `.cram` for
CRAM:
```js
{
  type: 'AlignmentsTrack',
  trackId: 'ngs-reads',
  name: 'NGS reads',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'BamAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/sample.bam',
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the track, falls back to the trackId when unset
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = ['assemblyName']`: name of the assembly (or assemblies) track belongs to
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the track
- `category: stringArray = []`: the category and sub-categories of a track
- `metadata: frozen = {}`: anything to add about this track
- `adapter: adapter config`: The source of this track's data. Its `type` names the adapter for the file format (`BamAdapter`, `Gff3TabixAdapter`, ...) and the rest of the object is that adapter's own slots — see the adapter pages for each. Most adapters also accept a…
- `textSearching.indexingAttributes: stringArray = ['Name', 'ID', 'symbol']`: list of which feature attributes to index for text searching — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToExclude: stringArray = ['CDS', 'exon']`: list of feature types to exclude in text search index — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToInclude: stringArray = []`: The only feature types to index, dropping every other type in the file. Empty (the default) means no allow list, i.e. index everything `indexingFeatureTypesToExclude` does not name. — advanced
- `textSearching.textSearchAdapter: optionalTextSearchAdapter`: a per-track name search index, normally a `TrixTextSearchAdapter` over what `jbrowse text-index --tracks` built; `'genes.ix'` is enough, searching this track's assemblies. Without one, this track's features are only findable through an…
- `displays: list of display configs`: An **array** of full display configs, e.g. `displays: [{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', color: 'green' }]`. Each entry names a display `type`; use this when you need exact control — your own `displayId`, different settings for two displays,…
- `formatDetails: FormatDetails`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's feature-details panel. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatDetails`.
- `formatAbout: FormatAbout`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's About dialog. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatAbout`.

BamAdapter.text:
# BamAdapter (Adapter config, alignments plugin)

Reads BAM alignment files, with a BAI or CSI index.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BamAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, csi may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.bai` index (pass `csi: true` for a
`.csi` index). For a differently-named index, set `index` explicitly with
the full slot form:
```js
{
  type: 'BamAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/sample.bam',
}
```

## Slots
- `bamLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bam', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the BAM file. Per-base mismatches come from the record's MD tag when it has one, and are otherwise computed against the assembly's reference sequence.
- `index: BamIndex`: The BAM index location and its kind. The `uri` shorthand derives both, so a config using it states neither.
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 5000000`: size to fetch in bytes over which to display a warning to the user that too much data will be fetched — advanced

BamIndex.text:
# BamIndex (Adapter config, core)

Where a BAM's index is and which of the two kinds it is. `indexType` is derived from the index file's own name where the config names a `.csi` and leaves it unset, so the usual config states neither — the `uri` shorthand derives both, and `csi: true` beside it switches the pair together. Spell `location` out for an index that does not sit beside its BAM; a `.csi` named there is read as a CSI without `indexType` as well.

## Slots
- `indexType: stringEnum (BAI, CSI) = 'BAI'`: `BAI` is the usual `samtools index` output. `CSI` is required for a reference longer than 512 Mb, which BAI cannot address. Derived from the index file name where the config names a `.csi` and leaves this unset.
- `location: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bam.bai', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the index. Only needed when it is not named `<file>.bam.bai` (or `.bam.csi`), the names the `uri` shorthand assumes.

BaseAssembly.text:
# BaseAssembly (Assembly Management config, core)

A `BaseAssembly` corresponds to the assemblies section of the config

A hand-authored human assembly. `sequence` is a `ReferenceSequenceTrack` whose
adapter points at a bgzipped+indexed FASTA — the `uri` shorthand auto-resolves
the companion `.fai`/`.gzi` index files. `geneticCodes` translates the
mitochondrial contig with the vertebrate mitochondrial code (NCBI table 2):
```js
{
  name: 'hg38',
  aliases: ['GRCh38'],
  sequence: {
    type: 'ReferenceSequenceTrack',
    trackId: 'hg38-ref',
    adapter: {
      type: 'BgzipFastaAdapter',
      uri: 'https://example.com/hg38.fa.gz',
    },
  },
  geneticCodes: { chrM: 2 },
}
```

## Slots
- `aliases: stringArray = []`: aliases are "reference name aliases" e.g. aliases for hg38 might be "GRCh38"
- `sequence: ReferenceSequenceTrack`: sequence refers to a reference sequence track that has an adapter containing, importantly, a sequence adapter such as IndexedFastaAdapter
- `refNameColors: stringArray = []`: Define custom colors for each reference sequence. Will cycle through this list if there are not enough colors for every sequence.
- `geneticCodes: frozen = {}`: Maps a reference sequence name to an NCBI genetic-code (translation table) id for sequences that don't use the standard code, e.g. `{ "chrM": 2 }` for the vertebrate mitochondrial code or `{ "chrPltd": 11 }` for a plastid. Drives the…
- `circularRefNames: stringArray = []`: The reference sequences that are circular: a plasmid, an organelle, a bacterial chromosome. The circular view closes a circle of one such sequence into a ring with no gap at its origin; every other sequence keeps the gap that marks its two…
- `geneticCodesLocation: maybeFileLocation`: Optional file (tab-separated `refName<TAB>geneticCodeId`, `#` comments allowed) to load the same refName-to-genetic-code mapping from, instead of inlining it — useful when a config generator emits a sidecar rather than inlining per…
- `refNameAliases.adapter: adapter config`: refNameAliases help resolve e.g. chr1 and 1 as the same entity the data for refNameAliases are fetched from an adapter, that is commonly a tsv like chromAliases.txt from UCSC or similar
- `cytobands.adapter: adapter config`: cytoband data is fetched from an adapter, and can be displayed by a view type as ideograms
- `displayName: string = ''`: A human readable display name for the assembly e.g. "Homo sapiens (hg38)" while the assembly name may just be "hg38"

BaseConnection.text:
# BaseConnection (Connection config, core)

Holds a connection's name and the assemblies its tracks belong to. Every connection type has these slots.

A shared base schema, not a type you write: use one of JB2TrackHubConnection, JBrowse1Connection, UCSCTrackHubConnection.

Note: JBrowse fetches the hub's track list when the connection loads and holds it in memory, and does **not** write it into a saved or shared session. The session stores only the tracks you open (under `connectionTrackConfigs`, keyed by `trackId`), so a shared session stays small even for a very large hub.

## Slots
- `name: string = 'nameOfConnection'`: a unique name for this connection
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: optional list of names of assemblies in this connection

BaseInternetAccount.text:
# BaseInternetAccount (Internet Account config, core)

Holds an internet account's name and description, the domains it handles, and the request header it sends credentials in. Every internet account type has these slots.

A shared base schema, not a type you write: use one of ExternalTokenInternetAccount, HTTPBasicInternetAccount, OAuthInternetAccount.

## Slots
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the internet account
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the internet account
- `authHeader: string = 'Authorization'`: request header for credentials
- `tokenType: string = ''`: a custom name for a token to include in the header
- `domains: stringArray = []`: array of valid domains the url can contain to use this account

BaseLinearAlignmentsDisplay.text:
# BaseLinearAlignmentsDisplay (Display config, alignments plugin)

The slots LinearAlignmentsDisplay and LGVSyntenyDisplay share: the coverage, pileup and read connection bands, and the `filter`, `unit`, `facet`, `sort`, `encoding` and `legend` every band reads. LinearAlignmentsDisplay adds the sashimi band, the `junction` filter fields and `pileup.bases`, which apply only to reads; a synteny block has no introns, basecaller tags or qualities.

A shared base schema, not a type you write: use one of LGVSyntenyDisplay, LinearAlignmentsDisplay.

## Slots
- `height: number = 250`: Starting height in pixels for the bands together; heightMode decides what a pileup deeper than this does
- `unit: stringEnum (read, chain) = 'read'`: The unit one row draws: a read, or a chain of a read, its mate and its split segments (the "Link mates and supplementary alignments" menu row)
- `filter: fieldPredicateList({ defaults: ALIGNMENTS_FILTER_DEFAULTS })`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries every one of which must hold. The read fields run before every band, so coverage counts only the reads they pass: `flags.UNMAP` and the other samtools flag names,…
- `facet: SectionFacet`: In-track stacked grouping, one labelled section per value: a read dimension (`strand`, `firstOfPairStrand`, `pairOrientation`, `pairing`, `split`, `spliced`, `svSignal`, `mapq`, `mateRefName`, `mateAssembly`), a tag (`tags.HP`), or any…
- `collapseSections: boolean = false`: Only consulted while `facet` is in effect. When set, each section draws as one row instead of a stack, and tint shading shows overlap depth instead of row count — the compact reading for a track with many sections (an all-vs-all synteny…
- `sort: AlignmentsSort`: The pileup's row order by one `field`: a whole-window order (`position`, `length`, `spliced`, `split`, `svSignal`) or a column sort at one base (`{ field: "strand", pos, refName }`).
- `encoding: AlignmentsEncoding`: The channels the reads paint through: `encoding.color`, the read fill.
- `legend: HiddenLegend`: The display's key: `show`, off by default.
- `coverage: CoverageBand`: The coverage histogram band: `show`, `height` (default 45), `encoding.y`, its depth axis, and the `interbase` and `alleles` layers, each with a `show` and a `filter`; `alleles.filter` floors each allele segment's share of its position's…
- `pileup: Pileup`: The stacked reads: `show`, `mark.height` (default 7), `maxLayoutHeight`, and the parts drawn on each read.
- `readConnections: ReadConnections`: The connections between mates and split segments: `show` (default off), `mark` (`link`, the arcs, or `rule`, the read cloud), `height`, `placement`, `encoding` (`color` and `strokeWidth`) and `ordinaryPairs`; the `connection` and…
- `heightMode: stringEnum (fixed, grow, fit) = 'fixed'`: Track-sizing strategy — how the track responds when there are more reads than fit (the menu sets `fit` from "Read height → Fit to track height" and `grow` from "Advanced → Track height → Autogrow"). `fixed` (the default) keeps…
- `growMaxHeight: number = 800`: Ceiling in pixels for the "autogrow track height" sizing mode; a pileup deeper than this grows to the ceiling and scrolls the rest. Does not apply to the fixed or fit modes, and does not limit how much is laid out (see… — advanced
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 1000000`: bytes a region may fetch before the display asks first; an adapter that sets its own limit overrides this — advanced
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

BaseLinearDisplay.text:
