BedAdapter.text:
# BedAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Reads plain-text BED files. The adapter loads the whole file into memory, so use `BedTabixAdapter` for large files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BedAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

Note: Named BED columns past `name`/`score`/`strand` (`itemRgb`, `thickStart`, ...) are only guaranteed for BED12 or a track with an `autoSql`/`columnNames`. For a BED7-BED11 file JBrowse cannot know what the extra columns mean, so it exposes them generically as `field6`, `field7`, ... and `feature.itemRgb` reads as `undefined` in a jexl callback. Set `columnNames` to refer to them by name.

```js
{
  type: 'BedAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/features.bed',
}
```

## Slots
- `bedLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bed.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: path to bed file, also allows gzipped bed
- `columnNames: stringArray = []`: List of column names. A column named like a standard BED column is parsed as that column's type (chromStart numeric, blockSizes a numeric list); any other column is text
- `scoreColumn: string = ''`: The column to use as a "score" attribute
- `autoSql: string = ''`: The autoSql definition for the data fields in the file
- `colRef: number = 0`: The column to use as a "refName" attribute
- `colStart: number = 1`: The column to use as a "start" attribute
- `colEnd: number = 2`: The column to use as a "end" attribute
- `disableGeneHeuristic: boolean = false`: Disable the heuristic that auto-detects BED12 features as gene/transcript structures. Useful for files that have BED12-like structure but are not genes (e.g. tandem duplications)

BedGraphAdapter.text:
# BedGraphAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Reads plain-text bedGraph signal files. The adapter loads the whole file into memory, so use `BedGraphTabixAdapter` for large files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BedGraphAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'BedGraphAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/signal.bedGraph',
}
```

## Slots
- `bedGraphLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bedgraph', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the plain-text bedGraph (`chrom start end value`, one line per interval). May be gzipped.
- `columnNames: stringArray = []`: List of column names

BedGraphTabixAdapter.text:
# BedGraphTabixAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Reads bgzip-compressed, tabix-indexed bedGraph signal files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BedGraphTabixAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, csi may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.tbi` index:
```js
{
  type: 'BedGraphTabixAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/signal.bedGraph.gz',
}
```

## Slots
- `bedGraphGzLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bedgraph', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bgzip-compressed bedGraph (`chrom start end value`, sorted by position). Must be bgzip rather than plain gzip, which tabix cannot index.
- `index: TabixIndex`: The tabix index location and its kind. The `uri` shorthand derives both, so a config using it states neither.
- `columnNames: stringArray = []`: List of column names

BedpeAdapter.text:
# BedpeAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Reads BEDPE files of paired breakends, such as structural variant calls within a single assembly.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BedpeAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'BedpeAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/sv.bedpe',
}
```

## Slots
- `bedpeLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bedpe.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: can be plaintext or gzipped, not indexed so loaded into memory on startup
- `columnNames: stringArray = []`: List of column names

BedTabixAdapter.text:
# BedTabixAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Reads bgzip-compressed, tabix-indexed BED files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BedTabixAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, csi may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.tbi` index; add `csi: true` for a
`.csi` index instead:
```js
{
  type: 'BedTabixAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/features.bed.gz',
}
```

## Slots
- `bedGzLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bed.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bgzip-compressed BED, sorted by position. Must be bgzip rather than plain gzip, which tabix cannot index.
- `index: TabixIndex`: The tabix index location and its kind. The `uri` shorthand derives both, so a config using it states neither.
- `columnNames: stringArray = []`: List of column names. A column named like a standard BED column is parsed as that column's type (chromStart numeric, blockSizes a numeric list); any other column is text
- `scoreColumn: string = ''`: The column to use as a "score" attribute
- `autoSql: string = ''`: The autoSql definition for the data fields in the file
- `disableGeneHeuristic: boolean = false`: Disable the heuristic that auto-detects BED12 features as gene/transcript structures. Useful for files that have BED12-like structure but are not genes (e.g. tandem duplications)

BgzipFastaAdapter.text:
# BgzipFastaAdapter (Adapter config, sequence plugin)

Reads a bgzip-compressed FASTA reference sequence, with its `.fai` and `.gzi` indexes.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BgzipFastaAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.fai` and `.gzi` indexes:
```js
{
  type: 'BgzipFastaAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/genome.fa.gz',
}
```

## Slots
- `fastaLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/seq.fa.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bgzip-compressed FASTA. Must be bgzip rather than plain gzip — `samtools faidx` cannot index the latter, and only bgzip supports the per-block random access that keeps a base-level view to one range request.
- `faiLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/seq.fa.gz.fai', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the `samtools faidx` index (`.fai`). It supplies the reference names and lengths as well as the offsets into the uncompressed sequence, so the assembly cannot load without it.
- `metadataLocation: maybeFileLocation`: Optional metadata file
- `gziLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/seq.fa.gz.gzi', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bgzip block index (`.gzi`), written beside the `.fai` by `samtools faidx` on a bgzipped FASTA. The index maps uncompressed offsets to compressed ones, so the adapter can issue a range request.

BgzipMafAdapter.text:
# BgzipMafAdapter (Adapter config, maf plugin)

A bgzip-compressed MAF with a Taffy `.tai` index — the form whole-genome multiple alignments are actually distributed in. HPRC release 2 publishes `hprc-v2.1-mc-grch38.full.maf.gz` (53 GB, 464 haplotypes) with a sibling `.tai`, and Cactus/taffy write the pair for any HAL export. The index gives random access, so a locus is a small ranged read rather than a download: a 10 kb query against HPRC's own index resolves to about 924 KB.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BgzipMafAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, nhUri may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the sibling `.tai` index; `nhUri` names the
Newick tree:
```js
{
  type: 'BgzipMafAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/aln.maf.gz',
}
```

## Slots
- `mafGzLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.maf.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: bgzip-compressed MAF file
- `taiLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.maf.gz.tai', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: The Taffy index. The same `.tai` format `BgzipTaffyAdapter` reads — it describes bgzf virtual offsets against reference coordinates and does not care which text format sits inside — so `taffy index` produces it for a MAF as readily as for…
- `samples: frozen = []`: string[] or {id:string,label:string,color?:string,assemblyName?:string,assemblyConfigLocation?:UriLocation}[]; assemblyName makes rows for that sample navigable to the genome named by assemblyName, and assemblyConfigLocation gives the…
- `nhLocation: maybeFileLocation`: newick tree naming and ordering the species rows; its leaf names are the sample ids, and any `samples` entries supply label/color overrides matched by id
- `summaryAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional swappable sub-adapter (a BedTabixAdapter over a maf2bed --summary BED, or a BigBedAdapter over UCSC bigMafSummary.bb) used for cheap zoom-out rendering; leave it unset to disable. The `.tai` makes a read cost the span on screen…
- `samplesTsvLocation: maybeFileLocation`: optional tab-separated table of per-sample metadata. It needs a header row, and its first column is the sample name exactly as the adapter spells it: a VCF sample, a MultiWiggle subtrack's name, a MAF species id. Every other column…
- `framesAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional sub-adapter (typically a BigBedAdapter over a UCSC multiz<N>wayFrames.bb) supplying each species' CDS reading frames for the frames strip, the codon view and the codon conservation band; leave it unset to disable

BgzipTaffyAdapter.text:
# BgzipTaffyAdapter (Adapter config, maf plugin)

Reads a bgzip-compressed TAF (Taffy) multiple alignment file through its `.tai` index.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BgzipTaffyAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, nhUri may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the sibling `.tai` index; `nhUri` names the
Newick tree:
```js
{
  type: 'BgzipTaffyAdapter',

```

## Slots
- `tafGzLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.taf.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: bgzip taffy file
- `taiLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.taf.gz.tai', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: taffy index
- `samples: frozen = []`: string[] or {id:string,label:string,color?:string,assemblyName?:string,assemblyConfigLocation?:UriLocation}[]; assemblyName makes rows for that sample navigable to the genome named by assemblyName, and assemblyConfigLocation gives the…
- `nhLocation: maybeFileLocation`: newick tree naming and ordering the species rows; its leaf names are the sample ids, and any `samples` entries supply label/color overrides matched by id
- `summaryAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional swappable sub-adapter (a BedTabixAdapter over a maf2bed --summary BED, or a BigBedAdapter over UCSC bigMafSummary.bb) used for cheap zoom-out rendering; leave it unset to disable. The zoom-out tier works on the same terms as…
- `samplesTsvLocation: maybeFileLocation`: optional tab-separated table of per-sample metadata. It needs a header row, and its first column is the sample name exactly as the adapter spells it: a VCF sample, a MultiWiggle subtrack's name, a MAF species id. Every other column…
- `framesAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional sub-adapter (typically a BigBedAdapter over a UCSC multiz<N>wayFrames.bb) supplying each species' CDS reading frames for the frames strip, the codon view and the codon conservation band; leave it unset to disable

BigBedAdapter.text:
# BigBedAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Reads BigBed files, the indexed binary form of BED.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BigBedAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'BigBedAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/features.bb',
}
```

## Slots
- `bigBedLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bb', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the BigBed file. The file has an index and summary zoom levels built in, so there is no separate index to configure.
- `scoreColumn: string = ''`: The column to use as a "score" attribute
- `aggregateField: string = 'geneName2'`: An attribute to aggregate features with
- `disableGeneHeuristic: boolean = false`: Disable the heuristic that auto-detects BED12 features as gene/transcript structures. Useful for files that have BED12-like structure but are not genes (e.g. tandem duplications)

BigBedTextSearchAdapter.text:
# BigBedTextSearchAdapter (Adapter config, bed plugin)

Finds features by the names a BigBed was built to look up, its `bedToBigBed -extraIndex` columns, which a UCSC hub declares with `searchIndex`. The hub's `searchTrix` index, when given, adds prefix and case-insensitive matching. A UCSC track hub connection configures one for its first gene track declaring a `searchIndex`, GenArk's `ncbiRefSeq`.

```js
{
  type: 'BigBedTextSearchAdapter',
  bigBedLocation: { uri: 'bbi/ncbiRefSeq.bb' },
  ixFilePath: { uri: 'ixIxx/ncbiRefSeq.ix' },
  ixxFilePath: { uri: 'ixIxx/ncbiRefSeq.ixx' },
}
```

## Slots
- `bigBedLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bb', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: the BigBed whose extra indexes resolve a name to its features
- `ixFilePath: maybeFileLocation`: a UCSC `searchTrix` `.ix`, whose records are the names the extra indexes hold. Unset, a search matches a name exactly as typed
- `ixxFilePath: maybeFileLocation`: the `.ixx` beside `ixFilePath`
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: List of assemblies covered by text search adapter

BigMafAdapter.text:
# BigMafAdapter (Adapter config, maf plugin)

Reads a UCSC bigMaf file, a BigBed that holds a MAF multiple alignment block in each record.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BigMafAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, nhUri may replace the location slot.

`samples` names the rows in the order they are drawn, and has to match the
species keys in the file — a bigMaf has the alignment but no display
order, so an omitted or misspelled name shows as a missing row rather than an
error:
```js
{
  type: 'BigMafAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/multiz.bb',
  samples: ['hg38', 'panTro6', 'rheMac10', 'mm39'],
}
```

## Slots
- `bigBedLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bb', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bigMaf file — a BigBed whose extra field holds the MAF alignment block, as built by UCSC's `mafToBigMaf` followed by `bedToBigBed -type=bed3+1 -as=bigMaf.as -tab`.
- `samples: frozen = []`: string[] or {id:string,label:string,color?:string,assemblyName?:string,assemblyConfigLocation?:UriLocation}[]; assemblyName makes rows for that sample navigable to the genome named by assemblyName, and assemblyConfigLocation gives the…
- `nhLocation: maybeFileLocation`: newick tree naming and ordering the species rows; its leaf names are the sample ids, and any `samples` entries supply label/color overrides matched by id
- `summaryAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional swappable sub-adapter (typically a BigBedAdapter over UCSC bigMafSummary.bb, which is published alongside the bigMaf) used for cheap zoom-out rendering; leave it unset to disable
- `samplesTsvLocation: maybeFileLocation`: optional tab-separated table of per-sample metadata. It needs a header row, and its first column is the sample name exactly as the adapter spells it: a VCF sample, a MultiWiggle subtrack's name, a MAF species id. Every other column…
- `framesAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional sub-adapter (typically a BigBedAdapter over a UCSC multiz<N>wayFrames.bb) supplying each species' CDS reading frames for the frames strip, the codon view and the codon conservation band; leave it unset to disable

BigWigAdapter.text:
# BigWigAdapter (Adapter config, wiggle plugin)

Reads BigWig quantitative signal files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BigWigAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'BigWigAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/coverage.bw',
}
```

## Slots
- `bigWigLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bw', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the BigWig file. The file has an index and precomputed zoom levels built in, so there is no separate index to configure and a whole-chromosome view reads summary bins rather than every point.
- `source: string = ''`: added as feature.get('source') on all features
- `resolutionMultiplier: number = 1`: Resolution multiplier applied to every fetch: <1 fetches more points (higher resolution), >1 fetches fewer (e.g. 2 = half as many points) — advanced

BlastTabularAdapter.text:
# BlastTabularAdapter (Adapter config, comparative-adapters plugin)

Reads BLAST tabular output (`-outfmt 6` or `7`) as pairwise alignments between a query and a target assembly.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "BlastTabularAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

The default `columns` are BLAST's own `-outfmt 6` order, so a file produced
without custom columns needs only the two assemblies naming which side is
which:
```js
{
  type: 'BlastTabularAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/hits.tsv',
  assemblyNames: ['grape', 'peach'],
  queryAssembly: 'grape',
  targetAssembly: 'peach',
}
```

## Slots
- `blastTableLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/blastTable.tsv', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the BLAST tabular output (`-outfmt 6` or `7`). Set `columns` to match if the run used a custom column list.
- `columns: string = 'qseqid sseqid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore'`: Optional space-separated column name list. If custom columns were used in outfmt, enter them here exactly as specified in the command. At least qseqid, sseqid, qstart, qend, sstart, and send are required
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: Array of assembly names to use for this file. The query assembly name is the first value in the array, target assembly name is the second
- `targetAssembly: string = ''`: Alternative to assemblyNames: the target assembly name
- `queryAssembly: string = ''`: Alternative to assemblyNames: the query assembly name

ChainAdapter.text:
# ChainAdapter (Adapter config, comparative-adapters plugin)

Reads UCSC chain alignment files, which need the query and target assembly names.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "ChainAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'ChainAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/aln.chain',
  queryAssembly: 'hg19',
  targetAssembly: 'hg38',
}
```

## Slots
- `chainLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/file.chain', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the UCSC chain file, as used by `liftOver` and produced by `axtChain`. May be gzipped; the whole file is read into memory.
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: Array of assembly names to use for this file. The query assembly name is the first value in the array, target assembly name is the second
- `targetAssembly: string = ''`: Alternative to assemblyNames: the target assembly name
- `queryAssembly: string = ''`: Alternative to assemblyNames: the query assembly name

ChordColor.text:
# ChordColor (Display setting config, circular-view plugin)

A variant chord's `encoding.color`: a CSS color or `jexl:` callback in `value` for every chord, or a `field` of the record whose values each take a range color, with a key on the circle. `svType` paints the structural-variant classes the variant displays paint. A string is the field.

```js
{ type: 'ChordVariantDisplay', encoding: { color: 'svType', opacity: 0.45 } }
```

## Slots
- `value: color = 'rgb(255,133,0)'`: A CSS color, or a jexl callback over `feature` returning one, for every chord. — callback args: feature
- `scale: ChordColorScale sub-schema`: How the field's values map to colors, Vega-Lite's scale object.
- `legend: ChordColorLegend sub-schema`: The key this channel draws.
- `field: featureField = ''`: a record field, svType say, or a jexl expression over feature, whose values each paint one range color with a key
- `scale.type: maybeStringEnum`: ordinal a range color per value of field; threshold a range color per interval between the cut points in domain; unset follows field
- `scale.domain: stringArray = []`: the values that take the range first, in order; under threshold, the ascending cut points, a value on a cut taking the interval above it
- `scale.range: colorArray = []`: CSS colors the domain takes, in order, continuing into the default palette past its end; under threshold one per interval, one more than the cuts
- `scale.unknown: maybeColor`: color for a value missing from domain. Unset: the next palette color where the display deals one, and the levels a preset field names, such as strand's, keep their own colors. A color: that color. "": no color dealt, so a feature paints…
- `scale.invalid: maybeColor`: color for a feature with no value under an ordinal scale's field; unset, the display's no-value color
- `scale.names: stringArray = []`: key name for each domain value, one each in order, or under threshold for each interval from the lowest; a value past the end of the list shows its own
- `legend.title: maybeString`: key title; unset keeps the display's own heading, "" draws none

ChordEncoding.text:
# ChordEncoding (Display setting config, circular-view plugin)

A variant chord display's `encoding`, the channels its chords paint through.

```js
{ type: 'ChordVariantDisplay', encoding: { color: { value: 'teal' } } }
```

## Slots
- `color: ChordColor`: The line color of each resting chord: `{ value }`, a CSS color or `jexl:` callback, or a field of the record, `svType` say, whose values each take a color with a key on the circle.
- `opacity: ChordOpacity`: The alpha of every resting chord, a [](/docs/config/chordopacity) object; a number is its `value`.

ChordMark.text:
# ChordMark (Display setting config, circular-view plugin)

A chord display's `mark`: how far each chord or ribbon curves in toward the center. A chord's curve scales with its length, so two ends at one locus draw a point at the rim.

```js
{ type: 'ChordVariantDisplay', displayId: 'sv-chords', mark: { depth: 0.5 } }
```

## Slots
- `depth: number = 0.9`: how deeply each chord curves toward the center, from 0 to 1: 1 runs a chord between opposite points straight through the center, and 0 bows every chord out toward the rim. A shorter chord curves less, in proportion to its length

ChordOpacity.text:
# ChordOpacity (Display setting config, circular-view plugin)

A variant chord display's `encoding.opacity`: one alpha for every resting chord, over its color's own. A number is written to `value`.

```js
{ type: 'ChordVariantDisplay', encoding: { opacity: 0.45 } }
```

## Slots
- `value: maybeNumber`: The alpha every resting chord draws at, 0 to 1, over its color's own; unset is 0.32.

ChordSyntenyDisplay.text:
# ChordSyntenyDisplay (Display config, circular-view plugin)

Draws a `SyntenyTrack` in a `CircularView`, with a ribbon joining the two spans of each alignment.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "ChordSyntenyDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: SyntenyTrack.

Adapters: BlastTabularAdapter, ChainAdapter, DeltaAdapter, MashMapAdapter, MCScanAnchorsAdapter, MCScanBlocksAdapter, MCScanSimpleAnchorsAdapter, MultiGenomeIndexedPAFAdapter, MultiGenomePAFAdapter, MultiPairwiseSyntenyAdapter, PAFAdapter, PairwiseIndexedPAFAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:ChordSyntenyDisplay".

The circular-view display for a `SyntenyTrack`: each alignment is a ribbon
between the span it covers on one side and the span its mate covers on the
other. The circular view's `encoding.color`, `encoding.opacity` and `filter` decide which
ribbons draw and in what color, as in the linear synteny view; these slots
are the hovered and selected fills:
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'volvox_self',
  name: 'Volvox self-alignment',
  assemblyNames: ['volvox', 'volvox'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/volvox_self.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'volvox',
    targetAssembly: 'volvox',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'ChordSyntenyDisplay',
      displayId: 'volvox_self-ChordSyntenyDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `mark: ChordMark`: How far each chord curves toward the center, a [](/docs/config/chordmark) object

ChordVariantDisplay.text:
# ChordVariantDisplay (Display config, circular-view plugin)

Draws the structural variants of a `VariantTrack` in a `CircularView`, each translocation as a chord across the circle.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "ChordVariantDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: VariantTrack.

Adapters: BedpeAdapter, SplitVcfTabixAdapter, StarFusionAdapter, VcfAdapter, VcfTabixAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:ChordVariantDisplay".

The circular-view display for a `VariantTrack` of structural variants;
translocations are drawn as chords across the circle. `encoding.color` is
the chord's resting color, a constant or a field of the record with a key; a
hovered chord darkens it and a selected one takes the theme's highlight:
```js
{
  type: 'VariantTrack',
  trackId: 'sv',
  name: 'Structural variants',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'VcfTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/sv.vcf.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'ChordVariantDisplay',
      displayId: 'sv-ChordVariantDisplay',
      encoding: { color: 'svType', opacity: 0.45 },
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `mark: ChordMark`: How far each chord curves toward the center, a [](/docs/config/chordmark) object
- `onChordClick: maybeString`: a jexl callback run when a chord is clicked, in place of opening the record's details; unset opens the details — callback args: feature, track
- `encoding: ChordEncoding`: The channels each resting chord paints through: `encoding.color`, its line color, and `encoding.opacity`, its alpha.

ChromSizesAdapter.text:
# ChromSizesAdapter (Adapter config, sequence plugin)

Reads the chromosome names and lengths in a UCSC-style `.chrom.sizes` file (tab-separated `name<TAB>length`), for an assembly with no sequence. Use it for karyotype, whole-genome or synteny views that need no base-level sequence.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "ChromSizesAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'ChromSizesAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/species.chrom.sizes',
}
```

## Slots
- `chromSizesLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/species.chrom.sizes', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the `.chrom.sizes` file — one `name<TAB>length` line per reference sequence. There is no sequence behind it, so base-level views of this assembly are empty.

CoverageAlleles.text:
# CoverageAlleles (Display setting config, core)

The coverage band's `alleles` layer: the colored segment each mismatched base takes in its position's depth bar. Its `filter` keeps the segments whose `fraction`, the allele's share of the position's depth, passes; the grey depth bar shows through where a segment is left out, and everywhere under `show: false`. The modification bars are not allele segments: `pileup.bases` draws them, and nothing here hides or floors them.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  coverage: { alleles: { filter: [{ field: 'fraction', gte: 0.2 }] } },
}
```
```js
{ type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay', coverage: { alleles: { show: false } } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: color the allele segments of the depth bars; off, the bars are plain grey
- `filter: fieldPredicateList()`: Entries on `fraction`, a floor from 0 to 1 written `gte`, the one test the band's draw makes. Empty colors every mismatch, sequencing errors included. Distinct from `pileup.fadeLowFrequency`, which fades the pileup's marks by the same…

CoverageBand.text:
# CoverageBand (Display setting config, core)

The coverage histogram band of the alignments and MAF displays, their `coverage` setting: whether it draws, its height, the insertion and clip marks drawn in it (`interbase`), which allele segments it colors (`alleles`), and its depth axis, `encoding.y`. On the alignments display, the modification bars in it follow the pileup's `bases` layer, which draws them beside its cells from the same calls.

```js
{ type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay', coverage: { height: 80 } }
```
```js
{ type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay', coverage: { show: false } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: draw the coverage band
- `height: number = 45`: height of the coverage band in pixels
- `encoding: CoverageEncoding`: The depth axis, `encoding.y`: its `scale`, `axis` and `rules`.
- `interbase: CoverageInterbase`: The insertion and clip marks between bases: `show`, and the `filter` deciding which positions get an indicator triangle.
- `alleles: CoverageAlleles`: The colored allele segments: `show`, and the `filter` on each one's `fraction`.

CoverageEncoding.text:
# CoverageEncoding (Display setting config, core)

The coverage band's `encoding`: `y`, its depth axis, a [YChannel](../ychannel). `scale.constant` starts at 1, which makes symlog exactly `log(depth+1)` with the knee at one read. `scale.fenceQuantile` stays at 1, the deepest base in view; the Coverage axis panel's Clip extreme outliers writes 0.99, which stops the axis at twice the 99th percentile of the covered bins' peaks.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  coverage: { encoding: { y: { scale: { type: 'log' } } } },
}
```

## Slots
- `y: YChannel`: The depth axis: `scale`, `axis` and `rules`.

CoverageInterbase.text:
# CoverageInterbase (Display setting config, core)

The coverage band's `interbase` layer: the insertion and clip count bars and their indicator triangles, drawn between the bases they sit between. Its `filter` picks the positions that earn a triangle.

```js
{ type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay', coverage: { interbase: { show: false } } }
```
```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  coverage: { interbase: { filter: [{ field: 'fraction', gt: 0.1 }] } },
}
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: draw the insertion and clip count bars and their indicator triangles
- `filter: fieldPredicateList({ defaults: Object.entries(DEFAULT_INTERBASE_INDICATOR_RULE).map( ([field, { min, strict }]) => strict ? { field, gt: min } : { field, gte:…`: Which positions get an indicator triangle, by `depth`, the reads covering the position, and `fraction`, its insertions and clips as a share of that depth, each a floor written `gte` or `gt`. Unwritten, a field keeps its default, `depth` at…

CramAdapter.text:
# CramAdapter (Adapter config, alignments plugin)

Reads CRAM alignments, fetching only the containers overlapping the visible region through the `.crai` index. Decoding happens against the enclosing assembly's sequence, so it has to be the reference the file was compressed against; a mismatched one isn't rejected, it just decodes into mismatches.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "CramAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.crai` index:
```js
{
  type: 'CramAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/sample.cram',
}
```

## Slots
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 5000000`: size in bytes over which to display a warning to the user that too much data will be fetched — advanced
- `useSliceWorkerPool: boolean = true`: decode CRAM slices on a pool of workers rather than in the thread that asked — advanced
- `cramLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.cram', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the CRAM file
- `craiLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.cram.crai', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the CRAM index (`.crai`). Only needed when it is not named `<file>.cram.crai`, the name the `uri` shorthand assumes.

CrisprGuideAdapter.text:
# CrisprGuideAdapter (Adapter config, sequence plugin)

Note: don't set `sequenceAdapter` — JBrowse supplies it from the assembly the track is displayed against. Setting it by hand pins the scan to one sequence source, and the track keeps scanning that source after the assembly's sequence changes.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "CrisprGuideAdapter", ... }.

The defaults are SpCas9 — `NGG` PAM, 20 nt guide, 3' PAM — and the adapter
scans the assembly's sequence, so the config has no file location.
A PAM occurs every few bases, so an unfiltered scan is denser than a display
can draw; the GC window and `excludePolyT` (guides containing `TTTT`, a
terminator for the pol III promoters guides are expressed from) keep the
usable ones. SaCas9 is the same track with `pam: 'NNGRRT'` and
`guideLength: 21`:
```js
{
  type: 'CrisprGuideAdapter',
  pam: 'NGG',
  guideLength: 20,
  pamLocation: '3prime',
  cutOffset: 3,
  minGcPercent: 40,
  maxGcPercent: 60,
  excludePolyT: true,
}
```

## Slots
- `sequenceAdapter: maybeFrozen`: discouraged: leave unset. JBrowse supplies the assembly's sequence adapter automatically; this override exists only for the rare case of scanning a sequence other than the one the track is displayed against.
- `pam: string = 'NGG'`: PAM motif in IUPAC codes, e.g. NGG for SpCas9, TTTV for Cas12a
- `guideLength: number = 20`: protospacer length in bp
- `pamLocation: stringEnum (3prime, 5prime) = '3prime'`: whether the PAM is 3' (Cas9) or 5' (Cas12a) of the protospacer
- `cutOffset: number = 3`: distance in bp from the PAM-proximal end of the protospacer to the cut on the protospacer-matching strand (3 for SpCas9, 18 for Cas12a)
- `cutOffsetBottom: number = 3`: same, for the cut on the opposite strand. Equal to `cutOffset` for a blunt cutter like SpCas9; larger for a staggered one like Cas12a (23), whose two cuts leave a 5' overhang.
- `minGcPercent: number = 0`: drop guides below this GC percent. A PAM occurs every ~8bp of genome, so an unfiltered scan is far denser than a display can draw; the defaults keep everything and leave the choice to the caller.
- `maxGcPercent: number = 100`: drop guides above this GC percent
- `excludePolyT: boolean = false`: drop guides containing TTTT, which terminates transcription from the pol III (U6/H1) promoters guides are usually expressed from
- `searchForward: boolean = true`: whether to scan the forward strand for PAMs
- `searchReverse: boolean = true`: whether to scan the reverse strand for PAMs

DeltaAdapter.text:
# DeltaAdapter (Adapter config, comparative-adapters plugin)

Reads MUMmer `.delta` alignment files, which need the query and target assembly names.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "DeltaAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'DeltaAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/aln.delta',
  queryAssembly: 'hg19',
  targetAssembly: 'hg38',
}
```

## Slots
- `deltaLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/file.delta', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the MUMmer `.delta` file written by `nucmer`/`promer` (also accepts the `delta-filter` output). May be gzipped; the whole file is read into memory.
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: Array of assembly names to use for this file. The query assembly name is the first value in the array, target assembly name is the second
- `targetAssembly: string = ''`: Alternative to assemblyNames: the target assembly name
- `queryAssembly: string = ''`: Alternative to assemblyNames: the query assembly name

DotplotAxis.text:
# DotplotAxis (View config, dotplot-view plugin)

The dotplot's `axis`: both genome axes, whose ticks `grid` carries across the plot and `labels` numbers.

```js
{ type: 'DotplotView', axis: { grid: false, labels: false } }
```

## Slots
- `grid: boolean = true`: carry each axis' ruler ticks across the plot
- `labels: boolean = true`: number the ticks along each axis; off keeps the ticks and sequence names

DotplotDisplay.text:
# DotplotDisplay (Display config, dotplot-view plugin)

Draws a `SyntenyTrack` as a dot plot inside a `DotplotView`.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "DotplotDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: SyntenyTrack.

Adapters: BlastTabularAdapter, ChainAdapter, DeltaAdapter, MashMapAdapter, MCScanAnchorsAdapter, MCScanBlocksAdapter, MCScanSimpleAnchorsAdapter, MultiGenomeIndexedPAFAdapter, MultiGenomePAFAdapter, MultiPairwiseSyntenyAdapter, PAFAdapter, PairwiseIndexedPAFAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:DotplotDisplay".

The dot-plot rendering of a `SyntenyTrack`, for use inside a `DotplotView`
(rather than the two-row `LinearSyntenyDisplay` or the plain-LGV
`LGVSyntenyDisplay`) — same track config, different display type:
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'hg38_vs_mm10',
  name: 'hg38 vs mm10',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38', 'mm10'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/hg38_vs_mm10.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'hg38',
    targetAssembly: 'mm10',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'DotplotDisplay',
      displayId: 'hg38_vs_mm10-DotplotDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

DropboxOAuthInternetAccount.text:
# DropboxOAuthInternetAccount (Internet Account config, authentication plugin)

Signs requests for Dropbox files with an OAuth 2.0 token, with the Dropbox endpoints and domains filled in.

Slots are top-level fields of the account's entry in internetAccounts.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:DropboxOAuthInternetAccount".

The Dropbox endpoints are pre-filled, so an entry needs only your own OAuth
app's `clientId`. Leave `domains` off and the account is still selectable by
hand in the Add Track form.
```js
{
  type: 'DropboxOAuthInternetAccount',
  internetAccountId: 'dropboxOAuth',
  name: 'Dropbox',
  clientId: 'your-dropbox-app-key',
}
```

## Slots
- `authEndpoint: string = 'https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize'`: the authorization code endpoint of the internet account
- `tokenEndpoint: string = 'https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token'`: the token endpoint of the internet account
- `needsPKCE: boolean = true`: boolean to indicate if the endpoint needs a PKCE code
- `domains: stringArray = []`: array of valid domains the url can contain to use this account
- `tokenType: string = 'Bearer'`: a custom name for a token to include in the header
- `clientId: string = ''`: id for the OAuth application
- `scopes: string = ''`: optional scopes for the authorization call
- `responseType: string = 'code'`: the type of response from the authorization endpoint. can be 'token' or 'code'
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the internet account
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the internet account
- `authHeader: string = 'Authorization'`: request header for credentials

ExternalTokenInternetAccount.text:
# ExternalTokenInternetAccount (Internet Account config, authentication plugin)

Sends a token that the user pastes in, or that an embedding portal supplies, with every request to a matching domain.

Slots are top-level fields of the account's entry in internetAccounts.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:ExternalTokenInternetAccount".

For a token the user pastes in, or that an embedding portal hands over.
JBrowse does not obtain the token itself — it prompts for one, then sends it
on every request to a matching domain.
```js
{
  type: 'ExternalTokenInternetAccount',
  internetAccountId: 'portalToken',
  name: 'Data portal token',
  domains: ['api.myportal.org'],
}
```

## Slots
- `validateWithHEAD: boolean = true`: validate the token with a HEAD request before using it
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the internet account
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the internet account
- `authHeader: string = 'Authorization'`: request header for credentials
- `tokenType: string = ''`: a custom name for a token to include in the header
- `domains: stringArray = []`: array of valid domains the url can contain to use this account

Facet.text:
# Facet (Display setting config, core)

The `facet` setting of the feature, multi-sample variant, multi-row and alignments displays: one labelled section of the track per value of a field. A string is the field; the object adds the order. The mark display's `MarkFacet` adds the steps each section runs. On the multi-sample variant displays the field is a sample attribute from the samples file, such as `population`, and it bands the sample rows by its value, with no chip.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', facet: 'strand' }
```
```js
{
  type: 'LinearBasicDisplay',
  facet: { field: 'gene_biotype', sort: ['protein_coding', 'lncRNA'] },
}
```
```js
{
  type: 'LinearAlignmentsDisplay',
  facet: { field: 'tags.HP', sort: ['1', '2'] },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: featureField = ''`: The feature field whose values each get a labelled section of the track: a field name, a dotted path into a structured field (`INFO.SVTYPE`, a read's `tags.HP`), a `jexl:` expression, or `strand`. A feature with no value stacks last, under…
- `sort: stringArray = []`: The values whose sections stack first, in order, as Vega-Lite's `sort` lists them: the rest follow sorted, and none is dropped. Empty stacks every section sorted, and a `strand` facet forward, reverse, then unstranded (`1`, `-1`, `0`).

FeatureContainers.text:
# FeatureContainers (Display setting config, features plugin)

The feature display's `containers`: the top-level types whose children always stack on rows of their own, as a proteoform's ORFs do.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', containers: { types: ['proteoform_orf'] } }
```

## Slots
- `types: stringArray = ['proteoform_orf']`: The container types; each also counts as `geneLike`.

FeatureDescriptionLabel.text:
# FeatureDescriptionLabel (Display setting config, features plugin)

The feature displays' `labels.description`, the line drawn under each feature's name: whether it `show`s, and the `field` it reads. A bare string is the field. Shown descriptions still hide where features crowd the screen, a zoom step before names do, whether or not names draw.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', labels: { description: { show: false } } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: draw a description line under each feature
- `field: featureField = 'jexl:get(feature,'note') || get(feature,'description') || get(feature,'function')'`: the field the description reads, such as `note`, or a `jexl:` expression over `feature`; the default reads `note`, else `description`, else `function`, and an empty value draws no description

FeatureEncoding.text:
# FeatureEncoding (Display setting config, core)

The canvas feature displays' `encoding`, the channels the features paint through.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', encoding: { color: 'gene_biotype' } }
```

## Slots
- `color: FeatureColor`: The main fill of each feature: `{ value }`, a CSS color or a jexl expression, or a field and the `scale` its values map through, with a key.

FeatureMark.text:
# FeatureMark (Display setting config, features plugin)

The canvas feature displays' `mark`, the box each feature draws as: its `height`, as the alignments display's `pileup.mark.height` is each read's.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', mark: { height: 6 } }
```

## Slots
- `height: number = 10`: The main body's height in px under `displayMode: 'normal'`; compact draws it at 0.6 of this and superCompact at 0.3, on the main thread, so a preset never refetches.

FeatureNameLabel.text:
# FeatureNameLabel (Display setting config, features plugin)

The feature displays' `labels.name`, the name drawn beside each feature: whether it `show`s, and the `field` it reads. A bare string is the field. Shown names still hide where features crowd the screen, except gene names while the genes alone have room.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', labels: { name: 'gene_name' } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: draw a name beside each feature
- `field: featureField = 'jexl:get(feature,'name') || get(feature,'id')'`: the field the name reads, such as `gene_name`, or a `jexl:` expression over `feature`; the default reads the name, else the ID, and an empty value draws no name

FeatureSubfeatureLabels.text:
# FeatureSubfeatureLabels (Display setting config, features plugin)

The feature display's `labels.subfeatures`, the names of a feature's parts: a gene's transcripts, a container's children, a polyprotein's cleavage products. `collapsed` draws none.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', labels: { subfeatures: { placement: 'below' } } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: draw the names of a feature's parts
- `placement: stringEnum (auto, below, overlay) = 'auto'`: `auto` names a polyprotein's cleavage products on their rows and no other part; `below` and `overlay` name every part, under its row or over it

FeatureTooltip.text:
# FeatureTooltip (Display setting config, features plugin)

The canvas feature displays' `tooltip`, the box hovering a feature opens: whether it `show`s, and the `field` its text reads. A bare string is the field.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearBasicDisplay',
  tooltip: "jexl:get(feature,'name') + ' ' + get(feature,'biotype')",
}
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: Off, hovering still highlights the feature and "Copy tooltip text" still copies it.
- `field: featureField = 'jexl:get(feature,'_mouseOver')||get(feature,'name')||get(feature,'function')||get(feature,'id')'`: Left at the default, the tooltip adds the description line (`labels.description`) as a second row.

FeatureTrack.text:
# FeatureTrack (Track config, features plugin)

Holds gene and other feature annotations, such as a GFF3 or BED file, which `LinearBasicDisplay` usually draws.

Slots are top-level fields of the track config, beside trackId and name.

Adapters: BedAdapter, BedTabixAdapter, BigBedAdapter, CrisprGuideAdapter, FromConfigAdapter, Gff3Adapter, Gff3TabixAdapter, GtfAdapter, GtfTabixAdapter, NCListAdapter, SequenceSearchAdapter, SPARQLAdapter.

Displays: LinearBasicDisplay, LinearManhattanDisplay, LinearMarkDisplay, LinearMultiRowFeatureDisplay, LinearScoreDisplay, LinearWiggleDisplay.

A minimal track. `adapter` points at the data file:
```js
{
  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'genes',
  name: 'Genes',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'Gff3TabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/genes.sorted.gff.gz',
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the track, falls back to the trackId when unset
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = ['assemblyName']`: name of the assembly (or assemblies) track belongs to
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the track
- `category: stringArray = []`: the category and sub-categories of a track
- `metadata: frozen = {}`: anything to add about this track
- `adapter: adapter config`: The source of this track's data. Its `type` names the adapter for the file format (`BamAdapter`, `Gff3TabixAdapter`, ...) and the rest of the object is that adapter's own slots — see the adapter pages for each. Most adapters also accept a…
- `textSearching.indexingAttributes: stringArray = ['Name', 'ID', 'symbol']`: list of which feature attributes to index for text searching — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToExclude: stringArray = ['CDS', 'exon']`: list of feature types to exclude in text search index — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToInclude: stringArray = []`: The only feature types to index, dropping every other type in the file. Empty (the default) means no allow list, i.e. index everything `indexingFeatureTypesToExclude` does not name. — advanced
- `textSearching.textSearchAdapter: optionalTextSearchAdapter`: a per-track name search index, normally a `TrixTextSearchAdapter` over what `jbrowse text-index --tracks` built; `'genes.ix'` is enough, searching this track's assemblies. Without one, this track's features are only findable through an…
- `displays: list of display configs`: An **array** of full display configs, e.g. `displays: [{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', color: 'green' }]`. Each entry names a display `type`; use this when you need exact control — your own `displayId`, different settings for two displays,…
- `formatDetails: FormatDetails`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's feature-details panel. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatDetails`.
- `formatAbout: FormatAbout`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's About dialog. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatAbout`.

FeatureTranscripts.text:
# FeatureTranscripts (Display setting config, features plugin)

The feature display's `transcripts`: which children read as a gene's isoforms, and the order they rank in. `field` names the attribute holding a curated tag and `sort` the tag values that rank first, in order, as a `facet` sorts; the isoforms past the list follow by coding length. The first-ranked is the one transcript `geneGlyphMode: 'representative'` draws, and the first kept when `auto` caps a gene at the rows the track has.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearBasicDisplay',
  transcripts: { field: 'tag', sort: ['MANE Select', 'Ensembl_canonical'] },
}
```

## Slots
- `types: stringArray = ['mRNA', 'transcript', 'primary_transcript', 'V_gene_segment', 'C_gene_segment', 'D_gene_segment', 'J_gene_segment']`: Types the `geneLike` filter field counts beside every gene, transcript and RNA type, and the fallback for recognizing a childless transcript as one of a gene's isoforms. Not the isoform test: keying that off this list dropped every…
- `field: string = 'tag'`: The attribute holding an isoform's curated "this one represents the gene" tag.
- `sort: stringArray = ['MANE Select', 'MANE_Select', 'RefSeq Select', 'Ensembl_canonical', 'MANE Plus Clinical', 'MANE_Plus_Clinical']`: The values of `field` that rank an isoform first, in order.

FeatureUtrs.text:
# FeatureUtrs (Display setting config, core)

The gene glyphs' `utrs`, the thinner boxes a coding transcript draws past its CDS, which `encoding.color` paints. Unset, a UTR takes its transcript's fill, a field's color or a constant, and the contrasting UTR blue where nothing sets a fill.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearBasicDisplay',
  utrs: { encoding: { color: { value: 'lightblue' } } },
}
```

## Slots
- `encoding: FeatureUtrEncoding sub-schema`: The channel the UTR boxes paint through.
- `encoding.color: FeatureUtrColor sub-schema`: A constant only: a UTR takes a field's color through its transcript's fill.
- `encoding.color.value: maybeColor`: a CSS color, or a `jexl:` callback over `feature` returning one, painting every UTR box over its transcript's fill — callback args: feature

FieldPredicate.text:
# FieldPredicate (Display setting config, core)

One entry of a `filter` list, Vega-Lite's field predicate: the `field` of each record and the tests its value must pass, every one given. A `filter` list admits a record that passes every entry. A value is missing when it is absent, empty, or a VCF's `.`; `valid: false` selects exactly those. A comparison reads the value as a number, so a missing value and text that is no number both fail it.

```js
filter: [{ field: 'length', gte: 10000 }, { field: 'identity', gte: 0.9 }]
```
```js
filter: [{ field: 'query', oneOf: ['chr1', 'chr2'] }]
```
```js
filter: [{ field: 'score', range: [100, 500] }]
```
```js
filter: [{ field: 'gene_group', valid: true }]
```
```js
filter: ['jexl:feature.end - feature.start > 1000']
```

## Slots
- `field: featureField = ''`: the field tested, as the display names its fields, or a jexl: expression computed per feature
- `equal: maybeFrozen`: the value must equal this
- `lt: maybeNumber`: the value must be below this
- `lte: maybeNumber`: the value must be at most this
- `gt: maybeNumber`: the value must be above this
- `gte: maybeNumber`: the value must be at least this
- `oneOf: maybeFrozen`: the value must be one of these
- `range: maybeFrozen`: Vega-Lite's [min, max], both ends included and a null end open; it loads as gte and lte, the tighter bound winning where either is also written
- `valid: maybeBoolean`: true admits only records with a value for the field, false only those without

FormatAbout.text:
# FormatAbout (Root config, core)

Holds jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in a track's About dialog. Every track has this schema, and so does the root config as `configuration.formatAbout`, which applies to every track at once. Where both are set the track's object is spread over the session's, so a track can override individual keys the global callback added.

On a track. The callback's variable is `config`, not `feature`, since the
dialog shows the track's configuration and no feature:
```js
{
  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'genes',
  name: 'Genes',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'Gff3TabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/genes.gff.gz',
  },
  formatAbout: {
    hideUris: true,
    config: "jexl:{Source:'GENCODE v44', adapter:undefined}",
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `formatAbout.config: frozen = {}`: callback returning an object of fields to merge over the config shown — callback args: config
- `formatAbout.hideUris: boolean = false`: leave file locations out of the About dialog, for a deployment that would rather not show users where the data sits. Hides URIs and local paths alike, drops the "Copy config" button, and suppresses the File info panel — a BAM's `@SQ UR:`…

FormatDetails.text:
# FormatDetails (Root config, core)

Holds jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in the feature-details panel. Every track has this schema, and so does the root config as `configuration.formatDetails`, which applies to every track at once. Where both are set, the callbacks merge with the track's object over the session's, so a track can override individual keys the global callback added, and the numeric slots take the track's value when the track sets one.

On a track. The callback returns an object merged over the feature: a new key
adds a row, an existing key rewrites it, and `undefined` hides it. A bare URL
is turned into a link for you, so no `<a>` markup is needed:
```js
{
  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'genes',
  name: 'Genes',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'Gff3TabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/genes.gff.gz',
  },
  formatDetails: {
    feature: "jexl:{ncbi:'https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/?term='+feature.name, phase:undefined}",
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `formatDetails.feature: frozen = {}`: callback returning an object of fields to merge onto the clicked feature. `track` is the track's config, so one session-wide callback can link out per assembly or name the track. A plain object works too, for fields that are the same on… —…
- `formatDetails.subfeatures: frozen = {}`: the same, applied to each subfeature down to `depth`. `parent` is the feature it sits in and `depth` how far down, 1 for a gene's transcript and 2 for the transcript's exon — callback args: feature, parent, depth, track
- `formatDetails.depth: maybeNumber`: The number of subfeature levels the `subfeatures` callback runs on, defaulting to 2, which reaches a gene's transcripts and their exons and CDSs; 1 stops at the transcripts. A track's value wins over the session's — advanced
- `formatDetails.maxDepth: maybeNumber`: The number of subfeature card levels the panel renders at all, independent of how deep `subfeatures` formats. Unset means no limit. A track's value wins over the session's — advanced

FromConfigAdapter.text:
# FromConfigAdapter (Adapter config, config plugin)

Supplies features written inline in the config, for a small feature set added through a URL or session spec.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "FromConfigAdapter", ... }.

```js
{
  type: 'FromConfigAdapter',
  features: [
    { uniqueId: 'f1', refName: 'ctgA', start: 100, end: 200, name: 'feature1' },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `adapterId: string = ''`: stable identifier used as the adapter cache key; avoids hashing the (potentially large) features array. optional — falls back to hash.
- `features: frozen = []`: the features themselves, as an array of plain objects. Each needs a `uniqueId`, `refName`, `start` and `end` (0-based half-open); anything else — `name`, `type`, `score`, `strand`, nested `subfeatures` — is copied onto the feature…

FromConfigRegionsAdapter.text:
# FromConfigRegionsAdapter (Adapter config, config plugin)

Supplies an assembly's reference names and sizes inline in the config, with no sequence.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "FromConfigRegionsAdapter", ... }.

Supplies refNames+sizes with no sequence, as the adapter of an assembly's
`sequence` (a `ReferenceSequenceTrack`):
```js
{
  type: 'ReferenceSequenceTrack',
  trackId: 'my_refseq',
  adapter: {
    type: 'FromConfigRegionsAdapter',
    features: [
      { uniqueId: 'ctgA', refName: 'ctgA', start: 0, end: 50000 },
      { uniqueId: 'ctgB', refName: 'ctgB', start: 0, end: 6079 },
    ],
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `adapterId: string = ''`: stable identifier used as the adapter cache key; avoids hashing the (potentially large) features array. optional — falls back to hash.
- `features: frozen = []`: one entry per reference sequence, each with a `uniqueId`, `refName`, `start: 0` and `end` set to that sequence's length. This is what defines the assembly's reference names and sizes; no bases are supplied, so base-level views are empty.

FromConfigSequenceAdapter.text:
# FromConfigSequenceAdapter (Adapter config, config plugin)

Supplies a reference sequence inline in the config, as features whose `seq` holds the bases for each region.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "FromConfigSequenceAdapter", ... }.

Used as the adapter of an assembly's `sequence` (a `ReferenceSequenceTrack`):
```js
{
  type: 'ReferenceSequenceTrack',
  trackId: 'my_refseq',
  adapter: {
    type: 'FromConfigSequenceAdapter',
    features: [
      { uniqueId: 'ctgA', refName: 'ctgA', start: 0, end: 10, seq: 'ATGCATGCAT' },
    ],
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `adapterId: string = ''`: stable identifier used as the adapter cache key; avoids hashing the (potentially large) features array. optional — falls back to hash.
- `features: frozen = []`: one entry per reference sequence, each with a `uniqueId`, `refName`, `start`, `end`, and a `seq` string holding the bases for that span. The config holds the bases, so this suits small sequences — a plasmid, a test contig — not a genome.

GCContentAdapter.text:
# GCContentAdapter (Adapter config, gccontent plugin)

Computes GC content (or GC skew) from an assembly's sequence at render time, so there is no data file to prepare: the sequence comes from the assembly the track is displayed against. Each score is the `op` over a `window` of bases, one every `step`; the `GCContentTrack` menu's GC parameters write all three.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "GCContentAdapter", ... }.

```js
{
  type: 'GCContentAdapter',
}
```

## Slots
- `sequenceAdapter: maybeFrozen`: the sequence scored in place of the assembly's own, such as a hard-masked FASTA on the same coordinates. Unset, the track scores the sequence of the assembly it is shown against, and follows that assembly's sequence if it changes — advanced
- `op: stringEnum (content, skew) = 'content'`: `content` is the fraction of bases that are G or C, in [0, 1]; `skew` is (G - C) / (G + C), in [-1, 1]
- `window: number = 100`: bp each score is computed over, centered on the bin it is drawn as. A step wider than the window widens it to the step, so every base is scored. 1 scores single bases; wider windows smooth the signal
- `step: number = 'auto'`: bp between successive scores, or `"auto"` to follow the zoom: the largest 1/2/5 rung (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, ... bp) at or under one point per pixel at the display's resolution. A step under the window overlaps the windows for a smoother signal

GCContentTrack.text:
# GCContentTrack (Track config, gccontent plugin)

GC content, or GC skew, of the assembly's sequence, computed as the view moves by a `GCContentAdapter` and drawn by the wiggle display. The adapter holds the op, the window and the step; the track menu's GC parameters write them there. The reference sequence track's menu has "Add GC content track", which makes one.

Slots are top-level fields of the track config, beside trackId and name.

Adapters: GCContentAdapter.

Displays: LinearWiggleDisplay.

```js
{
  type: 'GCContentTrack',
  trackId: 'gc',
  name: 'GC content',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'GCContentAdapter' },
}
```

## Slots
- `displays: list of display configs`: As on [every track](../basetrack#slot-displays), except that a `LinearWiggleDisplay` entry defaults to `mark.extent: 'none'`.
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the track, falls back to the trackId when unset
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = ['assemblyName']`: name of the assembly (or assemblies) track belongs to
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the track
- `category: stringArray = []`: the category and sub-categories of a track
- `metadata: frozen = {}`: anything to add about this track
- `adapter: adapter config`: The source of this track's data. Its `type` names the adapter for the file format (`BamAdapter`, `Gff3TabixAdapter`, ...) and the rest of the object is that adapter's own slots — see the adapter pages for each. Most adapters also accept a…
- `textSearching.indexingAttributes: stringArray = ['Name', 'ID', 'symbol']`: list of which feature attributes to index for text searching — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToExclude: stringArray = ['CDS', 'exon']`: list of feature types to exclude in text search index — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToInclude: stringArray = []`: The only feature types to index, dropping every other type in the file. Empty (the default) means no allow list, i.e. index everything `indexingFeatureTypesToExclude` does not name. — advanced
- `textSearching.textSearchAdapter: optionalTextSearchAdapter`: a per-track name search index, normally a `TrixTextSearchAdapter` over what `jbrowse text-index --tracks` built; `'genes.ix'` is enough, searching this track's assemblies. Without one, this track's features are only findable through an…
- `formatDetails: FormatDetails`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's feature-details panel. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatDetails`.
- `formatAbout: FormatAbout`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's About dialog. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatAbout`.

Gff3Adapter.text:
# Gff3Adapter (Adapter config, gff3 plugin)

Reads plain-text GFF3 files. The adapter loads the whole file into memory, so use `Gff3TabixAdapter` for large files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "Gff3Adapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'Gff3Adapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/genes.gff3',
}
```

## Slots
- `gffLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.gff', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the GFF3 file. May be gzipped; it is decompressed and parsed in full on first use, so the file has to fit in memory.

Gff3TabixAdapter.text:
# Gff3TabixAdapter (Adapter config, gff3 plugin)

Reads bgzip-compressed, tabix-indexed GFF3 files.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "Gff3TabixAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, csi may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.tbi` index; add `csi: true` for a
`.csi` index instead:
```js
{
  type: 'Gff3TabixAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/genes.gff3.gz',
}
```

## Slots
- `gffGzLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.gff.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bgzip-compressed GFF3, sorted by position. Must be bgzip rather than plain gzip, which tabix cannot index.
- `index: TabixIndex`: The tabix index location and its kind. The `uri` shorthand derives both, so a config using it states neither.
- `dontRedispatch: stringArray = [ 'chromosome', 'region', 'contig', 'supercontig', 'scaffold' ]`: the Gff3TabixAdapter has to "redispatch" if it fetches a region and features it finds inside that region extend outside the region we requested. you can disable this for certain feature types to avoid fetching e.g. the entire chromosome

GoogleDriveOAuthInternetAccount.text:
# GoogleDriveOAuthInternetAccount (Internet Account config, authentication plugin)

Signs requests for Google Drive files with an OAuth 2.0 token, with the Google endpoints, read-only Drive scope and domain filled in.

Slots are top-level fields of the account's entry in internetAccounts.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:GoogleDriveOAuthInternetAccount".

The Google endpoints and scopes are pre-filled, so an entry needs only your
own OAuth app's `clientId`.
```js
{
  type: 'GoogleDriveOAuthInternetAccount',
  internetAccountId: 'googleDriveOAuth',
  name: 'Google Drive',
  clientId: 'your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com',
}
```

## Slots
- `authEndpoint: string = 'https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth'`: the authorization code endpoint of the internet account
- `scopes: string = 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly'`: optional scopes for the authorization call
- `domains: stringArray = ['drive.google.com']`: array of valid domains the url can contain to use this account
- `responseType: string = 'token'`: the type of response from the authorization endpoint
- `tokenType: string = 'Bearer'`: a custom name for a token to include in the header
- `tokenEndpoint: string = ''`: the token endpoint of the internet account
- `needsPKCE: boolean = false`: boolean to indicate if the endpoint needs a PKCE code
- `clientId: string = ''`: id for the OAuth application
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the internet account
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the internet account
- `authHeader: string = 'Authorization'`: request header for credentials

GWASAdapter.text:
# GWASAdapter (Adapter config, gwas plugin)

Reads GWAS results from a bgzip-compressed, tabix-indexed BED-like file. The adapter is a `BedTabixAdapter` whose `scoreColumn` defaults to `neg_log_pvalue`, so a file loads with a Manhattan plot score and no further config.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "GWASAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri, csi may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'GWASAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/summary_stats.txt.gz',
}
```

## Slots
- `scoreColumn: string = 'neg_log_pvalue'`: BED column to read as the Manhattan plot score
- `scoreTransform: string = 'none'`: transform applied to `scoreColumn` to produce the Manhattan -log10(p) value: `none` (column is already -log10, e.g. Pan-UKBB neglog10_pval_*), `negLog10` (column is a raw p-value), `negLog10FromLn` (column is a natural-log p-value, e.g.… —…
- `ldAdapter: maybeFrozen`: optional PLINK .ld sub-adapter (PlinkLDAdapter / PlinkLDTabixAdapter) supplying each SNP's r² to an index SNP, which a fetch joins as the `r2` and `ld_role` fields while the Manhattan display's plot names one; leave it unset to disable
- `bedGzLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.bed.gz', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the bgzip-compressed BED, sorted by position. Must be bgzip rather than plain gzip, which tabix cannot index.
- `index: TabixIndex`: The tabix index location and its kind. The `uri` shorthand derives both, so a config using it states neither.
- `columnNames: stringArray = []`: List of column names. A column named like a standard BED column is parsed as that column's type (chromStart numeric, blockSizes a numeric list); any other column is text
- `autoSql: string = ''`: The autoSql definition for the data fields in the file
- `disableGeneHeuristic: boolean = false`: Disable the heuristic that auto-detects BED12 features as gene/transcript structures. Useful for files that have BED12-like structure but are not genes (e.g. tandem duplications)

GWASTrack.text:
# GWASTrack (Track config, gwas plugin)

Holds Genome-Wide Association Study (GWAS) results, drawn as a Manhattan plot.

Slots are top-level fields of the track config, beside trackId and name.

Adapters: GWASAdapter.

Displays: LinearManhattanDisplay.

A BED of raw p-values: `scoreTransform: 'negLog10'` turns each into
-log10(p) at load. `GWASAdapter` lists the other transforms:
```js
{
  type: 'GWASTrack',
  trackId: 'gwas',
  name: 'GWAS results',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'GWASAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/gwas.bed.gz',
    scoreColumn: 'p_value',
    scoreTransform: 'negLog10',
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the track, falls back to the trackId when unset
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = ['assemblyName']`: name of the assembly (or assemblies) track belongs to
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the track
- `category: stringArray = []`: the category and sub-categories of a track
- `metadata: frozen = {}`: anything to add about this track
- `adapter: adapter config`: The source of this track's data. Its `type` names the adapter for the file format (`BamAdapter`, `Gff3TabixAdapter`, ...) and the rest of the object is that adapter's own slots — see the adapter pages for each. Most adapters also accept a…
- `textSearching.indexingAttributes: stringArray = ['Name', 'ID', 'symbol']`: list of which feature attributes to index for text searching — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToExclude: stringArray = ['CDS', 'exon']`: list of feature types to exclude in text search index — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToInclude: stringArray = []`: The only feature types to index, dropping every other type in the file. Empty (the default) means no allow list, i.e. index everything `indexingFeatureTypesToExclude` does not name. — advanced
- `textSearching.textSearchAdapter: optionalTextSearchAdapter`: a per-track name search index, normally a `TrixTextSearchAdapter` over what `jbrowse text-index --tracks` built; `'genes.ix'` is enough, searching this track's assemblies. Without one, this track's features are only findable through an…
- `displays: list of display configs`: An **array** of full display configs, e.g. `displays: [{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', color: 'green' }]`. Each entry names a display `type`; use this when you need exact control — your own `displayId`, different settings for two displays,…
- `formatDetails: FormatDetails`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's feature-details panel. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatDetails`.
- `formatAbout: FormatAbout`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's About dialog. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatAbout`.

HicAdapter.text:
# HicAdapter (Adapter config, hic plugin)

Reads Hi-C contact matrices from a `.hic` file.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "HicAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

```js
{
  type: 'HicAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/map.hic',
}
```

## Slots
- `hicLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/my.hic', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the `.hic` contact matrix (Juicer / Juicebox format). The file holds every resolution and an index, so there is nothing else to configure — the display picks a bin size from the current zoom.
- `controlAdapter: maybeFrozen`: a second `HicAdapter`, the control condition the display's `observed/control` field divides by: both are scaled to one library depth, so two libraries sequenced to different depths compare. The two must be on one assembly; chromosome names…

HicColor.text:
# HicColor (Display setting config, hic plugin)

The Hi-C display's `encoding.color`: a bin's `observed` contact count, or its `observed/expected` or `observed/control` ratio, through a `linear`, `symlog` or `log` `scale.type` onto a named `scale.scheme`.

```js
{
  type: 'LinearHicDisplay',
  encoding: {
    color: { scale: { type: 'symlog', scheme: 'viridis', domainMax: 500 } },
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: stringEnum (observed, observed/expected, observed/control) = 'observed'`: observed, each bin's contact count; observed/expected, that count over the file's expected count at its distance; or observed/control, that count over the control file's, both scaled to one library depth
- `scale: HicColorScale sub-schema`: How a bin's value maps to a color, Vega-Lite's scale object.
- `scale.type: maybeStringEnum (linear, symlog, log)`: linear; symlog, d3's log(1 + count), which the Log scale toggle writes: it lifts sparse long-range bins off the floor, so only 0 paints as the domain's bottom does; or log, log2 of the count from a pinned domainMin or else 1, every bin at…
- `scale.scheme: maybeStringEnum (viridis, magma, inferno, cividis, juicebox, fall, reds, blues, redblue, purpleorange, redgreyblue, redyellowblue)`: the named ramp the field runs across; unset is the field's own, juicebox for count, which fades from transparent to red
- `scale.reverse: maybeBoolean`: Unset turns round viridis, magma, inferno and cividis, which run dark at their low end, since an unpainted bin is the page behind the matrix; the field's own scheme keeps the field's direction.
- `scale.domainMid: colorRampSlots.domainMid`: The value the ramp's middle stop sits at, so a diverging scheme centres on it and equal distances from it take equal colors; unset, the stops spread evenly across the domain.
- `scale.domainMin: maybeNumber`: the bottom of the scale; unset follows the loaded values, whose extent starts at 0 since no value is below it
- `scale.domainMax: maybeNumber`: the top of the scale's domain; unset follows the loaded counts
- `scale.domainQuantile: number = 0.95`: The value an unset `domainMax` follows: the loaded values' quantile, `0.95` so faint off-diagonal contacts read, or at `1` their maximum. The track menu's "Emphasize faint contacts" toggles it. Only the top clips, since the values' extent…
- `legend: HicColorLegend sub-schema`: The key this channel draws: `title` replaces the heading naming the field and binsize, and `""` draws none.
- `legend.title: maybeString`: key title; unset keeps the display's own heading, "" draws none

HicData.text:
# HicData (Display setting config, hic plugin)

What a Hi-C display's fetch reads of the file: `resolution` steps the binsize from the one the zoom picks, and `normalization` is the matrix normalization asked for.

One binsize finer than the zoom picks, with vanilla coverage:
```json
{
  "type": "LinearHicDisplay",
  "data": { "resolution": 1, "normalization": "VC" }
}
```

## Slots
- `resolution: number = 0`: binsizes finer than the zoom picks: 1 one finer, -1 one coarser, 0 follows the zoom
- `normalization: string = 'KR'`: preferred matrix normalization (KR, SCALE, VC, VC_SQRT, NONE); a scheme the file lacks falls back to one it has

HicEncoding.text:
# HicEncoding (Display setting config, hic plugin)

The Hi-C display's `encoding`, the channels its bins paint through.

```js
{ type: 'LinearHicDisplay', encoding: { color: 'observed/expected' } }
```

## Slots
- `color: HicColor`: The scale from a bin's value to its color: a `linear`, `symlog` or `log` scale onto a named scheme, over a domain whose unset ends follow the loaded counts.
