HiddenLegend.text:
# HiddenLegend (Display setting config, core)

The `legend` of a display whose key is off until asked for, a matrix's color ramp or the reads' fill.

## Slots
- `show: boolean = false`: draw the key

HierarchicalConfigSchema.text:
# HierarchicalConfigSchema (Root config, core)

Sets the hierarchical track selector's starting sort order, and which categories show as folders or start collapsed. Found on the root config as `configuration.hierarchical`.

## Slots
- `configuration.hierarchical.sort.trackNames: boolean = false`: start the track selector with tracks sorted alphabetically inside each category rather than in config order. Only the initial state — the selector's own "Sort track names" toggle overrides it from then on
- `configuration.hierarchical.sort.categories: boolean = false`: start the track selector with categories sorted alphabetically rather than in config order. Only the initial state — the selector's own "Sort categories" toggle overrides it from then on
- `configuration.hierarchical.defaultFolderCategories: stringArray = []`: list of category names to display as folders by default
- `configuration.hierarchical.defaultCollapsed.categoryNames: stringArray = []`: named top-level categories that start collapsed, e.g. `['ENCODE', 'RNA-seq']`. Once a user expands or collapses anything, the selector remembers their state instead
- `configuration.hierarchical.defaultCollapsed.topLevelCategories: boolean = false`: start every top-level category collapsed, so a config with many categories opens as a short list rather than a wall of tracks
- `configuration.hierarchical.defaultCollapsed.subCategories: boolean = false`: start every nested category collapsed while leaving the top level open, for deeply categorized track sets

HtsgetBamAdapter.text:
# HtsgetBamAdapter (Adapter config, alignments plugin)

Used to fetch data from Htsget endpoints in BAM format, using the gmod/bam library

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "HtsgetBamAdapter", ... }.

```js
{
  type: 'HtsgetBamAdapter',
  htsgetBase: 'https://htsget.example.com/reads',
  htsgetTrackId: 'NA12878',
}
```

## Slots
- `htsgetBase: fileLocation = { uri: '', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: The endpoint tickets are requested from. `htsgetTrackId` is appended to it, so a trailing slash produces a doubled one in the request path.
- `htsgetTrackId: string = ''`: the trackId, which is appended to the base URL

HTTPBasicInternetAccount.text:
# HTTPBasicInternetAccount (Internet Account config, authentication plugin)

Prompts for a username and password, and sends them in an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on requests to a matching domain.

Slots are top-level fields of the account's entry in internetAccounts.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:HTTPBasicInternetAccount".

An entry in the config's `internetAccounts`. JBrowse prompts for the username
and password the first time a file under one of `domains` is opened, and
sends them as an `Authorization: Basic …` header from then on.
```js
{
  type: 'HTTPBasicInternetAccount',
  internetAccountId: 'myLabServer',
  name: 'My lab server',
  description: 'Sequencing data behind the lab htaccess',
  domains: ['data.mylab.org'],
}
```

## Slots
- `tokenType: string = 'Basic'`: a custom name for a token to include in the header
- `validateWithHEAD: boolean = true`: validate the token with a HEAD request before using it
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the internet account
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the internet account
- `authHeader: string = 'Authorization'`: request header for credentials
- `domains: stringArray = []`: array of valid domains the url can contain to use this account

IndexedFastaAdapter.text:
# IndexedFastaAdapter (Adapter config, sequence plugin)

Reads an uncompressed FASTA reference sequence through its `samtools faidx` index, fetching the bases in view as byte ranges.

Slots go inside a track's adapter: "adapter": { "type": "IndexedFastaAdapter", ... }.

Shorthand: uri, baseUri may replace the location slot.

The `uri` shorthand auto-resolves the `.fai` index:
```js
{
  type: 'IndexedFastaAdapter',
  uri: 'https://example.com/genome.fa',
}
```

## Slots
- `fastaLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/seq.fa', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the FASTA file. Only the visible bases are fetched, as byte ranges resolved through the `.fai`, so the file itself is never downloaded whole.
- `faiLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/path/to/seq.fa.fai', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: location of the `samtools faidx` index (`.fai`). It supplies the reference names and lengths as well as the byte offsets, so the assembly cannot load without it.
- `metadataLocation: maybeFileLocation`: Optional metadata file

JB2TrackHubConnection.text:
# JB2TrackHubConnection (Connection config, data-management plugin)

Adds the tracks of another JBrowse 2 `config.json` to the session, along with any assemblies it declares that the session lacks.

Slots are top-level fields of the connection's entry in connections.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:JB2TrackHubConnection".

An entry in the config's `connections`, pointing at another JBrowse 2
`config.json`. Its tracks — and any assemblies it declares that the session
lacks — are added on connect, so one instance can publish a track set that
others subscribe to.
```js
{
  type: 'JB2TrackHubConnection',
  connectionId: 'jb2_hub_example',
  name: 'Shared JBrowse 2 tracks',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  configJsonLocation: { uri: 'https://example.com/jbrowse/config.json' },
}
```

## Slots
- `configJsonLocation: fileLocation = { uri: 'https://mysite.com/path/to/config.json', locationType: 'UriLocation', }`: location of the jb2 config file (usually called config.json)
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: optional list of genomes to import from this config.json, if empty all genomes will be imported
- `name: string = 'nameOfConnection'`: a unique name for this connection

JBrowse1Connection.text:
# JBrowse1Connection (Connection config, legacy-jbrowse plugin)

Adds the tracks of a JBrowse 1 data directory to the session, translated to their JBrowse 2 equivalents.

Slots are top-level fields of the connection's entry in connections.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:JBrowse1Connection".

An entry in the config's `connections`, pointing at a JBrowse 1 data
directory — the one holding `trackList.json` and `seq/`. Its tracks are
translated to JBrowse 2 equivalents on connect, which is the path for serving
an existing JBrowse 1 instance's data without re-processing it.
```js
{
  type: 'JBrowse1Connection',
  connectionId: 'jbrowse1_example',
  name: 'Legacy JBrowse 1 data',
  assemblyNames: ['hg19'],
  dataDirLocation: { uri: 'https://example.com/jbrowse1/data/' },
}
```

## Slots
- `dataDirLocation: fileLocation = { uri: 'https://mysite.com/jbrowse/data/', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: the location of the JBrowse 1 data directory, often something like https://mysite.com/jbrowse/data/
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: name of the assembly the connection belongs to, should be a single entry
- `name: string = 'nameOfConnection'`: a unique name for this connection

JBrowse1TextSearchAdapter.text:
# JBrowse1TextSearchAdapter (Adapter config, legacy-jbrowse plugin)

Searches a names index written by JBrowse 1's `generate-names.pl`. The `tracks` and `assemblyNames` slots list the tracks and assemblies the index covers.

An entry in `aggregateTextSearchAdapters`, pointing at the `names/`
directory JBrowse 1's `generate-names.pl` wrote — so an existing instance's
search index is reused rather than rebuilt with `jbrowse text-index`:
```js
{
  type: 'JBrowse1TextSearchAdapter',
  namesIndexLocation: { uri: 'https://example.com/jbrowse1/data/names/' },
  assemblyNames: ['hg19'],
}
```

## Slots
- `namesIndexLocation: fileLocation = { uri: '/volvox/names', locationType: 'UriLocation' }`: the location of the JBrowse1 names index data directory
- `tracks: stringArray = []`: List of tracks covered by text search adapter
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = []`: List of assemblies covered by text search adapter

JBrowseConfiguration.text:
# JBrowseConfiguration (Root config, core)

Holds the app-wide settings in the `configuration` key of a config file, beside `assemblies` and `tracks`.

## Slots
- `configuration.rpc: RpcManager.configSchema`: configuration for the RPC system that runs data adapters in web workers, see RpcOptions
- `configuration.formatDetails: FormatDetails`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in the feature-details panel of every track at once. A track can set the same ones in the track's `formatDetails` and override individual keys.
- `configuration.formatAbout: FormatAbout`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in the About dialog of every track at once. A track can set the same ones in the track's `formatAbout` and override individual keys.
- `configuration.shareURL: string = 'https://share.jbrowse.org/api/v1/'`: URL of the session-sharing backend used by the Share button, a JBrowse-hosted service by default — advanced
- `configuration.disableAnalytics: boolean = false`: disables collection of anonymous usage analytics — advanced
- `configuration.hierarchical: HierarchicalConfigSchema`: configuration for the hierarchical track selector, controlling sorting and default categories, see HierarchicalConfigSchema
- `configuration.preferences: PreferencesConfigSchema`: user preferences such as scroll-to-zoom and animation behavior, see PreferencesConfigSchema
- `configuration.theme: frozen = {}`: Material UI theme overrides applied to the JBrowse UI
- `configuration.extraThemes: frozen = {}`: additional named themes the user can switch between — advanced
- `configuration.logoPath: maybeFileLocation`: a custom logo image displayed in the app header; unset, the JBrowse logo — advanced

JBrowseRootConfig.text:
# JBrowseRootConfig (Root config, core)

Holds a whole JBrowse config file: the `config.json` of jbrowse-web, or a file with the `.jbrowse` extension in jbrowse-desktop.

## Slots
- `plugins: types.array(types.frozen<PluginDefinition>())`: defines plugins of the format ```typescript type PluginDefinition= { umdUrl: string, name:string } | { url: string, name: string } | { esmUrl: string } | { umdLoc: { uri: string } } | { esmLoc: { uri: string } } | { storePlugin: string }…
- `assemblies: types.array(assemblyConfigSchema)`: configuration of the assemblies in the instance, see BaseAssembly
- `tracks: types.frozen([] as TrackConfigEntry[])`: track configuration is an array of track config schemas. multiple instances of a track can exist that use the same configuration. Always uses frozen for performance - editing creates temporary MST models.
- `internetAccounts: list of internet account configs`: configuration for internet accounts, see InternetAccounts
- `aggregateTextSearchAdapters: list of text search adapter configs`: search indexes covering whole assemblies, as `jbrowse text-index` writes them or any pluggable text search adapter. A trix index can be just its `.ix` (`["trix/hg38.ix"]`), which takes the config's assembly when it has one; with several,…
- `connections: list of connection configs`: configuration for connections
- `defaultSession: types.optional(types.frozen(), { name: 'New Session', })`: the session loaded when no session is otherwise specified, e.g. the initial view shown on first load
- `preConfiguredSessions: types.array(types.frozen())`: named sessions bundled with the config that a user can open from the session selector

LaneRows.text:
# LaneRows (Display setting config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

The multi-way synteny display's `rows`: one lane per assembly below the anchor, so `assembly` is the one field, and the object is the arrangement a reader gives the lanes, written whole as every display's `rows` is. `sort` lists the lanes that stack first, in order, the rest following densest-first so a ribbon chain through adjacent lanes is cut as late as possible; `kept` names the lanes drawn, empty drawing the track's lanes or every lane. Haplotype lanes read off a graph follow by structure instead, below any lanes `sort` pins, so lanes whose deletions and insertions against the anchor…

```js
{
  type: 'MultiWaySyntenyDisplay',
  rows: { sort: ['GCF_000346465.2', 'poplar'], kept: ['GCF_000346465.2', 'poplar', 'citrus'] },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: stringEnum (assembly) = 'assembly'`: `assembly`, the one field a lane can be.
- `sort: stringArray = []`: The row order, as Vega-Lite's `sort` lists it: the rows listed lead, in this order, and none is dropped. The rest keep the order their source lists them in (a VCF's samples, a multi-BigWig's subtracks), or sort, digits by magnitude, where…
- `labels: stringMap = {}`: A label drawn beside a row in place of its name, by name.
- `tree: maybeString`: The dendrogram beside the rows, as newick. A clustering run writes it beside the order it produced, and a reorder that moves a row drops it.
- `treeProvenance: maybeFrozen`: The locus and settings `tree` was computed from; unset for a tree that arrived as data. A clustering run writes it with `tree`; a config copies the two together or leaves both out.
- `kept: stringArray = []`: The rows shown, by name: a clade picked off the tree, or the rows one key row stands for. Empty shows every row, and so does naming no current row where the track lists its rows.

LDColor.text:
# LDColor (Display setting config, variants plugin)

The LD display's `encoding.color` paints the statistic the cells show, `r2` or `dprime`, through a linear scale onto a named `scale.scheme`. An unset scheme is the metric's own, reds for r² and blues for D'. The domain is the statistic's 0 to 1 rather than the loaded values', so one r² paints one color on every track; `scale.domainMin` and `scale.domainMax` narrow it. The slots are the shared color channel's, so `jbrowse validate` and "Edit plot..." judge them as they judge any other display's. A string is the field.

```js
{
  type: 'LDTrackDisplay',
  encoding: {
    color: { field: 'dprime', scale: { scheme: 'viridis', domainMin: 0.2 } },
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `field: stringEnum (r2, dprime) = 'r2'`: The file column the cells show: `r2` (R², the R2/PHASED_R2 column) or `dprime` (D', the DP/ABS_DPRIME one). A file with only one of the two uses that one whichever is asked for, and the legend and the menu show which.
- `scale: LDColorScale sub-schema`: The ramp the statistic runs along, Vega-Lite's scale object.
- `scale.scheme: maybeStringEnum (viridis, magma, inferno, cividis, juicebox, fall, reds, blues, redblue, purpleorange, redgreyblue, redyellowblue)`: the named ramp the statistic runs across; unset is the field's own, reds for r2 and blues for dprime
- `scale.reverse: maybeBoolean`: Unset turns round viridis, magma, inferno and cividis, which run dark at their low end, since an unpainted cell is the page behind the matrix.
- `scale.domainMin: maybeNumber`: the value the bottom color paints, everything below it too; unset is 0
- `scale.domainMax: maybeNumber`: the value the top color paints, everything above it too; unset is 1
- `scale.domainMid: colorRampSlots.domainMid`: The value the ramp's middle stop sits at; unset, the stops spread evenly across the domain.
- `legend: LDColorLegend sub-schema`: The key this channel draws: `title` replaces the metric's name, and `""` draws none.
- `scale.type: maybeStringEnum (linear)`: linear, the one scale; unset is linear
- `legend.title: maybeString`: key title; unset keeps the display's own heading, "" draws none

LDEncoding.text:
# LDEncoding (Display setting config, variants plugin)

The LD display's `encoding`: `color`, the statistic the cells paint.

```js
{ type: 'LDTrackDisplay', encoding: { color: 'dprime' } }
```

## Slots
- `color: LDColor`: The statistic the cells show, `field` `r2` or `dprime`, and the linear ramp it paints through over the statistic's 0 to 1.

LDTrack.text:
# LDTrack (Track config, variants plugin)

Track type for displaying pre-computed linkage disequilibrium data (e.g., from PLINK --r2 output)

Slots are top-level fields of the track config, beside trackId and name.

Adapters: PlinkLDAdapter, PlinkLDTabixAdapter.

Displays: LDTrackDisplay.

`PlinkLDTabixAdapter` accepts the minimal `uri` shorthand below — it expects
a sibling `<uri>.tbi` index, equivalent to writing out the full
`ldLocation`/`index.location` slots:
```js
{
  type: 'LDTrack',
  trackId: 'ld',
  name: 'Linkage disequilibrium',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PlinkLDTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/plink.ld.gz',
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `name: string = ''`: descriptive name of the track, falls back to the trackId when unset
- `assemblyNames: stringArray = ['assemblyName']`: name of the assembly (or assemblies) track belongs to
- `description: string = ''`: a description of the track
- `category: stringArray = []`: the category and sub-categories of a track
- `metadata: frozen = {}`: anything to add about this track
- `adapter: adapter config`: The source of this track's data. Its `type` names the adapter for the file format (`BamAdapter`, `Gff3TabixAdapter`, ...) and the rest of the object is that adapter's own slots — see the adapter pages for each. Most adapters also accept a…
- `textSearching.indexingAttributes: stringArray = ['Name', 'ID', 'symbol']`: list of which feature attributes to index for text searching — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToExclude: stringArray = ['CDS', 'exon']`: list of feature types to exclude in text search index — advanced
- `textSearching.indexingFeatureTypesToInclude: stringArray = []`: The only feature types to index, dropping every other type in the file. Empty (the default) means no allow list, i.e. index everything `indexingFeatureTypesToExclude` does not name. — advanced
- `textSearching.textSearchAdapter: optionalTextSearchAdapter`: a per-track name search index, normally a `TrixTextSearchAdapter` over what `jbrowse text-index --tracks` built; `'genes.ix'` is enough, searching this track's assemblies. Without one, this track's features are only findable through an…
- `displays: list of display configs`: An **array** of full display configs, e.g. `displays: [{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', color: 'green' }]`. Each entry names a display `type`; use this when you need exact control — your own `displayId`, different settings for two displays,…
- `formatDetails: FormatDetails`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's feature-details panel. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatDetails`.
- `formatAbout: FormatAbout`: jexl callbacks that add, rewrite or hide fields in this track's About dialog. The same schema exists session-wide as `configuration.formatAbout`.

LDTrackDisplay.text:
# LDTrackDisplay (Display config, variants plugin)

Linkage disequilibrium heatmap read from an `LDTrack`'s pre-computed file — PLINK `--r2` output and the formats that follow it. JBrowse does not compute LD from genotypes; run plink (or an equivalent) and point this at the result.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LDTrackDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: LDTrack.

Adapters: PlinkLDAdapter, PlinkLDTabixAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LDTrackDisplay".

```js
{
  type: 'LDTrack',
  trackId: 'ld',
  name: 'Linkage disequilibrium',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PlinkLDTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/plink.ld.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LDTrackDisplay',
      displayId: 'ld-LDTrackDisplay',
      encoding: { color: { field: 'dprime' } },
      legend: { show: true },
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `lineZoneHeight: number = 100`: height of the band above the triangle holding the connector lines and labels — advanced
- `encoding: LDEncoding`: The cells' channels: `encoding.color`, the statistic the cells show, `field` `r2` or `dprime`, and the linear ramp it paints through over the statistic's 0 to 1.
- `legend: HiddenLegend`: The color ramp's key, off until asked for.
- `guides: LDGuides sub-schema`: The guides a hovered cell draws across the view at its pair's genomic positions.
- `guides.show: boolean = true`: on hover, draw guides across the view at the pair's genomic positions — advanced
- `labels: LDLabels sub-schema`: The text drawn at each variant's tick mark.
- `labels.name: LDNameLabel sub-schema`: Each variant's name, above its tick mark.
- `labels.name.show: boolean = false`: draw each variant name above its tick mark — advanced
- `tickHeight: number = 6`: height of the tick marks at the genomic positions — advanced
- `variantLayout: stringEnum (genomic, columns) = 'columns'`: `'columns'` draws every SNP one uniform square wide; `'genomic'` sizes the cells by the genomic distance between SNPs. The multi-sample variant display takes the same slot for the same choice. — advanced
- `height: number = 400`: default height of the display, the band above the triangle included
- `heightMode: stringEnum = 'fixed'`: fixed draws square cells at the triangle's natural half-width height; fit squashes it to fill the display height

Legend.text:
# Legend (Display setting config, core)

A display's `legend`: whether it draws its key, every channel's sections together. Hiding one section is the key's own close button, which the session forgets.

```js
{ type: 'LinearBasicDisplay', legend: { show: false } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = true`: draw the key

LGVSyntenyColor.text:
# LGVSyntenyColor (Display setting config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

The LGVSyntenyDisplay's `encoding.color`: the [AlignmentsColor](../alignmentscolor) channel, painting `strand` while it names neither a field nor a constant. `strand`, `mapq` and `mateRefName` (the query contig) are the fields a synteny block answers.

```js
{ type: 'LGVSyntenyDisplay', encoding: { color: 'mateRefName' } }
```

## Slots
- `value: maybeColor`: The fill of every read while no field paints. Arcs and pair orientations keep the theme's colors. Unset, the theme's read color.
- `scale: AlignmentsColorScale sub-schema`: How the field's values map to colors, Vega-Lite's scale object.
- `scale.invalid: maybeColor`: The fill of a read with no value under the field, Vega-Lite's word for a missing value's output: no tag, no attribute, or no mate under `mateRefName`. A `''` in `domain` colors it by its `range` entry instead.
- `scale.unknown: maybeColor`: The fill of a read whose tag, attribute, mate reference or MAPQ an ordinal `domain` leaves out, d3's `ordinal.unknown`: `unknown: "#999"` beside `domain: ["1", "2"]` on `tags.HP` paints every other haplotype grey, and the key lists them as…
- `scale.names: stringArray = []`: Names for each level or value `range` colors, in the same order, in the key, the hovers and the arc key: `names: ["Maternal", "Paternal"]` beside `domain: ["1", "2"]` on `tags.HP`.
- `legend: AlignmentsColorLegend sub-schema`: The key this channel draws.
- `field: string = ''`: field to color each read by: a preset field by its levels or bins; tags.XX reads a SAM tag; any other name reads as a facet over it does: mateAssembly, a feature attribute, a dotted path or a jexl: expression; split, spliced, pairing and…
- `scale.type: maybeStringEnum (ordinal, linear, threshold)`: ordinal a range color per value; linear a ramp over mapq or a numeric tag or attribute between domainMin and domainMax; threshold the bins domain cuts; unset, threshold over insertSize, insertSizeAndOrientation and mapq, and ordinal over…
- `scale.domain: stringArray = []`: for an ordinal scale, the values that take the range first, in order: a preset field's levels, insertSize's short, normal and long, with unmappedMate and interchrom under both insert-size fields, '' a read with no value, a MAPQ, 255 for…
- `scale.range: colorArray = []`: CSS colors an ordinal scale hands its domain in order, or with no domain a preset field's levels in their preset order, a threshold scale its bins, or a linear scale's stops, evenly spaced; a level left out keeps its default; empty uses…
- `scale.scheme: maybeStringEnum (viridis, magma, inferno, cividis, juicebox, fall, reds, blues, redblue, purpleorange, redgreyblue, redyellowblue)`: a named ramp: a ramp scale runs along it, a threshold that writes cuts takes one color per interval from end to end, and an ordinal scale that lists a domain one per value; range's colors, where it lists any, win over it
- `scale.reverse: maybeBoolean`: turns the ramp round, so its last color paints the bottom of a ramp's domain or a threshold's lowest interval; unset follows the field's preset, else runs as written
- `scale.domainMid: maybeNumber`: the value the ramp's middle stop sits at, so a diverging ramp centres somewhere other than the middle of the domain, both sides on one scale: the farther end of the domain reaches its end color and equal distances from the middle take…
- `scale.domainMin: maybeNumber`: the bottom of a ramp's domain; unset follows the loaded values
- `scale.domainMax: maybeNumber`: the top of a ramp's domain; unset follows the loaded values
- `scale.domainQuantile: number = 1`: the quantile an open end of a ramp follows over the loaded values: 1 their extremes, 0.99 clips the outermost 1% at each end, each sign measured on its own — advanced
- `legend.title: maybeString`: key title; unset keeps the display's own heading, "" draws none
- `legend.descending: maybeBoolean`: threshold key lists the highest interval first; unset follows the field's preset, else the lowest first

LGVSyntenyCoverage.text:
# LGVSyntenyCoverage (Display setting config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

The LGVSyntenyDisplay's `coverage` setting: the [CoverageBand](../coverageband) object with `show` defaulting to off.

```js
{ type: 'LGVSyntenyDisplay', coverage: { show: true } }
```

## Slots
- `show: boolean = false`: draw the coverage band
- `height: number = 45`: height of the coverage band in pixels
- `encoding: CoverageEncoding`: The depth axis, `encoding.y`: its `scale`, `axis` and `rules`.
- `interbase: CoverageInterbase`: The insertion and clip marks between bases: `show`, and the `filter` deciding which positions get an indicator triangle.
- `alleles: CoverageAlleles`: The colored allele segments: `show`, and the `filter` on each one's `fraction`.

LGVSyntenyDisplay.text:
# LGVSyntenyDisplay (Display config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

Draws a `SyntenyTrack`'s alignments in a linear genome view, stacked and colored the way an alignments display draws reads. It has the alignments display's bands and settings but the sashimi band, the `junction` filter fields, `pileup.bases` and `modifications`: a synteny block has no introns, basecaller tags or qualities.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LGVSyntenyDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: SyntenyTrack.

Adapters: BlastTabularAdapter, ChainAdapter, DeltaAdapter, MashMapAdapter, MCScanAnchorsAdapter, MCScanBlocksAdapter, MCScanSimpleAnchorsAdapter, MultiGenomeIndexedPAFAdapter, MultiGenomePAFAdapter, MultiPairwiseSyntenyAdapter, PAFAdapter, PairwiseIndexedPAFAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LGVSyntenyDisplay".

Shows a `SyntenyTrack`'s alignments in a plain linear view (rather than the
two-row synteny view). Same track config as a synteny track — just pick this
display type:
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'hg38_vs_mm10',
  name: 'hg38 vs mm10',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38', 'mm10'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/hg38_vs_mm10.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'hg38',
    targetAssembly: 'mm10',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LGVSyntenyDisplay',
      displayId: 'hg38_vs_mm10-LGVSyntenyDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `data: SyntenyData`: What the fetch reads, a [](/docs/config/syntenydata) object: `resolution` picks a tiered file's stored tier.
- `encoding: LGVSyntenyEncoding`: The alignments displays' `encoding` with `color` painting `strand` while it names neither a field nor a constant, where the base display paints the plain fill.
- `coverage: LGVSyntenyCoverage`: The alignments displays' `coverage` band with `show` defaulting to off: a synteny track hides the coverage histogram unless asked.
- `collapseSections: boolean = true`: One row per facet section by default: an all-vs-all track faceted by mate assembly draws each mate genome as a single band, with repeat depth shown as darker shading rather than as extra rows. Overrides the base alignments display's…
- `sort: LGVSyntenySort`: The row order, with `length` the default so big syntenic blocks cluster at the top; a string is the `field`.
- `height: number = 250`: Starting height in pixels for the bands together; heightMode decides what a pileup deeper than this does
- `unit: stringEnum (read, chain) = 'read'`: The unit one row draws: a read, or a chain of a read, its mate and its split segments (the "Link mates and supplementary alignments" menu row)
- `filter: fieldPredicateList({ defaults: ALIGNMENTS_FILTER_DEFAULTS })`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries every one of which must hold. The read fields run before every band, so coverage counts only the reads they pass: `flags.UNMAP` and the other samtools flag names,…
- `facet: SectionFacet`: In-track stacked grouping, one labelled section per value: a read dimension (`strand`, `firstOfPairStrand`, `pairOrientation`, `pairing`, `split`, `spliced`, `svSignal`, `mapq`, `mateRefName`, `mateAssembly`), a tag (`tags.HP`), or any…
- `legend: HiddenLegend`: The display's key: `show`, off by default.
- `pileup: Pileup`: The stacked reads: `show`, `mark.height` (default 7), `maxLayoutHeight`, and the parts drawn on each read.
- `readConnections: ReadConnections`: The connections between mates and split segments: `show` (default off), `mark` (`link`, the arcs, or `rule`, the read cloud), `height`, `placement`, `encoding` (`color` and `strokeWidth`) and `ordinaryPairs`; the `connection` and…
- `heightMode: stringEnum (fixed, grow, fit) = 'fixed'`: Track-sizing strategy — how the track responds when there are more reads than fit (the menu sets `fit` from "Read height → Fit to track height" and `grow` from "Advanced → Track height → Autogrow"). `fixed` (the default) keeps…
- `growMaxHeight: number = 800`: Ceiling in pixels for the "autogrow track height" sizing mode; a pileup deeper than this grows to the ceiling and scrolls the rest. Does not apply to the fixed or fit modes, and does not limit how much is laid out (see… — advanced
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 1000000`: bytes a region may fetch before the display asks first; an adapter that sets its own limit overrides this — advanced
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

LGVSyntenyEncoding.text:
# LGVSyntenyEncoding (Display setting config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

The LGVSyntenyDisplay's `encoding`, the channels its blocks paint through.

```js
{ type: 'LGVSyntenyDisplay', encoding: { color: 'mapq' } }
```

## Slots
- `color: LGVSyntenyColor`: The block fill, `strand` while it names neither a field nor a constant.

LGVSyntenySort.text:
# LGVSyntenySort (Display setting config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

The LGVSyntenyDisplay's `sort` setting: the [AlignmentsSort](../alignmentssort) object with `field` defaulting to `length`, so big syntenic blocks cluster at the top instead of interleaving with small ones.

```js
{ type: 'LGVSyntenyDisplay', sort: 'position' }
```

## Slots
- `field: string = 'length'`: position, length, spliced, split or svSignal order the whole window; strand, base, mapq, pairOrientation, a tags.XX tag, insertion, softclip or hardclip rank the reads over the column at pos
- `pos: maybeNumber`: a column sort's 0-based position
- `refName: maybeString`: a column sort's reference sequence
- `within: maybeNumber`: how many bases either side of pos an insertion, softclip or hardclip sort still ranks a mark

LinearAlignmentsDisplay.text:
# LinearAlignmentsDisplay (Display config, alignments plugin)

Draws the reads of an `AlignmentsTrack` as a stack of bands: the coverage histogram with the sashimi arcs over it, the read connections, and the pileup. Each band is one object, `coverage`, `sashimi`, `readConnections` and `pileup`, holding whether it draws and its height; the settings every band shares sit beside them: `filter`, one list of the read, junction and connection tests, `unit`, `facet`, `sort`, `encoding` and `legend`.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearAlignmentsDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: AlignmentsTrack.

Adapters: BamAdapter, CramAdapter, HtsgetBamAdapter, SamAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearAlignmentsDisplay".

Minimal BAM track — no display override needed for defaults. See the
[alignments track guide](/docs/config_guides/alignments_track) for all
adapter and display options:
```js
{
  type: 'AlignmentsTrack',
  trackId: 'ngs_reads',
  name: 'NGS reads',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'BamAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/sample.bam' },
}
```

## Slots
- `pileup: ReadsPileup`: The stacked reads, with the per-base layer drawn over them, whatever fills them: `bases: { show: true, encoding: { color: "modifications" } }`, `"bisulfite"`, `"baseQuality"` or `"base"`.
- `sashimi: Sashimi`: The splice-junction arcs, drawn in the coverage band: `show`, `height`, `placement` and `labels`; the `junction` filter fields filter the junctions drawn.
- `height: number = 250`: Starting height in pixels for the bands together; heightMode decides what a pileup deeper than this does
- `unit: stringEnum (read, chain) = 'read'`: The unit one row draws: a read, or a chain of a read, its mate and its split segments (the "Link mates and supplementary alignments" menu row)
- `filter: fieldPredicateList({ defaults: ALIGNMENTS_FILTER_DEFAULTS })`: The alignments drawn, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries every one of which must hold. The read fields run before every band, so coverage counts only the reads they pass: `flags.UNMAP` and the other samtools flag names,…
- `facet: SectionFacet`: In-track stacked grouping, one labelled section per value: a read dimension (`strand`, `firstOfPairStrand`, `pairOrientation`, `pairing`, `split`, `spliced`, `svSignal`, `mapq`, `mateRefName`, `mateAssembly`), a tag (`tags.HP`), or any…
- `collapseSections: boolean = false`: Only consulted while `facet` is in effect. When set, each section draws as one row instead of a stack, and tint shading shows overlap depth instead of row count — the compact reading for a track with many sections (an all-vs-all synteny…
- `sort: AlignmentsSort`: The pileup's row order by one `field`: a whole-window order (`position`, `length`, `spliced`, `split`, `svSignal`) or a column sort at one base (`{ field: "strand", pos, refName }`).
- `encoding: AlignmentsEncoding`: The channels the reads paint through: `encoding.color`, the read fill.
- `legend: HiddenLegend`: The display's key: `show`, off by default.
- `coverage: CoverageBand`: The coverage histogram band: `show`, `height` (default 45), `encoding.y`, its depth axis, and the `interbase` and `alleles` layers, each with a `show` and a `filter`; `alleles.filter` floors each allele segment's share of its position's…
- `readConnections: ReadConnections`: The connections between mates and split segments: `show` (default off), `mark` (`link`, the arcs, or `rule`, the read cloud), `height`, `placement`, `encoding` (`color` and `strokeWidth`) and `ordinaryPairs`; the `connection` and…
- `heightMode: stringEnum (fixed, grow, fit) = 'fixed'`: Track-sizing strategy — how the track responds when there are more reads than fit (the menu sets `fit` from "Read height → Fit to track height" and `grow` from "Advanced → Track height → Autogrow"). `fixed` (the default) keeps…
- `growMaxHeight: number = 800`: Ceiling in pixels for the "autogrow track height" sizing mode; a pileup deeper than this grows to the ceiling and scrolls the rest. Does not apply to the fixed or fit modes, and does not limit how much is laid out (see… — advanced
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 1000000`: bytes a region may fetch before the display asks first; an adapter that sets its own limit overrides this — advanced
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

LinearBasicDisplay.text:
# LinearBasicDisplay (Display config, features plugin)

Draws the genes and other features of a `FeatureTrack`, from a BED, GFF or similar file. The display adds the gene-glyph slots (isoforms, UTRs, chevrons) to the shared canvas base. `encoding.color` paints each feature's fill and `utrs.encoding.color` its UTRs; the intron lines, chevrons and strand arrows take the theme's stroke color.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearBasicDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: FeatureTrack.

Adapters: BedAdapter, BedTabixAdapter, BigBedAdapter, CrisprGuideAdapter, FromConfigAdapter, Gff3Adapter, Gff3TabixAdapter, GtfAdapter, GtfTabixAdapter, NCListAdapter, SequenceSearchAdapter, SPARQLAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearBasicDisplay".

A `FeatureTrack` with compact features. `displayMode` is `normal`,
`compact`, `superCompact` or `collapsed` (one row):
```js
{
  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'genes',
  name: 'Genes',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'Gff3TabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/genes.gff3.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearBasicDisplay',
      displayId: 'genes-LinearBasicDisplay',
      height: 200,
      displayMode: 'compact',
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 5000000`: Feature (GFF/BED) tracks are light text, and the tabix byte estimate is block-granular (a small region still pulls whole BGZF blocks), so a single gene can trip a tighter gate. — advanced
- `utrs: FeatureUtrs`: The UTR boxes, a [](/docs/config/featureutrs) object. Unset, a UTR takes its transcript's fill, a feature's own BED itemRgb included (matching UCSC's whole-item coloring), else a contrasting blue.
- `geneGlyphMode: stringEnum (auto, all, representative) = 'auto'`: Gene glyph display mode: "auto" collapses each gene to one transcript when zoomed out and trims the rest to what the track height holds, "all" draws every transcript and scrolls the surplus instead of trimming, "representative" shows one…
- `labels: FeatureLabels sub-schema`: The text drawn beside each feature: the base's name and description, and the names of its parts.
- `labels.name: FeatureNameLabel`: Each feature's name, a [](/docs/config/featurenamelabel) object.
- `labels.description: FeatureDescriptionLabel`: The line under each name, a [](/docs/config/featuredescriptionlabel) object.
- `labels.subfeatures: FeatureSubfeatureLabels`: The names of a feature's parts, a [](/docs/config/featuresubfeaturelabels) object.
- `chevrons: FeatureChevrons sub-schema`: The arrows on a feature's intron lines.
- `chevrons.show: boolean = true`: draw chevrons on intron lines pointing the way the feature reads
- `transcripts: FeatureTranscripts`: How a gene's isoforms are read and ranked, a [](/docs/config/featuretranscripts) object.
- `containers: FeatureContainers`: The top-level types whose children stack on rows of their own, a [](/docs/config/featurecontainers) object.
- `filter: fieldPredicateList()`: The features the display draws, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries a feature must all pass: a field of the feature's own (`{ field: "score", gte: 100 }`), a `jexl:` expression that must hold (`"jexl:feature.type ==…
- `tooltip: FeatureTooltip`: The box hovering a feature opens, a [](/docs/config/featuretooltip) object.
- `maxFeatureScreenDensity: number = 1`: maximum features per pixel before showing a "too many features" message — advanced
- `legend: Legend`: The display's color key, when it has one: the key an `encoding.color` field derives, or a variant track's consequence-impact / SV-type presets.
- `encoding: FeatureEncoding`: The channels the features paint through: `encoding.color`, each feature's main fill.
- `mark: FeatureMark`: The box each feature draws as, a [](/docs/config/featuremark) object: `{ height: 6 }`.
- `displayMode: stringEnum (normal, compact, superCompact, collapsed) = 'normal'`: Feature height preset, `normal` by default; `compact` and `superCompact` shrink the rows, and `collapsed` packs every feature onto a single row with all labels hidden
- `facet: SectionFacet`: One labelled section of the track per value of a field: `"strand"`, or `{ field, sort }` with the order its sections stack in.
- `heightMode: stringEnum (fixed, grow, fit) = 'fit'`: Track-sizing strategy — how the track responds when there are more features than fit (shared vocabulary with the alignments display, exposed in the "Track sizing" menu). `fit` (the default) keeps the track height and gives up descriptions,…
- `growMaxHeight: number = 800`: Ceiling in pixels for the "autogrow track height" sizing mode; a track with more content than this grows to the ceiling and scrolls the rest. Does not apply to the fixed or fit modes — advanced
- `height: number = 100`: default height for the track
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

# LinearFeatureBaseDisplay (Display config, features plugin)

Holds the slots shared by the canvas-drawn linear feature displays, which stack overlapping features in rows (pileup-style glyphs).

A shared base schema, not a type you write: use one of LinearBasicDisplay, LinearVariantDisplay.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearFeatureBaseDisplay".

LinearGenomeViewAxis.text:
# LinearGenomeViewAxis (View config, linear-genome-view plugin)

The linear genome view's `axis`: the ruler along its top, whose ticks `grid` carries down through the tracks.

```js
{ type: 'LinearGenomeView', axis: { grid: false } }
```

## Slots
- `grid: boolean = true`: carry the ruler's ticks down through the tracks

LinearGenomeViewConfigSchema.text:
# LinearGenomeViewConfigSchema (Root config, linear-genome-view plugin)

Sets defaults for every linear genome view, on the root config under `configuration.LinearGenomeViewPlugin`.

## Slots
- `configuration.LinearGenomeViewPlugin.trackLabels: string (offset, overlapping, hidden) = 'offset'`: The placement of a track's name: `offset` puts it on a line above the data, `overlapping` floats it over the top of the data to save vertical space, `hidden` omits it. The view menu's "Track labels" submenu sets the same thing per session

LinearHicDisplay.text:
# LinearHicDisplay (Display config, hic plugin)

Draws a `HicTrack`'s contact matrix as a triangular heatmap in the linear genome view, at a bin size that follows the zoom.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearHicDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: HicTrack.

Adapters: HicAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearHicDisplay".

A log color scale, one binsize coarser than the zoom picks, through the
`displayDefaults` shorthand. See the
[Hi-C track guide](/docs/config_guides/hic_track) for the rest:
```js
{
  type: 'HicTrack',
  trackId: 'hic',
  name: 'Hi-C',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'HicAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/contacts.hic' },
  displayDefaults: {
    encoding: { color: { scale: { type: 'symlog' } } },
    data: { resolution: -1 },
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `encoding: HicEncoding`: The channels the bins paint through: `encoding.color`, the scale from count to color.
- `legend: HiddenLegend`: The color ramp's key, off until asked for.
- `data: HicData`: What the fetch reads, a [](/docs/config/hicdata) object: `resolution` steps the binsize from the zoom's pick, `normalization` names the matrix normalization.
- `filter: fieldPredicateList()`: Floors, written `gte` or `gt`, on the counts a cell is built from: `observed`, the map's count, and under observed/control `control`, the control's, both before the depth scaling. A cell below a floor is left out before its ratio, so a…
- `height: number = 300`: default height for the Hi-C track
- `heightMode: stringEnum = 'fixed'`: fixed draws square cells at the triangle's natural half-width height; fit squashes it to fill the display height

LinearMafDisplay.text:
# LinearMafDisplay (Display config, maf plugin)

The display for a `MafTrack`: one row per aligned species, with a conservation summary above them. The slots are show/hide defaults and band sizes; the bands and overlays derive from the alignment and toggle from the track menu.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearMafDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: MafTrack.

Adapters: BgzipMafAdapter, BgzipTaffyAdapter, BigMafAdapter, MafTabixAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearMafDisplay".

Set through the track's `displayDefaults`, so the track opens in this state
for every viewer.
```js
{
  type: 'MafTrack',
  trackId: 'multiz_example',
  name: 'Multiz alignment',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'BigMafAdapter',
    bigBedLocation: { uri: 'https://example.com/multiz.bb' },
    samples: ['hg38', 'panTro6', 'rheMac10', 'mm39'],
  },
  displayDefaults: {
    rowHeight: 12,
    conservation: { show: true, height: 40 },
    axis: { labels: true },
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 5000000`: The bytes a region may cost before the display stops and offers to load it anyway, the whole budget since no MAF adapter declares a `fetchSizeLimit`. 5 Mb, as `LinearBasicDisplay` uses, because the index estimate is block-granular. —…
- `encoding: MafEncoding`: The channels the aligned cells paint through: `encoding.color`, the field that colors them (see [MafColor](../mafcolor)), and `encoding.y`, the field a row's bar height shows.
- `axis: RowAxis`: The guide down the left of the species rows: the species tree and each species' name. No `grid`: the rows keep a gap instead. The coverage band's value axis is `coverage.encoding.y.axis`.
- `rows: SampleRows`: The arrangement a reader gives the species rows, each member by row name. `sort` is the row order: the guide tree rotates to it while some rotation lists the species in that order; otherwise the listed species lead and the rest keep…
- `rowColor: RowColor`: A color per species row, drawn as the bar beside its label, over the color the adapter's `samples` entry gives it.
- `legend: Legend`: The color key for the active row rendering: codon-change categories, source-chromosome ranks, the identity ramp and the CDS frame swatches. In `bases` mode nothing draws, since there is nothing to key.
- `coverage: CoverageBand`: The coverage band: `show`, `height`, `encoding.y`, `interbase` and `alleles`, as the alignments display spells it.
- `alignments: MafAlignments`: The per-species rows, which take the height the bands above them leave: `show`, `rowProportion`, and the `inversions`, `frames` and `reference` parts.
- `conservation: MafConservation`: The band of identity to the reference: `show` (default off), `height` and `unit`, `base` or `codon`.
- `height: number = 300`: display height in pixels, the bands above the rows included; the rows divide what is left while row height fits, however many there are
- `rowHeight: number = 0`: per-row height in px, scrolling the rows that do not fit; 0 (the default) fits the rows to the display height instead, dividing it between them
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

LinearManhattanDisplay.text:
# LinearManhattanDisplay (Display config, gwas plugin)

The Manhattan plot: the default display of a GWAS track, and one a FeatureTrack can switch to. It is the mark display with a point per feature at its `score` as its default plot, so every mark, scale, facet and row setting applies, and a plot whose encoding names `r2` or `ld_role` joins each SNP's r² to the index SNP from the `GWASAdapter`'s `ldAdapter`.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearManhattanDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: GWASTrack.

Adapters: GWASAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearManhattanDisplay".

Minimal `GWASTrack` config. See the
[GWAS track guide](/docs/config_guides/gwas_track) for all options:
```js
{
  type: 'GWASTrack',
  trackId: 'gwas',
  name: 'GWAS results',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'GWASAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/gwas.bed.gz',
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `marks: list of Mark entries`: The plot, as `LinearMarkDisplay` reads it: unwritten, a point per feature at its `score`.
- `height: number = 100`: default height for the track
- `marks.encoding.shape.value: stringEnum (circle, triangle-down, diamond, square) = 'circle'`: `circle`, `triangle-down`, `diamond` or `square`, or a jexl callback over `feature` returning one, for a point mark whose shape is not a scale. — callback args: feature
- `marks.encoding.shape.field: featureField = ''`: The feature field an ordinal scale reads — or a jexl expression over `feature`, which is slower per feature and so the opt-in.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale: MarkShapeScale sub-schema`: How the field's values map to shapes, Vega-Lite's scale object.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.type: maybeStringEnum (ordinal)`: `ordinal` hands a shape from `range` to each distinct value of `field`. Unset beside a `field`, it is `ordinal`.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.range: stringEnumArray (circle, triangle-down, diamond, square) = []`: The shape names an ordinal scale hands out, in order. Empty is `circle`, `triangle-down`, `diamond`; `square` draws only where listed.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.domain: stringArray = []`: The values in legend order, walking `range` from the first entry; left empty, each value derives its shape from itself, so every region agrees.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.names: stringArray = []`: The key's name for each `domain` value, one each in order; a value past the end of the list shows its name.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend: MarkShapeLegend sub-schema`: The key this channel's scale draws.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend.title: maybeString`: The heading of the key an ordinal scale draws, naming what the shape marks. Unset, the key is titled with `field`; `""` is a key with no title.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend.values: stringArray = []`: The values the key lists, in this order; empty lists every value the loaded regions met. A value left out still takes its shape.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend.missingLabel: maybeString`: The key's name for a feature with nothing in `field`; unset is "(no value)". Vega-Lite's legend has no such member, so it keeps its JBrowse name.
- `marks.encoding.x: featureField = 'start'`: The feature field, or jexl expression over `feature`, giving the mark's left edge in bp.
- `marks.encoding.x2: MarkLocus`: The feature field, or jexl expression, giving the mark's right edge in bp, or for a link its far foot: an object naming the field holding the foot's sequence beside the one holding its position, where a mate may lie on another sequence.…
- `marks.encoding.y: featureField = ''`: The feature field, or jexl expression over `feature`, plotted on the score axis. A feature whose value is not a finite number is skipped. Empty reads what the steps before this mark's encode wrote, the way a ggplot2 stat names what its…
- `marks.encoding.row: featureField = ''`: The feature field, or jexl expression, naming the band the mark stands in, an integer from 0; a feature with nothing there sits on band 0. Empty reads the field the last `pileup` before this mark's encode wrote, this mark's own, the…
- `marks.encoding.color: MarkColor`: The mark's color: a field through an ordinal or continuous `scale`, written bare or as an object, or a constant `{ value }`, a CSS color or a jexl callback returning one. `legend` shapes the key the scale draws.
- `marks.encoding.shape: MarkShape sub-schema`: For a point mark: a field through an ordinal scale over `circle`, `triangle-down` and `diamond`, written bare or as an object, or a constant `{ value }`, one of those names, `square`, or a jexl callback returning one. `legend` shapes the…
- `marks.encoding.text: featureField = 'name'`: For a text mark: the feature field, or jexl expression over `feature`, it prints, `name` unset. A feature with nothing there prints nothing.
- `marks.encoding.size: MarkSize`: A point's diameter in px. The track menu's Point size writes every point mark's number.
- `marks.encoding.strokeWidth: MarkSize`: A stroked mark's width in px, Vega-Lite's stroke width: a rule's or a line's thickness, or a link's stroke; a field, which a link alone reads, goes through a linear or log `scale` into a width, `scale.range` the px at each end of the…
- `marks.mark: MarkDef`: What the mark draws, a [](/docs/config/markdef) object or its `type` alone: `bar`, `point`, `rule`, `line`, `rect`, `text` or `link`, with the members one type reads, a line's or a link's `interpolate`, a rect's `height` and a line's…
- `marks.encoding: MarkEncoding sub-schema`: The feature field each of the mark's channels reads. Every channel has a default, so `{}` draws a bar from `start` to `end` with no value.
- `marks.transform: MarkTransform`: Steps over the region's features before this mark encodes them, in order, after the display's own `transform`, and over each section alone under a facet. A `bin` then an `aggregate` grouped by `start` and `end` is a density: `count` per…
- `marks.minBpPerPx: number = 0`: The mark draws only when the view is at least this zoomed out, in bp per px. 0 sets no bound. With `maxBpPerPx` on another mark, one config shows a density zoomed out and the features zoomed in.
- `marks.maxBpPerPx: number = 0`: The mark draws only when the view is zoomed in past this, in bp per px. 0 sets no bound.
- `transform: MarkTransform`: Steps over the region's features before the facet splits them and before any mark's own, after `filter`: where a field the facet reads is made, such as a formula lifting a read's tag.
- `facet: MarkFacet`: Labelled sections, one per value of a field, each as tall as its steps pack it: `"HP"`, or `{ field, sort, transform }` with the order the sections stack in and the steps each runs before any mark's, a per-section `pileup` among them. A…
- `rows: Rows`: One row per value of a field: `"source"` over a multi-BigWig is one xyplot per file. The worker splits the features on the field as it does for `facet`, and the rows take the tree sidebar, the row labels, clustering and the arrangement…
- `rowColor: RowColor`: The bar beside each row's label, and the color of a mark naming none, or of a mark colored by the rows' own field. Under the default field `name`, a row's value paired with a color in `scale.domain`/`scale.range`, which the arrangement…
- `rowGroups: RowGroup`: An array of `{ match, group }` tagging each row with the `group` of the first entry whose regex its name matches, a row attribute: `facet: 'group'` stacks the groups in bands, and `rowColor: { field: 'group' }` colors them. A row no entry…
- `axis: RowAxisWithGrid`: The row axis down the left of the rows `rows` draws: the cluster tree, each row's value and, with `grid`, a line between rows. The value axis is `encoding.y.axis`.
- `encoding: MarkDisplayEncoding`: The channels the marks are read through, owned by the display rather than by a mark, a [MarkDisplayEncoding](../markdisplayencoding): `y`, the [YChannel](../ychannel) every mark's `encoding.y` shares, which names no field since each mark…
- `origin: number = 0`: The value bars grow from. The axis widens to include it whenever a bar mark is drawn.
- `legend: Legend`: The key for every mark whose color or shape is a scale; `show` defaults to on.
- `filter: fieldPredicateList()`: The features the display draws, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries a feature must all pass: a field of the feature's own (`{ field: "score", gte: 5 }`) or a `jexl:` expression that must hold.
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 1000000`: bytes a region may fetch before the display asks first; an adapter that sets its own limit overrides this — advanced
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…
- `rowHeight: number = 0`: per-row height in px under rows, scrolling the rows that do not fit; 0 (the default) fits the rows to the plot instead, dividing it between them

LinearMarkDisplay.text:
# LinearMarkDisplay (Display config, marks plugin)

A grammar of graphics over a feature, alignments or variant track: a list of marks — bars, points, rules, lines, spans, text or links — each with an encoding naming which feature fields feed its channels and a transform list run before it. One fetch per region evaluates every encoding in the worker; the marks draw in order over one score axis.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearMarkDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: FeatureTrack.

Adapters: BedAdapter, BedTabixAdapter, BigBedAdapter, CrisprGuideAdapter, FromConfigAdapter, Gff3Adapter, Gff3TabixAdapter, GtfAdapter, GtfTabixAdapter, NCListAdapter, SequenceSearchAdapter, SPARQLAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearMarkDisplay".

A BED score column as bars, colored by strand, with the key on screen,
and a per-10 kb count in its place once the view is wider than 100 bp
per px:
```js
{
  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'scores',
  name: 'Scores',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: { type: 'BedTabixAdapter', uri: 'https://example.com/scores.bed.gz' },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearMarkDisplay',
      displayId: 'scores-LinearMarkDisplay',
      marks: [
        {
          mark: 'bar',
          encoding: {
            y: 'score',
            color: { field: 'strand', scale: { type: 'ordinal' } },
          },
          maxBpPerPx: 100,
        },
        {
          mark: 'bar',
          transform: [
            { type: 'bin', step: 10000 },
            { type: 'aggregate', groupby: ['start', 'end'], ops: [{ op: 'count' }] },
          ],
          minBpPerPx: 100,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
```

- `marks.encoding.shape.value: stringEnum (circle, triangle-down, diamond, square) = 'circle'`: `circle`, `triangle-down`, `diamond` or `square`, or a jexl callback over `feature` returning one, for a point mark whose shape is not a scale. — callback args: feature
- `marks.encoding.shape.field: featureField = ''`: The feature field an ordinal scale reads — or a jexl expression over `feature`, which is slower per feature and so the opt-in.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale: MarkShapeScale sub-schema`: How the field's values map to shapes, Vega-Lite's scale object.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.type: maybeStringEnum (ordinal)`: `ordinal` hands a shape from `range` to each distinct value of `field`. Unset beside a `field`, it is `ordinal`.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.range: stringEnumArray (circle, triangle-down, diamond, square) = []`: The shape names an ordinal scale hands out, in order. Empty is `circle`, `triangle-down`, `diamond`; `square` draws only where listed.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.domain: stringArray = []`: The values in legend order, walking `range` from the first entry; left empty, each value derives its shape from itself, so every region agrees.
- `marks.encoding.shape.scale.names: stringArray = []`: The key's name for each `domain` value, one each in order; a value past the end of the list shows its name.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend: MarkShapeLegend sub-schema`: The key this channel's scale draws.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend.title: maybeString`: The heading of the key an ordinal scale draws, naming what the shape marks. Unset, the key is titled with `field`; `""` is a key with no title.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend.values: stringArray = []`: The values the key lists, in this order; empty lists every value the loaded regions met. A value left out still takes its shape.
- `marks.encoding.shape.legend.missingLabel: maybeString`: The key's name for a feature with nothing in `field`; unset is "(no value)". Vega-Lite's legend has no such member, so it keeps its JBrowse name.
- `marks.encoding.x: featureField = 'start'`: The feature field, or jexl expression over `feature`, giving the mark's left edge in bp.
- `marks.encoding.x2: MarkLocus`: The feature field, or jexl expression, giving the mark's right edge in bp, or for a link its far foot: an object naming the field holding the foot's sequence beside the one holding its position, where a mate may lie on another sequence.…
- `marks.encoding.y: featureField = ''`: The feature field, or jexl expression over `feature`, plotted on the score axis. A feature whose value is not a finite number is skipped. Empty reads what the steps before this mark's encode wrote, the way a ggplot2 stat names what its…
- `marks.encoding.row: featureField = ''`: The feature field, or jexl expression, naming the band the mark stands in, an integer from 0; a feature with nothing there sits on band 0. Empty reads the field the last `pileup` before this mark's encode wrote, this mark's own, the…
- `marks.encoding.color: MarkColor`: The mark's color: a field through an ordinal or continuous `scale`, written bare or as an object, or a constant `{ value }`, a CSS color or a jexl callback returning one. `legend` shapes the key the scale draws.
- `marks.encoding.shape: MarkShape sub-schema`: For a point mark: a field through an ordinal scale over `circle`, `triangle-down` and `diamond`, written bare or as an object, or a constant `{ value }`, one of those names, `square`, or a jexl callback returning one. `legend` shapes the…
- `marks.encoding.text: featureField = 'name'`: For a text mark: the feature field, or jexl expression over `feature`, it prints, `name` unset. A feature with nothing there prints nothing.
- `marks.encoding.size: MarkSize`: A point's diameter in px. The track menu's Point size writes every point mark's number.
- `marks.encoding.strokeWidth: MarkSize`: A stroked mark's width in px, Vega-Lite's stroke width: a rule's or a line's thickness, or a link's stroke; a field, which a link alone reads, goes through a linear or log `scale` into a width, `scale.range` the px at each end of the…
- `marks.mark: MarkDef`: What the mark draws, a [](/docs/config/markdef) object or its `type` alone: `bar`, `point`, `rule`, `line`, `rect`, `text` or `link`, with the members one type reads, a line's or a link's `interpolate`, a rect's `height` and a line's…
- `marks.encoding: MarkEncoding sub-schema`: The feature field each of the mark's channels reads. Every channel has a default, so `{}` draws a bar from `start` to `end` with no value.
- `marks.transform: MarkTransform`: Steps over the region's features before this mark encodes them, in order, after the display's own `transform`, and over each section alone under a facet. A `bin` then an `aggregate` grouped by `start` and `end` is a density: `count` per…
- `marks.minBpPerPx: number = 0`: The mark draws only when the view is at least this zoomed out, in bp per px. 0 sets no bound. With `maxBpPerPx` on another mark, one config shows a density zoomed out and the features zoomed in.
- `marks.maxBpPerPx: number = 0`: The mark draws only when the view is zoomed in past this, in bp per px. 0 sets no bound.

- `transform: MarkTransform`: Steps over the region's features before the facet splits them and before any mark's own, after `filter`: where a field the facet reads is made, such as a formula lifting a read's tag.
- `facet: MarkFacet`: Labelled sections, one per value of a field, each as tall as its steps pack it: `"HP"`, or `{ field, sort, transform }` with the order the sections stack in and the steps each runs before any mark's, a per-section `pileup` among them. A…
- `rows: Rows`: One row per value of a field: `"source"` over a multi-BigWig is one xyplot per file. The worker splits the features on the field as it does for `facet`, and the rows take the tree sidebar, the row labels, clustering and the arrangement…

- `rowGroups: RowGroup`: An array of `{ match, group }` tagging each row with the `group` of the first entry whose regex its name matches, a row attribute: `facet: 'group'` stacks the groups in bands, and `rowColor: { field: 'group' }` colors them. A row no entry…
- `axis: RowAxisWithGrid`: The row axis down the left of the rows `rows` draws: the cluster tree, each row's value and, with `grid`, a line between rows. The value axis is `encoding.y.axis`.
- `encoding: MarkDisplayEncoding`: The channels the marks are read through, owned by the display rather than by a mark, a [MarkDisplayEncoding](../markdisplayencoding): `y`, the [YChannel](../ychannel) every mark's `encoding.y` shares, which names no field since each mark…
- `origin: number = 0`: The value bars grow from. The axis widens to include it whenever a bar mark is drawn.
- `legend: Legend`: The key for every mark whose color or shape is a scale; `show` defaults to on.

- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

# LinearMultiRowFeatureDisplay (Display config, marks plugin)

Colored features in stacked rows, one row per value of a feature attribute: a chromosome painting, an ancestry painting, a chromatin-state track per cell type. It is the mark display with a `rect` per feature as its default plot, so every mark, scale, facet and row setting applies.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearMultiRowFeatureDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: FeatureTrack.

Adapters: BedAdapter, BedTabixAdapter, BigBedAdapter, CrisprGuideAdapter, FromConfigAdapter, Gff3Adapter, Gff3TabixAdapter, GtfAdapter, GtfTabixAdapter, NCListAdapter, SequenceSearchAdapter, SPARQLAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearMultiRowFeatureDisplay".

A custom BED with a column naming each row, its columns named by a
`#`-prefixed header line (tab-separated, shown space-aligned):
```text
#chrom  start    end      name  sample
chr1    0        2000000  seg1  HG00096
chr1    2000000  5500000  seg2  HG00096
chr1    0        3500000  seg3  HG00097
```

HG00097 above HG00096 regardless of file order:
```js

  type: 'FeatureTrack',
  trackId: 'ancestry_painting',
  name: 'Ancestry painting',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'BedTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/painting.bed.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearMultiRowFeatureDisplay',
      displayId: 'ancestry_painting-LinearMultiRowFeatureDisplay',
      rows: { field: 'sample', sort: ['HG00097', 'HG00096'] },
      rowColor: {
        scale: {
          domain: ['HG00096', 'HG00097'],
          range: ['#4e79a7', '#f28e2b'],
        },
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

LinearMultiSampleVariantDisplay.text:
# LinearMultiSampleVariantDisplay (Display config, variants plugin)

Draws the genotypes in a multi-sample `VariantTrack`, one row per sample or per phased haplotype.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearMultiSampleVariantDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: VariantTrack.

Adapters: BedpeAdapter, SplitVcfTabixAdapter, StarFusionAdapter, VcfAdapter, VcfTabixAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearMultiSampleVariantDisplay".

Minimal `VariantTrack` config selecting this display type. The `displays`
array form is required here (rather than the object shorthand) because
this is a non-default display type — see
[configuring displays](/docs/config_guides/tracks#configuring-displays):
```js
{
  type: 'VariantTrack',
  trackId: 'cohort',
  name: 'Cohort variants',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'VcfTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/cohort.vcf.gz',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearMultiSampleVariantDisplay',
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `height: number = 200`: Starting height in pixels for the whole display, including any band above the rows; drag-resizable, and the rows divide what is left while row height is on auto-fit
- `variantLayout: stringEnum (genomic, columns) = 'genomic'`: `'genomic'` draws each variant across the bases it covers; `'columns'` draws one equal-width column per variant in view, with a line tying each column to its position. Columns keep variants a few bases apart readable at any zoom, at the…
- `lineZoneHeight: number = 20`: Height of the band of connector lines above the columns, spent only in the `'columns'` layout. — advanced
- `filter: fieldPredicateList()`: The variants the display draws, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries a site must all pass: a field of the record's own, a `jexl:` expression that must hold, `minorAlleleFrequency`, the share of its called alleles the second…
- `axis: RowAxisWithGrid`: The guide down the left of the sample rows: the clustering tree, each sample's name and the lines between rows.
- `rows: SampleRows`: The rows are the file's samples, and the object is the arrangement a reader gives them, each member by row name: a sample in allele-count mode, a haplotype (`"<sample> HP<n>"`) in phased mode, where a sample name stands for all of its…
- `tooltip: SampleTooltip sub-schema`: The hover tooltip naming the genotype, the sample and the record under the pointer. Off, the crosshairs, the highlighted cell and the cross-display `session.hovered` channel stay.
- `tooltip.show: boolean = true`: show the hover tooltip over the genotype rows; the crosshairs and the hover highlight stay either way
- `unit: stringEnum (sample, haplotype) = 'sample'`: The unit one row draws: 'sample' colors each row by allele dosage, 'haplotype' draws one row per phased haplotype
- `encoding: VariantCellEncoding`: The genotype cells' channels: `encoding.color`, the hue of every cell with an alt allele.
- `shadeByDosage: boolean = true`: Compose the cell hue with the genotype's alt dosage — the fraction of its called alleles that are non-reference — so a homozygote paints the hue itself and a heterozygote a lighter version of it. Off paints each alt cell its flat hue.
- `legend: Legend`: The floating key over the display. It is clipped to the display's own bounds, so turn it off to size a short display to its rows rather than to its key.
- `rowColor: RowColor`: The bar beside each row's label: a sample-metadata attribute whose palette colors every row, or under `name` the colors a reader set row by row.
- `facet: Facet`: A sample-metadata attribute (a column in the adapter's samplesTsvLocation, e.g. `"population"`) whose values each take a band of rows; or `{ field, sort }`, the listed values banding first and the rest sorted. Unset, the rows keep their…
- `referenceDrawingMode: stringEnum (draw, skip) = 'skip'`: Whether to paint reference alleles: 'skip' (the default) fills the row background solid grey and paints only ALT alleles, which makes overlapping variants easier to pick out; 'draw' paints reference alleles like any other genotype.
- `rowHeight: number = 0`: per-row height in px, scrolling the rows that do not fit; 0 (the default) fits the rows to the display height instead, dividing it between them
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 1000000`: bytes a region may fetch before the display asks first; an adapter that sets its own limit overrides this — advanced
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

LinearReferenceSequenceDisplay.text:
# LinearReferenceSequenceDisplay (Display config, sequence plugin)

Draws a `ReferenceSequenceTrack` as rows of bases: the forward strand, the reverse complement and the translation frames.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearReferenceSequenceDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: ReferenceSequenceTrack.

Adapters: BgzipFastaAdapter, ChromSizesAdapter, FromConfigRegionsAdapter, FromConfigSequenceAdapter, IndexedFastaAdapter, TwoBitAdapter, UnindexedFastaAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearReferenceSequenceDisplay".

The display goes in the `displays` array of the assembly's `sequence` track,
which is where a `ReferenceSequenceTrack` is authored, so the display sets
no assembly name. `forward`, `reverse` and `translation` each turn their rows
on and off with `show`:
```js
sequence: {
  type: 'ReferenceSequenceTrack',
  trackId: 'refseq',
  adapter: {
    type: 'IndexedFastaAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/genome.fa',
  },
  displays: [
    {
      type: 'LinearReferenceSequenceDisplay',
      displayId: 'refseq-LinearReferenceSequenceDisplay',
      translation: { show: false },
    },
  ],
}
```

## Slots
- `height: maybeNumber`: explicit display height (e.g. from a drag-resize); unset means auto-fit to the zoom-aware computed height. See the model's `height` getter.
- `forward: SequenceForward sub-schema`: The forward-strand base row.
- `forward.show: boolean = true`: draw the rows
- `reverse: SequenceReverse sub-schema`: The reverse-complement base row; a protein sequence has none.
- `reverse.show: boolean = true`: draw the rows
- `translation: SequenceTranslation sub-schema`: The three translation frame rows per drawn strand; a protein sequence has none.
- `translation.show: boolean = true`: draw the rows
- `fetchSizeLimit: number = 1000000`: bytes a region may fetch before the display asks first; an adapter that sets its own limit overrides this — advanced
- `forceLoad: boolean = false`: Declarative equivalent of the "Force load" button on the "too much data" banner: when true the display always renders, however large the region or dense the features. Off by default (the gate guards against huge downloads). Set it on a… —…

LinearScoreDisplay.text:
# LinearScoreDisplay (Display config, core)

Config for the worked-example score display. Attaches to any `FeatureTrack`.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearScoreDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: FeatureTrack.

Adapters: BedAdapter, BedTabixAdapter, BigBedAdapter, CrisprGuideAdapter, FromConfigAdapter, Gff3Adapter, Gff3TabixAdapter, GtfAdapter, GtfTabixAdapter, NCListAdapter, SequenceSearchAdapter, SPARQLAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearScoreDisplay".

## Slots
- `height: number = 100`: height of the display in pixels
- `encoding: LinearScoreEncoding sub-schema`: The channels each box paints through, spelled as the built-in displays spell theirs: `color.value` fills every box, and `y.field` names the feature attribute read as the box height.
- `encoding.color.value: color = '#0068d1'`: fill color for every score box
- `encoding.y.field: string = 'score'`: feature attribute read as the score (box height); normalized per region

LinearSyntenyAxis.text:
# LinearSyntenyAxis (View config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

The linear synteny view's `axis`: each row's ruler, whose ticks `grid` carries down through the ribbons to the coordinates they pair with on the row below, so a ribbon's shear and stretch show.

```js
{ type: 'LinearSyntenyView', axis: { grid: true } }
```

## Slots
- `grid: boolean = false`: carry each row's ruler ticks down through the ribbons

LinearSyntenyDisplay.text:
# LinearSyntenyDisplay (Display config, linear-comparative-view plugin)

Draws a `SyntenyTrack` in a `LinearSyntenyView`, as ribbons joining the aligned regions of two stacked linear genome views.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearSyntenyDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: SyntenyTrack.

Adapters: BlastTabularAdapter, ChainAdapter, DeltaAdapter, MashMapAdapter, MCScanAnchorsAdapter, MCScanBlocksAdapter, MCScanSimpleAnchorsAdapter, MultiGenomeIndexedPAFAdapter, MultiGenomePAFAdapter, MultiPairwiseSyntenyAdapter, PAFAdapter, PairwiseIndexedPAFAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearSyntenyDisplay".

A `SyntenyTrack` config to paste into `tracks`. The adapter needs the query
(first) and target (second) assembly names, matched by the track's
`assemblyNames`. See the
[synteny track guide](/docs/config_guides/synteny_track) for all options:
```js
{
  type: 'SyntenyTrack',
  trackId: 'hg38_vs_mm10',
  name: 'hg38 vs mm10',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38', 'mm10'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'PAFAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/hg38_vs_mm10.paf',
    queryAssembly: 'hg38',
    targetAssembly: 'mm10',
  },
}
```

LinearVariantDisplay.text:
# LinearVariantDisplay (Display config, variants plugin)

Extends LinearFeatureBaseDisplay for GPU-accelerated variant rendering.

Slots go on a display entry: "displays": [{ "type": "LinearVariantDisplay", ... }], or in the track's displayDefaults.

Track type: VariantTrack.

Adapters: BedpeAdapter, SplitVcfTabixAdapter, StarFusionAdapter, VcfAdapter, VcfTabixAdapter.

Runtime API: docs topic "model:LinearVariantDisplay".

Minimal `VariantTrack` config. See the
[variant track guide](/docs/config_guides/variant_track) for all options:
```js
{
  type: 'VariantTrack',
  trackId: 'variants',
  name: 'Variants',
  assemblyNames: ['hg38'],
  adapter: {
    type: 'VcfTabixAdapter',
    uri: 'https://example.com/variants.vcf.gz',
  },
}
```

## Slots
- `filter: fieldPredicateList()`: The features the display draws, a list of [](/docs/config/fieldpredicate) entries a feature must all pass: a field of the feature's own (`{ field: "score", gte: 100 }`), a `jexl:` expression that must hold (`"jexl:feature.type ==…
- `tooltip: FeatureTooltip`: The box hovering a feature opens, a [](/docs/config/featuretooltip) object.
- `maxFeatureScreenDensity: number = 1`: maximum features per pixel before showing a "too many features" message — advanced
- `legend: Legend`: The display's color key, when it has one: the key an `encoding.color` field derives, or a variant track's consequence-impact / SV-type presets.
- `encoding: FeatureEncoding`: The channels the features paint through: `encoding.color`, each feature's main fill.
- `mark: FeatureMark`: The box each feature draws as, a [](/docs/config/featuremark) object: `{ height: 6 }`.
- `displayMode: stringEnum (normal, compact, superCompact, collapsed) = 'normal'`: Feature height preset, `normal` by default; `compact` and `superCompact` shrink the rows, and `collapsed` packs every feature onto a single row with all labels hidden
- `facet: SectionFacet`: One labelled section of the track per value of a field: `"strand"`, or `{ field, sort }` with the order its sections stack in.
